Source and target must be the same normalized repo identity, branch and exact OID. Apply preflights the complete set, reopens both roots through held handles, and journals the transfer:
127
128	- missing target: stage private temp (`0600`), stream/hash exact length, sync, then publish atomically without replacement;
129	- identical target: no-op/current;
130	- differing target: block unless `--replace`; replace requires the target digest observed in the displayed plan, private rollback copy, atomic swap, post-write rehash and rollback/reconciliation on failure;
131	- `--yes` never implies `--replace`; no deletion or last-writer-wins mode.
132
133	Target acceptance additionally retains each transferred file as an immutable, manifest-bound private recovery blob under the target transfer store; it materializes and rehashes that blob in staging. A source-deletion acknowledgement releases only ownership coordination: the blob, manifest and receipt reference remain immutable for the full recovery-receipt lifetime, including after A is gone and B’s working checkout is modified or evicted. They may be released only by a separately confirmed durable-receipt purge or after an independently restore-verified immutable backup supersedes them. B’s current-version replace/files/evict flows must honor this retention record. A must not treat a mutable working copy as deletion proof and must preserve its staged source if the target blob cannot be revalidated. Standalone `fleet files` may release the blob when source is retained, or use explicit `--retain-for-evict` to create recovery evidence.
134
135	Clamp final privacy to owner-only (`0600`, or `0700` only for explicitly executable source); do not copy ACL/xattr/owner/timestamps. Public human/JSON results contain path/size/state only—no content or hash. Native Windows targets remain capability-blocked before content is sent until the transport, ACL, reparse-point and atomicity contract is fully implemented and tested.
136
137	# Transfer protocol
138
139	## Target preparation
140
141	Separate branch/ref evidence from checkout evidence. For every selected task/current branch, A resolves `refs/heads/<branch>` directly through the shared Git common directory and captures exact OID/object format without requiring it to be checked out. Only branches with an existing checkout require conflict-free, operation-free, fully clean checkout evidence. COLD/unattached task refs must equal the freshly fetched/advertised remote tip before transfer and remain COLD on B with no checkout; this lets one repository transfer several serial branch-mode tasks without pretending they are all attached. Every published ref uses an explicit `<oid>:refs/heads/<branch>` ordinary push and the live remote tip must equal exactly that OID (not merely contain it).
142
143	Before A is fenced, B may only create a durable reservation, validate conflicts, and fetch expected objects into a private, non-discoverable transfer staging repository. Existing clones are reserved through the shared lease authority but no branch/worktree is moved; absent clones are staged under the private transfer directory rather than passed directly to `repo.Acquire`. Operation-owned incomplete staging can be verified and safely recreated/reused on retry, while any pre-existing or user-modified destination remains untouched.
144
145	After A’s fence is durable, B holds its repository/branch leases while publishing the target state. It matches all configured fetch/push identities and reuses exactly one clone; ambiguity blocks. If absent, it computes the final destination from B’s own path policy and materializes the verified staging clone without exposing a partial canonical checkout. It then creates/fast-forwards only the checkouts required by task state/mode. Ahead/diverged/dirty/live-agent targets block. Worktree tasks use B’s configured path and explicit expected ref; WARM worktree tasks get a checkout, COLD tasks do not. Branch/direct tasks may use canonical checkout only when unique and safe—never silently change mode. Acceptance may apply only deterministic, journaled portable files; it never runs `post_create`, dependency installers/copies, or other arbitrary provisioning inside the replayable distributed transaction. Transfer does not copy trust/credentials or open a runtime. Accepted HOT tasks become WARM; WARM/COLD stay as-is. After acceptance, B runs provisioning as a separate B-owned setup transaction through `dev resume` or `dev wt provision`; accepted existing WARM checkouts must enter this flow just like newly recreated worktrees. A private journal is bound to checkout identity/OID and provisioning-plan hash. Before each arbitrary command, fsync `running`; after success, fsync `completed`. A crash in `running` becomes `indeterminate` and is never auto-replayed—only explicit `--retry-indeterminate` or operator-attested `--mark-complete` can advance it. A journal cannot promise exactly-once for an external side effect, so automatic resume is limited to content-addressed/proven-idempotent steps. Context separately reports `transfer-complete` and `setup-pending/indeterminate/ready` so acceptance is never misrepresented as a fully provisioned environment.
146
147	## Sidecar rehydration
148
149	Portable task DTO contains stable ID, name/repo display, branch/base/mode/state/next/note/tags/timestamps and source provenance, but never A paths or runtime handles. On B, bind `RepoPath`/`WorktreePath` from B, clear runtime/agent hints, and import with exact-ID + revision conflict detection. Add task-store cross-process locking/CAS, but make the operation lease—not the task file—the authoritative fence so a selected branch with no task is still protected. Retrofit every current `dev` path that can mutate or expose a certified repository/branch/checkout/sidecar (`dev git`, lifecycle/TUI, adopt, worktree/repo/bootstrap/fleet setup, artifact finalization, local-file apply) to acquire/check the same lease before its first effect and hold it through Git/filesystem changes plus final CAS.
150
151	Catalog import preserves stable ID, metadata/tags/remote identity, adds B’s machine-specific location, and blocks pending move or conflicting ID/path/non-empty summaries. Note import preserves ID/repository ID/timestamps/tags/body; exact revision is idempotent, differing same-ID content blocks. Durable Markdown is written before disposable FTS rebuild; FTS failure is reported without rolling back durable notes. Note/file content travels only via bounded SSH stdin and is never echoed or cached.
152
153	## Idempotent no-two-writer handoff
154
155	Persist strict private source and target journals keyed by random transfer ID + manifest digest. Sequence:
156
157	1. **Plan**: live source/target assessment, no mutation.
158	2. **Publish**: create source intent; revalidate fingerprint; push/verify exact branch OIDs.
159	3. **Reserve/stage B**: durably reserve the target identities, validate sidecar/path conflicts and fetch objects into private staging only. Do not publish a working checkout, provision, write portable files, or expose target tasks.
160	4. **Fence A**: from an external coordinator, require caller/runtime outside all selected checkouts. Acquire all selected branch/repository operation leases in deterministic order, thereby drain already-started current-version mutators; while still holding them, revalidate Git/sidecar revisions, record B machine ID + fencing epoch durably, normalize HOT→WARM and then release the locks. Every later current-version source mutation sees the fence and fails. Keep every A byte.
161	5. **Accept/publish B**: under the same target reservations/leases, require the exact epoch/digest, revalidate staging and target state, publish/create the required checkouts, apply optional deterministic portable files, and import catalog/notes/tasks idempotently. Do not run arbitrary provisioning. Set B owner and write the acceptance receipt last; only then release the target reservation so ordinary B commands can see a writable accepted state and later run local `dev resume` provisioning.
162	6. **Complete/reconcile**: lost response is resolved through `fleet transfer status`; no distributed rollback. A remains present but fenced until explicit eviction or ownership return.
163
164	Same ID+digest resumes; same ID+different digest rejects. `abort` is terminal only before source fence and cleans solely journal-owned staging. After fence, `return` first acquires B’s leases, quiesces the exact manifest, writes a durable `returned` tombstone keyed by ID/digest/epoch that permanently rejects delayed prepare/accept replays, then lets A verify it and CAS-unfence the unchanged source while advancing the epoch. If B is unreachable or indeterminate, A remains safely fenced; generic `resume --force` cannot override a transfer fence. This permits a zero-writer window but never intentionally two cooperative writers. Document that raw Git and old binaries can bypass dev’s lease.
165
166	# Backup, reclaim, restore, and eviction
167
168	## Backup receipt
169
170	Add a fresh `gitx` recovery snapshot that inventories all local `refs/heads/*`, tags, notes, stash and other refs/OIDs; dirty/untracked/ignored/unreadable paths; Git operations/worktrees; LFS; submodules/nested repositories; shallow/partial clone, alternates and external/shared Git storage. Do not derive eviction cleanliness solely from `StatusOf`/`AnalyzeFinish`: enumerate index flags (`assume-unchanged`, `skip-worktree`, sparse-index state) without mutating the real index, then read/hash every materialized tracked path through held roots into a raw-byte manifest. The restore drill must independently materialize the receipt and compare exact working-tree bytes; hidden edits, unsafe sparse entries, clean/smudge-filter differences or missing external filter behavior must either enter an immutable recovery artifact or block/require a named discard. Repeat the flag/raw-byte proof during final eviction under the operation leases. Separately enumerate every private GitDir/common-dir administrative entry (config, hooks, info/exclude/attributes, rr-cache, reflogs and unknown files) through held roots. Classify only proven Git-managed/regenerable entries as reconstructible; preserve each remaining regular file in a private recovery artifact outside the eviction roots or require an item-scoped discard. Credential-bearing config is never uploaded to a Git remote. `RecoveryTopology` remains descriptive and is never promoted to proof.
171
172	`backup --push` authorizes one resolved effective push endpoint, not merely a remote name. Resolve Git rewrites plus every `pushurl`; if more than one effective destination exists, fail closed and require a dedicated single-endpoint recovery remote. Show the sanitized endpoint and exact ref mappings, bind both to the plan fingerprint, re-resolve immediately before push, refuse non-fast-forward/conflicting writes, and verify mappings at that same endpoint. Stash/custom refs require explicit receipt-scoped recovery mappings; unresolved reflog-only/unreachable objects remain blockers unless separately acknowledged for discard. Write an append-only private schema-v1 receipt only after verification; it records endpoint-set digest, exact ref/OID mappings, object/admin-artifact manifest digests, exclusions, source fingerprint and protocol versions—not credentials/raw URLs.
173
174	## Reclaim and restore proof
175
176	`reclaim` joins fresh evidence for every checkout/root, ref/object, Git-administrative entry, ignored file, immutable portable-file recovery blob, task/fence, catalog/note revision, artifact, all available runtime backends, caller containment, owned/shared bytes and configured fleet state. Each potentially unique item must map to an immutable recovery artifact/receipt, retained XDG state outside every deletion root, or a separately named item/category discard acknowledgement; a mutable live B working copy alone never qualifies. Stale/no-dev/unreachable evidence is indeterminate, never pass.
177
178	`restore --verify` restores into an isolated new staging directory, fetches every receipt mapping, verifies exact refs/OIDs and reachable object closure, restores and byte-verifies the classified Git-administrative artifact at the correct post-clone phase, and checks LFS/submodule proof where supported. It also materializes every portable-file recovery blob used by the eviction gate without exposing contents in output. Unsupported LFS/submodule/nested/external-object layouts block eviction rather than weakening the claim. Regular `restore --apply` uses the same plan/revalidation to reconstruct a real destination. A backup receipt without a successful matching restore drill cannot authorize eviction.
179
180	## Journaled actual eviction
181
182	`evict` never runs inside transfer. It defaults to the same report as reclaim and requires explicit `--apply`, exact target, matching receipt, current verified restore, and exact confirmation (`YES`; noninteractive `--yes` only with explicit target). Named acknowledgements such as `--discard-ignored`, `--discard-dirty`, `--discard-unreachable`, `--override-keep` are independent; `--yes` does not imply data loss and there is no generic `--force`.
183
184	Under recovery/task/catalog/Git operation leases, evict re-runs every check, closes only eligible runtime surfaces from outside them, waits and re-enumerates all backends, and freezes every reviewed checkout/Git root. Apply filesystem custody to **each** owned linked worktree before removal: write a per-root intent, use a Git-aware move into an unguessable same-parent private staging path so registration/common-dir remain valid, revoke traversal/new opens, completely enumerate file and directory descriptors into that staged inode tree, wait for existing handles to close, rerun that worktree’s index-flag/raw-byte proof, then remove the staged registration while preserving its branch/common-dir. A linked root that cannot be moved/probed/reproved blocks instead of falling back to ordinary `git worktree remove`.
185
186	After all linked roots are safely retired, apply the same sequence to the ordinary canonical clone: write/finalize its intent, atomically rename it into same-parent private staging, revoke new opens, drain all handles, and rerun the full raw-byte/Git-administrative manifest proof under custody before physical removal. If handle enumeration is unavailable/incomplete, any writer remains, or evidence changes at any root, preserve every affected staged root/intent and return indeterminate for later reconcile—never continue on an acknowledgement disguised as proof. External git dirs, alternates, cross-filesystem/shared-common-dir ambiguity, and platforms without the custody/open-handle contract block actual eviction.
187
188	Only after target bytes are absent: durably record source deletion completion on A, have B acknowledge it to release the transfer ownership hold (not the recovery blobs), remove A task records whose exact portable revisions were accepted by B (transfer receipt retains audit data), mark A catalog location `evicted` with recovery/restore reference, and clear the intent. If B/recovery evidence becomes unreachable after staging rename but before physical deletion, preserve the staged A root and reconcile rather than continue. Retain catalog metadata, quick-note copies, Git-administrative recovery artifacts, portable-file blobs, stats and transfer/recovery receipts outside clone roots for their receipt lifetimes; deleting those durable recovery assets is a future separately scoped, confirmed purge. Other ignored data blocks or needs its named discard acknowledgement.

255	// RecoverySnapshot is a read-only, content-free public description of ordinary
256	// Git state. Raw regular-file bodies are retained only in private maps and are
257	// available as defensive copies to the later recovery artifact builder.
258	type RecoverySnapshot struct {
259		Completeness RecoveryCompleteness   `json:"completeness"`
260		ObjectFormat string                 `json:"object_format,omitempty"`
261		Repository   RecoveryRepositoryFacts `json:"repository"`
262		Refs         []RecoveryRef          `json:"refs"`
263		Worktrees    []RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot `json:"worktrees"`
264		AdminRoots   []RecoveryAdminRoot    `json:"admin_roots"`
265		Findings     []RecoveryFinding      `json:"findings"`
266
267		trackedBytes map[string][]byte
268		adminBytes   map[string][]byte
269	}

271	// RawTrackedBytes returns a defensive copy of the raw working-tree bytes for a
272	// stably read materialized regular file.
273	func (snapshot RecoverySnapshot) RawTrackedBytes(worktreePath, relativePath string) ([]byte, bool) {
274		data, ok := snapshot.trackedBytes[recoveryTrackedKey(worktreePath, relativePath)]
275		if !ok {
276			return nil, false
277		}
278		return bytes.Clone(data), true
279	}
280
281	// RawAdminBytes returns a defensive copy of one stably read regular Git
282	// administrative file.
283	func (snapshot RecoverySnapshot) RawAdminBytes(root RecoveryAdminRootKind, relativePath string) ([]byte, bool) {
284		data, ok := snapshot.adminBytes[recoveryAdminKey(root, relativePath)]
285		if !ok {
286			return nil, false
287		}
288		return bytes.Clone(data), true
289	}
290
291	// HasBlockingFindings reports whether collection found either unsupported data
292	// topology or incomplete evidence. It is descriptive and does not itself grant
293	// any reclaim or eviction authorization.
294	func (snapshot RecoverySnapshot) HasBlockingFindings() bool {
295		for _, finding := range snapshot.Findings {
296			if finding.Blocking {
297				return true
298			}
299		}
300		return false
301	}
302
303	// RecoverySnapshotOf captures refs, registered worktrees, every worktree index
304	// and materialized tracked file, private Git administration, and unsupported
305	// storage topologies without modifying Git state. Ordinary probe failures are
306	// retained in Findings and produce a partial snapshot; cancellation is retained
307	// and also returned to the caller.
308	func RecoverySnapshotOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (RecoverySnapshot, error) {
309		snapshot := RecoverySnapshot{
310			Completeness: RecoveryCompletenessComplete,
311			Refs:         []RecoveryRef{},
312			Worktrees:    []RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot{},
313			AdminRoots:   []RecoveryAdminRoot{},
314			Findings:     []RecoveryFinding{},
315			trackedBytes: make(map[string][]byte),
316			adminBytes:   make(map[string][]byte),
317		}
318		collector := recoveryCollector{ctx: ctx, snapshot: &snapshot}
319		if err := collector.contextError("repository", dir); err != nil {
320			collector.finalize()
321			return snapshot, err
322		}
323
324		repository, err := Discover(ctx, dir)
325		if err != nil {
326			if cancelErr := collector.failure("repository-probe-failed", "repository", dir, err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
327				collector.finalize()
328				return snapshot, cancelErr
329			}
330			snapshot.Completeness = RecoveryCompletenessUnknown
331			collector.finalize()
332			return snapshot, err
333		}
334		snapshot.Repository = RecoveryRepositoryFacts{
335			Root:            repository.Root,
336			GitDir:          filepath.Clean(repository.GitDir),
337			CommonDir:       filepath.Clean(repository.GitCommonDir),
338			Bare:            repository.Bare,
339			PromisorRemotes: []string{},
340			Alternates:      []RecoveryAlternate{},
341		}
342
343		if err := collector.collectObjectFormat(repository); err != nil {
344			collector.finalize()
345			return snapshot, err
346		}
347		if err := collector.collectRefs(repository); err != nil {
348			collector.finalize()
349			return snapshot, err
350		}
351		if err := collector.collectRepositoryConfig(repository); err != nil {
352			collector.finalize()
353			return snapshot, err
354		}
355		if err := collector.collectShallow(repository); err != nil {
356			collector.finalize()
357			return snapshot, err
358		}
359		if err := collector.collectWorktreeList(repository); err != nil {
360			collector.finalize()
361			return snapshot, err
362		}
363		collector.collectStoragePlacement(repository)
364
365		for index := range snapshot.Worktrees {
366			if err := collector.collectWorktree(repository, &snapshot.Worktrees[index]); err != nil {
367				collector.finalize()
368				return snapshot, err
369			}
370		}
371		if err := collector.collectAdminRoots(repository); err != nil {
372			collector.finalize()
373			return snapshot, err
374		}
375		collector.collectObjectStoreFeatures(repository)
376		collector.finalize()
377		return snapshot, nil
378	}
379
380	type recoveryCollector struct {
381		ctx            context.Context
382		snapshot       *RecoverySnapshot
383		cancelRecorded bool
384	}
385
386	func (collector *recoveryCollector) contextError(scope, subject string) error {
387		if cause := context.Cause(collector.ctx); cause != nil {
388			if !collector.cancelRecorded {
389				collector.cancelRecorded = true
390				collector.addFinding(RecoveryFinding{
391					Code: "collection-cancelled", Kind: RecoveryFindingProbeFailure,
392					Scope: scope, Subject: subject, Blocking: true, Message: cause.Error(),
393				})
394			}
395			collector.markPartial(nil)
396			return cause
397		}
398		return nil
399	}
400
401	func (collector *recoveryCollector) failure(code, scope, subject string, err error, local *RecoveryCompleteness) error {
402		if cause := context.Cause(collector.ctx); cause != nil || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
403			if cause == nil {
404				cause = err
405			}
406			if !collector.cancelRecorded {
407				collector.cancelRecorded = true
408				collector.addFinding(RecoveryFinding{
409					Code: "collection-cancelled", Kind: RecoveryFindingProbeFailure,
410					Scope: scope, Subject: subject, Blocking: true, Message: cause.Error(),
411				})
412			}
413			collector.markPartial(local)
414			return cause
415		}
416		collector.markPartial(local)
417		collector.addFinding(RecoveryFinding{
418			Code: code, Kind: RecoveryFindingProbeFailure, Scope: scope,
419			Subject: subject, Blocking: true, Message: recoveryCleanText(err.Error()),
420		})
421		return nil
422	}
423
424	func (collector *recoveryCollector) blocker(code, scope, subject, message string) {
425		collector.addFinding(RecoveryFinding{
426			Code: code, Kind: RecoveryFindingBlocker, Scope: scope,
427			Subject: subject, Blocking: true, Message: message,
428		})
429	}
430
431	func (collector *recoveryCollector) addFinding(finding RecoveryFinding) {
432		finding.Code = recoveryIdentifier(finding.Code)
433		finding.Scope = recoveryIdentifier(finding.Scope)
434		finding.Subject = recoveryCleanSubject(finding.Subject)
435		finding.Message = recoveryCleanText(finding.Message)
436		collector.snapshot.Findings = append(collector.snapshot.Findings, finding)
437	}
438
439	func (collector *recoveryCollector) markPartial(local *RecoveryCompleteness) {
440		if collector.snapshot.Completeness != RecoveryCompletenessUnknown {
441			collector.snapshot.Completeness = RecoveryCompletenessPartial
442		}
443		if local != nil && *local != RecoveryCompletenessUnknown {
444			*local = RecoveryCompletenessPartial
445		}
446	}
447
448	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectObjectFormat(repository Repo) error {
449		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, repository.GitCommonDir, nil,
450			"rev-parse", "--show-object-format=storage")
451		if err != nil {
452			if cancelErr := collector.failure("object-format-probe-failed", "object-format", "repository", err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
453				return cancelErr
454			}
455		}
456		format := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
457		if format == "" {
458			if err == nil {
459				_ = collector.failure("object-format-parse-failed", "object-format", "repository", errors.New("Git returned an empty object format"), nil)
460			}
461			return nil
462		}
463		if strings.ContainsAny(format, "\x00\r\n \t") {
464			_ = collector.failure("object-format-parse-failed", "object-format", "repository", fmt.Errorf("unexpected object format %q", format), nil)
465			return nil
466		}
467		collector.snapshot.ObjectFormat = format
468		return nil
469	}
470
471	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectRefs(repository Repo) error {
472		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, repository.GitCommonDir, nil,
473			"for-each-ref", "--sort=refname", "--format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(objecttype)%00", "refs")
474		if err != nil {
475			if cancelErr := collector.failure("refs-probe-failed", "refs", "repository", err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
476				return cancelErr
477			}
478		}
479		refs, parseErr := parseRecoveryRefs(output)
480		collector.snapshot.Refs = refs
481		if parseErr != nil {
482			_ = collector.failure("refs-parse-failed", "refs", "repository", parseErr, nil)
483		}
484		return nil
485	}
486
487	func parseRecoveryRefs(output []byte) ([]RecoveryRef, error) {
488		refs := []RecoveryRef{}
489		var parseErrors []error
490		for recordIndex, record := range bytes.Split(output, []byte{'\n'}) {
491			record = bytes.TrimSuffix(record, []byte{'\r'})
492			if len(record) == 0 {
493				continue
494			}
495			fields := bytes.Split(record, []byte{0})
496			if len(fields) == 4 && len(fields[3]) == 0 {
497				fields = fields[:3]
498			}
499			if len(fields) != 3 {
500				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("ref record %d has %d fields", recordIndex, len(fields)))
501				continue
502			}
503			name, oid, objectType := string(fields[0]), string(fields[1]), string(fields[2])
504			if !utf8.ValidString(name) || !strings.HasPrefix(name, "refs/") || oid == "" || objectType == "" {
505				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("ref record %d is invalid", recordIndex))
506				continue
507			}
508			refs = append(refs, RecoveryRef{Name: name, OID: oid, ObjectType: objectType, Kind: recoveryRefKind(name)})
509		}
510		sort.Slice(refs, func(i, j int) bool { return refs[i].Name < refs[j].Name })
511		return refs, errors.Join(parseErrors...)
512	}
513
514	func recoveryRefKind(name string) RecoveryRefKind {
515		switch {
516		case strings.HasPrefix(name, "refs/heads/"):
517			return RecoveryRefHead
518		case strings.HasPrefix(name, "refs/tags/"):
519			return RecoveryRefTag
520		case strings.HasPrefix(name, "refs/notes/"):
521			return RecoveryRefNote
522		case name == "refs/stash":
523			return RecoveryRefStash
524		case strings.HasPrefix(name, "refs/remotes/"):
525			return RecoveryRefRemote
526		default:
527			return RecoveryRefOther
528		}
529	}
530
531	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectRepositoryConfig(repository Repo) error {
532		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, repository.GitCommonDir, nil,
533			"config", "--null", "--local", "--list")
534		if err != nil {
535			if cancelErr := collector.failure("config-probe-failed", "repository-config", "repository", err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
536				return cancelErr
537			}
538		}
539		var parseErrors []error
540		promisorRemotes := map[string]struct{}{}
541		for recordIndex, record := range recoveryNULRecords(output) {
542			newline := bytes.IndexByte(record, '\n')
543			if newline < 1 {
544				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("config record %d has no key/value separator", recordIndex))
545				continue
546			}
547			key := strings.ToLower(string(record[:newline]))
548			value := string(record[newline+1:])
549			switch {
550			case key == "extensions.partialclone":
551				if strings.TrimSpace(value) != "" {
552					collector.snapshot.Repository.PartialClone = true
553					promisorRemotes[strings.TrimSpace(value)] = struct{}{}
554				}
555			case strings.HasPrefix(key, "remote.") && strings.HasSuffix(key, ".promisor"):
556				remote := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "remote."), ".promisor")
557				parsed, boolErr := recoveryGitBool(value)
558				if boolErr != nil {
559					parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("config %s: %w", key, boolErr))
560					continue
561				}
562				if parsed {
563					collector.snapshot.Repository.Promisor = true
564					collector.snapshot.Repository.PartialClone = true
565					promisorRemotes[remote] = struct{}{}
566				}
567			case strings.HasPrefix(key, "remote.") && strings.HasSuffix(key, ".partialclonefilter"):
568				remote := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "remote."), ".partialclonefilter")
569				collector.snapshot.Repository.PartialClone = true
570				promisorRemotes[remote] = struct{}{}
571			case strings.HasPrefix(key, "filter.lfs."):
572				collector.snapshot.Repository.LFSConfigured = true
573			}
574		}
575		for remote := range promisorRemotes {
576			if remote != "" {
577				collector.snapshot.Repository.PromisorRemotes = append(collector.snapshot.Repository.PromisorRemotes, remote)
578			}
579		}
580		sort.Strings(collector.snapshot.Repository.PromisorRemotes)
581		if parseErr := errors.Join(parseErrors...); parseErr != nil {
582			_ = collector.failure("config-parse-failed", "repository-config", "repository", parseErr, nil)
583		}
584		return nil
585	}
586
587	func recoveryGitBool(value string) (bool, error) {
588		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value)) {
589		case "true", "yes", "on", "1":
590			return true, nil
591		case "false", "no", "off", "0", "":
592			return false, nil
593		default:
594			return false, fmt.Errorf("invalid Git boolean %q", value)
595		}
596	}
597
598	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectShallow(repository Repo) error {
599		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, repository.GitCommonDir, nil,
600			"rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository")
601		if err != nil {
602			if cancelErr := collector.failure("shallow-probe-failed", "object-store", "repository", err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
603				return cancelErr
604			}
605			return nil
606		}
607		shallow, parseErr := strconv.ParseBool(strings.TrimSpace(string(output)))
608		if parseErr != nil {
609			_ = collector.failure("shallow-parse-failed", "object-store", "repository", parseErr, nil)
610			return nil
611		}
612		collector.snapshot.Repository.Shallow = shallow
613		if shallow {
614			collector.blocker("shallow-repository", "object-store", "repository", "repository history is shallow")
615		}
616		return nil
617	}
618
619	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectWorktreeList(repository Repo) error {
620		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, repository.GitCommonDir, nil,
621			"worktree", "list", "--porcelain", "-z")
622		if err != nil {
623			if cancelErr := collector.failure("worktrees-probe-failed", "worktrees", "repository", err, nil); cancelErr != nil {
624				return cancelErr
625			}
626		}
627		worktrees, parseErr := parseRecoveryWorktrees(output)
628		if parseErr != nil {
629			_ = collector.failure("worktrees-parse-failed", "worktrees", "repository", parseErr, nil)
630		}
631		if len(worktrees) == 0 && repository.Root != "" {
632			worktrees = append(worktrees, RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot{
633				Path: repository.Root, GitDir: repository.GitDir, Bare: repository.Bare,
634				Main: true, Presence: RecoveryPresenceUnknown, Completeness: RecoveryCompletenessPartial,
635			})
636			if err == nil && parseErr == nil {
637				_ = collector.failure("worktrees-parse-failed", "worktrees", "repository", errors.New("Git returned no worktrees"), &worktrees[0].Completeness)
638			}
639		}
640		collector.snapshot.Worktrees = worktrees
641		return nil
642	}
643
644	func parseRecoveryWorktrees(output []byte) ([]RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot, error) {
645		worktrees := []RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot{}
646		var current *RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot
647		var parseErrors []error
648		flush := func() {
649			if current == nil {
650				return
651			}
652			if current.Path == "" {
653				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, errors.New("worktree record has no path"))
654			} else {
655				current.Main = len(worktrees) == 0
656				worktrees = append(worktrees, *current)
657			}
658			current = nil
659		}
660		for fieldIndex, raw := range bytes.Split(output, []byte{0}) {
661			if len(raw) == 0 {
662				flush()
663				continue
664			}
665			keyBytes, valueBytes, hasValue := bytes.Cut(raw, []byte{' '})
666			key, value := string(keyBytes), ""
667			if hasValue {
668				value = string(valueBytes)
669			}
670			if key == "worktree" {
671				flush()
672				current = &RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot{
673					Path: value, Presence: RecoveryPresenceUnknown, Completeness: RecoveryCompletenessComplete,
674					Operations: []RecoveryOperation{}, IndexEntries: []RecoveryIndexEntry{},
675					TrackedFiles: []RecoveryTrackedFile{}, DirtyPaths: []RecoveryDirtyPath{},
676					UntrackedPaths: []string{}, IgnoredPaths: []string{}, LFSPaths: []RecoveryLFSPath{},
677					Submodules: []RecoverySubmodule{}, NestedRepositories: []RecoveryNestedRepository{},
678				}
679				continue
680			}
681			if current == nil {
682				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("worktree field %d precedes a worktree path", fieldIndex))
683				continue
684			}
685			switch key {
686			case "HEAD":
687				current.Head = value
688			case "branch":
689				current.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(value, "refs/heads/")
690			case "detached":
691				current.Detached = true
692			case "bare":
693				current.Bare = true
694			case "locked":
695				current.Locked, current.LockedReason = true, value
696			case "prunable":
697				current.Prunable, current.PrunableReason = true, value
698			}
699		}
700		flush()
701		return worktrees, errors.Join(parseErrors...)
702	}
703
704	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectStoragePlacement(repository Repo) {
705		facts := &collector.snapshot.Repository
706		if repository.Root != "" {
707			inside, err := pathx.Contains(repository.Root, repository.GitDir)
708			if err != nil {
709				_ = collector.failure("git-dir-placement-probe-failed", "storage", "git-dir", err, nil)
710			} else {
711				facts.GitDirOutsideRoot = !inside
712			}
713		}
714		mainRoot := repository.Root
715		for _, worktree := range collector.snapshot.Worktrees {
716			if worktree.Main && worktree.Path != "" {
717				mainRoot = worktree.Path
718				break
719			}
720		}
721		if mainRoot != "" {

735	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectIndex(worktree *RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot) error {
736		output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, worktree.Path, nil,
737			"ls-files", "--stage", "-v", "-z", "--sparse", "--full-name")
738		if err != nil {
739			if cancelErr := collector.failure("index-probe-failed", "index", worktree.Path, err, &worktree.Completeness); cancelErr != nil {
740				return cancelErr
741			}
742		}
743		entries, parseErr := parseRecoveryIndex(output)
744		worktree.IndexEntries = entries
745		if parseErr != nil {
746			_ = collector.failure("index-parse-failed", "index", worktree.Path, parseErr, &worktree.Completeness)
747		}
748		for _, entry := range entries {

752		}

756	func parseRecoveryIndex(output []byte) ([]RecoveryIndexEntry, error) {
757		entries := []RecoveryIndexEntry{}
758		var parseErrors []error
759		for recordIndex, record := range recoveryNULRecords(output) {
760			header, pathBytes, ok := bytes.Cut(record, []byte{'\t'})
761			if !ok || len(pathBytes) == 0 || !utf8.Valid(pathBytes) {
762				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("index record %d has an invalid path field", recordIndex))
763				continue
764			}
765			fields := strings.Fields(string(header))
766			if len(fields) != 4 || len(fields[0]) != 1 {
767				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("index record %d has an invalid header", recordIndex))
768				continue
769			}
770			if _, modeErr := strconv.ParseUint(fields[1], 8, 32); modeErr != nil {
771				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("index record %d mode %q: %w", recordIndex, fields[1], modeErr))
772				continue
773			}
774			stage, stageErr := strconv.Atoi(fields[3])
775			if stageErr != nil || stage < 0 || stage > 3 {
776				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("index record %d has invalid stage %q", recordIndex, fields[3]))
777				continue
778			}
779			tag := fields[0][0]
780			upper := tag
781			if upper >= 'a' && upper <= 'z' {
782				upper -= 'a' - 'A'
783			}
784			entries = append(entries, RecoveryIndexEntry{
785				Path: string(pathBytes), Mode: fields[1], OID: fields[2], Stage: stage, Tag: fields[0],
786				AssumeUnchanged: tag >= 'a' && tag <= 'z', SkipWorktree: upper == 'S',
787			})
788		}
789		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
790			if entries[i].Path != entries[j].Path {
791				return entries[i].Path < entries[j].Path
792			}
793			if entries[i].Stage != entries[j].Stage {
794				return entries[i].Stage < entries[j].Stage
795			}
796			return entries[i].Mode < entries[j].Mode
797		})
798		return entries, errors.Join(parseErrors...)
799	}

851	func parseRecoveryStatus(output []byte) ([]RecoveryDirtyPath, []string, error) {
852		records := recoveryNULRecords(output)
853		dirty := []RecoveryDirtyPath{}
854		untracked := []string{}
855		var parseErrors []error
856		for index := 0; index < len(records); index++ {
857			record := string(records[index])
858			if record == "" {
859				continue
860			}
861			switch record[0] {
862			case '1', '2':
863				fields := strings.Fields(record)
864				path := statusPath(record)
865				if len(fields) < 2 || len(fields[1]) != 2 || path == "" {
866					parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("status record %d is malformed", index))
867					continue
868				}
869				change := RecoveryDirtyPath{
870					Path: path, Kind: "ordinary", IndexStatus: string(fields[1][0]), WorktreeStatus: string(fields[1][1]),
871				}
872				if record[0] == '2' {
873					change.Kind = "rename-or-copy"
874					if index+1 >= len(records) {
875						parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("rename status record %d has no source path", index))
876					} else {
877						index++
878						change.OldPath = string(records[index])
879					}
880				}
881				dirty = append(dirty, change)
882			case 'u':
883				fields := strings.Fields(record)
884				path := statusPath(record)
885				if len(fields) < 2 || len(fields[1]) != 2 || path == "" {
886					parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("unmerged status record %d is malformed", index))
887					continue
888				}
889				dirty = append(dirty, RecoveryDirtyPath{
890					Path: path, Kind: "unmerged", IndexStatus: string(fields[1][0]), WorktreeStatus: string(fields[1][1]),
891				})
892			case '?':
893				path := strings.TrimPrefix(record, "? ")
894				if path == record || path == "" {
895					parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("untracked status record %d is malformed", index))
896					continue
897				}
898				untracked = append(untracked, path)
899			case '#':
900				// Branch headers are allowed if a future caller adds --branch.
901			default:
902				parseErrors = append(parseErrors, fmt.Errorf("unknown status record %d type %q", index, record[0]))
903			}
904		}
905		sort.Slice(dirty, func(i, j int) bool {
906			return strings.Join([]string{dirty[i].Path, dirty[i].OldPath, dirty[i].Kind}, "\x00") <
907				strings.Join([]string{dirty[j].Path, dirty[j].OldPath, dirty[j].Kind}, "\x00")
908		})
909		sort.Strings(untracked)
910		return dirty, untracked, errors.Join(parseErrors...)
911	}

938	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectLFS(worktree *RecoveryWorktreeSnapshot) error {
939		paths := make(map[string]struct{}, len(worktree.IndexEntries)+len(worktree.UntrackedPaths)+len(worktree.IgnoredPaths))
940		for _, entry := range worktree.IndexEntries {
941			paths[entry.Path] = struct{}{}
942		}
943		for _, path := range worktree.UntrackedPaths {
944			paths[path] = struct{}{}
945		}
946		for _, path := range worktree.IgnoredPaths {
947			paths[path] = struct{}{}
948		}
949		ordered := make([]string, 0, len(paths))
950		for path := range paths {
951			ordered = append(ordered, path)
952		}
953		sort.Strings(ordered)
954		if len(ordered) == 0 {
955			return nil
956		}
957		var input bytes.Buffer
958		for _, path := range ordered {
959			input.WriteString(path)
960			input.WriteByte(0)
961		}
962		byPath := map[string]*RecoveryLFSPath{}
963		probes := []struct {
964			name   string
965			cached bool
966		}{
967			{"index", true},
968			{"worktree", false},
969		}
970		for _, probe := range probes {
971			args := []string{"check-attr"}
972			if probe.cached {
973				args = append(args, "--cached")
974			}
975			args = append(args, "-z", "--stdin", "filter")
976			output, err := recoveryGit(collector.ctx, worktree.Path, input.Bytes(), args...)
977			if err != nil {
978				if cancelErr := collector.failure("lfs-attribute-probe-failed", "lfs", worktree.Path+":"+probe.name, err, &worktree.Completeness); cancelErr != nil {
979					return cancelErr
980				}
981			}
982			values := recoveryNULRecords(output)
983			if len(values)%3 != 0 {
984				_ = collector.failure("lfs-attribute-parse-failed", "lfs", worktree.Path+":"+probe.name,
985					fmt.Errorf("Git returned %d attribute fields, want a multiple of three", len(values)), &worktree.Completeness)
986				continue
987			}
988			for field := 0; field < len(values); field += 3 {
989				path, attribute, value := string(values[field]), string(values[field+1]), string(values[field+2])
990				if attribute != "filter" || value != "lfs" {
991					continue
992				}
993				fact := byPath[path]
994				if fact == nil {
995					fact = &RecoveryLFSPath{Path: path}
996					byPath[path] = fact
997				}
998				if probe.cached {
999					fact.IndexAttributes = true
1000				} else {
1001					fact.WorktreeAttributes = true
1002				}
1003			}
1004		}
1005		for _, path := range ordered {
1006			if fact := byPath[path]; fact != nil {
1007				worktree.LFSPaths = append(worktree.LFSPaths, *fact)
1008				collector.blocker("lfs-path", "lfs", worktree.Path+":"+path, "path is governed by the Git LFS filter")
1009			}
1010		}
1011		return nil
1012	}

1040	func (collector *recoveryCollector) collectObjectStoreFeatures(repository Repo) {
1041		facts := &collector.snapshot.Repository
1042		for _, root := range collector.snapshot.AdminRoots {
1043			if root.Kind != RecoveryAdminCommonDir {
1044				continue
1045			}
1046			for _, entry := range root.Entries {
1047				if entry.Type == RecoveryEntryRegular && strings.HasPrefix(entry.Path, "objects/pack/") && strings.HasSuffix(entry.Path, ".promisor") {
1048					facts.PromisorPackFiles++
1049				}
1050			}
1051		}
1052		if facts.PromisorPackFiles > 0 {
1053			facts.Promisor = true
1054			facts.PartialClone = true
1055		}
1056
1057		seenAlternates := map[string]struct{}{}
1058		addAlternate := func(source, path string) {
1059			path = strings.TrimSpace(path)
1060			if path == "" {
1061				return
1062			}
1063			if !filepath.IsAbs(path) && source == "objects/info/alternates" {
1064				path = filepath.Join(repository.GitCommonDir, "objects", path)
1065			}
1066			if canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path); err == nil {
1067				path = canonical
1068			} else {
1069				_ = collector.failure("alternate-path-probe-failed", "object-store", path, err, nil)
1070				path = filepath.Clean(path)
1071			}
1072			key := source + "\x00" + path
1073			if _, exists := seenAlternates[key]; exists {
1074				return
1075			}
1076			seenAlternates[key] = struct{}{}
1077			facts.Alternates = append(facts.Alternates, RecoveryAlternate{Source: source, Path: path})
1078			collector.blocker("alternate-object-store", "object-store", path, "repository depends on an alternate object directory")
1079		}
1080
1081		if data, ok := collector.snapshot.adminBytes[recoveryAdminKey(RecoveryAdminCommonDir, "objects/info/alternates")]; ok {
1082			for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(string(data), "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
1083				addAlternate("objects/info/alternates", line)
1084			}
1085		}
1086		for _, path := range filepath.SplitList(os.Getenv("GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES")) {
1087			addAlternate("environment", path)
1088		}
1089		sort.Slice(facts.Alternates, func(i, j int) bool {
1090			return strings.Join([]string{facts.Alternates[i].Source, facts.Alternates[i].Path}, "\x00") <
1091				strings.Join([]string{facts.Alternates[j].Source, facts.Alternates[j].Path}, "\x00")
1092		})
1093		if facts.PartialClone {
1094			collector.blocker("partial-clone", "object-store", "repository", "repository uses partial-clone storage")
1095		}
1096		if facts.Promisor {
1097			collector.blocker("promisor-object-store", "object-store", "repository", "repository has promisor object storage")
1098		}
1099	}

1125			})
1126		}

1136				strings.Join([]string{right.Code, string(right.Kind), right.Scope, right.Subject, right.Message}, "\x00")

1140	func recoveryGit(ctx context.Context, dir string, input []byte, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
1141		if cause := context.Cause(ctx); cause != nil {
1142			return nil, cause
1143		}
1144		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
1145		command := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
1146		command.Dir = dir
1147		command.Env = recoveryEnvironment()
1148		if input != nil {
1149			command.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(input)
1150		}
1151		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
1152		command.Stdout = &stdout
1153		command.Stderr = &stderr
1154		if err := command.Run(); err != nil {
1155			if cause := context.Cause(ctx); cause != nil {
1156				return stdout.Bytes(), cause
1157			}
1158			return stdout.Bytes(), &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
1159		}
1160		return stdout.Bytes(), nil
1161	}

1163	func recoveryEnvironment() []string {
1164		environment := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+1)
1165		for _, entry := range os.Environ() {
1166			key, _, _ := strings.Cut(entry, "=")
1167			if key != "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS" {
1168				environment = append(environment, entry)
1169			}
1170		}
1171		return append(environment, "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0")
1172	}

1174	func recoveryNULRecords(output []byte) [][]byte {
1175		if len(output) == 0 {
1176			return nil
1177		}
1178		records := bytes.Split(output, []byte{0})
1179		if len(records) > 0 && len(records[len(records)-1]) == 0 {
1180			records = records[:len(records)-1]
1181		}
1182		return records
1183	}

1185	func recoveryDigest(data []byte) string {
1186		digest := sha256.Sum256(data)
1187		return recoveryDigestPrefix + hex.EncodeToString(digest[:])

1198	func recoveryCleanText(value string) string {
1199		value = strings.ToValidUTF8(value, "�")
1200		value = strings.Map(func(character rune) rune {
1201			if unicode.IsControl(character) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, character) {
1202				return ' '
1203			}
1204			return character
1205		}, value)
1206		return strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(strings.Fields(value), " "))

1217	func recoveryIdentifier(value string) string {
1218		value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
1219		var result strings.Builder
1220		lastDash := false
1221		for _, character := range value {
1222			if character >= 'a' && character <= 'z' || character >= '0' && character <= '9' || character == '.' || character == '/' || character == ':' || character == '_' {
1223				result.WriteRune(character)
1224				lastDash = false
1225				continue
1226			}
1227			if !lastDash {
1228				result.WriteByte('-')
1229				lastDash = true
1230			}
1231		}
1232		identifier := strings.Trim(result.String(), "-./:_")
1233		if identifier == "" {
1234			return "unknown"
1235		}
1236		return identifier
1237	}

1	// Package safefile provides held-root filesystem operations for untrusted
2	// relative paths. It keeps traversal relative to os.Root handles, rejects links
3	// and special files, revalidates filesystem identity, and detects observable
4	// source mutation while reading.
5	package safefile
6
7	import (
8		"context"

18	var (
19		// ErrChanged reports that a named root, child, or file no longer identifies
20		// the object observed by the caller.
21		ErrChanged = errors.New("filesystem object changed")
22		// ErrUnsafeType reports a symlink, reparse point, directory, or other
23		// non-regular object where a regular file was required.
24		ErrUnsafeType = errors.New("unsafe filesystem object type")
25		// ErrFileLimit reports a regular file whose bytes exceed the read policy.
26		ErrFileLimit = errors.New("file size limit exceeded")

29	// OpenRoot opens path as a held os.Root and proves that the pre-open and
30	// post-open names identify the held directory. Symlinks and reparse points are
31	// rejected rather than followed.
32	func OpenRoot(path string) (*os.Root, fs.FileInfo, error) {
33		before, err := os.Lstat(path)
34		if err != nil {
35			return nil, nil, err
36		}
37		if unsafeLink(before) {
38			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root is a symlink or reparse point: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
39		}
40		if !before.IsDir() {
41			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root is not a directory: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
42		}
43		root, err := os.OpenRoot(path)
44		if err != nil {
45			return nil, nil, err
46		}
47		held, err := root.Stat(".")
48		if err != nil {
49			_ = root.Close()
50			return nil, nil, err
51		}
52		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
53		if err != nil || unsafeLink(held) || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() ||
54			!os.SameFile(before, held) || !os.SameFile(current, held) {
55			_ = root.Close()
56			if err != nil {
57				return nil, nil, err
58			}
59			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root changed while opening: %w", ErrChanged)
60		}
61		return root, held, nil
62	}

135	// ReadStableRegular reads one child file while proving that the directory name,
136	// opened descriptor, and final directory name all identify the expected regular
137	// file with unchanged observable metadata. maxBytes must be non-negative; zero
138	// means unbounded. Supplying the FileInfo from an earlier directory listing
139	// detects replacement or mutation between selection and opening.
140	func ReadStableRegular(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
141		if root == nil {
142			return nil, nil, errors.New("read stable file: nil root")
143		}
144		if maxBytes < 0 {
145			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("negative maximum file size: %w", ErrFileLimit)
146		}
147		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
148			return nil, nil, err
149		}
150		before, err := root.Lstat(name)
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, nil, err
153		}
154		if expected == nil {
155			expected = before
156		}
157		if unsafeLink(before) || !before.Mode().IsRegular() {
158			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is not a regular file: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
159		}
160		if !sameStableSourceState(expected, before) {
161			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed before opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
162		}
163		if maxBytes > 0 && before.Size() > maxBytes {
164			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", before.Size(), maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
165		}
166
167		file, err := openRegularForRead(root, name)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, nil, err
170		}
171		defer file.Close()
172		opened, err := file.Stat()
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, nil, err
175		}
176		if unsafeLink(opened) || !opened.Mode().IsRegular() || !sameStableSourceState(expected, opened) {
177			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
178		}
179		current, err := root.Lstat(name)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, nil, err
182		}
183		if unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, current) {
184			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
185		}
186
187		data, err := readAllContext(ctx, file, maxBytes)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, nil, err
190		}
191		after, err := file.Stat()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, nil, err
194		}
195		current, err = root.Lstat(name)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, nil, err
198		}
199		if unsafeLink(after) || unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, after) ||
200			!sameStableSourceState(after, current) || after.Size() != int64(len(data)) {
201			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed during read: %w", ErrChanged)
202		}
203		return data, opened, nil
204	}

206	// SameFileState compares identity, mode, size, and modification time. Stable
207	// reads and observed-target replacement additionally compare platform change
208	// time where the operating system exposes it.
209	func SameFileState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
210		return left != nil && right != nil && os.SameFile(left, right) &&
211			left.Mode() == right.Mode() && left.Size() == right.Size() && left.ModTime().Equal(right.ModTime())
212	}
213
214	func sameStableSourceState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
215		return SameFileState(left, right) && samePlatformState(left, right)
216	}
217
218	func readAllContext(ctx context.Context, reader io.Reader, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
219		var data []byte
220		buffer := make([]byte, 64*1024)
221		for {
222			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
223				return nil, err
224			}
225			read, err := reader.Read(buffer)
226			if read > 0 {
227				if maxBytes > 0 && int64(read) > maxBytes-int64(len(data)) {
228					return nil, fmt.Errorf("source exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
229				}
230				data = append(data, buffer[:read]...)
231			}
232			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
233				return data, nil
234			}
235			if err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238			if read == 0 {
239				return nil, io.ErrNoProgress
240			}
241		}
242	}
243
244	func unsafeLink(info fs.FileInfo) bool {
245		return info != nil && (info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || isReparsePoint(info))
246	}

31	// CreateNoClobber stages data in an unguessable owner-private file, syncs it,
32	// applies finalMode, and atomically hard-links it to the absent destination.
33	// The hard-link publication is same-directory and cannot replace an existing
34	// path. This generic helper exists so callers such as repotemplate can preserve
35	// intentional public modes; secret-bearing callers should use
36	// CreatePrivateNoClobber.
37	func CreateNoClobber(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, data []byte, finalMode fs.FileMode) (fs.FileInfo, error) {

67		published, err = root.Lstat(name)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("refresh published file %q: %w", name, err)
70		}
71		if err := syncRoot(root); err != nil {
72			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sync destination directory after creating %q: %w", name, err)
73		}
74		return published, nil
75	}
76
77	// CreatePrivateNoClobber is CreateNoClobber with a clamped owner-only final
78	// mode. executable is the only way to grant execute permission.
79	func CreatePrivateNoClobber(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, data []byte, executable bool) (fs.FileInfo, error) {
80		if int64(len(data)) > CompiledMaxFileBytes {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", name, len(data), CompiledMaxFileBytes, ErrFileLimit)
82		}
83		return CreateNoClobber(ctx, root, name, data, OwnerPrivateMode(executable))
84	}
85
86	// AtomicReplace stages and syncs data in the target directory, revalidates the
87	// existing regular file against observed, and atomically renames the staged file
88	// over it. Atomic describes publication, not a filesystem compare-and-swap: the
89	// metadata check and rename are separate syscalls. Callers performing digest-CAS
90	// must hold an exclusive cooperative operation lease, obtain observed from a
91	// fresh stable read/hash, and retain any rollback copy before invoking this
92	// primitive. It never follows a symlink or reparse point.
93	func AtomicReplace(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, observed fs.FileInfo, data []byte, finalMode fs.FileMode) (fs.FileInfo, error) {
94		if root == nil {
95			return nil, errors.New("atomic replace: nil root")
96		}
97		if observed == nil {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("replace %q without observed state: %w", name, ErrReplaceTarget)
99		}
100		if err := validateTargetName(name); err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		if err := verifyReplaceTarget(root, name, observed); err != nil {
104			return nil, err
105		}
106		stagedName, staged, err := stageRegular(ctx, root, data, finalMode)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		defer func() {
111			if stagedName != "" {
112				_ = root.Remove(stagedName)
113			}
114		}()
115		if err := verifyReplaceTarget(root, name, observed); err != nil {
116			return nil, err
117		}
118		if err := root.Rename(stagedName, name); err != nil {
119			return nil, fmt.Errorf("atomically replace %q: %w", name, err)
120		}
121		stagedName = ""
122		published, err := root.Lstat(name)
123		if err != nil {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verify replacement %q: %w", name, err)
125		}
126		if unsafeLink(published) || !published.Mode().IsRegular() || !SameFileState(staged, published) {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("replacement %q does not match staging file: %w", name, ErrChanged)
128		}
129		if err := syncRoot(root); err != nil {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sync destination directory after replacing %q: %w", name, err)
131		}
132		return published, nil
133	}
134
135	// AtomicReplacePrivate is AtomicReplace with owner-only final permissions.
136	func AtomicReplacePrivate(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, observed fs.FileInfo, data []byte, executable bool) (fs.FileInfo, error) {
137		if int64(len(data)) > CompiledMaxFileBytes {
138			return nil, fmt.Errorf("file %q is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", name, len(data), CompiledMaxFileBytes, ErrFileLimit)
139		}
140		return AtomicReplace(ctx, root, name, observed, data, OwnerPrivateMode(executable))
141	}
142
143	func verifyReplaceTarget(root *os.Root, name string, observed fs.FileInfo) error {
144		current, err := root.Lstat(name)
145		if err != nil {
146			return fmt.Errorf("inspect replacement target %q: %w: %w", name, err, ErrReplaceTarget)
147		}
148		if unsafeLink(current) || !current.Mode().IsRegular() || !sameStableSourceState(observed, current) {
149			return fmt.Errorf("replacement target %q changed or is not a regular file: %w", name, ErrReplaceTarget)
150		}
151		return nil
152	}
153
154	func stageRegular(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, data []byte, finalMode fs.FileMode) (string, fs.FileInfo, error) {
155		if finalMode&^fs.ModePerm != 0 {
156			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported final file mode %s", finalMode)
157		}
158		var name string
159		var writer *os.File
160		for attempt := 0; attempt < 32; attempt++ {
161			candidate, err := randomStageName()
162			if err != nil {
163				return "", nil, err
164			}
165			writer, err = root.OpenFile(candidate, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
166			if err == nil {
167				name = candidate
168				break
169			}
170			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrExist) {
171				return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("create private staging file: %w", err)
172			}
173		}
174		if writer == nil {
175			return "", nil, errors.New("create private staging file: too many name collisions")
176		}
177		keep := true
178		defer func() {
179			if keep {
180				_ = writer.Close()
181				_ = root.Remove(name)
182			}
183		}()
184		if err := writeAllContext(ctx, writer, data); err != nil {
185			return "", nil, err
186		}
187		if err := writer.Chmod(finalMode.Perm()); err != nil {
188			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("set staged file mode: %w", err)
189		}
190		if err := writer.Sync(); err != nil {
191			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("sync staged file: %w", err)
192		}
193		opened, err := writer.Stat()
194		if err != nil {
195			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("inspect staged file: %w", err)
196		}
197		if err := writer.Close(); err != nil {
198			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("close staged file: %w", err)
199		}
200		keep = false
201		current, err := root.Lstat(name)
202		if err != nil {
203			_ = root.Remove(name)
204			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("reopen staged file name: %w", err)
205		}
206		if unsafeLink(current) || !current.Mode().IsRegular() || !SameFileState(opened, current) {
207			_ = root.Remove(name)
208			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("staging file changed before publication: %w", ErrChanged)
209		}
210		return name, current, nil
211	}
212
213	func validateTargetName(name string) error {
214		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
215			return fmt.Errorf("invalid atomic file name %q: %w", name, err)
216		}
217		return nil
218	}
219
220	func writeAllContext(ctx context.Context, writer io.Writer, data []byte) error {
221		for len(data) > 0 {
222			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
223				return err
224			}
225			written, err := writer.Write(data)
226			if err != nil {
227				return err
228			}
229			if written == 0 {
230				return io.ErrShortWrite
231			}
232			data = data[written:]
233		}
234		return context.Cause(ctx)
235	}
236
237	func randomStageName() (string, error) {
238		var random [16]byte
239		if _, err := rand.Read(random[:]); err != nil {
240			return "", fmt.Errorf("generate staging file name: %w", err)
241		}
242		return ".dev-safefile-" + hex.EncodeToString(random[:]) + ".tmp", nil
243	}

1	package safefile

3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6
7		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
8	)
9
10	const (
11		// CompiledMaxFiles is the maximum number of portable files accepted by one
12		// operation. Runtime policy may lower, but never raise, this ceiling.
13		CompiledMaxFiles = 128
14		// CompiledMaxFileBytes is the maximum size of one portable file.
15		CompiledMaxFileBytes int64 = 8 << 20
16		// CompiledMaxTotalBytes is the maximum aggregate portable payload size.
17		CompiledMaxTotalBytes int64 = 32 << 20
18		// CompiledMaxPathBytes bounds a slash-separated portable relative path.
19		CompiledMaxPathBytes = 4096
20		// CompiledMaxComponentBytes bounds one portable path component.
21		CompiledMaxComponentBytes = 255
22		// CompiledMaxPathDepth bounds portable path nesting.
23		CompiledMaxPathDepth = 64
24	)
25
26	var (
27		// ErrInvalidLimits reports a zero, negative, or above-ceiling policy.
28		ErrInvalidLimits = errors.New("invalid safe-file limits")
29		// ErrManifestLimit reports a manifest that exceeds its validated policy.
30		ErrManifestLimit = errors.New("safe-file manifest limit exceeded")
31		// ErrDuplicatePath reports the same exact portable path more than once.
32		ErrDuplicatePath = errors.New("duplicate safe-file path")
33	)
34
35	// Limits is the reusable compiled policy for portable file manifests. Every
36	// field is required and must be no greater than the corresponding compiled
37	// ceiling, allowing host configuration to lower limits without weakening them.
38	type Limits struct {
39		MaxFiles          int
40		MaxFileBytes      int64
41		MaxTotalBytes     int64
42		MaxPathBytes      int
43		MaxComponentBytes int
44		MaxPathDepth      int
45	}
46
47	// DefaultLimits returns the maximum policy supported by this binary.
48	func DefaultLimits() Limits {
49		return Limits{
50			MaxFiles:          CompiledMaxFiles,
51			MaxFileBytes:      CompiledMaxFileBytes,
52			MaxTotalBytes:     CompiledMaxTotalBytes,
53			MaxPathBytes:      CompiledMaxPathBytes,
54			MaxComponentBytes: CompiledMaxComponentBytes,
55			MaxPathDepth:      CompiledMaxPathDepth,
56		}
57	}
58
59	// Validate rejects incomplete policy and values above the compiled ceilings.
60	func (limits Limits) Validate() error {
61		maximum := DefaultLimits()
62		switch {
63		case limits.MaxFiles <= 0 || limits.MaxFiles > maximum.MaxFiles:
64			return fmt.Errorf("max files %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxFiles, maximum.MaxFiles, ErrInvalidLimits)
65		case limits.MaxFileBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxFileBytes > maximum.MaxFileBytes:
66			return fmt.Errorf("max file bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxFileBytes, maximum.MaxFileBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
67		case limits.MaxTotalBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxTotalBytes > maximum.MaxTotalBytes:
68			return fmt.Errorf("max total bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxTotalBytes, maximum.MaxTotalBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
69		case limits.MaxPathBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxPathBytes > maximum.MaxPathBytes:
70			return fmt.Errorf("max path bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxPathBytes, maximum.MaxPathBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
71		case limits.MaxComponentBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxComponentBytes > maximum.MaxComponentBytes:
72			return fmt.Errorf("max component bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxComponentBytes, maximum.MaxComponentBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
73		case limits.MaxPathDepth <= 0 || limits.MaxPathDepth > maximum.MaxPathDepth:
74			return fmt.Errorf("max path depth %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxPathDepth, maximum.MaxPathDepth, ErrInvalidLimits)
75		default:
76			return nil
77		}
78	}
79
80	// PathLimits projects the filesystem path portion of a validated policy.
81	func (limits Limits) PathLimits() pathx.PortablePathLimits {
82		return pathx.PortablePathLimits{
83			MaxPathBytes:      limits.MaxPathBytes,
84			MaxComponentBytes: limits.MaxComponentBytes,
85			MaxDepth:          limits.MaxPathDepth,
86		}
87	}
88
89	// Metadata is the content-free portion of one portable regular file used for
90	// validating counts, sizes, paths, and collisions before any bytes are opened.
91	type Metadata struct {
92		Path string
93		Size int64
94	}
95
96	// ValidateManifest enforces a validated limits policy over the complete file
97	// set, including exact duplicates and portable case/normalization collisions.
98	func ValidateManifest(files []Metadata, limits Limits) error {
99		if err := limits.Validate(); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if len(files) > limits.MaxFiles {
103			return fmt.Errorf("manifest has %d files; maximum is %d: %w", len(files), limits.MaxFiles, ErrManifestLimit)
104		}
105		paths := make([]string, 0, len(files))
106		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(files))
107		var total int64
108		for _, file := range files {
109			if file.Size < 0 {
110				return fmt.Errorf("file %q has negative size: %w", file.Path, ErrManifestLimit)
111			}
112			if file.Size > limits.MaxFileBytes {
113				return fmt.Errorf("file %q is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", file.Path, file.Size, limits.MaxFileBytes, ErrManifestLimit)
114			}
115			if _, exists := seen[file.Path]; exists {
116				return fmt.Errorf("path %q appears more than once: %w", file.Path, ErrDuplicatePath)
117			}
118			seen[file.Path] = struct{}{}
119			paths = append(paths, file.Path)
120			if file.Size > limits.MaxTotalBytes-total {
121				return fmt.Errorf("manifest exceeds %d total bytes: %w", limits.MaxTotalBytes, ErrManifestLimit)
122			}
123			total += file.Size
124		}
125		if err := pathx.ValidatePortablePathSet(paths, limits.PathLimits()); err != nil {
126			return err
127		}
128		return nil
129	}

242			t.Fatalf("outside target changed: %q, %v", body, err)
243		}

246	func TestFilePrimitivesRejectNonPortableNames(t *testing.T) {

301	// Build joins live local facts with optional external observations. It performs
302	// no probes and never places raw Git endpoints in the returned report.
303	func Build(input BuildInput) (Report, error) {
304		now := input.GeneratedAt
305		if now.IsZero() {
306			now = time.Now().UTC()
307		}
308		now = now.Round(0).UTC()
309
310		report := Report{
311			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion,
312			GeneratedAt:   now,
313			Repository: Repository{
314				Name: input.Context.Repo.Name, Display: input.Context.Repo.Display(),
315				Path: input.Context.Repo.Path, RealPath: optionalString(input.Context.Repo.RealPath),
316				CommonDir: optionalString(input.Context.Repo.CommonDir),
317				Bare:      input.Context.Repo.Bare, HasGit: input.Context.Repo.HasGit,
318			},
319			Sources:      []Source{},
320			Capabilities: []Capability{},
321			Remotes:      []Remote{},
322			Errors:       []CollectionError{},
323		}
324
325		report.Local = buildLocalFacts(input, &report.Errors)
326		if input.SelectedCheckout >= 0 && input.SelectedCheckout < len(report.Local.Checkouts) {
327			checkout := report.Local.Checkouts[input.SelectedCheckout]
328			report.SelectedCheckout = &CheckoutSelection{
329				Index: checkout.Index, Path: checkout.Path, Branch: checkout.Branch,
330				Canonical: checkout.Canonical, Ownership: checkout.Ownership,
331			}
332		} else {
333			message := "selected checkout is not present in the local checkout inventory"
334			if input.SelectionErr != nil {
335				message = cleanError(input.SelectionErr)
336			}
337			report.Errors = append(report.Errors, CollectionError{
338				Code: "selection-unavailable", Scope: "local", Subject: "selected-checkout", Message: message,
339			})
340		}
341
342		localIdentities := privateRemoteIdentities(input.Topology)
343		report.Remotes, report.Forge, report.Errors = buildRemoteFacts(now, input, report.Errors)
344		report.Fleet, report.Errors = buildFleetFacts(now, input.Fleet, localIdentities, report.Errors)
345
346		sources := buildSources(now, input, report)
347		report.Sources = sources
348		report.Capabilities = buildCapabilities(input, report)
349
350		readiness := AssessLocal(input.Context, input.SelectedCheckout, input.Hostname)
351		sourceMap := make(map[string]assessment.Source, len(sources))
352		for _, source := range sources {
353			sourceMap[source.ID] = source.assessmentSource()
354		}
355		gates := []assessment.Gate{
356			readinessGate("checkout-readiness", readiness.Checkout, sourcesNamed(sourceMap, "local.checkout")),
357			readinessGate("task-readiness", readiness.Task, sourcesNamed(sourceMap, "local.tasks", "local.runtime")),
358			readinessGate("worktree-readiness", readiness.Worktree, sourcesNamed(sourceMap, "local.worktrees", "local.runtime")),
359			{
360				Code: "whole-clone-eviction", Outcome: assessment.OutcomeIndeterminate,
361				Reasons: []assessment.Reason{{
362					Code: "recovery-proof-unavailable", Subject: "repository",
363					Detail:      "whole-clone eviction is not assessed by the context profile",
364					Remediation: "create and restore-verify a recovery receipt before eviction",
365				}},
366			},
367		}
368		assessmentReport, err := assessment.NewReport(assessment.ProfileCheap, now, gates)
369		if err != nil {
370			return Report{}, fmt.Errorf("seal repository context assessment: %w", err)
371		}
372		report.Assessment = assessmentReport
373
374		sort.Slice(report.Errors, func(i, j int) bool {
375			left, right := report.Errors[i], report.Errors[j]
376			return strings.Join([]string{left.Scope, left.Code, left.Subject, left.Message}, "\x00") <
377				strings.Join([]string{right.Scope, right.Code, right.Subject, right.Message}, "\x00")
378		})
379		return report, nil
380	}

382	func buildLocalFacts(input BuildInput, reportErrors *[]CollectionError) LocalFacts {
383		context := input.Context
384		local := LocalFacts{
385			Checkouts:                          make([]CheckoutFacts, 0, len(context.Checkouts)),
386			OtherTasks:                         []TaskFacts{},
387			ObservedLinkedWorktreeAdminEntries: context.WorktreeCount,
388			CheckoutsComplete:                  context.WorktreeErr == nil,
389			TaskInventoryComplete:              context.TaskErr == nil,
390			Runtimes:                           []RuntimeFacts{},
391		}
392		if context.WorktreeErr == nil {
393			count := context.WorktreeCount
394			local.LinkedWorktreeCount = &count
395		} else {
396			*reportErrors = append(*reportErrors, collectionError("worktree-inventory-failed", "local", "worktrees", context.WorktreeErr))
397		}
398		if context.TaskErr != nil {
399			*reportErrors = append(*reportErrors, collectionError("task-inventory-failed", "local", "tasks", context.TaskErr))
400		}
401
402		for index, checkout := range context.Checkouts {
403			facts := CheckoutFacts{
404				Index: index, Path: checkout.Worktree.Path, Canonical: index == 0,
405				Ownership: checkout.Ownership, Locked: checkout.Worktree.Locked,
406				LockedReason:   optionalString(strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.LockedReason)),
407				Prunable:       checkout.Worktree.Prunable,
408				PrunableReason: optionalString(strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.PrunableReason)),

585	func buildRemoteEndpoint(raw string, records map[string][]forge.RemoteRepo, forgeAvailable, exactForge bool) (RemoteEndpoint, []string, *endpointBuildError) {
586		transport, displayIdentity, displayOK := publicEndpointIdentity(raw)
587		forgeMatch := "unavailable"
588		if forgeAvailable {
589			forgeMatch = "none"
590		}
591		endpoint := RemoteEndpoint{Transport: transport, Identity: optionalString(displayIdentity), ForgeMatch: forgeMatch}
592		privateIdentity := privateRemoteIdentity(raw)
593		if !displayOK {
594			message := "endpoint has no display-safe cross-host identity"
595			endpoint.Error = &message
596			return endpoint, nil, &endpointBuildError{Code: "remote-identity-unavailable", Message: message}
597		}
598
599		candidates := dedupeForgeRecords(records[privateIdentity])
600		var exact *forge.RemoteRepo
601		matched := []string{}
602		switch len(candidates) {
603		case 1:
604			if exactForge {
605				exact = &candidates[0]
606			}
607			endpoint.ForgeMatch = "exact"
608			matched = append(matched, forgeRecordKey(candidates[0]))
609		case 0:
610			if forgeAvailable {
611				endpoint.ForgeMatch = "none"
612			}
613		default:
614			endpoint.ForgeMatch = "ambiguous"
615			message := fmt.Sprintf("normalized endpoint identity matches %d forge records", len(candidates))
616			endpoint.Error = &message
617			for _, candidate := range candidates {
618				matched = append(matched, forgeRecordKey(candidate))
619			}
620			if web, ok := forge.DeriveWebURL(forge.WebURLRequest{Remote: raw}); ok {
621				endpoint.WebURL = &web
622			}
623			return endpoint, matched, &endpointBuildError{Code: "forge-match-ambiguous", Message: message}
624		}
625		if web, ok := forge.DeriveWebURL(forge.WebURLRequest{Remote: raw, Exact: exact}); ok {
626			endpoint.WebURL = &web
627		}
628		return endpoint, matched, nil
629	}

969	func publicEndpointIdentity(raw string) (transport, identity string, ok bool) {
970		if !utf8.ValidString(raw) || containsControl(raw) {
971			return "unknown", "", false
972		}
973		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
974		if trimmed == "" {
975			return "unknown", "", false
976		}
977		redacted := trimmed
978		if parsed, err := url.Parse(trimmed); err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" {
979			transport = strings.ToLower(parsed.Scheme)
980			parsed.User = nil
981			parsed.RawQuery = ""
982			parsed.ForceQuery = false
983			parsed.Fragment = ""
984			redacted = parsed.String()
985		} else {
986			if index := strings.IndexAny(redacted, "?#"); index >= 0 {
987				redacted = redacted[:index]
988			}
989			colon := strings.IndexByte(redacted, ':')
990			at := strings.LastIndexByte(redacted, '@')
991			if at >= 0 && colon > at {
992				transport = "ssh"
993				redacted = "git@" + redacted[at+1:]
994			} else if filepath.IsAbs(redacted) || strings.HasPrefix(redacted, ".") || strings.HasPrefix(redacted, "~") {
995				transport = "local"
996			} else {
997				transport = "unknown"
998			}
999		}
1000		identity = catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(redacted)
1001		if identity == "" || containsControl(identity) {
1002			return transport, "", false
1003		}
1004		return transport, identity, true
1005	}

1007	func forgeRecordsByIdentity(records []forge.RemoteRepo) map[string][]forge.RemoteRepo {

1012				identity := privateRemoteIdentity(raw)

1014					continue
1015				}
1016				if _, exists := seen[identity]; exists {
1017					continue
1018				}
1019				seen[identity] = struct{}{}
1020				result[identity] = append(result[identity], record)

1022		}

1026	func dedupeForgeRecords(records []forge.RemoteRepo) []forge.RemoteRepo {

1033			}

1037		sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return forgeRecordKey(result[i]) < forgeRecordKey(result[j]) })

1111	func cleanError(err error) string {

1116	}

1118	// cleanText removes controls and structurally redacts URL/scp-like tokens while
1119	// preserving enough of an error to diagnose which probe failed.
1120	func cleanText(value string) string {
1121		value = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
1122			if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
1123				return ' '
1124			}
1125			return r
1126		}, value)
1127		fields := strings.Fields(value)
1128		for index, field := range fields {
1129			fields[index] = redactTextToken(field)
1130		}
1131		return strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(fields, " "))
1132	}
1133
1134	func redactTextToken(token string) string {
1135		prefix := strings.TrimLeft(token, "([{<\"'")
1136		leading := token[:len(token)-len(prefix)]
1137		core := strings.TrimRight(prefix, ")]}>\"',;.")
1138		trailing := prefix[len(core):]
1139		if parsed, err := url.Parse(core); err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" {
1140			parsed.User = nil
1141			parsed.RawQuery = ""
1142			parsed.ForceQuery = false
1143			parsed.Fragment = ""
1144			return leading + parsed.String() + trailing
1145		}
1146		colon := strings.IndexByte(core, ':')
1147		at := strings.LastIndexByte(core, '@')
1148		if at > 0 && colon > at {
1149			core = "[redacted]@" + core[at+1:]
1150			if query := strings.IndexAny(core, "?#"); query >= 0 {
1151				core = core[:query]
1152			}
1153		}
1154		return leading + core + trailing
1155	}
1156
1157	func containsControl(value string) bool {
1158		return strings.IndexFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
1159			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r)
1160		}) >= 0
1161	}
1162
1163	func safeIdentifier(value string) string {
1164		value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
1165		var b strings.Builder
1166		lastDash := false
1167		for _, r := range value {
1168			if r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' {
1169				b.WriteRune(r)
1170				lastDash = false
1171			} else if !lastDash {
1172				b.WriteByte('-')
1173				lastDash = true
1174			}
1175		}
1176		result := strings.Trim(b.String(), "-")
1177		if result == "" {
1178			return "unknown"
1179		}
1180		return result
1181	}
1182
1183	func optionalString(value string) *string {
1184		if value == "" {
1185			return nil
1186		}
1187		copy := value
1188		return &copy
1189	}
1190

1192		if value.IsZero() {
1193			return nil
1194		}
1195		copy := value.Round(0).UTC()

1202		}

12	// Readiness is one cheap, local-only context projection. It intentionally

18	}

20	// LocalReadiness keeps independently actionable checkout, task, and worktree

37	// AssessLocal derives readiness from facts already collected by inventory. It
38	// does not run Git, inspect a runtime, or contact a forge/fleet host.
39	func AssessLocal(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int, hostname string) LocalReadiness {
40		return LocalReadiness{
41			Checkout: assessCheckout(context, selectedIndex),
42			Task:     assessTasks(context, selectedIndex, hostname),
43			Worktree: assessWorktrees(context, selectedIndex),
44		}
45	}
