497	func (a *Authority) writeState(state Snapshot) error {
498		state = canonicalSnapshot(state)
499		if err := validateSnapshot(state); err != nil {
500			return err
501		}
502		if err := ensurePrivateDir(a.root); err != nil {
503			return err
504		}
505		temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(a.root, ".authority-*.tmp")
506		if err != nil {
507			return fmt.Errorf("create operation lease state temp file: %w", err)
508		}
509		name := temporary.Name()
510		defer os.Remove(name)
511		if err := setPrivateMode(name, 0o600); err != nil {
512			_ = temporary.Close()
513			return err
514		}
515		encoder := json.NewEncoder(temporary)
516		encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
517		if err := encoder.Encode(state); err != nil {
518			_ = temporary.Close()
519			return fmt.Errorf("encode operation lease state: %w", err)
520		}
521		if err := temporary.Sync(); err != nil {
522			_ = temporary.Close()
523			return fmt.Errorf("sync operation lease state: %w", err)
524		}
525		if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
526			return fmt.Errorf("close operation lease state: %w", err)
527		}
528		if err := replaceFile(name, a.statePath()); err != nil {
529			return fmt.Errorf("publish operation lease state: %w", err)
530		}
531		if err := syncDirectory(a.root); err != nil {
532			return fmt.Errorf("sync operation lease directory: %w", err)
533		}
534		return nil
535	}

537	func validateSnapshot(state Snapshot) error {
538		if state.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion {
539			return fmt.Errorf("operation lease schema_version %d: want %d", state.SchemaVersion, SchemaVersion)
540		}
541		bindings := make(map[string]string, len(state.Bindings))
542		for _, binding := range state.Bindings {
543			if err := binding.Validate(); err != nil {
544				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease binding: %w", err)
545			}
546			if _, exists := bindings[binding.OperationID]; exists {
547				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease repeats binding %s", binding.OperationID)
548			}
549			bindings[binding.OperationID] = binding.Digest
550		}
551		type activeSignature struct {
552			Token     Token
553			MachineID string
554			Kind      string
555		}
556		activeOperations := make(map[string]activeSignature)
557		terminalOperations := make(map[string]Tombstone)
558		seenKeys := make(map[string]struct{}, len(state.Records))
559		var maxRecordEpoch uint64
560		for _, record := range state.Records {
561			if err := record.Key.Validate(); err != nil {
562				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease record: %w", err)
563			}
564			canonicalKey := record.Key.canonical()
565			if _, exists := seenKeys[canonicalKey]; exists {
566				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease state repeats key %s", record.Key.subject())
567			}
568			seenKeys[canonicalKey] = struct{}{}
569			if record.Epoch == 0 || record.Epoch > state.LastEpoch {
570				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s has invalid epoch %d", record.Key.subject(), record.Epoch)
571			}
572			if record.Epoch > maxRecordEpoch {
573				maxRecordEpoch = record.Epoch
574			}
575			if record.Reservation != nil && record.Fence != nil {
576				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s has both reservation and fence", record.Key.subject())
577			}
578			for _, named := range []struct {
579				name  string
580				claim *Claim
581			}{{"reservation", record.Reservation}, {"fence", record.Fence}} {
582				if named.claim == nil {
583					continue
584				}
585				if err := named.claim.Token.Validate(); err != nil {
586					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s on %s: %w", named.name, record.Key.subject(), err)
587				}
588				if digest, exists := bindings[named.claim.Token.OperationID]; !exists || digest != named.claim.Token.Digest {
589					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s on %s has no matching permanent binding", named.name, record.Key.subject())
590				}
591				if named.claim.Token.Epoch != record.Epoch {
592					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s on %s has epoch %d, record has %d", named.name, record.Key.subject(), named.claim.Token.Epoch, record.Epoch)
593				}
594				if named.claim.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
595					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s on %s has no created_at", named.name, record.Key.subject())
596				}
597				if named.claim.MachineID != "" {
598					if err := machineid.Validate(named.claim.MachineID); err != nil {
599						return err
600					}
601				}
602				signature := activeSignature{Token: named.claim.Token, MachineID: named.claim.MachineID, Kind: named.name}
603				if prior, exists := activeOperations[named.claim.Token.OperationID]; exists {
604					if !prior.Token.matches(signature.Token) || prior.MachineID != signature.MachineID || prior.Kind != signature.Kind {
605						return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s has inconsistent active claims", named.claim.Token.OperationID)
606					}
607				} else {
608					activeOperations[named.claim.Token.OperationID] = signature
609				}
610			}
611			seenTombstones := make(map[string]struct{}, len(record.Tombstones))
612			for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
613				switch tombstone.Kind {
614				case TombstoneAborted, TombstoneReturned:
615				default:
616					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s has unknown tombstone kind %q", record.Key.subject(), tombstone.Kind)
617				}
618				if err := tombstone.Token.Validate(); err != nil {
619					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease tombstone on %s: %w", record.Key.subject(), err)
620				}
621				if digest, exists := bindings[tombstone.Token.OperationID]; !exists || digest != tombstone.Token.Digest {
622					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease tombstone on %s has no matching permanent binding", record.Key.subject())
623				}
624				if tombstone.AdvancedEpoch <= tombstone.Token.Epoch || tombstone.AdvancedEpoch > record.Epoch || tombstone.AdvancedEpoch > state.LastEpoch {
625					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease tombstone on %s has invalid advanced epoch %d", record.Key.subject(), tombstone.AdvancedEpoch)
626				}
627				if tombstone.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
628					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease tombstone on %s has no created_at", record.Key.subject())
629				}
630				if prior, exists := terminalOperations[tombstone.Token.OperationID]; exists {
631					if !prior.Token.matches(tombstone.Token) || prior.Kind != tombstone.Kind || prior.AdvancedEpoch != tombstone.AdvancedEpoch {
632						return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s has inconsistent terminal records", tombstone.Token.OperationID)
633					}
634				} else {
635					terminalOperations[tombstone.Token.OperationID] = tombstone
636				}
637				identity := fmt.Sprintf("%s\x00%s\x00%d", tombstone.Token.OperationID, tombstone.Token.Digest, tombstone.Token.Epoch)
638				if _, exists := seenTombstones[identity]; exists {
639					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s repeats a terminal token", record.Key.subject())
640				}
641				seenTombstones[identity] = struct{}{}
642				if record.Reservation != nil && record.Reservation.Token.matches(tombstone.Token) || record.Fence != nil && record.Fence.Token.matches(tombstone.Token) {
643					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s has a terminal token still active", record.Key.subject())
644				}
645			}
646		}
647		if state.LastEpoch != maxRecordEpoch {
648			return fmt.Errorf("operation lease last_epoch %d does not match latest record epoch %d", state.LastEpoch, maxRecordEpoch)
649		}
650		for operationID := range activeOperations {
651			if _, terminal := terminalOperations[operationID]; terminal {
652				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s is both active and terminal", operationID)
653			}
654		}
655		return nil
656	}

658	func canonicalSnapshot(state Snapshot) Snapshot {
659		result := Snapshot{
660			SchemaVersion: state.SchemaVersion,
661			LastEpoch:     state.LastEpoch,
662			Bindings:      append([]Binding(nil), state.Bindings...),
663			Records:       make([]Record, len(state.Records)),
664		}
665		sort.Slice(result.Bindings, func(i, j int) bool { return result.Bindings[i].OperationID < result.Bindings[j].OperationID })
666		for index, record := range state.Records {
667			result.Records[index] = cloneRecord(record)
668			if result.Records[index].Reservation != nil {
669				result.Records[index].Reservation.CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Reservation.CreatedAt)
670			}
671			if result.Records[index].Fence != nil {
672				result.Records[index].Fence.CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Fence.CreatedAt)
673			}
674			for tombstoneIndex := range result.Records[index].Tombstones {
675				result.Records[index].Tombstones[tombstoneIndex].CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Tombstones[tombstoneIndex].CreatedAt)
676			}
677			sort.Slice(result.Records[index].Tombstones, func(i, j int) bool {
678				left, right := result.Records[index].Tombstones[i], result.Records[index].Tombstones[j]
679				if left.Token.Epoch != right.Token.Epoch {
680					return left.Token.Epoch < right.Token.Epoch
681				}
682				if left.Token.OperationID != right.Token.OperationID {
683					return left.Token.OperationID < right.Token.OperationID
684				}
685				if left.Token.Digest != right.Token.Digest {
686					return left.Token.Digest < right.Token.Digest
687				}
688				return left.Kind < right.Kind
689			})
690		}
691		sort.Slice(result.Records, func(i, j int) bool { return result.Records[i].Key.canonical() < result.Records[j].Key.canonical() })
692		return result
693	}
694
695	func cloneRecord(record Record) Record {
696		result := record
697		if record.Reservation != nil {
698			copy := *record.Reservation
699			result.Reservation = &copy
700		}
701		if record.Fence != nil {
702			copy := *record.Fence
703			result.Fence = &copy
704		}
705		result.Tombstones = append([]Tombstone(nil), record.Tombstones...)
706		return result
707	}
708
709	func findRecord(records []Record, key Key) *Record {
710		canonical := key.canonical()
711		for index := range records {
712			if records[index].Key.canonical() == canonical {
713				return &records[index]
714			}
715		}
716		return nil
717	}
718
719	func ensureRecord(state *Snapshot, key Key) *Record {
720		if record := findRecord(state.Records, key); record != nil {
721			return record
722		}
723		state.Records = append(state.Records, Record{Key: key})
724		return &state.Records[len(state.Records)-1]
725	}

727	func allocateEpoch(state *Snapshot) (uint64, error) {
728		if state.LastEpoch == math.MaxUint64 {
729			return 0, errors.New("operation lease epoch exhausted")
730		}
731		state.LastEpoch++
732		return state.LastEpoch, nil
733	}

735	func activeClaim(record Record) (*Claim, string) {
736		if record.Reservation != nil {
737			return record.Reservation, "reservation"
738		}
739		if record.Fence != nil {
740			return record.Fence, "fence"
741		}
742		return nil, ""
743	}

745	func hasTerminal(record Record, token Token) bool {
746		for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
747			if tombstone.Token.matches(token) {
748				return true
749			}
750		}
751		return false

754	func ensureBinding(state *Snapshot, request Request) bool {
755		for _, binding := range state.Bindings {
756			if binding.OperationID == request.OperationID {
757				return false
758			}
759		}
760		state.Bindings = append(state.Bindings, Binding{OperationID: request.OperationID, Digest: request.Digest})
761		return true
762	}

764	func checkOperationReuse(state Snapshot, keys []Key, request Request) error {
765		for _, binding := range state.Bindings {
766			if binding.OperationID != request.OperationID {
767				continue
768			}
769			if binding.Digest != request.Digest {
770				return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s was permanently bound to another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
771			}
772			break
773		}
774		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
775		for _, key := range keys {
776			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
777		}
778		for _, record := range state.Records {
779			for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
780				if tombstone.Token.OperationID != request.OperationID {
781					continue
782				}
783				if tombstone.Token.Digest != request.Digest {
784					return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s was used with another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
785				}
786				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s is terminal: %w", request.OperationID, ErrReturned)
787			}
788			claim, _ := activeClaim(record)
789			if claim == nil || claim.Token.OperationID != request.OperationID {
790				continue
791			}
792			if claim.Token.Digest != request.Digest {
793				return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s is active with another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
794			}
795			if _, exists := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !exists {
796				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s is active on a different key set: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
797			}
798		}
799		return nil
800	}

802	func checkHierarchyClaims(state Snapshot, keys []Key, request Request) error {
803		requestedKeys := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
804		requestedRepositories := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
805		repositoryWide := make(map[string]bool, len(keys))
806		for _, key := range keys {
807			requestedKeys[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
808			requestedRepositories[key.Repository] = struct{}{}
809			if key.Scope == ScopeRepository {
810				repositoryWide[key.Repository] = true
811			}
812		}
813		for _, record := range state.Records {
814			claim, kind := activeClaim(record)
815			if claim == nil {
816				continue
817			}
818			if _, requested := requestedKeys[record.Key.canonical()]; requested {
819				continue
820			}
821			if _, sameRepository := requestedRepositories[record.Key.Repository]; !sameRepository {
822				continue
823			}
824			if record.Key.Scope != ScopeRepository && !repositoryWide[record.Key.Repository] {
825				continue
826			}
827			return blockedOrConflict(record.Key, kind, *claim, request)
828		}
829		return nil
830	}
831
832	func blockedOrConflict(key Key, kind string, claim Claim, request Request) error {
833		if claim.Token.OperationID == request.OperationID {
834			return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s conflicts with its active %s: %w", request.OperationID, kind, ErrConflict)
835		}
836		return &BlockedError{Key: key, Kind: kind, OperationID: claim.Token.OperationID}
837	}

839	func validateGuardKeySet(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token) error {
840		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
841		for _, key := range keys {
842			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
843		}
844		matched := 0
845		for _, record := range state.Records {
846			claim, _ := activeClaim(record)
847			if claim == nil || !claim.Token.matches(token) {
848				continue
849			}
850			if _, included := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !included {
851				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d owns a larger key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrConflict)
852			}
853			matched++
854		}
855		if matched != len(keys) {
856			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d does not own the exact guard key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrEpochMismatch)
857		}
858		return nil
859	}

861	func validateClaimKeySet(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token, claimKind string) error {
862		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
863		for _, key := range keys {
864			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
865		}
866		matched := 0
867		for _, record := range state.Records {
868			var claim *Claim
869			if claimKind == "reservation" {
870				claim = record.Reservation
871			} else {
872				claim = record.Fence
873			}
874			if claim == nil || !claim.Token.matches(token) {
875				continue
876			}
877			if _, included := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !included {
878				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d owns a larger key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrConflict)
879			}
880			matched++
881		}
882		if matched != len(keys) {
883			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d does not own the exact key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrEpochMismatch)
884		}
885		return nil
886	}

888	func matchingTerminal(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token, kind TombstoneKind) (uint64, bool, error) {
889		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
890		for _, key := range keys {
891			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
892		}
893		var epoch uint64
894		matched := 0
895		for _, record := range state.Records {
896			for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
897				if !tombstone.Token.matches(token) {
898					continue
899				}
900				if tombstone.Kind != kind {
901					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d ended as %s: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, tombstone.Kind, ErrReturned)
902				}
903				if _, included := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !included {
904					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d is terminal on a larger key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrConflict)
905				}
906				if epoch == 0 {
907					epoch = tombstone.AdvancedEpoch
908				} else if epoch != tombstone.AdvancedEpoch {
909					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s has inconsistent terminal epochs: %w", token.OperationID, ErrConflict)
910				}
911				matched++
912				break
913			}
914		}
915		if matched == 0 {
916			return 0, false, nil
917		}
918		if matched != len(keys) {
919			return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s is terminal on only part of the key set: %w", token.OperationID, ErrConflict)
920		}
921		return epoch, true, nil
922	}

924	func ensurePrivateDir(path string) error {
925		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o700); err != nil {
926			return err
927		}
928		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
929		if err != nil {
930			return err
931		}
932		if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
933			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a private directory", path)
934		}
935		if err := setPrivateMode(path, 0o700); err != nil {
936			return err
937		}
938		info, err = os.Lstat(path)
939		if err != nil {
940			return err
941		}
942		private, err := privateModeMatches(path, info.Mode(), 0o700)
943		if err != nil {
944			return fmt.Errorf("inspect operation lease directory permissions: %w", err)
945		}
946		if !private {
947			return fmt.Errorf("operation lease directory %s permissions are not private (want 0700 or a protected owner-only policy)", path)
948		}
949		return nil
950	}

952	func canonicalTime(value time.Time) time.Time {
953		return value.Round(0).UTC()
954	}

193	func TestEpochPromotionAndReturnTombstoneAreIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
194		root := t.TempDir()
195		authority := New(root)
196		repository := "github.com/team/project"
197		keys := []Key{BranchKey(repository, "main"), RepositoryKey(repository)}
198		request := testRequest("transfer-return")
199
200		reservation, err := authority.Reserve(context.Background(), keys, request)
201		if err != nil {
202			t.Fatal(err)
203		}
204		repeatedReservation, err := authority.Reserve(context.Background(), []Key{keys[1], keys[0]}, request)
205		if err != nil || !reservation.matches(repeatedReservation) {
206			t.Fatalf("idempotent reservation = %+v, %v; want %+v", repeatedReservation, err, reservation)
207		}
208		fence, err := authority.Fence(context.Background(), keys, request)
209		if err != nil {
210			t.Fatal(err)
211		}
212		if fence.Epoch <= reservation.Epoch {
213			t.Fatalf("fence epoch = %d, reservation epoch = %d", fence.Epoch, reservation.Epoch)
214		}
215		repeatedFence, err := authority.Fence(context.Background(), []Key{keys[1], keys[0]}, request)
216		if err != nil || !fence.matches(repeatedFence) {
217			t.Fatalf("idempotent fence = %+v, %v; want %+v", repeatedFence, err, fence)
218		}
219		guardCalled := false
220		if err := authority.WithGuard(context.Background(), keys[:1], &fence, func() error { guardCalled = true; return nil }); !errors.Is(err, ErrConflict) {
221			t.Fatalf("partial owner guard = %v, want key-set conflict", err)
222		}
223		if guardCalled {
224			t.Fatal("partial owner guard callback ran")
225		}
226		if _, err := authority.Return(context.Background(), keys[:1], fence); !errors.Is(err, ErrConflict) {
227			t.Fatalf("partial Return = %v, want key-set conflict", err)
228		}
229		recordsBeforeReturn, err := authority.Inspect(context.Background(), keys)
230		if err != nil {
231			t.Fatal(err)
232		}
233		for _, record := range recordsBeforeReturn {
234			if record.Fence == nil || !record.Fence.Token.matches(fence) {
235				t.Fatalf("partial Return changed record: %+v", record)
236			}
237		}
238
239		returnedEpoch, err := authority.Return(context.Background(), keys, fence)
240		if err != nil {
241			t.Fatal(err)
242		}
243		if returnedEpoch <= fence.Epoch {
244			t.Fatalf("returned epoch = %d, fence epoch = %d", returnedEpoch, fence.Epoch)
245		}
246		repeatedReturn, err := authority.Return(context.Background(), []Key{keys[1], keys[0]}, fence)
247		if err != nil || repeatedReturn != returnedEpoch {
248			t.Fatalf("idempotent Return = %d, %v; want %d", repeatedReturn, err, returnedEpoch)
249		}
250		if err := authority.WithGuard(context.Background(), keys, &fence, func() error { return nil }); !errors.Is(err, ErrReturned) {
251			t.Fatalf("delayed owner guard = %v, want terminal", err)
252		}
253		if _, err := authority.Fence(context.Background(), keys, request); !errors.Is(err, ErrReturned) {
254			t.Fatalf("delayed Fence = %v, want terminal", err)
255		}
256		if err := authority.WithMutation(context.Background(), keys, func() error { return nil }); err != nil {
257			t.Fatalf("ordinary guard after return: %v", err)
258		}
259
260		reloaded := New(root)
261		records, err := reloaded.Inspect(context.Background(), keys)
262		if err != nil {
263			t.Fatal(err)
264		}
265		for _, record := range records {
266			if record.Fence != nil || record.Reservation != nil || len(record.Tombstones) != 1 {
267				t.Fatalf("reloaded returned record = %+v", record)
268			}
269			if got := record.Tombstones[0]; got.Kind != TombstoneReturned || !got.Token.matches(fence) || got.AdvancedEpoch != returnedEpoch {
270				t.Fatalf("reloaded tombstone = %+v", got)
271			}
272		}
273
274		newFence, err := reloaded.Fence(context.Background(), keys, testRequest("transfer-new"))
275		if err != nil {
276			t.Fatal(err)
277		}
278		if newFence.Epoch <= returnedEpoch {
279			t.Fatalf("new fence epoch = %d, returned epoch = %d", newFence.Epoch, returnedEpoch)
280		}
281	}

307		for name, keys := range map[string][]Key{

309			"reverse": {second, first},
310		} {

314					entered <- name
315					<-release
316					return nil
317				})
318			}(name, keys)

321		case <-entered:
322		case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
323			t.Fatal("neither multi-key guard acquired")
324		}
325		select {
326		case secondEntry := <-entered:
327			t.Fatalf("both overlapping guards entered concurrently; second = %s", secondEntry)
328		case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
329		}
330		close(release)
331		done := make(chan struct{})
332		go func() { wait.Wait(); close(done) }()
333		select {
334		case <-done:
335		case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
336			t.Fatal("opposite-order guards deadlocked")
337		}
338	}

 // UnsupportedSchemaError describes a record whose schema this version cannot
 // read. It supports errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupportedSchema).
 type UnsupportedSchemaError struct {
    ID      string
    Version int
 }

 func (e *UnsupportedSchemaError) Error() string {
    if e.ID == "" {
        return fmt.Sprintf("catalog schema version %d: %v", e.Version, ErrUnsupportedSchema)
    }
    return fmt.Sprintf("catalog asset %s has schema version %d: %v", e.ID, e.Version, ErrUnsupportedSchema)
 }

 func (e *UnsupportedSchemaError) Unwrap() error { return ErrUnsupportedSchema }

14	const (
15		localSystemSID    = "S-1-5-18"
16		administratorsSID = "S-1-5-32-544"
17	)
18
19	// setPrivateMode installs a protected DACL. Windows os.FileMode permission
20	// bits only model the read-only attribute and cannot establish privacy.
21	func setPrivateMode(path string, want fs.FileMode) error {
22		inheritance := ""
23		switch want.Perm() {
24		case 0o600:
25		case 0o700:
26			inheritance = "OICI"
27		default:
28			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported private Windows mode %04o", want.Perm())
29		}
30		current, _, err := privateSIDs()
31		if err != nil {
32			return err
33		}
34		ace := func(sid string) string {
35			return fmt.Sprintf("(A;%s;GA;;;%s)", inheritance, sid)
36		}
37		descriptor, err := windows.SecurityDescriptorFromString("D:P" + ace(current) + ace(localSystemSID) + ace(administratorsSID))
38		if err != nil {
39			return fmt.Errorf("build private Windows security descriptor: %w", err)
40		}
41		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
42		if err != nil {
43			return fmt.Errorf("read private Windows DACL: %w", err)
44		}
45		if dacl == nil {
46			return fmt.Errorf("private Windows security descriptor has no DACL")
47		}
48		err = windows.SetNamedSecurityInfo(
49			path,
50			windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT,
51			windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION,
52			nil,
53			nil,
54			dacl,
55			nil,
56		)
57		runtime.KeepAlive(descriptor)
58		if err != nil {
59			return fmt.Errorf("set private Windows DACL: %w", err)
60		}
61		return nil
62	}
63
64	func privateModeMatches(path string, _ fs.FileMode, _ fs.FileMode) (bool, error) {
65		current, allowed, err := privateSIDs()
66		if err != nil {
67			return false, err
68		}
69		descriptor, err := windows.GetNamedSecurityInfo(path, windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT, windows.OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION)
70		if err != nil {
71			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner and DACL: %w", err)
72		}
73		owner, _, err := descriptor.Owner()
74		if err != nil {
75			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner: %w", err)
76		}
77		if !privateSIDAllowed(owner, allowed) {
78			return false, nil
79		}
80		control, _, err := descriptor.Control()
81		if err != nil {
82			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows security descriptor control: %w", err)
83		}
84		if control&windows.SE_DACL_PROTECTED == 0 {
85			return false, nil
86		}
87		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
88		if err != nil {
89			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL: %w", err)
90		}
91		if dacl == nil {
92			return false, nil
93		}
94		seenCurrent := false
95		for index := uint16(0); index < dacl.AceCount; index++ {
96			var ace *windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE
97			if err := windows.GetAce(dacl, uint32(index), &ace); err != nil {
98				return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL entry %d: %w", index, err)
99			}
100			switch ace.Header.AceType {
101			case windows.ACCESS_DENIED_ACE_TYPE:
102				continue
103			case windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE:
104			default:
105				return false, nil
106			}
107			sid := (*windows.SID)(unsafe.Pointer(&ace.SidStart))
108			value := sid.String()
109			if _, ok := allowed[value]; !ok {
110				return false, nil
111			}
112			if value == current {
113				seenCurrent = true
114			}
115		}
116		return seenCurrent, nil
117	}
118
119	func privateSIDAllowed(sid *windows.SID, allowed map[string]struct{}) bool {
120		if sid == nil {
121			return false
122		}
123		_, ok := allowed[sid.String()]
124		return ok
125	}
126
127	func privateSIDs() (string, map[string]struct{}, error) {
128		user, err := windows.GetCurrentProcessToken().GetTokenUser()
129		if err != nil {
130			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("read current Windows user: %w", err)
131		}
132		current := user.User.Sid.String()
133		if current == "" {
134			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("current Windows user has an invalid SID")
135		}
136		return current, map[string]struct{}{
137			current:           {},
138			localSystemSID:    {},
139			administratorsSID: {},
140		}, nil
141	}
142
143	func replaceFile(source, destination string) error {
144		from, err := windows.UTF16PtrFromString(source)
145		if err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		to, err := windows.UTF16PtrFromString(destination)
149		if err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		return windows.MoveFileEx(from, to, windows.MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|windows.MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)
153	}
154

49					Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
50					GitDir: g.GitCommonDir, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir,
51					MainRoot: g.MainRoot, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
52				}, selectedPath, false)
53
54				kind := "main checkout"
55				if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
56					kind = "linked worktree"
57				}
58				field("repo", fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", g.Name, kind))
59				field("checkout", config.Contract(selectedPath))
60				if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
61					field("main", config.Contract(g.MainRoot))
62				}
63
64				var selected *inventory.RepoCheckout
65				if local.SelectedCheckout >= 0 && local.SelectedCheckout < len(local.Context.Checkouts) {
66					selected = &local.Context.Checkouts[local.SelectedCheckout]
67				}
68				if selected == nil {
69					field("branch", style.warning("— checkout unavailable"))
70				} else if g.Bare {
71					field("branch", "(bare repository)")
72				} else if selected.StatusErr != nil {
73					field("branch", style.warning("— Git status unavailable"))
74					app.warnf("could not inspect checkout status: %v", selected.StatusErr)
75				} else {
76					st := selected.Status
77					branch := st.Branch
78					if st.Detached {
79						branch = "(detached HEAD)"
80					}
81					field("branch", fmt.Sprintf("%s  %s", branch, style.git(st.Summary())))
82					if st.Dirty() {
83						field("changes", style.warning(st.Breakdown()))
84						if types := st.TypeBreakdown(); types != "" {
85							field("types", style.warning(types))
86						}
87					}
88					if st.Upstream != "" {
89						field("upstream", st.Upstream)
90					} else {
91						field("upstream", style.warning("— not published"))
92					}
93					if st.Conflicted > 0 {
94						field("conflicts", style.danger(fmt.Sprintf("%d unmerged path(s) — resolve before anything else", st.Conflicted)))
95					}
96				}
97				field("readiness", repocontext.AssessLocal(local.Context, local.SelectedCheckout, config.Hostname()).Summary())
98				if base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, g.MainRoot); base != "" {
99					field("default", base)
100				}
101				if k := forge.Detect(ctx, g.MainRoot); k != forge.Unknown {
102					field("forge", fmt.Sprint(k))
103				}
104
105				if local.Context.WorktreeErr == nil && len(local.Context.Checkouts) > 1 {
106					field("worktrees", fmt.Sprint(len(local.Context.Checkouts)))
107					for index, checkout := range local.Context.Checkouts {
108						marker := "  "
109						if index == local.SelectedCheckout {
110							marker = "→ "
111						}
112						name := checkout.Branch()
113						if name == "" {
114							name = "(detached)"
115						}
116						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s%-28s %s\n", marker, name, config.Contract(checkout.Worktree.Path))
117					}
118				} else if local.Context.WorktreeErr != nil {
119					app.warnf("could not inspect linked worktrees: %v", local.Context.WorktreeErr)
120				}
121
122				rt := app.Runtime()
123				if _, ok := rt.(runtime.AgentActivityLister); ok {
124					activities, err := checkoutAgentActivities(ctx, rt, selectedPath, "")
125					if err != nil {
126						app.warnf("could not inspect live agent activity: %v", err)
127					} else if len(activities) == 0 {
128						field("activities", style.dim("— none"))
129					} else {
130						for _, activity := range activities {
131							name := activity.Name
132							if name == "" {
133								name = activity.Agent
134							}
135							field("activity", style.success(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s %s (%s)",
136								name, activity.Status, activity.PaneID, activity.WorkspaceID)))
137						}
138					}
139				}
140
141				if local.Context.TaskErr != nil {
142					field("task", style.warning("— task inventory unavailable"))
143					app.warnf("could not inspect tracked tasks: %v", local.Context.TaskErr)
144					return nil
145				}
146				if selected == nil || len(selected.Tasks) == 0 {
147					field("task", style.warning("— not tracked; `dev start` to record it"))
148					return nil
149				}
150				t := selected.Tasks[0]
151				field("task", fmt.Sprintf("%s %s (%s)", style.taskStateFor(t.State.Label(), t.State.Icon()), t.Title(), t.ID))
152				field("owner", dash(t.Owner))
153				field("next", dash(t.Next))
154				if t.Note != "" {
155					field("note", t.Note)
156				}
157				if t.AgentSession != "" {
158					field("agent", style.success(t.AgentSession))
159				}
160				if host := config.Hostname(); !t.OwnedBy(host) {
161					app.warnf("this task is owned by %s — pushing from here can diverge the branch", t.Owner)
162				}
163				return nil
164			},
165		}
166	}

498		state = canonicalSnapshot(state)
499		if err := validateSnapshot(state); err != nil {
500			return err
501		}
502		if err := ensurePrivateDir(a.root); err != nil {
503			return err
504		}
505		temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(a.root, ".authority-*.tmp")
506		if err != nil {
507			return fmt.Errorf("create operation lease state temp file: %w", err)
508		}
509		name := temporary.Name()
510		defer os.Remove(name)

512			_ = temporary.Close()
513			return err
514		}

522			_ = temporary.Close()

532			return fmt.Errorf("sync operation lease directory: %w", err)
533		}
534		return nil
535	}

545			}
546			if _, exists := bindings[binding.OperationID]; exists {
547				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease repeats binding %s", binding.OperationID)
548			}
549			bindings[binding.OperationID] = binding.Digest
550		}

567			}
568			seenKeys[canonicalKey] = struct{}{}

595					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s on %s has no created_at", named.name, record.Key.subject())

597				if named.claim.MachineID != "" {

600					}

606					}

617				}
618				if err := tombstone.Token.Validate(); err != nil {

620				}

629				}

632						return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s has inconsistent terminal records", tombstone.Token.OperationID)
633					}
634				} else {
635					terminalOperations[tombstone.Token.OperationID] = tombstone
636				}
637				identity := fmt.Sprintf("%s\x00%s\x00%d", tombstone.Token.OperationID, tombstone.Token.Digest, tombstone.Token.Epoch)
638				if _, exists := seenTombstones[identity]; exists {

640				}
641				seenTombstones[identity] = struct{}{}

643					return fmt.Errorf("operation lease key %s has a terminal token still active", record.Key.subject())
644				}
645			}
646		}
647		if state.LastEpoch != maxRecordEpoch {
648			return fmt.Errorf("operation lease last_epoch %d does not match latest record epoch %d", state.LastEpoch, maxRecordEpoch)
649		}
650		for operationID := range activeOperations {
651			if _, terminal := terminalOperations[operationID]; terminal {
652				return fmt.Errorf("operation lease %s is both active and terminal", operationID)
653			}
654		}
655		return nil

658	func canonicalSnapshot(state Snapshot) Snapshot {
659		result := Snapshot{
660			SchemaVersion: state.SchemaVersion,
661			LastEpoch:     state.LastEpoch,
662			Bindings:      append([]Binding(nil), state.Bindings...),
663			Records:       make([]Record, len(state.Records)),
664		}
665		sort.Slice(result.Bindings, func(i, j int) bool { return result.Bindings[i].OperationID < result.Bindings[j].OperationID })
666		for index, record := range state.Records {
667			result.Records[index] = cloneRecord(record)
668			if result.Records[index].Reservation != nil {
669				result.Records[index].Reservation.CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Reservation.CreatedAt)
670			}
671			if result.Records[index].Fence != nil {
672				result.Records[index].Fence.CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Fence.CreatedAt)
673			}
674			for tombstoneIndex := range result.Records[index].Tombstones {
675				result.Records[index].Tombstones[tombstoneIndex].CreatedAt = canonicalTime(result.Records[index].Tombstones[tombstoneIndex].CreatedAt)
676			}
677			sort.Slice(result.Records[index].Tombstones, func(i, j int) bool {
678				left, right := result.Records[index].Tombstones[i], result.Records[index].Tombstones[j]
679				if left.Token.Epoch != right.Token.Epoch {
680					return left.Token.Epoch < right.Token.Epoch
681				}
682				if left.Token.OperationID != right.Token.OperationID {
683					return left.Token.OperationID < right.Token.OperationID
684				}
685				if left.Token.Digest != right.Token.Digest {
686					return left.Token.Digest < right.Token.Digest
687				}
688				return left.Kind < right.Kind
689			})
690		}
691		sort.Slice(result.Records, func(i, j int) bool { return result.Records[i].Key.canonical() < result.Records[j].Key.canonical() })
692		return result
693	}
694
695	func cloneRecord(record Record) Record {
696		result := record
697		if record.Reservation != nil {
698			copy := *record.Reservation
699			result.Reservation = &copy
700		}
701		if record.Fence != nil {
702			copy := *record.Fence
703			result.Fence = &copy
704		}
705		result.Tombstones = append([]Tombstone(nil), record.Tombstones...)
706		return result
707	}

709	func findRecord(records []Record, key Key) *Record {
710		canonical := key.canonical()
711		for index := range records {
712			if records[index].Key.canonical() == canonical {
713				return &records[index]
714			}
715		}
716		return nil
717	}

719	func ensureRecord(state *Snapshot, key Key) *Record {
720		if record := findRecord(state.Records, key); record != nil {
721			return record
722		}
723		state.Records = append(state.Records, Record{Key: key})
724		return &state.Records[len(state.Records)-1]
725	}

727	func allocateEpoch(state *Snapshot) (uint64, error) {
728		if state.LastEpoch == math.MaxUint64 {
729			return 0, errors.New("operation lease epoch exhausted")
730		}
731		state.LastEpoch++
732		return state.LastEpoch, nil
733	}

735	func activeClaim(record Record) (*Claim, string) {

738		}
739		if record.Fence != nil {
740			return record.Fence, "fence"

742		return nil, ""

749			}

754	func ensureBinding(state *Snapshot, request Request) bool {
755		for _, binding := range state.Bindings {
756			if binding.OperationID == request.OperationID {
757				return false
758			}
759		}
760		state.Bindings = append(state.Bindings, Binding{OperationID: request.OperationID, Digest: request.Digest})
761		return true

764	func checkOperationReuse(state Snapshot, keys []Key, request Request) error {
765		for _, binding := range state.Bindings {
766			if binding.OperationID != request.OperationID {
767				continue
768			}
769			if binding.Digest != request.Digest {
770				return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s was permanently bound to another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
771			}
772			break
773		}
774		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
775		for _, key := range keys {
776			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
777		}
778		for _, record := range state.Records {
779			for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
780				if tombstone.Token.OperationID != request.OperationID {
781					continue
782				}
783				if tombstone.Token.Digest != request.Digest {
784					return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s was used with another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
785				}
786				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s is terminal: %w", request.OperationID, ErrReturned)
787			}
788			claim, _ := activeClaim(record)
789			if claim == nil || claim.Token.OperationID != request.OperationID {
790				continue
791			}
792			if claim.Token.Digest != request.Digest {
793				return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s is active with another digest: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
794			}
795			if _, exists := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !exists {
796				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s is active on a different key set: %w", request.OperationID, ErrConflict)
797			}
798		}
799		return nil
800	}

802	func checkHierarchyClaims(state Snapshot, keys []Key, request Request) error {
803		requestedKeys := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
804		requestedRepositories := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
805		repositoryWide := make(map[string]bool, len(keys))
806		for _, key := range keys {
807			requestedKeys[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
808			requestedRepositories[key.Repository] = struct{}{}
809			if key.Scope == ScopeRepository {
810				repositoryWide[key.Repository] = true
811			}
812		}
813		for _, record := range state.Records {
814			claim, kind := activeClaim(record)
815			if claim == nil {
816				continue
817			}
818			if _, requested := requestedKeys[record.Key.canonical()]; requested {
819				continue
820			}
821			if _, sameRepository := requestedRepositories[record.Key.Repository]; !sameRepository {
822				continue
823			}
824			if record.Key.Scope != ScopeRepository && !repositoryWide[record.Key.Repository] {
825				continue
826			}
827			return blockedOrConflict(record.Key, kind, *claim, request)
828		}
829		return nil
830	}

832	func blockedOrConflict(key Key, kind string, claim Claim, request Request) error {
833		if claim.Token.OperationID == request.OperationID {
834			return fmt.Errorf("operation id %s conflicts with its active %s: %w", request.OperationID, kind, ErrConflict)
835		}
836		return &BlockedError{Key: key, Kind: kind, OperationID: claim.Token.OperationID}
837	}

839	func validateGuardKeySet(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token) error {
840		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
841		for _, key := range keys {
842			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
843		}
844		matched := 0
845		for _, record := range state.Records {
846			claim, _ := activeClaim(record)
847			if claim == nil || !claim.Token.matches(token) {
848				continue
849			}
850			if _, included := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !included {
851				return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d owns a larger key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrConflict)
852			}
853			matched++
854		}
855		if matched != len(keys) {
856			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d does not own the exact guard key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrEpochMismatch)
857		}
858		return nil
859	}

861	func validateClaimKeySet(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token, claimKind string) error {
862		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
863		for _, key := range keys {
864			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
865		}
866		matched := 0
867		for _, record := range state.Records {
868			var claim *Claim
869			if claimKind == "reservation" {

873			}

879			}
880			matched++
881		}

884		}

888	func matchingTerminal(state Snapshot, keys []Key, token Token, kind TombstoneKind) (uint64, bool, error) {
889		requested := make(map[string]struct{}, len(keys))
890		for _, key := range keys {
891			requested[key.canonical()] = struct{}{}
892		}
893		var epoch uint64
894		matched := 0
895		for _, record := range state.Records {
896			for _, tombstone := range record.Tombstones {
897				if !tombstone.Token.matches(token) {
898					continue
899				}
900				if tombstone.Kind != kind {
901					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d ended as %s: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, tombstone.Kind, ErrReturned)
902				}
903				if _, included := requested[record.Key.canonical()]; !included {
904					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s epoch %d is terminal on a larger key set: %w", token.OperationID, token.Epoch, ErrConflict)
905				}
906				if epoch == 0 {
907					epoch = tombstone.AdvancedEpoch
908				} else if epoch != tombstone.AdvancedEpoch {
909					return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s has inconsistent terminal epochs: %w", token.OperationID, ErrConflict)
910				}
911				matched++
912				break
913			}
914		}
915		if matched == 0 {
916			return 0, false, nil
917		}
918		if matched != len(keys) {
919			return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("operation %s is terminal on only part of the key set: %w", token.OperationID, ErrConflict)
920		}
921		return epoch, true, nil
922	}

924	func ensurePrivateDir(path string) error {
925		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o700); err != nil {
926			return err
927		}
928		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
929		if err != nil {
930			return err
931		}
932		if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
933			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a private directory", path)
934		}
935		if err := setPrivateMode(path, 0o700); err != nil {
936			return err
937		}
938		info, err = os.Lstat(path)
939		if err != nil {
940			return err
941		}
942		private, err := privateModeMatches(path, info.Mode(), 0o700)
943		if err != nil {
944			return fmt.Errorf("inspect operation lease directory permissions: %w", err)
945		}
946		if !private {
947			return fmt.Errorf("operation lease directory %s permissions are not private (want 0700 or a protected owner-only policy)", path)
948		}
949		return nil
950	}

19	// setPrivateMode installs a protected DACL. Windows os.FileMode permission
20	// bits only model the read-only attribute and cannot establish privacy.
21	func setPrivateMode(path string, want fs.FileMode) error {
22		inheritance := ""
23		switch want.Perm() {
24		case 0o600:
25		case 0o700:
26			inheritance = "OICI"
27		default:
28			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported private Windows mode %04o", want.Perm())
29		}
30		current, _, err := privateSIDs()
31		if err != nil {
32			return err
33		}
34		ace := func(sid string) string {
35			return fmt.Sprintf("(A;%s;GA;;;%s)", inheritance, sid)
36		}
37		descriptor, err := windows.SecurityDescriptorFromString("D:P" + ace(current) + ace(localSystemSID) + ace(administratorsSID))
38		if err != nil {
39			return fmt.Errorf("build private Windows security descriptor: %w", err)
40		}
41		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
42		if err != nil {
43			return fmt.Errorf("read private Windows DACL: %w", err)
44		}
45		if dacl == nil {
46			return fmt.Errorf("private Windows security descriptor has no DACL")
47		}
48		err = windows.SetNamedSecurityInfo(
49			path,
50			windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT,
51			windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION,
52			nil,
53			nil,
54			dacl,
55			nil,
56		)
57		runtime.KeepAlive(descriptor)
58		if err != nil {
59			return fmt.Errorf("set private Windows DACL: %w", err)
60		}
61		return nil
62	}

64	func privateModeMatches(path string, _ fs.FileMode, _ fs.FileMode) (bool, error) {
65		current, allowed, err := privateSIDs()
66		if err != nil {
67			return false, err
68		}
69		descriptor, err := windows.GetNamedSecurityInfo(path, windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT, windows.OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION)
70		if err != nil {
71			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner and DACL: %w", err)
72		}
73		owner, _, err := descriptor.Owner()
74		if err != nil {
75			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner: %w", err)
76		}
77		if !privateSIDAllowed(owner, allowed) {
78			return false, nil
79		}
80		control, _, err := descriptor.Control()
81		if err != nil {
82			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows security descriptor control: %w", err)
83		}
84		if control&windows.SE_DACL_PROTECTED == 0 {
85			return false, nil
86		}
87		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
88		if err != nil {
89			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL: %w", err)
90		}
91		if dacl == nil {
92			return false, nil
93		}
94		seenCurrent := false
95		for index := uint16(0); index < dacl.AceCount; index++ {
96			var ace *windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE
97			if err := windows.GetAce(dacl, uint32(index), &ace); err != nil {
98				return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL entry %d: %w", index, err)
99			}
100			switch ace.Header.AceType {
101			case windows.ACCESS_DENIED_ACE_TYPE:
102				continue
103			case windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE:
104			default:
105				return false, nil
106			}
107			sid := (*windows.SID)(unsafe.Pointer(&ace.SidStart))
108			value := sid.String()
109			if _, ok := allowed[value]; !ok {
110				return false, nil
111			}
112			if value == current {
113				seenCurrent = true
114			}
115		}
116		return seenCurrent, nil
117	}

119	func privateSIDAllowed(sid *windows.SID, allowed map[string]struct{}) bool {
120		if sid == nil {
121			return false
122		}
123		_, ok := allowed[sid.String()]
124		return ok
125	}

127	func privateSIDs() (string, map[string]struct{}, error) {

131		}
132		current := user.User.Sid.String()
133		if current == "" {
134			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("current Windows user has an invalid SID")
135		}
136		return current, map[string]struct{}{
137			current:           {},
138			localSystemSID:    {},
139			administratorsSID: {},
140		}, nil
141	}

19	// setPrivateMode installs a protected DACL. Windows os.FileMode permission
20	// bits only model the read-only attribute and cannot establish privacy.
21	func setPrivateMode(path string, want fs.FileMode) error {
22		inheritance := ""
23		switch want.Perm() {
24		case 0o600:
25		case 0o700:
26			inheritance = "OICI"
27		default:
28			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported private Windows mode %04o", want.Perm())
29		}
30		current, _, err := privateSIDs()
31		if err != nil {
32			return err
33		}
34		ace := func(sid string) string {
35			return fmt.Sprintf("(A;%s;GA;;;%s)", inheritance, sid)
36		}
37		descriptor, err := windows.SecurityDescriptorFromString("D:P" + ace(current) + ace(localSystemSID) + ace(administratorsSID))
38		if err != nil {
39			return fmt.Errorf("build private Windows security descriptor: %w", err)
40		}
41		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
42		if err != nil {
43			return fmt.Errorf("read private Windows DACL: %w", err)
44		}
45		if dacl == nil {
46			return fmt.Errorf("private Windows security descriptor has no DACL")
47		}
48		err = windows.SetNamedSecurityInfo(
49			path,
50			windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT,
51			windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION,
52			nil,
53			nil,
54			dacl,
55			nil,
56		)
57		runtime.KeepAlive(descriptor)
58		if err != nil {
59			return fmt.Errorf("set private Windows DACL: %w", err)
60		}
61		return nil
62	}
63
64	func privateModeMatches(path string, _ fs.FileMode, _ fs.FileMode) (bool, error) {
65		current, allowed, err := privateSIDs()
66		if err != nil {
67			return false, err
68		}
69		descriptor, err := windows.GetNamedSecurityInfo(path, windows.SE_FILE_OBJECT, windows.OWNER_SECURITY_INFORMATION|windows.DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION)
70		if err != nil {
71			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner and DACL: %w", err)
72		}
73		owner, _, err := descriptor.Owner()
74		if err != nil {
75			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows owner: %w", err)
76		}
77		if !privateSIDAllowed(owner, allowed) {
78			return false, nil
79		}
80		control, _, err := descriptor.Control()
81		if err != nil {
82			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows security descriptor control: %w", err)
83		}
84		if control&windows.SE_DACL_PROTECTED == 0 {
85			return false, nil
86		}
87		dacl, _, err := descriptor.DACL()
88		if err != nil {
89			return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL: %w", err)
90		}
91		if dacl == nil {
92			return false, nil
93		}
94		seenCurrent := false
95		for index := uint16(0); index < dacl.AceCount; index++ {
96			var ace *windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE
97			if err := windows.GetAce(dacl, uint32(index), &ace); err != nil {
98				return false, fmt.Errorf("read Windows DACL entry %d: %w", index, err)
99			}
100			switch ace.Header.AceType {
101			case windows.ACCESS_DENIED_ACE_TYPE:
102				continue
103			case windows.ACCESS_ALLOWED_ACE_TYPE:
104			default:
105				return false, nil
106			}
107			sid := (*windows.SID)(unsafe.Pointer(&ace.SidStart))
108			value := sid.String()
109			if _, ok := allowed[value]; !ok {
110				return false, nil
111			}
112			if value == current {
113				seenCurrent = true
114			}
115		}
116		return seenCurrent, nil
117	}
118
119	func privateSIDAllowed(sid *windows.SID, allowed map[string]struct{}) bool {
120		if sid == nil {
121			return false
122		}
123		_, ok := allowed[sid.String()]
124		return ok
125	}
126
127	func privateSIDs() (string, map[string]struct{}, error) {
128		user, err := windows.GetCurrentProcessToken().GetTokenUser()
129		if err != nil {
130			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("read current Windows user: %w", err)
131		}
132		current := user.User.Sid.String()
133		if current == "" {
134			return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("current Windows user has an invalid SID")
135		}
136		return current, map[string]struct{}{
137			current:           {},
138			localSystemSID:    {},
139			administratorsSID: {},
140		}, nil
141	}
142
143	func replaceFile(source, destination string) error {
144		from, err := windows.UTF16PtrFromString(source)
145		if err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		to, err := windows.UTF16PtrFromString(destination)
149		if err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		return windows.MoveFileEx(from, to, windows.MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|windows.MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)
153	}
154
155	// MoveFileEx with MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH durably publishes the replacement.
156	// Windows does not expose a portable directory fsync through os.File.
157	func syncDirectory(string) error { return nil }
158

42
43	# dev-cli
44
45	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
46	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
47
48	```
49	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
50	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
51	herdr / tmux / zellij
52	                a per-host live runtime
53	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
54	```
55
56	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
57	human/task facts such as identity, checkout mode, **state**, **owner** and **next
58	action** in one TOML file per task under configured `paths.state_dir/tasks`
59	(default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks`); transient pane data is not persisted.
60
61	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
62	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
63	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
64	abandoning a task.
65
66	## Check it is there first
67
68	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
69
70	```bash
71	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
72	dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
73	```
74
75	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `zellij`, `gh`, `glab` and Azure CLI
76	each enable more and degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step
77	hard-depend on one.
78
79	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
80
81	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
82	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
83
84	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
85	|---|---|---|---|
86	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
87	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | owned by that harness; not a transcript-relocation guarantee |
88	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
89
90	**Rule of thumb: if code/history/plan must remain reviewable or a human may
91	return tomorrow, use `dev`. Use native isolation only when the harness owns the
92	entire turn-scoped lifecycle.**
93
94	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
95	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
96	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
97	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
98
99	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
100	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
101	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
102
103	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
104
105	## The task lifecycle
106
107	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
108	|---|---|---|---|
109	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
110	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
111	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
112	| ✅ `done` | merged | may remain open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
113
114	```bash
115	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
116	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
117	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
118	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
119	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
120	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
121	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
122	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>                # arm final transcript handoff
123	dev done                                           # TTY wizard: inspect dirty state, then FF/PR/merged
124	dev done --ff                                      # → done/MERGED; resources kept
125	dev retire "token refresh"                         # external-only cleanup → RETIRED
126	```
127
128	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
129	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
130	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
131
132	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`. Before integrating or deleting an
133	agent-owned checkout, read `references/agent-retirement.md`.
134
135	## Pick the task's checkout mode
136
137	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
138
139	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
140	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
141	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
142	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
143	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
144	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
145	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
146
147	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
148	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
149	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
150
151	## Parallel background work
152
153	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
154	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
155	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
156	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
157	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
158
159	`dev` guards writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume when another
160	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
161	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; Herdr resolves the current
162	pane before excluding it. Pure repo/worktree/TUI open is navigation to the live
163	owner, not writer authorization. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless
164	agents already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
165
166	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
167	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Inspect the effective SpecStory/provider
168	command: local wrappers may already be elevated, so never claim they are safe or
169	append a conflicting mode. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not cleanup done.
170
171	## Everyday commands
172
173	```bash
174	dev                        # interactive dashboard (plain listing when piped)
175	dev note add "thought"     # append to repo containing cwd
176	dev note search "query"    # rebuilds FTS index if needed
177	dev edit                   # open the effective config; generate it first if absent
178	dev ls                     # what am I working on, everywhere
179	dev ls --json              # stable machine-readable form (also over ssh)
180	dev status                 # what is this directory: repo, branch, task, session
181	dev sweep                  # what has gone stale or drifted, and what to do
182	dev sweep --apply          # act on it, confirming each change
183	dev sweep --merged-worktrees  # from main, audit contained tracked/untracked worktrees
184	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid>  # arm exact post-writer artifact commit
185	dev artifact list          # finalization handoffs and receipts
186	dev done --ff              # integrate only; runtime/worktree stay alive
187	dev retire <task>          # external-only close/wait/remove/reap
188
189	dev git uncommit           # soft reset with a per-worktree message receipt
190	dev git recommit           # reuse that exact message with normal hooks
191	dev git pull-rebase        # exact stash OID + index-preserving restore
192	dev git amend-all          # add -A + no-edit amend; hooks remain enabled
193
194	dev start                  # context-aware wizard; confirms before creating
195	dev start -t "token refresh" --base main  # fast managed worktree task
196
197	dev wt create feat/auth --base main    # worktree at the configured path
198	dev wt list                            # every worktree of this repo
199	dev wt plan                            # what a new worktree would be set up with
200	dev wt plan --write                    # seed a committed .dev.toml from it
201	dev wt rm feat/auth                    # remove the checkout; the branch stays
202
203	dev repo list --sizes      # repos, recovery topology, owned logical bytes
204	dev repo list --no-remote  # local Git with no configured remote
205	dev repo list --local-only # branches lacking a remote-backed upstream
206	dev repo context [repo]    # agent-ready checkouts, Git, runtime and task state
207	dev repo clone owner/name  # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
208	dev repo clone https://dev.azure.com/acme/Platform/_git/api
209	dev repo sync --all        # fetch + prune, and report what moved
210	dev fleet list              # aggregate repo/task/runtime state over SSH
211	dev fleet sync api --push   # publish, then fast-forward safe matching checkouts
212	dev repo remote [query]     # search configured forge inventories
213	dev bootstrap ~/code       # recursively inventory an existing machine
214	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects   # plan a non-destructive symlink catalog
215	dev gitignore              # .gitignore from GitHub templates + the common bits
216	dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
217
218	dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
219	dev tries mark redis-streams --add important  # durable personal metadata
220	dev tries archive redis-streams               # reversible; does not delete
221	dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
222
223	dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
224	dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
225	dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
226	dev summary                # current machine-wide agent context
227	dev journal                # today's agent-ready development journal
228	dev journal --since 7d --metrics | opencode run "summarize this"
229	dev cache list             # regenerable forge/fleet/size/gitignore/note-index caches
230	dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages
231	```
232
233	Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
234
235	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
236
237	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
238	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
239	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
240
241	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
242	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
243
244	```bash
245	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
246	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
247	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
248	```
249
250	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
251	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
252
253	## Dashboard and forge inventory
254
255	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style
256	h/l. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
257	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
258	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
259
260	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
261	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
262	account can access. A private cache is shown immediately; stale rows stay
263	searchable while refresh runs. `/` filters provider, owner/name, visibility and
264	description, with `vis:private` for an exact visibility match. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
265	confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
266	for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query and `--refresh`
267	forces a complete synchronization.
268
269	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
270	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
271	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
272	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
273	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
274	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
275	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
276	does not launch the receiving agent.
277
278	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
279	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
280	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
281	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
282	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
283	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
284	one repository.
285
286	Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in and cloud-only:
287
288	```toml
289	[[forge.azure_devops]]
290	organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
291	project = "Platform"
292	```
293
294	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs
295	the extension, logs in, changes Azure defaults, or stores a PAT.
296
297	FLEET calls each configured host's own `dev` over SSH, preserving its XDG paths.
298	Enter prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an SSH login shell.
299	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
300	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
301
302	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
303	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
304	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
305	expand linked worktrees; children
306	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
307	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
308	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
309	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
310	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
311	it.
312
313	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
314	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
315	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
316	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
317	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
318
319	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
320	explicitly. Runtime
321	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
322
323	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
324	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
325	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
326	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
327	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
328	the binding should be portable across machines.
329
330	## Repository quick notes
331
332	Read `references/notes.md` before adding/searching/editing/deleting notes or
333	when deciding whether content belongs in dev vs td/beads.
334
335	Quick notes are multiple timestamped Markdown files under configured
336	`paths.state_dir/notes/<catalog-id>/` (default `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`); the
337	catalog ID attaches them to the canonical clone across worktrees, symlinks and
338	moves. `dev` does not synchronize notes or catalog state, so cross-host
339	attachment requires syncing both. SQLite FTS at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db`
340	is disposable: clearing it removes no thoughts and the next search rebuilds it.
341
342	TUI context keys: `n` quick-adds on TASKS/REPOS; `N` browses with `/` search,
343	Enter expand, `a` add, `e` editor, and confirmed `d` delete. In TRY, `n` remains
344	“new Try.” REMOTE needs a local clone.
345
346	## Editing configuration
347
348	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
349	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
350	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
351
352	## Rules for agents
353
354	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
355	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
356	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
357
358	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
359	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
360	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
361	   history unattended.
362
363	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
364	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
365	   user before overriding it.
366
367	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
368	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
369	   for them. For merged worktree cleanup, run `dev sweep --merged-worktrees`
370	   from the canonical main checkout, present every candidate and blocker as a
371	   QA question, and use `--apply --yes` only after the user explicitly approves
372	   that exact set. Branch deletion remains a separate `--delete-branches` opt-in.
373
374	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
375	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
376	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
377
378	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
379	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
380	   pushed.
381
382	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
383	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
384	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
385	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
386	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
387	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
388	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
389
390	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
391	   panes isolate *agents*. A writer claim in one checkout needs explicit
392	   disjoint ownership; pure open/focus may navigate to the existing owner.
393
394	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
395	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json`. Never infer from
396	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
397	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
398	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
399
400	10. **Launcher profile and effective permissions are explicit.** Standard
401	    Claude/Codex put the complete native command inside SpecStory `-c`; verified
402	    `*-copilot-once` wrappers already wrap SpecStory but inherit effective
403	    provider permissions, which may be dangerous. Never append a conflicting
404	    safer mode to an elevated command. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
405
406	11. **Cleanup is external, never self-triggered by agent state.** Herdr `done`
407	    means a turn settled. Arm and finalize exact artifacts first; `dev done`
408	    integrates only, and `dev retire` must run outside the target workspace.
409	    Never run raw `git worktree remove --force` against the caller's checkout.
410
411	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
412	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
413	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
414	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
415
416	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
417	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
418	   their judgement, not yours.
419
420	14. **Treat Markdown notes as durable and notes.db as cache.** Never delete
421	   configured `paths.state_dir/notes` to fix search; use `dev cache clear notes`
422	   and reindex. Note deletion itself requires explicit confirmation, and `dev`
423	   does not synchronize note/catalog state between hosts.
424
425	15. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
426	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
427	   `dev cache clear` only for regenerable remote/size/gitignore/note-FTS caches.
428
429	16. **Archive is not eviction.** `dev tries archive` is a reversible hidden move
430	   on the same filesystem; it does not free space. Phase 1 has no project-data
431	   delete command. Never substitute `rm -rf` merely because a remote exists —
432	   no-remote, local-only refs, ignored files and stash are independent risks.
433
434	17. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
435	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
436	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
437
438	18. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
439	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
440	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
441	   does not duplicate them.
442
443	## When to use this skill
444
445	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
446	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
447	- Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
448	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
449	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
450	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
451	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
452	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
453	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
454	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
455	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
456	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
457	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
458
459	## When NOT to use it
460
461	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
462	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
463	- **Standalone Herdr pane/agent control** — that is the `herdr` skill. The
464	  `dev start --json` cross-tool launch workflow remains here.
465	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
466
467	## Reference files
468
469	- `references/notes.md` — read before repository quick-note operations or
470	  choosing the boundary with td/beads.
471	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
472	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
473	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
474	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
475	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
476	  work moves between machines.
477	- `references/agent-retirement.md` — prepare/finalize/integrate/retire, caller
478	  safety, exact transcript handling and orphaned-runtime recovery.
479	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
480	  including native worktree grouping, collisions and cleanup semantics.
481	- `references/parallel-agents.md` — read before launching parallel background
482	  work; exact JSON/pane validation, SpecStory profiles and permissions.
483	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
484	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
485
486	## Gotchas
487
488	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
489	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private child-only
490	  file descriptor, reads one NUL-terminated path and calls `builtin cd` without
491	  evaluating command output. Without the wrapper, the binary's printable legacy
492	  directive cannot change the parent shell — that is not a bug.
493	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
494	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
495	  skips that and leaves you to it.
496	- **Only explicitly included, gitignored stable regular files are copied.**
497	  Source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused; existing targets
498	  are reported skipped, not copied. Do not universally include
499	  `.claude/settings.local.json`: only sticky/plain-Claude profiles opt in.
500	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
501	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
502	- **Bare `dev done` is interactive only on a TTY.** It reports branch relation
503	  and dirty-content equivalence, then offers commit/discard and FF/PR/cleanup.
504	  Non-interactive use remains report-only without `--ff`/`--pr`. Unique discard
505	  requires `DROP` or explicit `--dirty=discard --yes`.
506	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
507	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
508

552	22	- `indeterminate`: probe 失敗、stale、unsupported 或 coverage 不完整；
