603	73	# Architecture
604	74
605	75	## Shared domains
606	76
607	77	- 新增 `internal/assessment`: schema/version、evidence provenance/freshness/completeness、gate/outcome/reason code、canonical fingerprint 與 outcome reduction；保持 presentation-neutral，讓 inventory/transfer/recovery/local-files 各自產生 evidence。
608	78	- 擴充 `internal/inventory/repo_context.go`: 保留每個 checkout 的 status error、runtime enumeration error、Git topology、catalog/note/artifact摘要、safe remotes、fleet observations 與 scoped gates；CLI/TUI 消費同一 aggregate，不能再以 `tui.RepoRow` 當 domain contract。
609	79	- 新增 `internal/lease`: 獨立於 task/transfer 的 cooperative operation authority；以 canonical Git identity + branch/repository scope 鎖定，保存 reservation/fence epoch，讓所有目前版本的 Git/worktree/artifact/local-file/task mutator 在任何 side effect 前共用同一 lock/guard。
610	80	- 新增 `internal/transfer`: portable task DTO、source/target plan、strict wire protocol、private object/sidecar staging、journal/store、phase transition、sidecar import、fencing/abort/return/reconciliation。
611	81	- 新增 `internal/localfiles`: project manifest resolution、ignored-file expansion、held-root snapshot、plan/conflict policy、bounded wire payload、target apply/rollback/immutable recovery copy/receipt；供 `fleet files` 與 `fleet transfer --with-local-files` 共用。
612	82	- 新增 `internal/recovery`: all-ref 與 Git-administrative manifest/artifact/receipt、reclaim assessment、restore drill/apply、eviction intent/reconciliation。
613	83	- 擴充 `internal/wt` provisioning service：以 checkout/OID + plan hash 為 key 的 private setup journal；content-addressed/idempotent steps 可重播，任意 command 逐步記錄 `pending/running/completed/indeterminate`。
614	84	- 新增 `internal/forge/weburl.go`: 從 live Git endpoint 或 exact forge match 保守產生 display-safe HTTPS URL；raw Git URL 與 public DTO 分離。
615	85	- CLI orchestration 拆到 `internal/cli/repo_context.go`、`fleet_files.go`、`fleet_transfer.go`、`backup.go`、`reclaim.go`、`restore.go`、`evict.go`；既有 `fleet.Transport` 只負責 transport，不承擔 policy。
616	86
617	87	Reuse rather than duplicate:
618	88
619	89	- repository/checkout identity: `gitx.Discover`, `repo.Resolve/Discover`, `pathx.Canonical/Contains`;
620	90	- local Git: `gitx.StatusOf`, `Worktrees`, `WorktreeFor`, `RecoveryTopologyOf`, `InProgress`, `AnalyzeFinish`, `Run`;
621	91	- fleet identity/transport: `catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity`, `fleet.Transport`, candidate matching/FF classification extracted from `fleet.ApplySync`;
622	92	- lifecycle safety: `retire.Inspect`, `CloseAndWait`, target revalidation, `runtime.All()`;
623	93	- target acquisition/provisioning: `repo.Acquire`, `wt.Manager`, target-local trusted settings;
624	94	- durable identity/state: catalog `WithLock`/locations, note revision + file lock, artifact intent/reachability;
625	95	- filesystem safety: extract held-`os.Root` traversal/stable reads/portable path validation from `internal/repotemplate/snapshot.go`, and use `lockx` plus note/experiment intent/atomic-write ordering;
626	96	- disk ownership: `diskusage.Target/Usage` for owned vs shared bytes.
627	97
628	98	## Stable machine and protocol identity
629	99
630	100	Create a private, durable machine UUID (independent state stores make this host-local) and expose it through a non-secret capability command. Add an optional expected machine ID to each `remotes.toml` host; any mutating transfer/files/restore operation requires it to be pinned and match, while list/status may merely warn. SSH host-key validation remains mandatory.
631	101
632	102	All new hidden commands use separate strict v1 envelopes, bounded stdin/stdout/stderr, `DisallowUnknownFields`, EOF checks, schema/capability negotiation, exact machine/repo/branch/OID binding and idempotency IDs. Add non-PTY `ssh -T` protocol mode and disable agent/X11/port forwarding; probe compatibility before sending note bodies or file content. Old/no-dev/incompatible targets fail before payload transmission.
633	103
634	104	# Repository context and safe remote links
635	105
636	106	Extend `dev repo context` rather than adding another status synonym. Human/JSON sections:
637	107
638	108	1. identity, selected checkout, generated time and source provenance;
639	109	2. canonical + linked worktrees, per-checkout Git/error/activity;
640	110	3. tasks, owner/fence, artifacts and every observed runtime backend;
641	111	4. every Git remote with role (current upstream/origin/upstream), sanitized endpoint identity, provider and safe plain HTTPS web URL when confidently derivable;
642	112	5. matching configured fleet hosts, path/branch/task/runtime summaries, live/stale/unreachable/incompatible state and snapshot age;
643	113	6. scoped readiness and stable blocker/remediation codes;
644	114	7. coverage/errors, including the explicit statement that fleet means configured hosts only.
645	115
646	116	`--json` is a new additive schema-v1 report; unknown/error values remain null/status entries, never zeroed or silently omitted. Raw credential-bearing Git URLs, note bodies, local-file hashes/content and secret query/fragment/userinfo never enter public output. `--refresh` may update caches, but cached forge/fleet facts are display-only and can never satisfy a mutating gate. TUI gets only the cheap local readiness summary and shared renderer; ordinary row rendering must not trigger SSH, forge refresh or all-object scans.
647	117
648	118	Web URL order: exact live forge record URL, strict Azure transform, literal recognized/configured GitHub/GitLab host transform, otherwise unavailable. Strip/reject userinfo, query, fragment, controls, ambiguous escaping and unsupported ports; SSH aliases do not become browser hosts. Render a plain URL (terminal may linkify it) rather than introducing OSC-8 width/security complexity.
649	119
650	120	# Portable local files
651	121
652	122	Add a new project-owned `[local_files]` section in `.dev-cli/config.toml` with explicit portable relative patterns, plus repeatable ad-hoc `--file`. Do not inherit existing `worktree.include` defaults: a repository may propose candidates, but only the explicit `fleet files` invocation or `transfer --with-local-files` authorizes off-machine export. Define a small portable glob grammar, expand it locally to sorted exact paths, and send no glob over the wire.
653	123
654	124	For every file, both hosts must prove it is untracked and ignored under their own Git configuration; tracked files travel through Git. Only bounded regular files are accepted—no directories, symlinks/reparse points, sockets, devices, FIFOs, `.git`, nested repositories or submodule boundaries. Initial hard ceilings: 128 files, 8 MiB/file, 32 MiB total, bounded path/component depth; host settings may lower but not raise compiled limits.
655	125
656	126	Plan states are `ready`, `current`, `blocked-conflict`, `blocked-ineligible`, `blocked-unsafe`, `missing`, `failed`. 657	127
658	128	- missing target: stage private temp (`0600`), stream/hash exact length, sync, then publish atomically without replacement;
659	129	- identical target: no-op/current;
660	130	- differing target: block unless `--replace`; replace requires the target digest observed in the displayed plan, private rollback copy, atomic swap, post-write rehash and rollback/reconciliation on failure;
661	131	- `--yes` never implies `--replace`; no deletion or last-writer-wins mode.
662	132

They may be released only by a separately confirmed durable-receipt purge or after an independently restore-verified immutable backup supersedes them. 664	134

666	136
667	137	# Transfer protocol
668	138
669	139	## Target preparation
670	140
671	141	Separate branch/ref evidence from checkout evidence. For every selected task/current branch, A resolves `refs/heads/<branch>` directly through the shared Git common directory and captures exact OID/object format without requiring it to be checked out. Only branches with an existing checkout require conflict-free, operation-free, fully clean checkout evidence. COLD/unattached task refs must equal the freshly fetched/advertised remote tip before transfer and remain COLD on B with no checkout; this lets one repository transfer several serial branch-mode tasks without pretending they are all attached. Every published ref uses an explicit `<oid>:refs/heads/<branch>` ordinary push and the live remote tip must equal exactly that OID (not merely contain it).
672	142
673	143	Before A is fenced, B may only create a durable reservation, validate conflicts, and fetch expected objects into a private, non-discoverable transfer staging repository. Existing clones are reserved through the shared lease authority but no branch/worktree is moved; absent clones are staged under the private transfer directory rather than passed directly to `repo.Acquire`. Operation-owned incomplete staging can be verified and safely recreated/reused on retry, while any pre-existing or user-modified destination remains untouched.
674	144
675	145	After A’s fence is durable, B holds its repository/branch leases while publishing the target state. It matches all configured fetch/push identities and reuses exactly one clone; ambiguity blocks. If absent, it computes the final destination from B’s own path policy and materializes the verified staging clone without exposing a partial canonical checkout. It then creates/fast-forwards only the checkouts required by task state/mode. Ahead/diverged/dirty/live-agent targets block. Worktree tasks use B’s configured path and explicit expected ref; WARM worktree tasks get a checkout, COLD tasks do not. Branch/direct tasks may use canonical checkout only when unique and safe—never silently change mode. Acceptance may apply only deterministic, journaled portable files; it never runs `post_create`, dependency installers/copies, or other arbitrary provisioning inside the replayable distributed transaction. Transfer does not copy trust/credentials or open a runtime. Accepted HOT tasks become WARM; WARM/COLD stay as-is. After acceptance, B runs provisioning as a separate B-owned setup transaction through `dev resume` or `dev wt provision`; accepted existing WARM checkouts must enter this flow just like newly recreated worktrees. A private journal is bound to checkout identity/OID and provisioning-plan hash. Before each arbitrary command, fsync `running`; after success, fsync `completed`. A crash in `running` becomes `indeterminate` and is never auto-replayed—only explicit `--retry-indeterminate` or operator-attested `--mark-complete` can advance it. A journal cannot promise exactly-once for an external side effect, so automatic resume is limited to content-addressed/proven-idempotent steps. Context separately reports `transfer-complete` and `setup-pending/indeterminate/ready` so acceptance is never misrepresented as a fully provisioned environment.
676	146
677	147	## Sidecar rehydration
678	148
679	149	Portable task DTO contains stable ID, name/repo display, branch/base/mode/state/next/note/tags/timestamps and source provenance, but never A paths or runtime handles. On B, bind `RepoPath`/`WorktreePath` from B, clear runtime/agent hints, and import with exact-ID + revision conflict detection. Add task-store cross-process locking/CAS, but make the operation lease—not the task file—the authoritative fence so a selected branch with no task is still protected. Retrofit every current `dev` path that can mutate or expose a certified repository/branch/checkout/sidecar (`dev git`, lifecycle/TUI, adopt, worktree/repo/bootstrap/fleet setup, artifact finalization, local-file apply) to acquire/check the same lease before its first effect and hold it through Git/filesystem changes plus final CAS.
680	150
681	151	Catalog import preserves stable ID, metadata/tags/remote identity, adds B’s machine-specific location, and blocks pending move or conflicting ID/path/non-empty summaries. Note import preserves ID/repository ID/timestamps/tags/body; exact revision is idempotent, differing same-ID content blocks. Durable Markdown is written before disposable FTS rebuild; FTS failure is reported without rolling back durable notes. Note/file content travels only via bounded SSH stdin and is never echoed or cached.
682	152
683	153	## Idempotent no-two-writer handoff
684	154
685	155	Persist strict private source and target journals keyed by random transfer ID + manifest digest. Sequence:
686	156
687	157	1. **Plan**: live source/target assessment, no mutation.
688	158	2. **Publish**: create source intent; revalidate fingerprint; push/verify exact branch OIDs.
689	159	3. **Reserve/stage B**: durably reserve the target identities, validate sidecar/path conflicts and fetch objects into private staging only. Do not publish a working checkout, provision, write portable files, or expose target tasks.
690	160	4. **Fence A**: from an external coordinator, require caller/runtime outside all selected checkouts. Acquire all selected branch/repository operation leases in deterministic order, thereby drain already-started current-version mutators; while still holding them, revalidate Git/sidecar revisions, record B machine ID + fencing epoch durably, normalize HOT→WARM and then release the locks. Every later current-version source mutation sees the fence and fails. Keep every A byte.
691	161	5. **Accept/publish B**: under the same target reservations/leases, require the exact epoch/digest, revalidate staging and target state, publish/create the required checkouts, apply optional deterministic portable files, and import catalog/notes/tasks idempotently. Do not run arbitrary provisioning. Set B owner and write the acceptance receipt last; only then release the target reservation so ordinary B commands can see a writable accepted state and later run local `dev resume` provisioning.
692	162	6. **Complete/reconcile**: lost response is resolved through `fleet transfer status`; no distributed rollback. A remains present but fenced until explicit eviction or ownership return.
693	163
694	164	Same ID+digest resumes; same ID+different digest rejects. `abort` is terminal only before source fence and cleans solely journal-owned staging. After fence, `return` first acquires B’s leases, quiesces the exact manifest, writes a durable `returned` tombstone keyed by ID/digest/epoch that permanently rejects delayed prepare/accept replays, then lets A verify it and CAS-unfence the unchanged source while advancing the epoch. If B is unreachable or indeterminate, A remains safely fenced; generic `resume --force` cannot override a transfer fence. This permits a zero-writer window but never intentionally two cooperative writers. Document that raw Git and old binaries can bypass dev’s lease.

696	166	# Backup, reclaim, restore, and eviction
697	167
698	168	## Backup receipt
699	169
700	170	Add a fresh `gitx` recovery snapshot that inventories all local `refs/heads/*`, tags, notes, stash and other refs/OIDs; dirty/untracked/ignored/unreadable paths; Git operations/worktrees; LFS; submodules/nested repositories; shallow/partial clone, alternates and external/shared Git storage. Repeat the flag/raw-byte proof during final eviction under the operation leases. Separately enumerate every private GitDir/common-dir administrative entry (config, hooks, info/exclude/attributes, rr-cache, reflogs and unknown files) through held roots. Classify only proven Git-managed/regenerable entries as reconstructible; preserve each remaining regular file in a private recovery artifact outside the eviction roots or require an item-scoped discard. Credential-bearing config is never uploaded to a Git remote. `RecoveryTopology` remains descriptive and is never promoted to proof.

702	172	`backup --push` authorizes one resolved effective push endpoint, not merely a remote name. 704	174	## Reclaim and restore proof
705	175
706	176	`reclaim` joins fresh evidence for every checkout/root, ref/object, Git-administrative entry, ignored file, immutable portable-file recovery blob, task/fence, catalog/note revision, artifact, all available runtime backends, caller containment, owned/shared bytes and configured fleet state. Unsupported LFS/submodule/nested/external-object layouts block eviction rather than weakening the claim. Regular `restore --apply` uses the same plan/revalidation to reconstruct a real destination. 710	180	## Journaled actual eviction
711	181
712	182	`evict` never runs inside transfer. It defaults to the same report as reclaim and requires explicit `--apply`, exact target, matching receipt, current verified restore, and exact confirmation (`YES`; noninteractive `--yes` only with explicit target). Named acknowledgements such as `--discard-ignored`, `--discard-dirty`, `--discard-unreachable`, `--override-keep` are independent; `--yes` does not imply data loss and there is no generic `--force`.
713	183
714	184	Under recovery/task/catalog/Git operation leases, evict re-runs every check, closes only eligible runtime surfaces from outside them, waits and re-enumerates all backends, and freezes every reviewed checkout/Git root. 715	185
716	186	After all linked roots are safely retired, apply the same sequence to the ordinary canonical clone: write/finalize its intent, atomically rename it into same-parent private staging, revoke new opens, drain all handles, and rerun the full raw-byte/Git-administrative manifest proof under custody before physical removal. If handle enumeration is unavailable/incomplete, any writer remains, or evidence changes at any root, preserve every affected staged root/intent and return indeterminate for later reconcile—never continue on an acknowledgement disguised as proof. 3590	137	# Transfer protocol
3591	138
3592	139	## Target preparation
3593	140
3594	141	Separate branch/ref evidence from checkout evidence. For every selected task/current branch, A resolves `refs/heads/<branch>` directly through the shared Git common directory and captures exact OID/object format without requiring it to be checked out. Only branches with an existing checkout require conflict-free, operation-free, fully clean checkout evidence. COLD/unattached task refs must equal the freshly fetched/advertised remote tip before transfer and remain COLD on B with no checkout; this lets one repository transfer several serial branch-mode tasks without pretending they are all attached. Every published ref uses an explicit `<oid>:refs/heads/<branch>` ordinary push and the live remote tip must equal exactly that OID (not merely contain it).
3595	142
3596	143	Before A is fenced, B may only create a durable reservation, validate conflicts, and fetch expected objects into a private, non-discoverable transfer staging repository. Existing clones are reserved through the shared lease authority but no branch/worktree is moved; absent clones are staged under the private transfer directory rather than passed directly to `repo.Acquire`. Operation-owned incomplete staging can be verified and safely recreated/reused on retry, while any pre-existing or user-modified destination remains untouched.
3597	144
3598	145	After A’s fence is durable, B holds its repository/branch leases while publishing the target state. It matches all configured fetch/push identities and reuses exactly one clone; ambiguity blocks. If absent, it computes the final destination from B’s own path policy and materializes the verified staging clone without exposing a partial canonical checkout. It then creates/fast-forwards only the checkouts required by task state/mode. Ahead/diverged/dirty/live-agent targets block. Worktree tasks use B’s configured path and explicit expected ref; WARM worktree tasks get a checkout, COLD tasks do not. Branch/direct tasks may use canonical checkout only when unique and safe—never silently change mode. Acceptance may apply only deterministic, journaled portable files; it never runs `post_create`, dependency installers/copies, or other arbitrary provisioning inside the replayable distributed transaction. Transfer does not copy trust/credentials or open a runtime. Accepted HOT tasks become WARM; WARM/COLD stay as-is. After acceptance, B runs provisioning as a separate B-owned setup transaction through `dev resume` or `dev wt provision`; accepted existing WARM checkouts must enter this flow just like newly recreated worktrees. A private journal is bound to checkout identity/OID and provisioning-plan hash. Before each arbitrary command, fsync `running`; after success, fsync `completed`. A crash in `running` becomes `indeterminate` and is never auto-replayed—only explicit `--retry-indeterminate` or operator-attested `--mark-complete` can advance it. A journal cannot promise exactly-once for an external side effect, so automatic resume is limited to content-addressed/proven-idempotent steps. Context separately reports `transfer-complete` and `setup-pending/indeterminate/ready` so acceptance is never misrepresented as a fully provisioned environment.

3609	156

3611	158	2. **Publish**: create source intent; revalidate fingerprint; push/verify exact branch OIDs.

18	remote/shared-Git restore. Non-Git experiments need a real archive/export
19	format before they can be called recoverable. Do not infer safety merely from

22	### P2 · L — Versioned orthogonal task integration phases
23	The backward-compatible retirement MVP derives READY/MERGED/RETIRED while
24	persisting the existing hot/warm/cold/done state. A future task schema should
25	separate execution disposition from integration phase, adopt strict versioned
26	decoding plus cross-process update locks, and explicitly migrate ambiguous

28	fields, so this requires a deliberate minimum-version/downgrade policy.

31	Persist PR/MR identity and extend forge adapters to report open/draft/merged
32	state, merge commit and method. Until then `done --merged` proves ordinary
33	ancestry and squash completion requires explicit operator attestation; never
34	infer a squash solely because the source branch disappeared.

37	The TUI now renders immediately and probes repositories in the background with
38	bounded concurrency, reducing perceived startup latency. A 56-repo refresh
39	still takes roughly three seconds because status + latest commit remain live Git
40	queries. If inventories grow into the hundreds, persist a short-lived snapshot
41	and stream changed rows into the model; keep `r` as the explicit live refresh.

44	Research and detect repo-local task stores without making either a core

46

48	- beads: <https://github.com/gastownhall/beads>
49
50	Both may create dot-folders inside a repo. An adapter should report which
51	backend is present, delegate through its CLI, and avoid copying its task data
52	into dev's own notes/tasks. Decide only after comparing lifecycle, multi-agent
53	locking, git noise, cross-machine sync, archival and uninstall behavior. Until

62	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated

67	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a

70	## Deliberately not doing
71
72	### Installing dependencies
73	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
74	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
75	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
76	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
77	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
78	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
79
80	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
81	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
82
83	### A second git database
84	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. Durable stores hold
85	human intent and identity: task state/owner/next action, asset tags/notes,
86	experiment lifecycle and per-host location. Recovery receipts may record one
87	past verification, but apply must verify again. Live branches, remotes,
88	ahead/behind, dirty state and sizes remain derived/cache-only; a durable tool
89	that disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
90
91	### Syncing runtime state between machines
92	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
93	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
94	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much

100	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.

1	// Package localfiles plans and applies one-way transfers of explicitly selected,
2	// ignored local files between exact repository checkouts.
3	package localfiles
4
5	import (
6		"crypto/sha256"
7		"encoding/hex"
8		"encoding/json"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"sort"
12		"strconv"
13		"strings"
14		"unicode"
15
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/fleet"
18		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/machineid"
19		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/safefile"
20		"github.com/google/uuid"
21	)
22
23	const (
24		SchemaVersion              = 1
25		MaxPlanEnvelopeBytes int64 = 2 << 20
26		// A maximum raw payload is 32 MiB; JSON base64 plus bounded metadata fits in
27		// 48 MiB. Both client transport and target decoder enforce this ceiling.
28		MaxApplyEnvelopeBytes int64 = 48 << 20
29		MaxApplyResponseBytes int64 = 2 << 20
30	)
31
32	type State string
33
34	const (
35		StateReady             State = "ready"
36		StateCurrent           State = "current"
37		StateBlockedConflict   State = "blocked-conflict"
38		StateBlockedIneligible State = "blocked-ineligible"
39		StateBlockedUnsafe     State = "blocked-unsafe"
40		StateMissing           State = "missing"
41		StateFailed            State = "failed"
42		StateCreated           State = "created"
43		StateReplaced          State = "replaced"
44		StateRolledBack        State = "rolled-back"
45		StateReconcile         State = "reconcile"
46	)
47
48	func (s State) validPlan() bool {
49		switch s {
50		case StateReady, StateCurrent, StateBlockedConflict, StateBlockedIneligible,
51			StateBlockedUnsafe, StateMissing, StateFailed:
52			return true
53		default:
54			return false
55		}
56	}
57
58	func (s State) validResult() bool {
59		return s.validPlan() || s == StateCreated || s == StateReplaced || s == StateRolledBack || s == StateReconcile
60	}
61
62	// PublicFile is the complete public per-file surface. Digests, content,
63	// environment values, absolute roots, and base64 never enter this type.
64	type PublicFile struct {
65		Path  string `json:"path"`
66		Size  int64  `json:"size"`
67		Mode  string `json:"mode"`
68		State State  `json:"state"`
69	}
70
71	// Report is used for both report-only plans and apply results.
72	type Report struct {
73		SchemaVersion int          `json:"schema_version"`
74		Files         []PublicFile `json:"files"`
75	}
76
77	func (r Report) Successful() bool {
78		for _, file := range r.Files {
79			switch file.State {
80			case StateReady, StateCurrent, StateCreated, StateReplaced:
81			default:
82				return false
83			}
84		}
85		return len(r.Files) > 0
86	}

88	// Pattern records local provenance only. It is never serialized to a target.

103	func (b Binding) Validate() error {
104		if b.RemoteIdentity == "" || b.RemoteIdentity != catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(b.RemoteIdentity) {
105			return errors.New("binding has no canonical remote identity")
106		}

114			return fmt.Errorf("source machine: %w", err)
115		}
116		if err := machineid.Validate(b.TargetMachine); err != nil {
117			return fmt.Errorf("target machine: %w", err)
118		}
119		if b.SourceMachine == b.TargetMachine {
120			return errors.New("source and target machine IDs must differ")
121		}

139	func validateFileSpecs(files []FileSpec, limits safefile.Limits) error {
140		metadata := make([]safefile.Metadata, len(files))

142			if index > 0 && files[index-1].Path >= file.Path {
143				return errors.New("file manifest paths must be unique and sorted")
144			}

171			MaxTotalBytes: r.Limits.MaxTotalBytes, MaxPathBytes: r.Limits.MaxPathBytes,

176	func (r PlanRequest) Validate() error {

179		}
180		parsed, err := uuid.Parse(r.RequestID)
181		if err != nil || parsed == uuid.Nil || parsed.String() != r.RequestID {
182			return errors.New("plan request has an invalid request ID")
183		}
184		if err := r.Binding.Validate(); err != nil {
185			return err
186		}
187		if err := r.Limits.Validate(); err != nil {

190		if err := r.SafeLimits().Validate(); err != nil {
191			return fmt.Errorf("safe-file limits: %w", err)
192		}
193		if len(r.Files) == 0 {
194			return errors.New("plan request has no exact files")
195		}

224		ProtocolVersion int        `json:"protocol_version"`
225		RequestID       string     `json:"request_id"`
226		ManifestDigest  string     `json:"manifest_digest"`

233	func (r PlanResponse) PublicReport() Report {
234		files := make([]PublicFile, len(r.Files))
235		for index := range r.Files {
236			files[index] = r.Files[index].PublicFile
237		}
238		return Report{SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, Files: files}

241	func (r PlanResponse) Validate(request PlanRequest) error {
242		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
243			return err
244		}
245		if r.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || r.ProtocolVersion != fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion ||
246			r.RequestID != request.RequestID || r.ManifestDigest != request.ManifestDigest ||
247			r.TargetMachine != request.Binding.TargetMachine {
248			return errors.New("plan response binding does not match request")
249		}
250		if !validDigest(r.TargetCheckout) {
251			return errors.New("plan response has an invalid checkout identity")
252		}
253		if len(r.Files) != len(request.Files) {
254			return errors.New("plan response file count does not match request")
255		}
256		for index, file := range r.Files {
257			spec := request.Files[index]
258			if file.Path != spec.Path || file.Size != spec.Size || file.Mode != spec.Mode || !file.State.validPlan() {
259				return fmt.Errorf("plan response metadata for %q does not match request", spec.Path)
260			}
261			switch file.Action {
262			case actionCurrent:
263				if file.State != StateCurrent || file.TargetSHA256 != spec.SHA256 || file.TargetMode != spec.Mode {
264					return fmt.Errorf("plan response current observation for %q is invalid", spec.Path)
265				}
266			case actionCreate:
267				if file.State != StateReady || file.TargetSHA256 != "" || file.TargetMode != "" {
268					return fmt.Errorf("plan response create observation for %q is invalid", spec.Path)
269				}
270			case actionReplace:
271				if !request.Replace || file.State != StateReady || !validDigest(file.TargetSHA256) || !validFileMode(file.TargetMode) {
272					return fmt.Errorf("plan response replace observation for %q is invalid", spec.Path)
273				}
274			case "":
275				if file.State == StateReady || file.State == StateCurrent {
276					return fmt.Errorf("plan response for %q omits a required action", spec.Path)
277				}
278				if file.TargetSHA256 != "" && !validDigest(file.TargetSHA256) {
279					return fmt.Errorf("plan response for %q has an invalid target digest", spec.Path)
280				}
281				if file.TargetMode != "" && !validFileMode(file.TargetMode) {
282					return fmt.Errorf("plan response for %q has an invalid target mode", spec.Path)
283				}
284			default:
285				return fmt.Errorf("plan response for %q has an unknown action", spec.Path)
286			}
287		}
288		if !validDigest(r.PlanDigest) || r.PlanDigest != planDigest(request, r) {
289			return errors.New("plan response digest does not match")
290		}
291		return nil
292	}

296		Content string `json:"content_base64"`

316	func (r ApplyResponse) PublicReport() Report {

318	}

320	func (r ApplyResponse) Validate(request PlanRequest, plan PlanResponse) error {
321		if r.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || r.ProtocolVersion != fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion ||
322			r.RequestID != request.RequestID || r.PlanDigest != plan.PlanDigest || len(r.Files) != len(request.Files) {
323			return errors.New("apply response binding does not match plan")
324		}
325		for index, file := range r.Files {
326			spec := request.Files[index]
327			if file.Path != spec.Path || file.Size != spec.Size || file.Mode != spec.Mode || !file.State.validResult() {
328				return fmt.Errorf("apply response metadata for %q does not match plan", spec.Path)
329			}
330			expected := StateCurrent
331			switch plan.Files[index].Action {
332			case actionCreate:
333				expected = StateCreated
334			case actionReplace:
335				expected = StateReplaced
336			case actionCurrent:
337			default:
338				return fmt.Errorf("apply response action for %q is invalid", spec.Path)
339			}
340			if file.State != expected {
341				return fmt.Errorf("apply response state for %q does not match plan", spec.Path)
342			}
343		}
344		return nil
345	}
346
347	func manifestDigest(request PlanRequest) string {
348		payload := struct {
349			Domain    string           `json:"domain"`
350			RequestID string           `json:"request_id"`
351			Binding   Binding          `json:"binding"`
352			Limits    fleet.FileLimits `json:"limits"`
353			Replace   bool             `json:"replace"`
354			Files     []FileSpec       `json:"files"`
355		}{"dev-local-files-manifest-v1", request.RequestID, request.Binding, request.Limits, request.Replace, request.Files}
356		return digestJSON(payload)
357	}
358
359	func planDigest(request PlanRequest, response PlanResponse) string {
360		files := append([]PlanFile(nil), response.Files...)
361		payload := struct {
362			Domain         string     `json:"domain"`
363			ManifestDigest string     `json:"manifest_digest"`
364			TargetMachine  string     `json:"target_machine_id"`
365			TargetCheckout string     `json:"target_checkout_id"`
366			Files          []PlanFile `json:"files"`
367		}{"dev-local-files-plan-v1", request.ManifestDigest, response.TargetMachine, response.TargetCheckout, files}
368		return digestJSON(payload)
369	}
370
371	func digestJSON(value any) string {
372		data, _ := json.Marshal(value)
373		digest := sha256.Sum256(data)
374		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(digest[:])
375	}
376
377	func digestBytes(value []byte) string {
378		digest := sha256.Sum256(value)
379		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(digest[:])
380	}
381
382	func validDigest(value string) bool {
383		if !strings.HasPrefix(value, "sha256:") || len(value) != len("sha256:")+sha256.Size*2 {
384			return false
385		}
386		decoded, err := hex.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(value, "sha256:"))
387		return err == nil && len(decoded) == sha256.Size && value == strings.ToLower(value)
388	}
389
390	func validOID(value string) bool {
391		if len(value) != 40 && len(value) != 64 || value != strings.ToLower(value) {
392			return false
393		}
394		_, err := hex.DecodeString(value)
395		return err == nil
396	}
397
398	func validFileMode(value string) bool {
399		if len(value) != 4 {
400			return false
401		}
402		mode, err := strconv.ParseUint(value, 8, 12)
403		return err == nil && mode <= 0o777
404	}
405
406	func validateText(name, value string) error {
407		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) {
408			return fmt.Errorf("%s is required and must be trimmed", name)
409		}
410		for _, r := range value {
411			if unicode.IsControl(r) {
412				return fmt.Errorf("%s contains a control character", name)
413			}
414		}
415		return nil
416	}
417
418	func sortedPublic(files []PublicFile) []PublicFile {
419		result := append([]PublicFile(nil), files...)
420		sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool { return result[i].Path < result[j].Path })
421		return result
422	}

13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/safefile"
14	)
15
16	const maxWalkEntries = 200_000
17
18	var dependencyComponents = map[string]struct{}{
19		"node_modules": {}, ".venv": {}, "venv": {}, "vendor": {},
20		"__pycache__": {}, ".tox": {}, "target": {}, ".terraform": {},
21		"dist": {}, "build": {}, ".next": {},
22	}
23
24	// Expand resolves validated project and --file patterns locally into a sorted,
25	// duplicate-free list of exact slash paths. It never follows links or descends
26	// into Git metadata, nested repositories, submodules, or dependency trees.
27	func Expand(root string, patterns []Pattern, limits safefile.Limits) ([]string, error) {
28		if err := limits.Validate(); err != nil {
29			return nil, err
30		}
31		if len(patterns) == 0 {
32			return nil, errors.New("no local-file patterns were configured or passed with --file")
33		}
34		for _, pattern := range patterns {
35			if err := projectconfig.ValidateLocalFilePattern(pattern.Value); err != nil {
36				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s: %w", patternSource(pattern), err)
37			}
38			for _, component := range strings.Split(pattern.Value, "/") {
39				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
40					return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s enters dependency directory %q", patternSource(pattern), component)
41				}
42			}
43		}
44		rootInfo, err := os.Lstat(root)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, fmt.Errorf("inspect source checkout: %w", err)
47		}
48		if !rootInfo.IsDir() || rootInfo.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
49			return nil, errors.New("source checkout is not a held regular directory")
50		}
51
52		matches := map[string]struct{}{}
53		matchedPatterns := make([]bool, len(patterns))
54		visited := 0
55		err = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(filename string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
56			if walkErr != nil {
57				return walkErr
58			}
59			if filename == root {
60				return nil
61			}
62			visited++
63			if visited > maxWalkEntries {
64				return fmt.Errorf("source checkout exceeds %d entries while expanding local-file patterns", maxWalkEntries)
65			}
66			relative, err := filepath.Rel(root, filename)
67			if err != nil {
68				return err
69			}
70			slash := filepath.ToSlash(relative)
71			components := strings.Split(slash, "/")
72			base := strings.ToLower(components[len(components)-1])
73			if entry.IsDir() {
74				if base == ".git" {
75					return filepath.SkipDir
76				}
77				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[base]; blocked {
78					for _, pattern := range patterns {
79						if matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
80							return fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern enters dependency directory %q", slash)
81						}
82					}
83					return filepath.SkipDir
84				}
85				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(filename, ".git")); err == nil {
86					return filepath.SkipDir
87				} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
88					return fmt.Errorf("inspect nested repository boundary %s: %w", slash, err)
89				}
90			}
91			matched := false
92			for index, pattern := range patterns {
93				if !entry.IsDir() && matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
94					matchedPatterns[index] = true
95					matched = true
96				}
97			}
98			if matched {
99				matches[slash] = struct{}{}
100			}
101			if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 && entry.IsDir() {
102				return filepath.SkipDir
103			}
104			return nil
105		})
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, err
108		}
109		for index, matched := range matchedPatterns {
110			if !matched {
111				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s matched no source path", patternSource(patterns[index]))
112			}
113		}
114		paths := make([]string, 0, len(matches))
115		for path := range matches {
116			paths = append(paths, path)
117		}
118		sort.Strings(paths)
119		if len(paths) > limits.MaxFiles {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("patterns expanded to %d paths; maximum is %d", len(paths), limits.MaxFiles)
121		}
122		return paths, nil
123	}
124
125	func patternSource(pattern Pattern) string {
126		if strings.TrimSpace(pattern.Source) == "" {
127			return "explicit input"
128		}
129		return pattern.Source
130	}
131
132	func matchPattern(pattern, candidate string) bool {
133		patternParts := strings.Split(pattern, "/")
134		candidateParts := strings.Split(candidate, "/")
135		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
136		memo := map[key]bool{}
137		seen := map[key]bool{}
138		var match func(int, int) bool
139		match = func(patternIndex, candidateIndex int) bool {
140			state := key{patternIndex, candidateIndex}
141			if seen[state] {
142				return memo[state]
143			}
144			seen[state] = true
145			var result bool
146			switch {
147			case patternIndex == len(patternParts):
148				result = candidateIndex == len(candidateParts)
149			case patternParts[patternIndex] == "**":
150				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex) ||
151					candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && match(patternIndex, candidateIndex+1)
152			case candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && matchComponent(patternParts[patternIndex], candidateParts[candidateIndex]):
153				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex+1)
154			}
155			memo[state] = result
156			return result
157		}
158		return match(0, 0)
159	}
160
161	func matchComponent(pattern, candidate string) bool {
162		p, c := []rune(pattern), []rune(candidate)
163		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
164		memo := map[key]bool{}
165		seen := map[key]bool{}
166		var match func(int, int) bool
167		match = func(pi, ci int) bool {
168			state := key{pi, ci}
169			if seen[state] {
170				return memo[state]
171			}
172			seen[state] = true
173			var result bool
174			switch {
175			case pi == len(p):
176				result = ci == len(c)
177			case p[pi] == '*':
178				result = match(pi+1, ci) || ci < len(c) && match(pi, ci+1)
179			case ci < len(c) && (p[pi] == '?' || p[pi] == c[ci]):
180				result = match(pi+1, ci+1)
181			}
182			memo[state] = result
183			return result
184		}
185		return match(0, 0)
186	}
187
188	func hasDependencyComponent(path string) bool {
189		for _, component := range strings.Split(path, "/") {
190			if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
191				return true
192			}
193		}
194		return false
195	}

16	var (
17		ErrUnsafe     = errors.New("portable file path is unsafe")
18		ErrIneligible = errors.New("portable file is not untracked and ignored")
19		ErrDrift      = errors.New("portable file checkout state changed")
20	)
21
22	type observation struct {
23		exists bool
24		info   fs.FileInfo
25		data   []byte
26		digest string
27	}
28
29	func observePath(ctx context.Context, checkout, slashPath string, limits safefile.Limits, read bool) (observation, error) {
30		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableSlashPath(slashPath, limits.PathLimits()); err != nil {
31			return observation{}, fmt.Errorf("path %q: %w: %w", slashPath, err, ErrUnsafe)
32		}
33		if hasDependencyComponent(slashPath) {
34			return observation{}, fmt.Errorf("path %q enters a dependency directory: %w", slashPath, ErrUnsafe)
35		}
36		held, err := openHeldParent(checkout, slashPath, false)
37		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
38			return observation{exists: false}, nil
39		}
40		if err != nil {
41			return observation{}, fmt.Errorf("open path %q: %w: %w", slashPath, err, ErrUnsafe)
42		}
43		finish := func(result observation, operationErr error) (observation, error) {
44			closeErr := held.close()
45			if operationErr != nil {
46				return observation{}, errors.Join(operationErr, closeErr)
47			}
48			if closeErr != nil {
49				return observation{}, fmt.Errorf("verify held path %q: %w", slashPath, closeErr)
50			}
51			return result, nil
52		}
53		name := pathBase(slashPath)
54		info, err := held.parent.Lstat(name)
55		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
56			return finish(observation{exists: false}, nil)
57		}
58		if err != nil {
59			return finish(observation{}, fmt.Errorf("inspect path %q: %w", slashPath, err))
60		}
61		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
62			return finish(observation{}, fmt.Errorf("path %q is not a regular file: %w", slashPath, ErrUnsafe))
63		}
64		result := observation{exists: true, info: info}
65		if read {
66			data, stable, err := safefile.ReadStableRegular(ctx, held.parent, name, info, limits.MaxFileBytes)
67			if err != nil {
68				return finish(observation{}, fmt.Errorf("read path %q: %w", slashPath, err))
69			}
70			result.info, result.data, result.digest = stable, data, digestBytes(data)
71		}
72		return finish(result, nil)
73	}
74
75	func proveGitEligibility(ctx context.Context, checkout, slashPath string) error {
76		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableSlashPath(slashPath, safefile.DefaultLimits().PathLimits()); err != nil {
77			return fmt.Errorf("path %q: %w", slashPath, ErrUnsafe)
78		}
79		literal := ":(literal)" + slashPath
80		tracked, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "ls-files", "-z", "--", literal)
81		if err != nil {
82			return fmt.Errorf("inspect Git tracking for %q: %w", slashPath, err)
83		}
84		if tracked != "" {
85			return fmt.Errorf("path %q is tracked: %w", slashPath, ErrIneligible)
86		}
87		components := strings.Split(slashPath, "/")
88		for index := range components {
89			prefix := strings.Join(components[:index+1], "/")
90			staged, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z", "--", ":(literal)"+prefix)
91			if err != nil {
92				return fmt.Errorf("inspect Git mode for %q: %w", slashPath, err)
93			}
94			for _, record := range strings.Split(staged, "\x00") {
95				if strings.HasPrefix(record, "160000 ") {
96					return fmt.Errorf("path %q crosses a submodule: %w", slashPath, ErrUnsafe)
97				}
98			}
99		}
100		_, err = gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "check-ignore", "--no-index", "--quiet", "--", slashPath)
101		if err == nil {
102			return nil
103		}
104		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
105		if errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 {
106			return fmt.Errorf("path %q is not ignored on this host: %w", slashPath, ErrIneligible)
107		}
108		return fmt.Errorf("inspect Git ignore status for %q: %w", slashPath, err)
109	}
110

38	func PrepareSource(ctx context.Context, options SourceOptions) (*Source, Report, error) {
39		if err := options.Limits.Validate(); err != nil {
40			return nil, Report{}, err
41		}
42		if err := options.Binding.Validate(); err != nil {
43			return nil, Report{}, err
44		}
45		paths, err := Expand(options.Checkout, options.Patterns, options.Limits)
46		if err != nil {
47			return nil, Report{}, err
48		}
49		if err := pathx.ValidatePortablePathSet(paths, options.Limits.PathLimits()); err != nil {
50			return nil, Report{}, err
51		}
52		requestID := options.RequestID
53		if requestID == "" {
54			requestID = uuid.NewString()
55		}
56		request := PlanRequest{
57			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
58			RequestID: requestID, Binding: options.Binding, Limits: limitsToWire(options.Limits),
59			Replace: options.Replace,
60		}
61		report := Report{SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion}
62		blocked := false
63		for _, path := range paths {
64			public := PublicFile{Path: path, Mode: "0600", State: StateFailed}
65			observed, observeErr := observePath(ctx, options.Checkout, path, options.Limits, true)
66			if observeErr != nil {
67				public.State = stateForError(observeErr)
68				report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
69				blocked = true
70				continue
71			}
72			if !observed.exists {
73				public.State = StateMissing
74				report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
75				blocked = true
76				continue
77			}
78			public.Size = observed.info.Size()
79			if observed.info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 != 0 {
80				public.Mode = "0700"
81			}
82			if eligibilityErr := proveGitEligibility(ctx, options.Checkout, path); eligibilityErr != nil {
83				public.State = stateForError(eligibilityErr)
84				report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
85				blocked = true
86				continue
87			}
88			public.State = StateReady
89			report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
90			request.Files = append(request.Files, FileSpec{
91				Path: path, Size: observed.info.Size(), Mode: public.Mode, SHA256: observed.digest,
92			})
93		}
94		report.Files = sortedPublic(report.Files)
95		if blocked {
96			return nil, report, ErrPlanBlocked
97		}
98		sort.Slice(request.Files, func(i, j int) bool { return request.Files[i].Path < request.Files[j].Path })
99		request.ManifestDigest = manifestDigest(request)
100		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
101			return nil, report, err
102		}
103		return &Source{checkout: options.Checkout, request: request}, report, nil
104	}

106	// BuildEnvelope performs the source-side apply revalidation and includes bytes
107	// only for target actions that create or explicitly replace a file.
108	func (s *Source) BuildEnvelope(ctx context.Context, plan PlanResponse, retainForEvict bool) (ApplyEnvelope, error) {
109		if s == nil {
110			return ApplyEnvelope{}, errors.New("build local-files envelope from nil source")
111		}
112		if err := plan.Validate(s.request); err != nil {
113			return ApplyEnvelope{}, err
114		}
115		envelope := ApplyEnvelope{
116			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
117			Request: s.request, Plan: plan, RetainForEvict: retainForEvict,
118		}
119		for index, planned := range plan.Files {
120			if planned.Action == actionCurrent {
121				continue
122			}
123			if planned.Action != actionCreate && planned.Action != actionReplace {
124				return ApplyEnvelope{}, ErrPlanBlocked
125			}
126			spec := s.request.Files[index]
127			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, s.checkout, spec.Path); err != nil {
128				return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source path %q changed eligibility: %w", spec.Path, ErrDrift)
129			}
130			observed, err := observePath(ctx, s.checkout, spec.Path, s.request.SafeLimits(), true)
131			if err != nil || !observed.exists || observed.info.Size() != spec.Size || observed.digest != spec.SHA256 ||
132				(observed.info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 != 0) != spec.executable() {
133				return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source path %q changed after planning: %w", spec.Path, ErrDrift)
134			}
135			envelope.Payloads = append(envelope.Payloads, Payload{
136				Path: spec.Path, Content: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(observed.data),
137			})
138		}
139		if err := envelope.Validate(); err != nil {
140			return ApplyEnvelope{}, err
141		}
142		return envelope, nil
143	}

145	func (e ApplyEnvelope) Validate() error {
146		if e.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || e.ProtocolVersion != fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion {
147			return errors.New("unsupported local-files apply protocol")
148		}
149		if err := e.Request.Validate(); err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		if err := e.Plan.Validate(e.Request); err != nil {
153			return err
154		}
155		expected := map[string]FileSpec{}
156		for index, planned := range e.Plan.Files {
157			if planned.Action == actionCreate || planned.Action == actionReplace {
158				expected[e.Request.Files[index].Path] = e.Request.Files[index]
159			}
160		}
161		if len(e.Payloads) != len(expected) {
162			return errors.New("apply payload count does not match target actions")
163		}
164		seen := map[string]bool{}
165		var total int64
166		for index, payload := range e.Payloads {
167			if index > 0 && e.Payloads[index-1].Path >= payload.Path {
168				return errors.New("apply payload paths must be unique and sorted")
169			}
170			spec, ok := expected[payload.Path]
171			if !ok || seen[payload.Path] {
172				return fmt.Errorf("unexpected apply payload for %q", payload.Path)
173			}
174			seen[payload.Path] = true
175			decoded, err := base64.StdEncoding.Strict().DecodeString(payload.Content)
176			if err != nil || base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(decoded) != payload.Content {
177				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q is not canonical base64", payload.Path)
178			}
179			if int64(len(decoded)) != spec.Size || digestBytes(decoded) != spec.SHA256 {
180				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q does not match its manifest", payload.Path)
181			}
182			if int64(len(decoded)) > e.Request.SafeLimits().MaxFileBytes || int64(len(decoded)) > e.Request.SafeLimits().MaxTotalBytes-total {
183				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q exceeds negotiated limits", payload.Path)
184			}
185			total += int64(len(decoded))
186		}
187		return nil
188	}

190	func stateForError(err error) State {
191		switch {
192		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnsafe), errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrUnsafeType), errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrNotPortable), errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrPathCollision):
193			return StateBlockedUnsafe
194		case errors.Is(err, ErrIneligible):
195			return StateBlockedIneligible
196		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
197			return StateMissing
198		default:
199			return StateFailed
200		}
201	}
202
203	func limitsToWire(limits safefile.Limits) fleet.FileLimits {
204		return fleet.FileLimits{
205			MaxFiles: limits.MaxFiles, MaxFileBytes: limits.MaxFileBytes,
206			MaxTotalBytes: limits.MaxTotalBytes, MaxPathBytes: limits.MaxPathBytes,
207			MaxComponentBytes: limits.MaxComponentBytes, MaxPathDepth: limits.MaxPathDepth,
208		}
209	}
210
211	// NegotiateLimits takes the lower value for every policy field and validates
212	// both sides against this binary's compiled ceilings.
213	func NegotiateLimits(local safefile.Limits, remote fleet.FileLimits) (safefile.Limits, error) {
214		if err := local.Validate(); err != nil {
215			return safefile.Limits{}, err
216		}
217		remoteLimits := safefile.Limits{
218			MaxFiles: remote.MaxFiles, MaxFileBytes: remote.MaxFileBytes,
219			MaxTotalBytes: remote.MaxTotalBytes, MaxPathBytes: remote.MaxPathBytes,
220			MaxComponentBytes: remote.MaxComponentBytes, MaxPathDepth: remote.MaxPathDepth,
221		}
222		if err := remoteLimits.Validate(); err != nil {
223			return safefile.Limits{}, err
224		}
225		result := safefile.Limits{
226			MaxFiles:          min(local.MaxFiles, remoteLimits.MaxFiles),
227			MaxFileBytes:      min(local.MaxFileBytes, remoteLimits.MaxFileBytes),
228			MaxTotalBytes:     min(local.MaxTotalBytes, remoteLimits.MaxTotalBytes),
229			MaxPathBytes:      min(local.MaxPathBytes, remoteLimits.MaxPathBytes),
230			MaxComponentBytes: min(local.MaxComponentBytes, remoteLimits.MaxComponentBytes),
231			MaxPathDepth:      min(local.MaxPathDepth, remoteLimits.MaxPathDepth),
232		}
233		return result, result.Validate()
234	}

101	func (s *Service) resolveTarget(ctx context.Context, binding Binding) (targetCheckout, error) {
102		if err := binding.Validate(); err != nil {
103			return targetCheckout{}, err
104		}
105		options := repo.DefaultOptions()
106		if s.Config.Bootstrap.MaxDepth > 0 {
107			options.MaxDepth = s.Config.Bootstrap.MaxDepth
108		}
109		repositories, err := repo.Discover(ctx, s.Config.DiscoveryRoots(), options)
110		if err != nil {
111			return targetCheckout{}, err
112		}
113		type candidate struct {
114			path      string
115			commonDir string
116		}
117		var candidates []candidate
118		for _, repository := range repositories {
119			if repository.Bare || !repository.HasGit {
120				continue
121			}
122			gitRepo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, repository.Path)
123			if err != nil {
124				continue
125			}
126			matched, err := checkoutHasIdentity(ctx, gitRepo.Root, binding.RemoteIdentity)
127			if err != nil || !matched {
128				continue
129			}
130			candidates = append(candidates, candidate{path: gitRepo.Root, commonDir: gitRepo.GitCommonDir})
131		}
132		sort.Slice(candidates, func(i, j int) bool { return candidates[i].commonDir < candidates[j].commonDir })
133		switch len(candidates) {
134		case 0:
135			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetAbsent}
136		case 1:
137		default:
138			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetAmbiguous}
139		}
140		worktree, checkedOut, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, candidates[0].path, binding.Branch)
141		if err != nil {
142			return targetCheckout{}, err
143		}
144		if !checkedOut || worktree.Bare || worktree.Prunable {
145			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetFetchedOnly}
146		}
147		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}")
148		if err != nil {
149			return targetCheckout{}, err
150		}
151		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, worktree.Path)
152		if err != nil {
153			return targetCheckout{}, err
154		}
155		if status.Detached || status.Branch != binding.Branch || head != binding.HeadOID || worktree.Head != binding.HeadOID {
156			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetStale}
157		}
158		checkout := targetCheckout{
159			root: worktree.Path, commonDir: candidates[0].commonDir,
160			identity: binding.RemoteIdentity, branch: binding.Branch, head: head,
161		}
162		checkout.id = digestJSON(struct {
163			Domain    string `json:"domain"`
164			CommonDir string `json:"common_dir"`
165			Root      string `json:"root"`
166			Branch    string `json:"branch"`
167			Head      string `json:"head"`
168		}{"dev-local-files-checkout-v1", checkout.commonDir, checkout.root, checkout.branch, checkout.head})
169		return checkout, nil
170	}

172	func checkoutHasIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout, wanted string) (bool, error) {
173		names, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote")
174		if err != nil {
175			return false, err
176		}
177		for _, name := range strings.Fields(names) {
178			for _, kind := range []string{"--all"} {
179				urls, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote", "get-url", kind, name)
180				if err != nil {
181					continue
182				}
183				for _, raw := range strings.Split(urls, "\n") {
184					if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw) == wanted {
185						return true, nil
186					}
187				}
188			}
189			pushURLs, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote", "get-url", "--push", "--all", name)
190			if err == nil {
191				for _, raw := range strings.Split(pushURLs, "\n") {
192					if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw) == wanted {
193						return true, nil
194					}
195				}
196			}
197		}
198		return false, nil
199	}

201	func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, request PlanRequest) (PlanResponse, error) {
202		if s == nil {
203			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("nil local-files service")
204		}
205		if s.platform() == "windows" {
206			return PlanResponse{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetIncompatible}
207		}
208		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
209			return PlanResponse{}, err
210		}
211		id, err := s.machineID(ctx)
212		if err != nil {
213			return PlanResponse{}, err
214		}
215		if id != request.Binding.TargetMachine {
216			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("target machine identity changed after capability probe")
217		}
218		hostLimits := s.Config.LocalFiles.Limits()
219		if err := hostLimits.Validate(); err != nil {
220			return PlanResponse{}, err
221		}
222		negotiated, err := NegotiateLimits(hostLimits, request.Limits)
223		if err != nil || negotiated != request.SafeLimits() {
224			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("plan limits do not match target policy")
225		}
226		checkout, err := s.resolveTarget(ctx, request.Binding)
227		if err != nil {
228			return PlanResponse{}, err
229		}
230		response := PlanResponse{
231			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
232			RequestID: request.RequestID, ManifestDigest: request.ManifestDigest,
233			TargetMachine: id, TargetCheckout: checkout.id,
234		}
235		for _, spec := range request.Files {
236			planned := PlanFile{PublicFile: spec.public(StateFailed)}
237			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path); err != nil {
238				planned.State = stateForError(err)
239				response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
240				continue
241			}
242			observed, err := observePath(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path, request.SafeLimits(), true)
243			if err != nil {
244				planned.State = stateForError(err)
245				response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
246				continue
247			}
248			targetMode := ""
249			if observed.exists {
250				targetMode = fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm())
251			}
252			switch {
253			case !observed.exists:
254				planned.State, planned.Action = StateReady, actionCreate
255			case observed.digest == spec.SHA256 && targetMode == spec.Mode:
256				planned.State, planned.Action, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateCurrent, actionCurrent, observed.digest, targetMode
257			case request.Replace:
258				planned.State, planned.Action, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateReady, actionReplace, observed.digest, targetMode
259			default:
260				planned.State, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateBlockedConflict, observed.digest, targetMode
261			}
262			response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
263		}
264		response.PlanDigest = planDigest(request, response)
265		if err := response.Validate(request); err != nil {
266			return PlanResponse{}, err
267		}
268		return response, nil
269	}

53	type operationStore struct {
54		root      string
55		requestID string
56		operation string

59	func defaultStoreRoot() string {
60		return filepath.Join(devconfig.DataHome(), "dev", "local-files", "v1")
61	}
62
63	func newOperationStore(root, requestID string) (*operationStore, error) {
64		if root == "" {
65			root = defaultStoreRoot()
66		}
67		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(root)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve local-files store: %w", err)
70		}
71		if err := ensurePrivateDirectory(canonical); err != nil {
72			return nil, err
73		}
74		operation := filepath.Join(canonical, requestID)
75		return &operationStore{root: canonical, requestID: requestID, operation: operation}, nil
76	}
77
78	func openOperationStore(root, requestID string) (*operationStore, bool, error) {
79		if root == "" {
80			root = defaultStoreRoot()
81		}
82		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(root)
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, false, err
85		}
86		store := &operationStore{root: canonical, requestID: requestID, operation: filepath.Join(canonical, requestID)}
87		info, err := os.Lstat(store.operation)
88		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
89			return store, false, nil
90		}
91		if err != nil {
92			return nil, false, err
93		}
94		if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 != 0 {
95			return nil, false, errors.New("local-files operation store is not a private directory")
96		}
97		return store, true, nil
98	}
99
100	func (s *operationStore) ensureLayout() error {
101		for _, directory := range []string{s.operation, s.blobDir(), s.rollbackDir()} {
102			if err := ensurePrivateDirectory(directory); err != nil {
103				return err
104			}
105		}
106		return nil
107	}
108
109	func (s *operationStore) journalPath() string  { return filepath.Join(s.operation, journalFilename) }
110	func (s *operationStore) manifestPath() string { return filepath.Join(s.operation, "manifest.json") }
111	func (s *operationStore) blobDir() string      { return filepath.Join(s.operation, "blobs") }
112	func (s *operationStore) rollbackDir() string  { return filepath.Join(s.operation, "rollback") }
113	func (s *operationStore) blobPath(index int) string {
114		return filepath.Join(s.blobDir(), fmt.Sprintf("%03d", index))
115	}

117		return filepath.Join(s.rollbackDir(), fmt.Sprintf("%03d", index))
118	}

120	func (s *operationStore) loadJournal() (journal, error) {
121		data, err := readPrivateFile(s.journalPath(), 2<<20)
122		if err != nil {
123			return journal{}, err
124		}
125		var value journal
126		if err := fleet.UnmarshalStrict(data, 2<<20, &value); err != nil {
127			return journal{}, fmt.Errorf("decode local-files journal: %w", err)
128		}
129		if err := validateJournal(value); err != nil {
130			return journal{}, err
131		}
132		return value, nil
133	}
134
135	func validateJournal(value journal) error {
136		if value.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || value.RequestID == "" || !validDigest(value.PlanDigest) || !validDigest(value.ManifestDigest) {
137			return errors.New("invalid local-files journal binding")
138		}
139		switch value.Phase {
140		case phaseStaged, phaseApplying, phaseCompleted, phaseRolledBack, phaseReconcile:
141		default:
142			return errors.New("invalid local-files journal phase")
143		}
144		for index, file := range value.Files {
145			if index > 0 && value.Files[index-1].Path >= file.Path {
146				return errors.New("local-files journal paths are not sorted")
147			}
148			switch file.Action {
149			case actionCurrent, actionCreate, actionReplace:
150			default:
151				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid action")
152			}
153			if !file.State.validResult() {
154				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid result state")
155			}
156			if file.Size < 0 || file.Mode != "0600" && file.Mode != "0700" {
157				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid public metadata")
158			}
159			if file.Action == actionReplace && (!validDigest(file.OldSHA256) || !validFileMode(file.OldMode)) {
160				return errors.New("local-files replacement journal lacks rollback binding")
161			}
162		}
163		if !sort.StringsAreSorted(value.CreatedDirs) {
164			return errors.New("local-files journal directories are not sorted")
165		}
166		return nil
167	}
168
169	func (s *operationStore) writeJournal(value journal) error {
170		if err := validateJournal(value); err != nil {
171			return err
172		}
173		return writePrivateJSON(s.journalPath(), value)
174	}
175
176	func (s *operationStore) writeManifest(envelope ApplyEnvelope) error {
177		manifest := struct {
178			SchemaVersion  int        `json:"schema_version"`
179			RequestID      string     `json:"request_id"`
180			Binding        Binding    `json:"binding"`
181			ManifestDigest string     `json:"manifest_digest"`
182			PlanDigest     string     `json:"plan_digest"`
183			Files          []FileSpec `json:"files"`
184		}{SchemaVersion, envelope.Request.RequestID, envelope.Request.Binding,
185			envelope.Request.ManifestDigest, envelope.Plan.PlanDigest, envelope.Request.Files}
186		return writePrivateJSON(s.manifestPath(), manifest)
187	}
188
189	func (s *operationStore) writeBlob(filename string, content []byte, executable bool) error {
190		if existing, err := readPrivateFile(filename, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes); err == nil {
191			if digestBytes(existing) != digestBytes(content) {
192				return errors.New("existing local-files blob does not match operation")
193			}
194			return nil
195		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
196			return err
197		}
198		parentPath := filepath.Dir(filename)
199		root, rootInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
200		if err != nil {
201			return err
202		}
203		defer root.Close()
204		name := filepath.Base(filename)
205		if _, err := safefile.CreatePrivateNoClobber(context.Background(), root, name, content, executable); err != nil {
206			return err
207		}
208		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, rootInfo); err != nil {
209			return err
210		}
211		readback, err := readPrivateFile(filename, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
212		if err != nil || digestBytes(readback) != digestBytes(content) {
213			return errors.New("local-files blob failed post-write verification")
214		}
215		return nil
216	}
217
218	func (s *operationStore) readBlob(index int, rollback bool, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
219		path := s.blobPath(index)
220		if rollback {
221			path = s.rollbackPath(index)
222		}
223		return readPrivateFile(path, maxBytes)
224	}
225
226	func (s *operationStore) cleanupPayloads(retain bool) error {
227		var result error
228		if !retain {
229			result = errors.Join(result, os.RemoveAll(s.blobDir()), removeIfPresent(s.manifestPath()))
230		}
231		result = errors.Join(result, os.RemoveAll(s.rollbackDir()))
232		return result
233	}
234
235	func removeIfPresent(path string) error {
236		err := os.Remove(path)
237		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
238			return nil
239		}
240		return err
241	}
242
243	func ensurePrivateDirectory(path string) error {
244		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o700); err != nil {
245			return err
246		}
247		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
248		if err != nil {
249			return err
250		}
251		if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
252			return errors.New("local-files state path is not a directory")
253		}
254		if err := os.Chmod(path, 0o700); err != nil {
255			return err
256		}
257		info, err = os.Lstat(path)
258		if err != nil || info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 != 0 {
259			return errors.New("local-files state directory is not owner-private")
260		}
261		return nil
262	}
263
264	func writePrivateJSON(path string, value any) error {
265		parentPath := filepath.Dir(path)
266		if err := ensurePrivateDirectory(parentPath); err != nil {
267			return err
268		}
269		data, err := json.Marshal(value)
270		if err != nil {
271			return err
272		}
273		data = append(data, '\n')
274		root, rootInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
275		if err != nil {
276			return err
277		}
278		defer root.Close()
279		name := filepath.Base(path)
280		current, statErr := root.Lstat(name)
281		switch {
282		case errors.Is(statErr, fs.ErrNotExist):
283			_, err = safefile.CreatePrivateNoClobber(context.Background(), root, name, data, false)
284		case statErr != nil:
285			return statErr
286		case !current.Mode().IsRegular() || current.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || current.Mode().Perm()&0o077 != 0:
287			return errors.New("local-files state file is not a private regular file")
288		default:
289			_, err = safefile.AtomicReplacePrivate(context.Background(), root, name, current, data, false)
290		}
291		if err != nil {
292			return err
293		}
294		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, rootInfo); err != nil {
295			return err
296		}
297		readback, err := readPrivateFile(path, 2<<20)
298		if err != nil || string(readback) != string(data) {
299			return errors.New("local-files state file failed post-write verification")
300		}
301		return nil
302	}
303
304	func readPrivateFile(path string, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
305		parentPath := filepath.Dir(path)
306		root, rootInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
307		if err != nil {
308			return nil, err
309		}
310		defer root.Close()
311		name := filepath.Base(path)
312		info, err := root.Lstat(name)
313		if err != nil {
314			return nil, err
315		}
316		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 != 0 {
317			return nil, errors.New("local-files state file is not a private regular file")
318		}
319		data, _, err := safefile.ReadStableRegular(context.Background(), root, name, info, maxBytes)
320		if err != nil {
321			return nil, err
322		}
323		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, rootInfo); err != nil {
324			return nil, err
325		}
326		return data, nil
327	}

1	package localfiles

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6
7		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/fleet"
8	)
9
10	var (
11		ErrNoRemoteDev     = errors.New("target does not provide a compatible dev protocol")
12		ErrUnreachable     = errors.New("target host is unreachable")
13		ErrRemoteTimeout   = errors.New("target protocol timed out")
14		ErrMachinePin      = errors.New("target machine ID does not match the configured host pin")
15		ErrMachineUnpinned = errors.New("mutating local-file apply requires host.machine_id")
16	)
17
18	type Runner interface {
19		RunWithOptions(context.Context, fleet.Host, []string, []byte, fleet.RunOptions) fleet.Result
20	}
21
22	type Client struct{ Runner Runner }
23
24	func (c Client) run(ctx context.Context, host fleet.Host, args []string, stdin []byte, maxResponse int64) ([]byte, error) {
25		if c.Runner == nil {
26			return nil, errors.New("local-files client has no fleet transport")
27		}
28		// Capability and plan are read-only. Apply is permanently bound to its
29		// request ID and plan digest by the target journal, so an authentication-only
30		// retry cannot duplicate an unbound mutation.
31		result := c.Runner.RunWithOptions(ctx, host, args, stdin, fleet.RunOptions{Retry: fleet.RetryAuthentication})
32		if int64(len(result.Stdout)) > maxResponse {
33			return nil, errors.New("target protocol response exceeded its bound")
34		}
35		if result.ExitCode == 0 && result.CaptureError == "" {
36			return result.Stdout, nil
37		}
38		switch {
39		case result.TimedOut || result.ExitCode == 124:
40			return nil, ErrRemoteTimeout
41		case result.ExitCode == 127:
42			return nil, ErrNoRemoteDev
43		case result.ExitCode == 255:
44			return nil, ErrUnreachable
45		default:
46			return nil, ErrNoRemoteDev
47		}
48	}
49
50	func (c Client) Probe(ctx context.Context, host fleet.Host) (fleet.CapabilityResponse, error) {
51		request := fleet.LocalFilesCapabilityRequest()
52		body, err := fleet.MarshalBounded(request, fleet.MaxCapabilityBytes)
53		if err != nil {
54			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, err
55		}
56		responseBody, err := c.run(ctx, host, []string{"fleet", "_capability"}, body, fleet.MaxCapabilityBytes)
57		if err != nil {
58			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, err
59		}
60		var response fleet.CapabilityResponse
61		if err := fleet.UnmarshalStrict(responseBody, fleet.MaxCapabilityBytes, &response); err != nil {
62			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
63		}
64		if err := response.Validate(request); err != nil {
65			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
66		}
67		if host.MachineID != "" && host.MachineID != response.MachineID {
68			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, ErrMachinePin
69		}
70		if !response.Supported {
71			return fleet.CapabilityResponse{}, errors.New("target does not support local-file payloads")
72		}
73		return response, nil
74	}
75
76	func (c Client) Plan(ctx context.Context, host fleet.Host, capability fleet.CapabilityResponse, request PlanRequest) (PlanResponse, error) {
77		if capability.MachineID != request.Binding.TargetMachine {
78			return PlanResponse{}, ErrMachinePin
79		}
80		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
81			return PlanResponse{}, err
82		}
83		body, err := fleet.MarshalBounded(request, MaxPlanEnvelopeBytes)
84		if err != nil {
85			return PlanResponse{}, err
86		}
87		responseBody, err := c.run(ctx, host, []string{"fleet", "_files-plan"}, body, MaxPlanEnvelopeBytes)
88		if err != nil {
89			return PlanResponse{}, err
90		}
91		var response PlanResponse
92		if err := fleet.UnmarshalStrict(responseBody, MaxPlanEnvelopeBytes, &response); err != nil {
93			return PlanResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
94		}
95		if err := response.Validate(request); err != nil {
96			return PlanResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
97		}
98		return response, nil
99	}
100
101	func (c Client) Apply(ctx context.Context, host fleet.Host, capability fleet.CapabilityResponse, envelope ApplyEnvelope) (ApplyResponse, error) {
102		if host.MachineID == "" {
103			return ApplyResponse{}, ErrMachineUnpinned
104		}
105		if host.MachineID != capability.MachineID || envelope.Request.Binding.TargetMachine != capability.MachineID {
106			return ApplyResponse{}, ErrMachinePin
107		}
108		if err := envelope.Validate(); err != nil {
109			return ApplyResponse{}, err
110		}
111		body, err := fleet.MarshalBounded(envelope, MaxApplyEnvelopeBytes)
112		if err != nil {
113			return ApplyResponse{}, err
114		}
115		responseBody, err := c.run(ctx, host, []string{"fleet", "_files-apply"}, body, MaxApplyResponseBytes)
116		if err != nil {
117			return ApplyResponse{}, err
118		}
119		var response ApplyResponse
120		if err := fleet.UnmarshalStrict(responseBody, MaxApplyResponseBytes, &response); err != nil {
121			return ApplyResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
122		}
123		if err := response.Validate(envelope.Request, envelope.Plan); err != nil {
124			return ApplyResponse{}, ErrNoRemoteDev
125		}
126		return response, nil
127	}

1	package projectconfig

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6		"unicode"

9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/safefile"
11	)
12
13	var localFileDependencyComponents = map[string]bool{
14		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "vendor": true,
15		"__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "target": true, ".terraform": true,
16		"dist": true, "build": true, ".next": true,
17	}
18
19	// ValidateLocalFilePattern validates the deliberately small cross-platform
20	// grammar accepted by [local_files]. Literal path components use portable slash
21	// paths; '*' and '?' match within one component and a component equal to '**'
22	// matches zero or more components. Character classes, escaping, volumes, and
23	// platform-specific separators are intentionally unsupported.
24	func ValidateLocalFilePattern(value string) error {
25		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) {
26			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is required and must be trimmed")
27		}
28		if !utf8.ValidString(value) {
29			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is not valid UTF-8")
30		}
31		if len(value) > safefile.CompiledMaxPathBytes {
32			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is %d bytes; maximum is %d", len(value), safefile.CompiledMaxPathBytes)
33		}
34		if strings.ContainsRune(value, '\\') {
35			return fmt.Errorf("pattern must use '/' separators")
36		}
37		if strings.HasPrefix(value, "/") || strings.HasSuffix(value, "/") || strings.Contains(value, "//") {
38			return fmt.Errorf("pattern must be a clean repository-relative slash path")
39		}
40		if strings.ContainsAny(value, "[]{}") {
41			return fmt.Errorf("pattern supports only '*', '?' and whole-component '**' wildcards")
42		}
43		components := strings.Split(value, "/")
44		if len(components) > safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth {
45			return fmt.Errorf("pattern has %d components; maximum is %d", len(components), safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth)
46		}
47		for _, component := range components {
48			if localFileDependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)] {
49				return fmt.Errorf("pattern enters dependency directory %q", component)
50			}
51			if component == "**" {
52				continue
53			}
54			if strings.Contains(component, "**") {
55				return fmt.Errorf("'**' must occupy a complete path component")
56			}
57			placeholder := strings.NewReplacer("*", "x", "?", "x").Replace(component)
58			if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(placeholder, safefile.CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
59				return fmt.Errorf("component %q: %w", component, err)
60			}
61			for _, r := range component {
62				if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
63					return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a control character", component)
64				}
65			}
66		}
67		return nil
68	}
69

17		// WebURLSourceAzureRemote is a remote accepted by Azure's strict URL mapper.

22	)
23
24	// WebURLConfidence describes why a derived link is safe to expose.

26

29		WebURLConfidenceStrict       WebURLConfidence = "strict"
30		WebURLConfidenceConservative WebURLConfidence = "conservative"
31	)

33	// WebURL is a plain, display-safe HTTPS repository URL with derivation
34	// metadata. URL never contains userinfo, query, or fragment components.
35	type WebURL struct {
36		URL        string           `json:"url"`
37		Provider   Kind             `json:"provider"`
38		Source     WebURLSource     `json:"source"`
39		Confidence WebURLConfidence `json:"confidence"`
40	}
