8	# Commands and configuration
9
10	Use the authored map for intent and the embedded generated reference for exact flags. The generated block comes from the binary's Cobra command tree and is checked by `dev skill sync --check`.
11
12	## Command map
13
14	| Goal | Commands |
15	|---|---|
16	| task lifecycle | `start`, `park`, `resume`, `done`, `retire`, `sweep`, `ls`, `status` |
17	| agent artifacts | `prepare`, `artifact finalize`, `artifact list`, `artifact discard` |
18	| guarded Git transactions | `git uncommit`, `git recommit`, `git pull-rebase`, `git amend-all`, `git setup` |
19	| linked worktrees | `wt list`, `wt create`, `wt open`, `wt rm`, `wt plan`, `wt provision` |
20	| repositories/remotes | `repo list`, `repo context`, `repo new`/`repo create`, `repo clone`, `repo setup`, `repo open`, `repo sync`, `repo remote`, `repo mark` |
21	| repository quick notes | `note add`, `note list`, `note show`, `note search`, `note edit`, `note delete`, `note path`, `note reindex` |
22	| machine inventory | `bootstrap`, `adopt`, `doctor` |
23	| experiments | `try`, `tries …`, `graduate` |
24	| terminal UI | `tui`, `tui tools` |
25	| configuration/shell | `config init/show/path/edit/trust`, `config scaffolds init/show/path/edit`, `shell-init`, completion |
26	| remote fleet | `fleet list`, `fleet status`, `fleet sync`, `fleet open`, `fleet config …` |
27	| agent skills | `skill list`, `skill add`, `skill update`, `skill install`, `skill sync`, `skill print` |
28	| generated policy/assets | `gitignore`, `skill install/sync` |
29	| activity/data | `summary`, `journal`, `stats …`, `cache …` |
30	| help | `help [topic]` |
31
32	Run `dev <command> --help` for the installed binary; this site describes the repository version identified in its freshness metadata.
33
34	## High-value structured interfaces
35
36	```bash
37	dev ls --json
38	dev repo list --json
39	dev repo context [repo]
40	dev repo remote --json
41	dev repo new NAME --json
42	dev repo clone <ref> --json
43	dev repo setup [repo-or-path] --preset PRESET --json
44	dev note list [repo] --json
45	dev note search <query> --json
46	dev note show <note-id> --json
47	dev bootstrap --json
48	```
49
50	Prefer JSON or the agent-ready Markdown context over parsing human tables. Tables are optimized for terminals and may change columns/width without changing the structured contract.
51
52	Every `dev repo list --json` row includes `notes.count`. When a latest note exists, the same object adds `notes.latest_id`, `notes.latest_preview`, and `notes.latest_updated`; these optional fields are omitted when the count is zero. `dev note list --json` and `dev note search --json` return arrays of complete note records, while `dev note show --json` returns one complete record.
53
54	## Repository bootstrap
55
56	Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
57	`new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
58	reference:
59
60	| Command | Behavior |
61	|---|---|
62	| `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
63	| `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
64	| `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
65	| `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
66
67	A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
68	new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
69	meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”
70
71	Across these commands, controls include `--preset`, `--path`, typed input values through
72	`--set`, item selection through `--enable`/`--disable`, `--check-in
73	<auto|commit|stage|none>`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--handoff
74	<stay|cd|open|start>`. `repo new` additionally accepts `--template`,
75	`--template-ref`, and `--template-subdir`. JSON mode is non-interactive and
76	never changes directory or opens a runtime. Dry-run performs no target
77	repository mutation; clone setup can only be planned in detail after the clone
78	exists. Use the generated reference below for each command's exact flag
79	availability.
80
81	The wizard renders the selected scaffold and workflow summary before target
82	repository mutation. The built-in presets are:
83
84	- `minimal`: `main`, README, and an initial commit; this preserves existing
85	  scripted `repo new NAME` behavior.
86	- `agent-ready`: extends `minimal` with common ignores, starter `AGENTS.md`,
87	  and project-scoped `.claude/settings.json` plus `.claude/plans/`.
88	  `agent-history-hygiene` and `project-knowledge-harness` are offered but are
89	  not selected silently. When selected, dev installs them and runs reviewed
90	  built-in initializers for their project surfaces before the initial commit;
91	  downloaded skill scripts are not executed for these built-ins. Matching
92	  skills with the same source and identical agent targets share one installer
93	  invocation, while their setup phases still run per skill. The history
94	  initializer creates `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.gitleaks.toml`, then
95	  ensures `.specstory/.gitignore` contains rules for SpecStory's `.project.json`
96	  and `statistics.json`, never the trackable `.specstory/history/` directory.
97	  Existing custom ignore content and its mode are preserved; only missing
98	  managed rules are appended.
99
100	After preset selection, the new-repository wizard asks “Customize preset and
101	template options?” with a default of no. The ordinary `agent-ready` flow uses
102	its reviewed template, file, input, and skill defaults without presenting each
103	question. Answer yes—or provide customization flags—to expand those controls.
104
105	Presets can add typed `string`, `bool`, and `choice` inputs, text templates,
106	hooks, and project skills. Hooks run in fixed `before_commit`, `after_commit`,
107	and `after_remote` phases. The safe hook form is an argv `command`; a shell
108	`run` is explicit, and only `interactive = true` loads an interactive shell.
109	Required failures stop later commit/remote steps; optional failures are
110	reported as warnings. Produced local files are retained for recovery. Native
111	initializers and preset files are repeat-safe; custom hooks and skill setup are
112	responsible for their own idempotency.
113
114	### Snapshot templates
115
116	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` seeds a fresh repository from a content
117	snapshot. `SOURCE` may be a local directory/repository, Git URL, or owner/name.
118	For a Git source, `--template-ref` selects an arbitrary branch, tag, or commit;
119	`--template-subdir` selects a clean relative directory as the new repository
120	root. Without a ref, a local Git working tree includes existing tracked files
121	plus untracked files that are not ignored by Git; ignored build/cache content
122	is omitted. A non-Git directory snapshots its complete current tree.
123
124	The new repository does not inherit source history or remotes. Dev excludes
125	every source `.git` entry, rejects traversal, symlinks and special files,
126	preserves regular-file modes, and validates the complete snapshot before
127	creating the destination. Snapshot files take precedence when the selected
128	scaffold would write the same path; the scaffold still fills missing files and
129	runs the selected initializers. Source and destination traversal is performed
130	relative to held `os.Root` handles, and file bytes come from the already-open
131	validated source handle rather than a second mutable pathname lookup.
132
133	Confirmation and human dry-run output show a bounded preview of selected paths
134	and warn when a local source is a live working-tree/directory snapshot rather
135	than a commit. Credential-bearing URL userinfo is removed from summaries,
136	structured output, and clone/template errors.
137
138	Presets expose the same operation through scalar `template`, `template_ref`,
139	and `template_subdir` fields. They inherit normally and explicit CLI flags win,
140	which supports one starter catalog repository plus a child preset for each
141	subfolder.
142
143	### Check-in policy
144
145	The interactive wizard offers `commit`, `stage`, and `none`; scripts may also
146	pass `auto`. The behavior is:
147
148	| Value | Behavior |
149	|---|---|
150	| `commit` | `git add -A`, commit with `--message`/the preset message, then run `after_commit` setup |
151	| `stage` | run `before_commit` setup, then `git add -A`; leave the checkout staged and do not run `after_commit` |
152	| `none` | leave generated changes unstaged and uncommitted |
153	| `auto` | for `repo new`, use `initial_check_in` and compatible `initial_commit`; clone/setup otherwise perform no automatic check-in |
154
155	In `stage` mode, dev best-effort writes `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in the exact
156	worktree Git directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 reads this
157	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)
158	as the initial message for lowercase `c`; uppercase `C` and Git itself do not use this integration. An
159	existing different draft is preserved and reported rather than overwritten.
160	This is an implementation-detail adapter, not `commit.template`.
161
162	Staging is the durable outcome: if the optional lazygit draft cannot be
163	written, dev emits a warning and retains the staged index instead of rolling it
164	back.
165
166	Staged setup cannot create an upstream, and `handoff=start` requires committed
167	setup because a new worktree would omit the staged files. `stay`, `cd`, and
168	`open` remain available for review. `repo setup --commit` is retained as a
169	compatibility alias for `--check-in=commit`; `--message` applies to both commit
170	and stage. Structured results retain `committed` and add `staged`,
171	`staged_paths`, `commit_message`, `commit_draft_provider`, and a content-free
172	`template` summary where applicable.
173
174	### Upstream publishing
175
176	Before offering publication, dev probes `gh` and `glab` without changing
177	state. A provider is offered only when its CLI is installed and authenticated;
178	otherwise the wizard gives the relevant installation or login guidance.
179	Local-only is the default, and a newly published repository defaults private.
180
181	Publishing uses the local repository name and configured description, then asks
182	for the provider namespace/owner, visibility, and whether to push the
183	initial/current branch. Dev creates the empty GitHub or GitLab repository after
184	required local setup and commit steps succeed, then adds/verifies `origin` and
185	optionally pushes with upstream tracking. A
186	provider, name-conflict, or push failure never deletes the local checkout or
187	an upstream that was already created.
188
189	Publishing from `repo setup` requires `--check-in=commit` (or the compatible
190	`--commit` flag), so the newly created upstream cannot omit the generated setup
191	changes. `--check-in=stage` is incompatible with any new upstream; for a new
192	repository, `none` may create an intentionally empty upstream only with
193	`--push=false`.
194
195	### Handoff
196
197	`stay` prints the result only. `cd` uses the trusted `shell-init` wrapper to
198	change the parent shell. `open` opens the configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime
199	and falls back to `cd` when runtime is `none`. `start` continues into the
200	existing task wizard with the repository fixed, and is unavailable when setup
201	leaves uncommitted files that a new worktree would omit. Neither repository
202	bootstrap nor `dev start` launches a coding agent.
203
204	All shared TTY text fields in the repository, task-start, and finish wizards
205	use an inline editor: Left/Right, Home/End, Delete/Backspace, insertion at the
206	cursor, and Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation work as terminal actions rather than being
207	inserted as raw escape bytes. Buffered and piped non-TTY input retains its
208	line-oriented behavior.
209
210	## `dev done` finish flags
211
212	`dev done` for branch/worktree tasks integrates through exactly one of `--ff` (rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it) or `--pr` (push and open a pull/merge request). Omitting both opens the interactive finish wizard on a TTY — see [Change-stream workflow](../guides/change-stream-workflow.md) for the prompts.
213
214	A dirty checkout is handled by `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` (default `auto`):
215
216	| Value | Behavior |
217	|---|---|
218	| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
219	| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
220	| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
221	| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |
222
223	`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive confirmation step. `--keep-worktree` keeps the worktree after `--ff` integration (default: removed once merged), `--push` also pushes the resulting branch, and `--delete-branch` deletes the branch once its commits are contained in the base — never a branch with unpushed commits.
224
225	## Configuration
226
227	```bash
228	dev config init
229	dev config show
230	dev config path
231	dev config scaffolds init
232	dev config scaffolds show
233	dev config scaffolds path
234	dev config scaffolds edit
235	```
236
237	`config init` detects local roots and writes explicit defaults. A missing config file is allowed; the built-in defaults keep core Git behavior usable, but generated config is recommended because it makes machine policy reviewable.
238
239	Key sections:
240
241	| Section | Controls |
242	|---|---|
243	| `[paths]` | scan roots, project/tries/worktree roots, worktree template, state path |
244	| `[runtime]` | `auto`, Herdr, tmux, Zellij, or none plus metadata settings |
245	| `[worktree]` | ignored includes, linked dirs, setup commands, strategies, timeout |
246	| `[forge]` / `[[forge.azure_devops]]` | complete remote inventory cache TTL and opt-in Azure organization/project targets |
247	| `[bootstrap]` | recursion, symlink handling, index/layout policy |
248	| `[tui]` / `[[tui.tools]]` | columns, sorting, and external-tool bindings |
249	| `[stats]` | sampler and optional WakaTime import |
250	| `[update]` | `check` (default `true`) — allow the once-a-day "newer release available" hint and its background cache refresh; `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` overrides it |
251
252	Repository quick-note Markdown is durable under configured `paths.state_dir/notes`, which defaults to `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`. The full-text index at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` is disposable and rebuilds from those files; changing `paths.state_dir` does not move the cache.
253
254	### Scaffold presets
255
256	Global repository recipes live at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml` (or
257	the root `--scaffolds` override). Every authored file declares `version = 1`.
258	A compact preset looks like:
259
260	```toml
261	version = 1
262	default_preset = "team"
263	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
264
265	[presets.team]
266	extends = "agent-ready"
267	handoff = "cd"
268	initial_check_in = "stage"
269	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
270	template_ref = "v2"
271	template_subdir = "services/go"
272
273	[[presets.team.inputs]]
274	id = "deployment"
275	type = "choice"
276	choices = ["none", "docker"]
277	default = "none"
278
279	[[presets.team.files]]
280	id = "service-readme"
281	source = "service/README.md" # templates/service/README.md beside this file
282	destination = "docs/service.md"
283
284	[[presets.team.hooks]]
285	id = "verify"
286	phase = "before_commit"
287	command = ["make", "test"]
288	required = true
289
290	[[presets.team.skills]]
291	id = "knowledge"
292	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
293	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
294	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
295	default = true
296
297	[presets.team.skills.setup]
298	phase = "before_commit"
299	interpreter = "bash"
300	script = "scripts/init.sh"
301	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
302	required = true
303	```
304
305	Skill setup normally names a project-local script inside the installed skill.
306	The shipped recommendations instead use `builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` or
307	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`; these fixed reviewed initializers do
308	not execute downloaded skill code.
309
310	A preset may extend one parent. Scalars override; simple lists replace; files,
311	hooks, and skills merge by `id`, and an inherited item can be disabled with
312	`enabled = false`. A `[[presets.*.files]]` rendering source must remain in the
313	`templates/` tree next to its config source; that file-level mechanism is
314	separate from the repository snapshot `template` scalar above. Destinations
315	must remain inside the repository, and a skill setup script must remain inside
316	the installed skill directory. `initial_check_in` accepts `commit`, `stage`, or
317	`none`; the legacy `initial_commit` boolean remains readable, but a preset must
318	not set both.
319
320	### Safe project overlays
321
322	A repository may commit these fixed files:
323
324	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning and repository
325	  setup wizard defaults.
326	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`: project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
327	  setup using the same versioned schema.
328
329	```toml
330	# .dev-cli/config.toml
331	version = 1
332
333	[worktree]
334	include = [".env.example"]
335	strategy = "reinstall"
336
337	[repo.setup]
338	preset = "team"
339	handoff = "cd"
340	check_in = "stage"
341	```
342
343	Effective precedence, lowest to highest, is built-ins, global config/scaffolds,
344	legacy `.dev.toml`, the target repository's `.dev-cli/*`, then explicit CLI or
345	wizard choices. `.dev.toml` remains readable for compatibility; new project
346	configuration should use `.dev-cli/config.toml`. Global `default_preset` and the
347	project `[repo.setup]` preset, handoff, and check-in fields seed interactive
348	wizard choices; they do not change scripted defaults, which are controlled by
349	the corresponding flags. The legacy `commit` boolean remains readable, but may
350	not be combined with `check_in` in the same layer.
351
352	Project files cannot override host paths, state location, runtime backend,
353	forge inventory or credentials, stats, update, bootstrap, or TUI policy. They
354	also cannot silently publish a repository. Before a post-create command from
355	`.dev-cli/config.toml`, or a hook or skill setup from project
356	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, executes, dev asks to trust the canonical repository
357	plus an execution-content hash. Changed executable content requires new
358	consent; non-interactive use without a matching trust record fails closed.
359	Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Keep credentials and
360	host-specific paths in user config or ignored environment files, never in a
361	committed project overlay.
362
363	Project-authored skill setup must use a local source so its bytes can be bound
364	to the trust hash. Remote project skills may still be installed, but cannot
365	declare executable setup; global presets remain host-owned policy.
366
367	## Colored output
368
369	Every human-readable surface applies semantic ANSI color through a small set of roles: `title`/`header`/`prompt` (bold cyan), `label`/`dim` (dim), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `danger` (bold red), `review` (magenta, for a PR/review handoff), and `strong`/`code` for Markdown. Values that carry their own meaning are colored by that meaning rather than by a fixed role:
370
371	| Value | Green | Yellow | Red |
372	|---|---|---|---|
373	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`, `ahead`, `behind`, `no checkout` | `conflict`, `error` |
374	| Task state | `hot`, `done` | `warm`, `cold`, `parked` | — |
375	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`, `no-dev` | `unreachable`, `timeout`, `incompatible` |
376	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`, `failed` |
377	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`, `finalizing` | `failed` |
378
379	`dev journal` and `dev summary` emit Markdown, so their headings and fenced code blocks are styled the same way `dev help <topic>` styles a quick-reference page. In command help, only the names you can type — command names and flag specs — are colored; descriptions stay plain, and the column alignment cobra computes is unaffected because a terminal gives an escape sequence no width.
380
381	Control it with the global `--color <auto|always|never>` flag (default `auto`). `auto` disables color when output is not attached to a terminal, when `NO_COLOR` is set to any non-empty value, or when `TERM=dumb`. The setting reaches the interactive dashboard as well, so `dev --color never` renders it without color. `--json` output is never colored regardless of mode. There is no config-file field for color — `--color` and the environment are the only controls, so piping `dev` never requires `--color never` to stay clean.
382
383	## Shell integration
384
385	```bash
386	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"
387	dev shell-init fish | source
388	```
389
390	The trusted `shell-init` output defines a wrapper because a child process cannot change its parent's working directory. For navigation commands, that wrapper reads a NUL-terminated path from a private child-only file descriptor and calls `builtin cd`; it does not evaluate ordinary `dev` command output as shell code.

60	Repository setup 仍與 acquisition 分開。Acquisition 部分，`new`/`create` 會區分

110	### Snapshot templates
111
112	`dev repo new NAME --template SOURCE` 會用 content snapshot 建立全新 repository。
113	`SOURCE` 可為 local directory/repository、Git URL 或 owner/name。Git source 可用
114	`--template-ref` 指定任意 branch、tag 或 commit；`--template-subdir` 則指定作為新
115	repository root 的乾淨 relative directory。未指定 ref 時，local Git working tree 會
116	包含現存 tracked files，以及未被 Git ignore 的 untracked files；ignored build/cache
117	content 會省略。Non-Git directory 則 snapshot 完整 current tree。
118
119	新 repository 不會繼承 source history 或 remotes。Dev 會排除每個 source `.git`

121	destination 前驗證完整 snapshot。若 snapshot 與 selected scaffold 寫入同一路徑，
122	snapshot 優先；scaffold 仍會補齊缺少的 files 並執行 selected initializers。
123	Source 與 destination traversal 都相對於 held `os.Root` handles 進行；file bytes 來自
124	已開啟且驗證過的 source handle，不會再次依 mutable pathname lookup。
125
126	Confirmation 與 human dry-run output 會顯示 bounded selected-path preview；local source
127	若是 live working-tree/directory snapshot 而非 commit，也會明確 warning。含 credential
128	的 URL userinfo 會從 summaries、structured output 與 clone/template errors 移除。
129
130	Preset 可用 scalar `template`、`template_ref`、`template_subdir` 宣告同一操作。它們依
131	一般 inheritance 規則 resolve，explicit CLI flags 優先，因此可以一個 starter catalog

134	### Check-in policy
135
136	Interactive wizard 提供 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；script 也可傳 `auto`：
137
138	| 值 | 行為 |
139	|---|---|
140	| `commit` | `git add -A`，以 `--message`／preset message commit，再執行 `after_commit` setup |
141	| `stage` | 執行 `before_commit` setup 後 `git add -A`；保留 staged checkout，不執行 `after_commit` |
142	| `none` | generated changes 保持 unstaged、uncommitted |
143	| `auto` | `repo new` 使用 `initial_check_in` 與相容的 `initial_commit`；clone/setup 則不自動 check-in |
144
145	`stage` mode 會 best-effort 在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入
146	`LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`。[Lazygit v0.59.0 會讀取此
147	file](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，並將它作為小寫 `c` 的 initial message；大寫
148	`C` 與 Git 本身不使用此 integration。不同內容的既有 draft 會保留並回報 warning，
149	不會被覆寫。這是 implementation-detail adapter，不是 `commit.template`。
150
151	Staging 才是 durable outcome：optional lazygit draft 若無法寫入，dev 會發出 warning
152	並保留 staged index，不會 rollback。
153
154	Staged setup 不能建立 upstream；`handoff=start` 也要求已 commit 的 setup，因為新
155	worktree 會漏掉 staged files。`stay`、`cd`、`open` 仍可供 review。`repo setup
156	--commit` 保留為 `--check-in=commit` 的 compatibility alias；`--message` 同時適用於
157	commit 與 stage。Structured result 保留 `committed`，並在適用時加入 `staged`、
158	`staged_paths`、`commit_message`、`commit_draft_provider` 與不含 file content 的
159	`template` summary。

161	### Upstream publishing
162
163	提供 publishing 選項前，dev 會以 read-only 方式 probe `gh` 與 `glab`。只有 CLI 已
164	安裝且完成 authentication 的 provider 才會出現；否則 wizard 顯示對應的安裝或 login
165	指引。預設 local-only，新 publish 的 repository 預設 private。
166
167	Publishing 會沿用 local repository name 與 configured description，再詢問 provider
168	namespace/owner、visibility，以及是否 push initial/current branch。Dev 會在必要的
169	local setup 與 commit steps 成功後建立空的 GitHub 或 GitLab repository，再新增／驗證
170	`origin`，並可選擇以 upstream tracking push。Provider、name-conflict 或 push failure
171	絕不刪除 local checkout，也不會刪除已建立的 upstream。
172
173	從 `repo setup` publish 時必須使用 `--check-in=commit`（或相容的 `--commit` flag），
174	避免新建 upstream 漏掉本次產生的 setup changes。`--check-in=stage` 與任何新 upstream
175	不相容；對新 repository 而言，`none` 只有搭配 `--push=false` 才能建立刻意保持空白的
176	upstream。

178	### Handoff
179
180	`stay` 只輸出結果；`cd` 透過受信任的 `shell-init` wrapper 改變 parent shell；
181	`open` 開啟 configured Herdr/tmux/Zellij runtime，runtime 為 `none` 時退回 `cd`；
182	`start` 會固定此 repository 並接續現有 task wizard。Setup 留下 uncommitted files、
183	導致新 worktree 會遺漏它們時，`start` 不可用。Repository bootstrap 與
184	`dev start` 都不會啟動 coding agent。
185
186	Repository、task-start 與 finish wizard 共用的 TTY text fields 都使用 inline editor：
187	Left/Right、Home/End、Delete/Backspace、cursor 位置插入與 Esc/Ctrl-C cancellation 會
188	被解讀為 terminal actions，不會成為 raw escape bytes。Buffered 或 piped non-TTY input
189	仍維持 line-oriented behavior。

191	## `dev done` finish flags
192
193	`dev done` 對 branch/worktree task 只透過下列其中一種方式 integrate：`--ff`（rebase 到 base 再 fast-forward）或 `--pr`（push 並開啟 pull/merge request）。兩者都省略時，在 TTY 上會開啟 interactive finish wizard —— 提示內容見[變更流工作流程](../guides/change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
194
195	Dirty checkout 由 `--dirty <auto|fail|commit|discard>` 處理（預設 `auto`）：
196
197	| 值 | 行為 |
198	|---|---|
199	| `auto` | interactive：提示 commit 或 discard；non-interactive：直接失敗，等同 `fail` |
200	| `fail` | dirty checkout 時拒絕 finish |
201	| `commit` | 用 `--message`/`-m` commit 全部變更（未指定時 interactive 會提示輸入） |
202	| `discard` | reset tracked 變更並移除 untracked files；具破壞性，沒有 TTY 時需要 `--yes` |
203
204	`--yes`/`-y` 用來確認選定的 finish plan；non-interactive 的 `--dirty discard` 必須要有它，其他情況則是跳過 interactive 確認步驟。`--keep-worktree` 讓 `--ff` integration 後仍保留 worktree（預設 merge 後移除），`--push` 會一併 push 產生的 branch，`--delete-branch` 只在 branch 的 commits 已被 base 包含時才刪除它 —— 有 unpushed commits 的 branch 永遠不會被刪除。

231	| `[update]` | `check`（預設 `true`）— 允許每天一次的「有新版」提示與其背景 cache refresh；`DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可覆寫 |

233	Repository quick-note Markdown 是 configured `paths.state_dir/notes` 下的 durable data；該路徑預設為 `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/notes`。`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/notes.db` 的 full-text index 是 disposable，會從 Markdown 重建；調整 `paths.state_dir` 不會移動 cache。

235	### Scaffold presets
236
237	Global repository recipes 位於 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml`（或 root
238	`--scaffolds` override）。每個 authored file 都必須宣告 `version = 1`。精簡 preset
239	範例：
240
241	```toml
242	version = 1
243	default_preset = "team"
244	default_agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
245
246	[presets.team]
247	extends = "agent-ready"
248	handoff = "cd"
249	initial_check_in = "stage"
250	template = "acme/starter-catalog"
251	template_ref = "v2"
252	template_subdir = "services/go"
253
254	[[presets.team.inputs]]
255	id = "deployment"
256	type = "choice"
257	choices = ["none", "docker"]
258	default = "none"
259
260	[[presets.team.files]]
261	id = "service-readme"
262	source = "service/README.md" # 此檔案旁的 templates/service/README.md
263	destination = "docs/service.md"
264
265	[[presets.team.hooks]]
266	id = "verify"
267	phase = "before_commit"
268	command = ["make", "test"]
269	required = true
270
271	[[presets.team.skills]]
272	id = "knowledge"
273	source = "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills"
274	name = "project-knowledge-harness"
275	agents = ["claude-code", "codex"]
276	default = true
277
278	[presets.team.skills.setup]
279	phase = "before_commit"
280	interpreter = "bash"
281	script = "scripts/init.sh"
282	args = ["--target", "{{path}}", "--project-name", "{{name}}"]
283	required = true
284	```
285
286	Skill setup 一般會指定 installed skill 內的 project-local script。內建推薦項目則使用
287	`builtin = "agent-history-hygiene"` 或
288	`builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`；這些固定且經 review 的 initializer 不會執行
289	下載回來的 skill code。
290
291	Preset 最多 extend 一個 parent。Scalar 會 override；simple lists 會 replace；files、
292	hooks 與 skills 依 `id` merge，inherited item 可用 `enabled = false` 停用。
293	`[[presets.*.files]]` 的 rendering source 必須留在 config source 旁的 `templates/`
294	tree；這個 file-level mechanism 與前述 repository snapshot `template` scalar 不同。
295	Destination 必須留在 repository 內，skill setup script 也必須位於 installed skill
296	directory 內。`initial_check_in` 接受 `commit`、`stage`、`none`；legacy
297	`initial_commit` boolean 仍可讀，但同一 preset 不可同時設定兩者。
298
299	### Safe project overlays
300
301	Repository 可 commit 兩個固定檔案：
302
303	- `.dev-cli/config.toml`：allowlisted worktree provisioning 與 repository setup
304	  wizard defaults。
305	- `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`：使用同一 versioned schema 的 project presets、
306	  templates、hooks 與 skill setup。
307
308	```toml
309	# .dev-cli/config.toml
310	version = 1
311
312	[worktree]
313	include = [".env.example"]
314	strategy = "reinstall"
315
316	[repo.setup]
317	preset = "team"
318	handoff = "cd"
319	check_in = "stage"
320	```
321
322	Effective precedence 由低至高為 built-ins、global config/scaffolds、legacy
323	`.dev.toml`、target repository 的 `.dev-cli/*`，最後是 explicit CLI 或 wizard
324	choices。`.dev.toml` 為相容性仍可讀；新的 project configuration 應使用
325	`.dev-cli/config.toml`。Global `default_preset` 與 project `[repo.setup]` 的 preset、
326	handoff、check-in fields 只用來預填 interactive wizard choices；它們不會改變
327	scripted defaults，後者由對應 flags 控制。Legacy `commit` boolean 仍可讀，但同一
328	layer 不可與 `check_in` 並用。
329
330	Project files 不能 override host paths、state location、runtime backend、forge
331	inventory 或 credentials、stats、update、bootstrap 或 TUI policy，也不能靜默 publish
332	repository。執行來自 `.dev-cli/config.toml` 的 post-create command，或來自 project
333	`.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 的 hook／skill setup 前，dev 會依 canonical repository 加
334	execution-content hash 詢問 trust；executable content 變更後必須重新同意，
335	non-interactive 且沒有 matching trust record 時 fail closed。Legacy `.dev.toml` 保留其
336	compatibility behavior。Credential 與 host-specific path 應放 user config 或 ignored
337	environment file，絕不放 committed project overlay。
338
339	Project-authored skill setup 必須使用 local source，讓實際 bytes 能納入 trust hash。
340	Remote project skill 仍可安裝，但不能宣告 executable setup；global preset 則仍屬於
341	host-owned policy。
342
343	## 彩色輸出
344
345	所有 human-readable 介面都透過一組 semantic role 套用 ANSI color：`title`/`header`/`prompt`（bold cyan）、`label`/`dim`（dim）、`success`（green）、`warning`（yellow）、`danger`（bold red）、代表 PR/review handoff 的 `review`（magenta），以及 Markdown 用的 `strong`/`code`。本身帶有意義的值依其意義上色，而非固定 role：
346
347	| 值 | 綠色 | 黃色 | 紅色 |
348	|---|---|---|---|
349	| Git status | `clean` | `dirty`、`ahead`、`behind`、`no checkout` | `conflict`、`error` |
350	| Task state | `hot`、`done` | `warm`、`cold`、`parked` | — |
351	| Fleet host | `ok` | `stale`、`no-dev` | `unreachable`、`timeout`、`incompatible` |
352	| Skill update | `current` | `update` | `missing`、`failed` |
353	| Artifact intent | `finalized` | `armed`、`finalizing` | `failed` |
354
355	`dev journal` 與 `dev summary` 輸出 Markdown，因此其 heading 與 fenced code block 的樣式與 `dev help <topic>` 的 quick-reference 頁面相同。在 command help 中只有你會實際輸入的名稱 —— command 名稱與 flag spec —— 會上色；description 保持原色，且 cobra 計算出的欄位對齊不受影響，因為 terminal 不會給 escape sequence 任何寬度。
356
357	用全域的 `--color <auto|always|never>` flag 控制（預設 `auto`）。`auto` 在 output 未連接 terminal、`NO_COLOR` 被設為任何非空值，或 `TERM=dumb` 時會停用 color。此設定同樣會傳到 interactive dashboard，因此 `dev --color never` 也會讓儀表板不上色。`--json` output 不論 mode 為何都不會上色。目前沒有對應的 config-file 欄位 —— `--color` 與 environment 是僅有的控制方式，因此 pipe `dev` 的輸出不需要額外傳 `--color never` 就是乾淨的。
358	## Shell integration
359
360	```bash
361	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"
362	dev shell-init fish | source
363	```
364
365	Child process 不能改變 parent working directory，因此受信任的 `shell-init` output 會定義 wrapper。Navigation command 執行時，wrapper 從 private child-only file descriptor 讀取 NUL-terminated path，再呼叫 `builtin cd`；它不會把一般 `dev` command output 當成 shell code evaluate。
366

2	description: Record dev-cli dependencies, upstream preview status, documentation constraints, and behavior that is intentionally incomplete.

8
9	# Compatibility and known limitations
10
11	This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
12
13	## dev-cli capability matrix
14
15	| Capability | Dependency | Without it |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
18	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
19	| named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
20	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
21	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
22	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
23	| remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
24	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
25	| staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
26	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
27	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
28	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
29	| terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
30	| in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` prints the package manager's upgrade command instead |
31
32	## Confirmed project limitations
33
34	### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
35
36	Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
37
38	Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
39
40	### Pull-request completion is not tracked automatically
41
42	`dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge to infer that a request later merged. Verify integration and finish/reconcile deliberately; do not assume remote merge implies local DONE.
43
44	### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
45
46	The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
47
48	### Built-in forge cache TTL differs from generated config
49
50	`dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
51
52	Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
53	still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
54	longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
55	`--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
56	inventory has been searched.
57
58	### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
59
60	`repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
61	directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
62	`c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
63	lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
64	plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
65	draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
66	is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
67	and printed message remain the recovery path.
68
69	### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
70
71	`dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
72
73	- There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
74	- Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
75	- `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
76	- The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
77
78	### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
79
80	A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
81
82	## Current behaviors that are implemented
83
84	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
85
86	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
87	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
88	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
89	- Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
90	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
91
92	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
93	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
94	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
95	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
96
97	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
98	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
99	- `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
100	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
101	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
102	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
103	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
104	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
105	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
106	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
107	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
108	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
109	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
110	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
111	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
112	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
113	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, and refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured).
114	- `dev upgrade` downloads the current release for this platform, verifies it against the release `SHA256SUMS`, and replaces the running binary with an atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run). It defers to Homebrew, Scoop or `go install` when one of them owns the file.
115	- An interactive `dev` command prints one dim "newer release available" line at most once a day, read from the day-old release cache; it never blocks on the network. `[update] check = false` or `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` disables it.
116
117	## Claude Code status matrix
118
119	| Surface | Status on 2026-08-28 | Compatibility note |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| core agentic loop/tools | official | exact tools depend on surface/model/policy |
122	| worktree isolation | official, rapidly evolving | cleanup, baseRef, resume, and safety details are version-sensitive |
123	| subagents | official | fork/background defaults and naming changed across 2.1.x |

129	`TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` are historical tools removed in v2.1.178. The old `Task` worker tool name was replaced by `Agent`; do not confuse either with Task-list metadata tools.
130
131	## Documentation-stack limitations
132
133	- `mkdocs-static-i18n` reports that `zh-TW` is not a Lunr language, so Chinese search does not receive a dedicated Lunr stemmer/segmenter. Navigation and pages still build.
134	- `mkdocs-llmstxt` skips pages after static-i18n remaps them. This project replaces that empty output with a deterministic local generator and runs strict builds again.
135	- The copy-to-LLM plugin's button labels remain English on zh-TW pages; this is cosmetic.
136	- MkDocs and Material are pinned below their next major versions because the selected plugin stack targets MkDocs 1.x/Material 9.x.
137
138	## Reporting a compatibility change
139
140	Update the owning guide, both languages, this matrix, and [Sources and freshness](sources-freshness.md). Include the tested binary/version and a code/test or official-source link. Never preserve a known false statement for backward documentation compatibility.

18

20	|---|---|---|
21	| 核心 repository/task/worktree 操作 | Git | 無法使用；Git 是唯一 hard runtime dependency |
22	| grouped runtime 與 agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` 改試 tmux、Zellij，最後 none |
23	| named terminal session | tmux 或相容 Zellij | `none` 保留核心 behavior 與 shell navigation |
24	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | authenticated `gh` | Git 可用時 branch 仍能 push，可能需 browser/manual flow |
25	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | authenticated `glab` | 同樣 graceful fallback |
26	| repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` 或 `glab` | local repository/scaffold 仍可使用；wizard 會說明如何 login |
27	| remote repository snapshot template | Git，加上 source 所需的 network/authentication | validation 會在建立 destination 前失敗，rendered URL userinfo 會 redact；local template 仍可使用 |
28	| setup-capable project skills | skills provider 與 entrypoint interpreter | 未選取的 skill 會跳過；selected required setup 若缺少 interpreter，會在 scaffold mutation 前失敗；先取得的 clone 會保留 |
29	| staged lazygit message prefill | 會讀取 `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` 的 lazygit version | files 仍保持 staged，dev 會印出建議 message；一般 Git commit 仍可使用 |
30	| worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager（`uv`、npm、Cargo 等） | plan 回報 missing tool 並保留 checkout |
31	| interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | 透過 pipe 執行 bare `dev` 時輸出 plain task list |
32	| repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` 與 FTS5 | 不需要外部 `sqlite3` executable |
33	| Windows 上的 terminal multiplexing | tmux/Zellij/Herdr（僅 POSIX） | Windows 一律使用 `none` backend；`dev shell-init powershell` 仍能移動 shell |
34	| in-place self-update | standalone install（非 Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`） | `dev upgrade` 改為印出對應套件管理器的升級指令 |
35
36	## 已確認的專案限制
37
38	### Note search 與 filesystem durability 依文字及平台而異
39
40	Latin note query 使用 term-wise prefix FTS 與 SQLite ranking。Non-ASCII query 改用 literal term-wise substring matching，因為 SQLite 的 `unicode61` tokenizer 不會切分任意 CJK substrings；這些結果不使用相同的 FTS ranking。
41
42	所有支援平台的 note write 都會 sync file 並 atomic rename。Unix 也會在 rename/delete 後 sync containing directory。Windows implementation 無法提供 directory-fsync 步驟，因此 sudden power loss 時的 durability guarantee 較窄。Cooperating `dev` processes 的 concurrent mutations 會被 serialized，且每次 Markdown replacement 都是 atomic；任意 external writer 不會參與這個 lock。
43
44	### Pull request completion 不會自動追蹤
45
46	`dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。目前 `dev sweep` 不會 query forge 推斷 request 後來已 merge。請驗證 integration 後再刻意 finish/reconcile；不能假設 remote merge 代表 local DONE。
47
48	### Agent session capture 只有保留欄位，尚未接線
49
50	Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
51
52	### Built-in forge cache TTL 與 generated config 不同
53
54	`dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
55
56	較舊的 generated config 可能包含 `forge.remote_limit = 100`。此欄位仍可解析，
57	但 forge inventory 現在會完整 pagination，因此不再限制 synchronization。
58	`dev config init` 不再寫入它；`dev repo remote --limit` 只在完整 inventory 搜尋
59	完成後限制 rendered matches。
60
61	### Lazygit staged-message prefill 是 best effort
62
63	`repo --check-in=stage` 會在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入 pending message。
64	[Lazygit v0.59.0 的小寫 `c` 會使用該
65	檔案](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，但這是 lazygit implementation detail，不是 Git
66	interface；大寫 `C` 與一般 `git commit` 不會讀取它。Dev 不會覆寫內容不同的既有
67	draft。Draft write failure 只會產生 warning；staging 仍視為成功且不會 rollback。若
68	upstream integration 日後改變，staged index 與已印出的 message 仍是 recovery path。
69
70	### Windows 是 build target，不是 full-feature 平台
71
72	`dev` 可在 `windows/amd64` 與 `windows/arm64` 編譯並執行，每個 release 都會附各自的 `.zip`。核心的 repository、task 與 worktree 操作可用。差異：
73
74	- 沒有 tmux、Zellij 或 Herdr，因此 runtime backend 一律是 `none`。Grouped runtime/agent activity 與 named session 無法使用；`cd` 指令與 PowerShell wrapper 仍可運作。
75	- Shell integration 是 `dev shell-init powershell`。POSIX shell 透過 file descriptor 3 回傳目錄；PowerShell 無法繼承它，wrapper 改用 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳入 temp-file path。
76	- `dev fleet open` 會啟動子 shell（`%COMSPEC%`），而非取代 process，因為 Windows 沒有 `exec(2)`。
77	- Domain test suites 仍有部分假設 POSIX filesystem，因此 Windows CI 的 test 僅供參考，compilation、`go vet` 與 build 則為強制項。
78
79	### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
80
81	Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
82
83	## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
84
85	以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
86
87	- `dev repo new|create`、`repo clone` 與 `repo setup` 共用 preset-driven bootstrap pipeline。Plain explicit `repo new NAME` 仍維持 minimal；清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name 會改走 clone acquisition，保留 source history/remote。無參數 wizard 的第一個欄位也會偵測同樣 reference；建立新 repository 時，預設為 no 的 customization gate 讓正常 `agent-ready` flow 保持精簡。Text fields 使用 TTY inline editor，因此 cursor keys 會編輯內容，不會插入 raw escape bytes；non-TTY reader 維持 line-oriented behavior。
88	- `repo new` 可從 local directory/repository 或 Git source 的 optional branch、tag、commit 與 confined subdirectory 建立 fresh-history snapshot。未 pin 的 local Git tree 包含 tracked 加 untracked non-ignored files；non-Git directory 包含完整 current tree。Source `.git` metadata 會排除、URL userinfo 會 redact，不安全的 file types/paths 會在 destination 建立前失敗，held root/file handles 會限制 mutable-path races。Human plan 會預覽 paths 並警告 live snapshot，preset 也可選擇 catalog-repository subfolder。
89	- Repository setup 支援 `--check-in=commit|stage|none`（`auto` 用於 preset compatibility）。Staged setup 會執行 before-commit setup 與 `git add -A`，但不執行 `after_commit` phase；它不能 publish 或 handoff 到 `start`，並可依前述方式預填 lazygit 小寫 `c`。
90	- Source 與 agent targets 相同的 selected skills 會共用一次 installer invocation。`agent-history-hygiene` initializer 會寫入 pre-commit/gitleaks policy，並將缺少的 machine-local `.project.json`／`statistics.json` 規則 merge 進 `.specstory/.gitignore`；custom content 與 transcript history 都保持可追蹤。
91	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` 與 `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 僅能保存 portable setup policy。Executable project configuration 會綁定 canonical Git common directory 與 exact content hash；hash 改變後必須重新信任。
92
93	- `dev start --focus` 會在 non-JSON creation 後 activate runtime。
94	- TUI navigation 會拒絕開啟 checkout 不存在的 COLD task，並要求使用 `dev resume`。
95	- Runtime handle 現在保存 backend provenance，cleanup 前會重新驗證。
96	- `auto` runtime selection 已在 tmux 與 none 之間加入 Zellij。
97
98	- `dev done` 在省略 `--ff`/`--pr` 且為 TTY 時會開啟 interactive finish wizard，把 dirty checkout 拿去跟 base 比較（commit、discard 或 cancel），不再直接拒絕任何 uncommitted change；non-interactive caller 仍須明確傳入 `--dirty` policy，且 destructive discard 需要 `--yes`。
99	- Human-readable output 現在具備 semantic color（`--color auto|always|never`），在 `NO_COLOR` 已設定、`TERM=dumb`，或 stdout/stderr 不是 terminal 時會自動停用。
100	- `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED：它不會關閉呼叫端 runtime、移除 worktree 或刪除 branch。Cleanup 已移交 `dev retire`，後者必須從目標 workspace 之外執行，會拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，並在每次關閉 runtime 之後重新驗證 Git state。`dev done --delete-branch` 現在會直接報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`，`--keep-worktree` 則以 no-op 警告。
101	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` 直接從 Git 列舉 linked worktrees，而非從 task registry，因此 branch 已被 base 包含的 unmanaged worktree 也能被 retire。Containment 本身絕不等於許可；dirty state、未 finalize 的 artifact、進行中的 Git operation 與 runtime 拒絕條件都仍會阻擋，且未加 `--delete-branches` 時 branch 一律保留。
102	- `dev sweep` 會把 branch 已不存在於 Git 的 branch-backed task 視為 dead，並提供 reap 該 record 的建議。這種 task 無法 finish、resume 或 retire，因為這些路徑都必須先解析 branch；在 `--apply` 之前該建議仍只是報告。
103	- 未知 command 會被回報，而不是被丟棄。`dev` 關閉了 cobra 自己的 error 輸出，先前又額外略過所有訊息開頭為 `unknown command` 的 error，因此打錯 command 時兩個 stream 都沒有任何輸出。現在會把訊息、cobra 的「Did you mean this?」建議，以及指向 `--help` 的提示寫到 stderr，exit status 為 1。
104	- 對 command family 傳入多餘的 argument 現在是 error，而不是安靜地印出 help。`dev wt bogus` 過去會印出 `dev wt` help 並 exit 0，因為 family 本身沒有 `Run`；現在每個 family node 都會回報未知 subcommand 並 exit 1，而單獨執行 family 仍會印出 help 並 exit 0。
105	- Argument 數量與 flag 錯誤會印出該 command 的 usage block。該 block 是否上色仍由 `--color` 決定。
106	- 每個 command family 的 help 都附上 ASCII orientation diagram 與 `See also: dev help <topic>` 指引，且 `dev help <command>` 會把 command 名稱或 alias 解析成對應 topic，因此 `dev help wt` 會連到 worktrees 頁面。
107	- Semantic color 已覆蓋所有 human-readable 介面，包含 interactive dashboard：`dev --color never`、`NO_COLOR` 與 `TERM=dumb` 現在也會關閉 dashboard 的顏色，先前並不會。
108	- `dev sweep` 會 reap repository 目錄已不存在的 task。這種 record 先前無法被 binary 中任何 command 觸及：`done`、`resume`、`park` 與 `retire` 都會先解析 repository，dead-branch 規則排除 direct mode，stale-worktree 規則又需要有記錄的 worktree path。若有 live runtime session 則不會提出此建議，且 reap 只移除 dev 的 intent record。
109	- `dev sweep` 會回報 task 記錄中存在、但 Git 未註冊，且只包含 agent artifact 目錄的 checkout。只有在其中每個檔案都與 repository 既有檔案 byte-identical 時才提議移除；其餘一律回報為 salvage 工作，即使加上 `--apply` 也絕不移除。
110	- `dev sweep` 會處理 worktree 仍在磁碟上的 cold task。Inventory 一直有為 `dev ls` 與 dashboard 計算這項 drift，但 sweep 從未讀取它，因此只能顯示、無法處理。
111	- `dev retire <path>` 會 reap 對應的 task record。先前只有 by-task 形式會設定 task identity，因此以 path 退休同一個 checkout 會留下 record；DONE 狀態與 identity 檢查維持不變。
112	- `dev version` 會回報目前執行的 build 是否為已發布的 release，`dev doctor` 也帶有同一行資訊。先前工具中沒有任何地方能回答「我是不是最新的？」，而 `go install ...@latest` 只會解析到最新的 tag，因此未 tag 的 feature 對安裝者而言等同不存在。
113	- Release 會發布各平台 archive 與 `SHA256SUMS`，並以 `CHANGELOG.md` 對應段落作為 release notes。先前的 release 只產生 GitHub release 物件，因此那些版本本來就沒有附加檔案。
114	- Release 會在 Unix `.tar.gz` 之外一併發布 Windows `.zip`，並更新附在 release 上的 in-repo Scoop manifest（設定 token 時也會 push 到 bucket）。
115	- `dev upgrade` 會下載此平台目前的 release、以 release `SHA256SUMS` 驗證，再以 atomic rename 取代執行中的 binary（Windows 會把 live `.exe` 移到旁邊，下次執行時清除）。若 Homebrew、Scoop 或 `go install` 擁有該檔案，則改為印出對應指令。
116	- Interactive `dev` command 每天最多印一行 dim 的「有新版」提示，來源是一天內的 release cache，永不因網路而 block。`[update] check = false` 或 `DEV_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` 可停用。
117

8	# Sources and freshness
9
10	This site mixes product documentation, external specifications, fast-moving harness behavior, project policy, and history. Every page identifies which kind of statement it contains and when it was checked.
11
12	## Authority order
13
14	1. **dev-cli behavior:** repository code, tests, E2E, and generated command reference.
15	2. **Git semantics:** current `git-scm.com` manuals for the relevant installed Git version.
16	3. **GitHub collaboration:** current GitHub Docs.
17	4. **Claude Code behavior:** current Anthropic documentation, with preview/experimental/version labels.
18	5. **Standards:** named versioned specifications such as Conventional Commits 1.0.0 and SemVer 2.0.0.
19	6. **Historical context:** dated archives and older project essays, never a current operating rule.
20	7. **Project policy:** explicitly labeled recommendations; not presented as an upstream guarantee.
21
22	A lower item may explain motivation but cannot override a higher authority's implementation claim.

docs/claude/worktree-isolation.md:66:Claude Code copies only paths that both match and are Git-ignored; tracked files already arrive through checkout. Keep the list minimal, review secret exposure, and install dependencies in the new directory.

docs/guides/remote-fleet.zh-TW.md:100:`e` 會用 `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` 開啟 `remotes.toml`——也就是這個 view 實際對應的檔案，而不是其他 view 中 `e` 所開啟的 dev 自身 `config.toml`。離開編輯器後，`dev` 會先重新解析該檔案才使用它。解析失敗、出現未知欄位，或含有明文密碼的檔案權限有問題時，都會被回報並保留原本的資料列，因此打錯字不會安靜地讓某台 host 從 fleet 中消失。檔案解析成功則會立即對所有已設定的 host 觸發一次 live reload。
docs/guides/remote-fleet.md:30:Hosts live in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` (override the path with the global `--remotes <path>` flag). `config init` writes a starter file (`--force` to overwrite, `--stdout` to print without writing); `config edit` opens it in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` (`--editor` overrides); `config show` prints the effective configuration with any plaintext password redacted; `config path` prints the resolved path.

docs/guides/remote-fleet.md:66:| `dev fleet config edit` | `--editor <cmd>` | Open `remotes.toml` in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` |

docs/guides/remote-fleet.md:84:`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` is durable, user-authored configuration, on the same footing as `config.toml` — `dev fleet config init`/`edit` manage it, and nothing regenerates it automatically.
docs/guides/remote-fleet.md:96:`e` opens `remotes.toml` in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` — the file this view is about, rather than dev's own `config.toml`, which `e` opens everywhere else. On leaving the editor `dev` reparses the file before using it. A parse failure, an unknown field, or a permissions problem on a file holding a plaintext password is reported and the previous rows are kept, so a typo cannot silently drop a host from the fleet. A file that parses triggers an immediate live reload of every configured host.

401	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. Inside Herdr/tmux/Zellij it
402	switches the current client; outside it exits the dashboard and attaches to
403	the target session. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
404	for the next action and `c` edits it. In REPOS, `enter` is pure ad-hoc open,
405	`space` expands linked worktrees inline, `m` edits repository tags/summary,
406	`s` starts an isolated worktree task, and `d` starts a tracked direct task.
407	On TASKS and REPOS, `n` quick-adds a repository thought and `N` opens its notes
408	overlay. Expanded children carry their own Git/session/task state and can be
409	opened directly. In TRY, `n` creates or clones an experiment;
410	`space` opens mark/deprecate/archive/restore/graduate actions; `a` includes
411	retained history. In SKILLS, `a` opens the upstream interactive installer, `c`
412	performs the opt-in read-only network check, and `u` confirms before updating
413	only the selected lock-managed skill. `r` reloads local state without checking
414	the network. `?` opens the complete context-sensitive key map. That makes
415	the branch/worktree and lifecycle costs explicit rather than silently applying
416	them to every directory.
417
418	REPOS also has an agent-handoff copy menu. Press `y`, then `y` for contextual
419	Markdown, `p` for the checkout path, `b` for the branch, `s` for runtime/agent

959	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's

981	`dev fleet list` runs each machine's own `dev`, so its XDG config and paths stay
982	host-local. Missing `dev` installations are reported as `no-dev`; unreachable
983	hosts can fall back to the last private XDG snapshot. The FLEET TUI view exposes
984	the same inventory and Enter opens a selected path through remote Herdr when its
985	server is active, otherwise through `ssh -t` and a login shell.
986
987	`dev fleet sync <repo> --push` publishes the clean source branch, then fetches
988	matching clones by normalized Git remote identity. Only a clean checkout of the
989	same branch that is strictly behind is fast-forwarded. Dirty, ahead, divergent,
990	ambiguous and unreachable targets remain untouched and make the command fail;
991	hosts without `dev` or without that repository are explicitly ignored.

993	## The agent skill
994
995	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
996	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
997	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
998	reading none.
999
1000	```bash
1001	dev skill list       # merged project + global inventory
1002	dev skill list --check --json
1003	dev skill add        # interactive wizard for daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
1004	dev skill update project-knowledge-harness --global --yes
1005	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
1006	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
1007	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
1008	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
1009	```
1010
1011	`dev skill add [package]` is only a shortcut into the upstream interactive
1012	wizard. It never selects all skills or agents. Listing uses an already
1013	available/cached `skills` CLI and never downloads it; add/update are explicit
1014	actions and may access the network. Project scope resolves to the current Git
1015	checkout root, so invoking the command from a nested directory gives the same
1016	inventory.
1017
1018	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
1019	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
1020	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
1021	responsibility.

610
611	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
612	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
613	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
614	command detected from the lockfiles. Included files must remain the same
615	regular file through open; source swaps and symlinked destination parents are
616	refused, existing destinations are reported as skipped, and contents are never
617	logged:
618
619	```toml
620	[worktree]
621	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
622	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
623	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
624	```
625
626	`.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal include. Add that exact path
627	only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude launcher and verify it
628	arrives. `claude-copilot-once` preserves an existing Copilot pin and creates/
629	removes only one it added when absent; its proxy must already run.
630	`codex-copilot-once` injects backend via CLI and may auto-start its proxy path,
631	so neither wrapper needs the copied file.
632
633	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
634	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
635	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
636
637	```toml
638	[worktree]
639	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
640
641	[worktree.strategies]
642	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
643	```
644
645	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
646	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
647	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
648
649	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
650	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
651	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds
652	`<repo>/.dev-cli/config.toml` from it, so
653	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
654
```
</details></tool-use>

201
202	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
203
204	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
205	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
206	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
207
208	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
209	`paths.scan_roots` plus exact `paths.repo_paths` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
210
211	```bash
212	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
213	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
214	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
215	```
216
217	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
218	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
219
220	## Creating and setting up repositories
221
222	Read `references/repository-bootstrap.md` before creating a published repo,
223	running project-owned hooks, or installing setup-capable skills. A bare
224	`dev repo new` is interactive; `dev repo new NAME` deliberately retains the
225	minimal README + initial-commit contract. A clear Git URL, local Git path, or
226	`owner/name` argument to `new` or `create` automatically clones and preserves
227	its remote; template and upstream-creation flags cannot accompany that route.
228	Explicit `repo clone` remains available when scripts should state acquisition
229	directly.
230	`repo new --template` snapshots a local directory or Git tree into a fresh
231	history; it is not a clone. `--template-ref` and `--template-subdir` select the
232	exact source tree.
233
234	Use `--check-in=commit|stage|none` to choose whether generated changes are
235	committed, staged for human review, or left unstaged (`auto` follows a new
236	repository's preset and otherwise defaults to none). `repo setup --commit`
237	remains the compatibility spelling for commit.
238	Stage mode cannot create an upstream and cannot hand dirty setup directly to
239	`start`.
240
241	On a TTY, wizard fields are real inline editors: arrows, Home/End,
242	Backspace and Delete edit typed text rather than inserting escape sequences.
243	Esc or Ctrl-C cancels; piped input remains line-oriented.
244
245	The create/setup wizard asks one customization-gate question after preset
246	selection. Declining uses resolved defaults and skips detailed template,
247	README/gitignore/license/agent/skill questions; explicit customization flags or
248	a required input without a default make yes the suggested answer.
249
250	Global recipes live in `scaffolds.toml`. Repositories may commit the allowlisted
251	`.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, but executable project
252	configuration in those files must be trusted by its exact content hash before
253	it runs. Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior.
254
255	## Dashboard and forge inventory
256
257	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style
258	h/l. TRY `n` creates an experiment; `space` opens metadata/lifecycle actions;
259	`a` includes retained history. Archive is a reversible same-filesystem move,
260	not deletion or disk reclamation. `?` opens the full key map.
261
262	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` plus configured Azure DevOps
263	organization/project targets lazily and fully paginates every repository the
264	account can access. A private cache is shown immediately; stale rows stay
265	searchable while refresh runs. `/` filters provider, owner/name, visibility and
266	description, with `vis:private` for an exact visibility match. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
267	confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote [query] --json`
268	for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query and `--refresh`
269	forces a complete synchronization.
270
271	`dev journal` derives calendar-day reports from Git rather than storing a
272	second history database. The default current-user report adds existing
273	session/WakaTime observations, matching task intent and recent dirty-worktree
274	snapshots, clearly separated from committed history. `auto` expands at most 100
275	commit details while retaining complete aggregates; `--max-commits 0` is
276	unlimited. Use `--author <email>` or `--all-authors` for commit-only team views,
277	and `--json` for a stable structured report. dev generates the context only; it
278	does not launch the receiving agent.

280	`dev summary` is the complementary current-state view across this machine. It
281	combines durable repositories and present active/deprecated Tries with live Git,
282	worktree, task, runtime, recovery and catalog facts. The default `auto` Markdown
283	expands active work and leaves quiet projects in a compact index; `--attention`
284	selects both active work and recovery hazards, while `--json` always emits the
285	complete selected snapshot. Use journal for time ranges and `repo context` for
286	one repository.

289

293	project = "Platform"
294	```

296	Install Azure CLI's `azure-devops` extension separately. `dev` never installs

299	FLEET calls each configured host's own `dev` over SSH, preserving its XDG paths.
300	Enter prefers Herdr remote navigation and falls back to an SSH login shell.
301	`dev fleet sync` is explicit and strict: it only fast-forwards a clean checkout
302	of the same behind-only branch; dirty/ahead/diverged clones are never rewritten.
303
304	REPOS has LIVE, LATEST and asynchronous SIZE. SIZE is logical
305	checkout+private-Git bytes; shared Git is separate and marked `+S`. Detail also
306	shows no-remote/local-only/multi-upstream recovery topology. Press space to
307	expand linked worktrees; children
308	show their own Git/session/task state and mark harness-owned or untracked
309	checkouts `(ephemeral)` / `(external)`. Press `y` followed by `y/p/b/s/w` to
310	copy contextual Markdown, path, branch, runtime/agent sessions, or every
311	worktree path. `dev repo context [repo]` prints the full Markdown without a TUI.
312	`[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R` reverses
313	it.
314
315	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
316	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
317	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
318	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
319	regenerable forge/size/gitignore/note-FTS data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
320
321	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
322	explicitly. Runtime
323	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
324
325	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
326	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
327	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
328	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
329	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
330	the binding should be portable across machines.

452	## When to use this skill
453

497	## Gotchas
498
499	- **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
500	  output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
501	  (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
502	  file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
503	  `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
504	  wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
505	  shell — that is not a bug.
506	- **Windows runs without a multiplexer.** There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr on
507	  Windows, so the runtime backend is always `none`; `dev fleet open` starts a
508	  child shell instead of replacing the process. `dev upgrade` self-replaces only
509	  a standalone install and otherwise prints the Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`
510	  command.
511	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
512	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`

521	  complete current tree. Human plans preview paths and warn about live unpinned
522	  sources. URL userinfo is redacted, while held root/directory/file handles
523	  confine traversal. Symlinks, special files, traversal and source changes fail
524	  closed, and the snapshot applies only to an otherwise-empty new repo.
525	- **Lazygit commit drafts are a best-effort adapter.** `--check-in=stage` writes
526	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` in that worktree's Git directory so lowercase `c`
527	  can preload the proposed message. This is not `commit.template` or
528	  `COMMIT_EDITMSG`, uppercase `C` and other clients need not read it, and an
529	  existing different draft is preserved. Draft write/sync failure is a warning,
530	  not rollback: the successfully staged index remains ready for manual commit.
531	- **Agent history remains reviewable.** Built-in `agent-history-hygiene` seeds
532	  `.specstory/.gitignore` only for machine-local `.project.json` and generated
