```text
171	// strategyFor resolves the strategy for one ecosystem, narrowing to something
172	// sound and recording why when it has to.
173	func (s Settings) strategyFor(e Ecosystem) (Strategy, string) {
174		want := s.Strategy
175		if _, ok := ParseStrategy(string(want)); !ok {
176			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
177				e.Name, want, joinStrategies())
178		}
179		if v, ok := s.Strategies[e.Name]; ok {
180			if parsed, ok := ParseStrategy(v); ok {
181				want = parsed
182			} else {
183				return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
184					e.Name, v, joinStrategies())
185			}
186		}
187		// An ecosystem with no dependency directory has nothing to copy or share,
188		// so those strategies collapse to reinstalling — which for a global cache
189		// is nearly free anyway.
190		if len(e.DepDirs) == 0 && (want == Copy || want == Link) {
191			return Reinstall, ""
192		}
193		if ok, hazard := e.SupportsStrategy(want); !ok {
194			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s is unsound here — %s; using reinstall instead",
195				e.Name, want, hazard)
196		}
197		return want, ""
198	}

200	func joinStrategies() string {
201		parts := make([]string, len(Strategies))
202		for i, s := range Strategies {
203			parts[i] = string(s)
204		}
205		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
206	}

208	// BuildPlan computes what provisioning a new worktree of repoPath would do.
209	// It reads the filesystem and asks git which files are ignored, but changes
210	// nothing.
211	func BuildPlan(ctx context.Context, set Settings, repoPath string) Plan {
212		p := Plan{RepoPath: repoPath, Ecosystems: DetectEcosystems(repoPath)}
213
214		// Gitignored files to carry over.
215		if files, err := ignoredMatching(ctx, repoPath, set.Include); err != nil {
216			p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, "could not list ignored files: "+err.Error())
217		} else {
218			for _, rel := range files {
219				info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel))
220				if err != nil {
221					continue
222				}
223				if info.IsDir() {
224					continue // directories belong to `link`, not `include`
225				}
226				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
227					Kind: StepCopyFile, What: rel,
228					Why: "gitignored, so the checkout would not have it",
229				})
230			}
231		}
232
233		// Explicit symlinks, which are always the user's own decision.
234		for _, rel := range set.Link {
235			step := Step{Kind: StepLinkDir, What: rel, Why: "configured in worktree.link"}
236			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel)); err != nil {
237				step.Skipped, step.Why = true, "not present in the source checkout"
238			}
239			p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
240		}
241
242		// Dependencies, per ecosystem.
243		//
244		// The strategy and post_create are separate axes. A strategy says how a
245		// dependency directory arrives; post_create says what commands run. So an
246		// explicit command list replaces the *derived install commands* but still
247		// leaves copy and link in effect — a project that bootstraps with `make
248		// setup` may still want its node_modules copied rather than rebuilt.
249		explicit := !set.Cmds.Auto
250		for _, e := range p.Ecosystems {
251			strategy, warn := set.strategyFor(e)
252			if warn != "" {
253				p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, warn)
254			}
255
256			switch strategy {
257			case Copy, Link:
258				kind, verb := StepCopyDir, "copied"
259				if strategy == Link {
260					kind, verb = StepLinkDir, "shared"
261				}
262				for _, dir := range e.DepDirs {
263					step := Step{
264						Kind: kind, What: dir, Ecosystem: e.Name,
265						Why: fmt.Sprintf("%s dependencies, %s instead of reinstalling", e.Manager, verb),
266					}
267					if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, dir)); err != nil {
268						step.Skipped = true
269						step.Why = "not present in the source checkout — nothing to " + string(strategy)
270					}
271					p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
272				}
273
274			case Skip:
275				if explicit {
276					continue
277				}
278				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
279					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
280					Why: "strategy is skip", Skipped: true,
281				})
282
283			default: // Reinstall
284				if explicit {
285					continue // the configured command list replaces this
286				}
287				step := Step{
288					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
289					Why: e.Marker + " detected",
290				}
291				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
292					step.Skipped = true
293					step.Why = e.Tool + " is not installed on this machine"
294					p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings,
295						fmt.Sprintf("%s needs %s, which is not installed — worktrees will come up without its dependencies",
296							e.Name, e.Tool))
297				}

299			}

303		if explicit {
304			for _, c := range set.Cmds.Commands {
305				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{Kind: StepRun, What: c, Why: "configured in worktree.post_create"})
306			}

309	}

311	// ignoredMatching asks git which of the patterns name real, ignored files.
312	//
313	// Using git rather than matching by hand means .gitignore semantics —
314	// negations, directory rules, nested ignore files — are exactly right, and
315	// that a *tracked* file matching a pattern is never returned. A tracked file
316	// is already in the new checkout on the correct branch; copying the source
317	// branch's version over it would be wrong.
318	func ignoredMatching(ctx context.Context, src string, patterns []string) ([]string, error) {
319		if len(patterns) == 0 {
320			return nil, nil
321		}
322		args := []string{"ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--"}
323		args = append(args, patterns...)
324		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, src, args...)
325		if err != nil {
326			return nil, err
327		}
328		var rels []string
329		for _, f := range strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(out, "\x00"), "\x00") {
330			if f != "" {
331				rels = append(rels, f)
332			}
333		}
334		return rels, nil
335	}
```

```text
35	// Limits is the reusable compiled policy for portable file manifests. Every
36	// field is required and must be no greater than the corresponding compiled
37	// ceiling, allowing host configuration to lower limits without weakening them.
38	type Limits struct {
39		MaxFiles          int

47	// DefaultLimits returns the maximum policy supported by this binary.
48	func DefaultLimits() Limits {
49		return Limits{
50			MaxFiles:          CompiledMaxFiles,
51			MaxFileBytes:      CompiledMaxFileBytes,
52			MaxTotalBytes:     CompiledMaxTotalBytes,
53			MaxPathBytes:      CompiledMaxPathBytes,
54			MaxComponentBytes: CompiledMaxComponentBytes,
55			MaxPathDepth:      CompiledMaxPathDepth,
56		}
57	}

59	// Validate rejects incomplete policy and values above the compiled ceilings.
60	func (limits Limits) Validate() error {
61		maximum := DefaultLimits()
62		switch {
63		case limits.MaxFiles <= 0 || limits.MaxFiles > maximum.MaxFiles:
64			return fmt.Errorf("max files %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxFiles, maximum.MaxFiles, ErrInvalidLimits)
65		case limits.MaxFileBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxFileBytes > maximum.MaxFileBytes:
66			return fmt.Errorf("max file bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxFileBytes, maximum.MaxFileBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)

68			return fmt.Errorf("max total bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxTotalBytes, maximum.MaxTotalBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
69		case limits.MaxPathBytes <= 0 || limits.MaxPathBytes > maximum.MaxPathBytes:
70			return fmt.Errorf("max path bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxPathBytes, maximum.MaxPathBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)

72			return fmt.Errorf("max component bytes %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxComponentBytes, maximum.MaxComponentBytes, ErrInvalidLimits)
73		case limits.MaxPathDepth <= 0 || limits.MaxPathDepth > maximum.MaxPathDepth:
74			return fmt.Errorf("max path depth %d must be between 1 and %d: %w", limits.MaxPathDepth, maximum.MaxPathDepth, ErrInvalidLimits)
75		default:
76			return nil
77		}
78	}

89	// Metadata is the content-free portion of one portable regular file used for
90	// validating counts, sizes, paths, and collisions before any bytes are opened.
91	type Metadata struct {
92		Path string
93		Size int64
94	}
95
96	// ValidateManifest enforces a validated limits policy over the complete file
97	// set, including exact duplicates and portable case/normalization collisions.
98	func ValidateManifest(files []Metadata, limits Limits) error {
99		if err := limits.Validate(); err != nil {
100			return err
101		}
102		if len(files) > limits.MaxFiles {
103			return fmt.Errorf("manifest has %d files; maximum is %d: %w", len(files), limits.MaxFiles, ErrManifestLimit)
104		}
105		paths := make([]string, 0, len(files))
106		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(files))
107		var total int64
108		for _, file := range files {
109			if file.Size < 0 {
110				return fmt.Errorf("file %q has negative size: %w", file.Path, ErrManifestLimit)
111			}
112			if file.Size > limits.MaxFileBytes {
113				return fmt.Errorf("file %q is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", file.Path, file.Size, limits.MaxFileBytes, ErrManifestLimit)
114			}
115			if _, exists := seen[file.Path]; exists {
116				return fmt.Errorf("path %q appears more than once: %w", file.Path, ErrDuplicatePath)
117			}
118			seen[file.Path] = struct{}{}
119			paths = append(paths, file.Path)
120			if file.Size > limits.MaxTotalBytes-total {
121				return fmt.Errorf("manifest exceeds %d total bytes: %w", limits.MaxTotalBytes, ErrManifestLimit)
122			}
123			total += file.Size
124		}
125		if err := pathx.ValidatePortablePathSet(paths, limits.PathLimits()); err != nil {
126			return err
127		}
128		return nil
129	}
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Identifying potential catalog bugs**

I’m noticing a few potential bugs in the catalog. First, I think I need to create `validateCreateInput` before `WithLock`. It calls `s.now`, which seems benign, but if `s` is nil, it could panic. Next, `CreateUnderLock` prepares a candidate inside the lock, assuming `s.Dir` exists because lockx creates it. Additionally, while importing, I see it validates updates but doesn't fully account for existing differences in timestamps, potentially causing stale imports. Lastly, merging experiments could silently preserve nil values, which might lead to issues. 

**Assessing potential asymmetries and conflicts**

I’m considering potential asymmetries where the target has experiment provenance but the source does not. This may cause issues like preserving differences. A conflict exists if `current.Name` is not equal to `incoming.Name`, which may prevent syncing renamed display labels. Then, with the registry, `EnsureRepository` calls `r.match` under store lock, ensuring no deadlocks occur. However, `r.match` may become ambiguous with remote entries, and importantly, there’s a possibility of costly operations under lock if not managed properly. Plus, two entries could share the same restore path without issues. 

**Analyzing asset claims and path handling**

I need to consider preventing asset claims, especially regarding `canonicalLocationPaths`, which canonicalizes missing paths by using the nearest existing ones. On Windows, case sensitivity plays a crucial role. Using `pathx.Canonical`, paths like `C:\Repo` and `c:\repo` may not compare properly due to case differences. Functions like `EvalSymlinks` might not guarantee canonical casing either. This could create conflicts on Windows’ case-insensitive filesystem, allowing two different IDs to claim the same location, which could lead to issues with remote imports.
</details></think>

```text
1	package gitx

3	import (
4		"context"

6		"sort"

8	)
9
10	// Remote describes every configured fetch/push location for one Git remote.
11	// Multiple URLs are preserved because Git can fetch from one place and push to
12	// several destinations.
13	type RemoteInfo struct {
14		Name      string   `json:"name"`
15		FetchURLs []string `json:"fetch_urls,omitempty"`
16		PushURLs  []string `json:"push_urls,omitempty"`
17	}
18
19	// BranchUpstream is one local branch and the tracking ref configured for it.
20	type BranchUpstream struct {
21		Branch   string `json:"branch"`
22		OID      string `json:"oid"`
23		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
24		Remote   string `json:"remote,omitempty"`
25	}
26
27	// RecoveryTopology is repository-wide publication structure. It deliberately
28	// does not claim that matching names mean the commits are backed up; reclaim
29	// performs remote-ref containment checks against this inventory later.
30	type RecoveryTopology struct {
31		Remotes  []RemoteInfo     `json:"remotes"`
32		Branches []BranchUpstream `json:"branches"`
33
34		LocalOnlyBranches []string `json:"local_only_branches,omitempty"`
35		UpstreamRemotes   []string `json:"upstream_remotes,omitempty"`
36	}
37
38	// HasRemote reports whether any remote is configured.
39	func (t RecoveryTopology) HasRemote() bool { return len(t.Remotes) > 0 }
40
41	// MultipleRemotes distinguishes several configured remotes from branches that
42	// merely use different upstreams.
43	func (t RecoveryTopology) MultipleRemotes() bool { return len(t.Remotes) > 1 }
44
45	// MultipleUpstreams reports local branches tracking more than one remote.
46	func (t RecoveryTopology) MultipleUpstreams() bool { return len(t.UpstreamRemotes) > 1 }
47
48	// Summary is the compact CLI/TUI form. Local-only branches remain visible even
49	// when a repository has one or more remotes.
50	func (t RecoveryTopology) Summary() string {
51		if len(t.Remotes) == 0 {
52			if len(t.LocalOnlyBranches) > 0 {
53				return fmt.Sprintf("none · local:%d", len(t.LocalOnlyBranches))
54			}
55			return "none"
56		}
57		names := make([]string, len(t.Remotes))
58		for index, remote := range t.Remotes {
59			names[index] = remote.Name
60		}
61		summary := strings.Join(names, ",")
62		if len(t.LocalOnlyBranches) > 0 {
63			summary += fmt.Sprintf(" · local:%d", len(t.LocalOnlyBranches))
64		}
65		return summary
66	}
67
68	// RecoveryTopologyOf reads all configured remotes and every local branch's
69	// upstream. Two Git processes cover the repository regardless of branch count.
70	func RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (RecoveryTopology, error) {
71		remoteOutput, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "-v")
72		if err != nil {
73			return RecoveryTopology{}, err
74		}
75		branchOutput, err := run(ctx, dir, "for-each-ref",
76			"--format=%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:remotename)",
77			"refs/heads")
78		if err != nil {
79			return RecoveryTopology{}, err
80		}
81
82		topology := RecoveryTopology{Remotes: parseRemoteInventory(remoteOutput)}
83		configured := make(map[string]struct{}, len(topology.Remotes))
84		for _, remote := range topology.Remotes {
85			configured[remote.Name] = struct{}{}
86		}
87		upstreamRemotes := map[string]struct{}{}
88		for _, line := range strings.Split(branchOutput, "\n") {
89			if line == "" {
90				continue
91			}
92			fields := strings.Split(line, "\x00")
93			if len(fields) != 4 {
94				return RecoveryTopology{}, fmt.Errorf("parse branch upstream record %q", line)
95			}
96			branch := BranchUpstream{
97				Branch: fields[0], OID: fields[1], Upstream: fields[2], Remote: fields[3],
98			}
99			topology.Branches = append(topology.Branches, branch)
100			_, remoteConfigured := configured[branch.Remote]
101			if branch.Upstream == "" || branch.Remote == "" || branch.Remote == "." || !remoteConfigured {
102				topology.LocalOnlyBranches = append(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, branch.Branch)
103				continue
104			}
105			upstreamRemotes[branch.Remote] = struct{}{}
106		}
107		for remote := range upstreamRemotes {
108			topology.UpstreamRemotes = append(topology.UpstreamRemotes, remote)
109		}
110		sort.Strings(topology.UpstreamRemotes)
111		sort.Strings(topology.LocalOnlyBranches)
112		sort.Slice(topology.Branches, func(i, j int) bool { return topology.Branches[i].Branch < topology.Branches[j].Branch })
113		return topology, nil
114	}
115
116	func parseRemoteInventory(output string) []RemoteInfo {
117		byName := map[string]*RemoteInfo{}
118		for _, line := range strings.Split(output, "\n") {
119			name, rest, ok := strings.Cut(line, "\t")
120			if !ok || name == "" {
121				continue
122			}
123			kind := ""
124			switch {
125			case strings.HasSuffix(rest, " (fetch)"):
126				kind = "fetch"
127				rest = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, " (fetch)")
128			case strings.HasSuffix(rest, " (push)"):
129				kind = "push"
130				rest = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, " (push)")
131			default:
132				continue
133			}
134			remote := byName[name]
135			if remote == nil {
136				remote = &RemoteInfo{Name: name}
137				byName[name] = remote
138			}
139			switch kind {
140			case "fetch":
141				remote.FetchURLs = appendUnique(remote.FetchURLs, rest)
142			case "push":
143				remote.PushURLs = appendUnique(remote.PushURLs, rest)
144			}
145		}
146		names := make([]string, 0, len(byName))
147		for name := range byName {
148			names = append(names, name)
149		}
150		sort.Strings(names)
151		remotes := make([]RemoteInfo, 0, len(names))
152		for _, name := range names {
153			remote := *byName[name]
154			sort.Strings(remote.FetchURLs)
155			sort.Strings(remote.PushURLs)
156			remotes = append(remotes, remote)
157		}
158		return remotes
159	}
160
161	func appendUnique(values []string, value string) []string {
162		for _, current := range values {
163			if current == value {
164				return values
165			}
166		}
167		return append(values, value)
168	}
169
```

```text
1	package config

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	)
7
8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}
```

```text
85	// reportDetection explains what was found, so the user can see whether the

87	func reportDetection(app *App, l config.Layout) {

97			switch r {
98			case l.ProjectRoot:
99				role = "scan root, new projects land here"
100			case l.TriesRoot:
101				role = "scan root, experiments"
102			}
103			t.Add(r, fmt.Sprintf("%d", l.Found[r]), role)
104		}

116	// renderStarterConfig fills the annotated template with detected paths. Paths
117	// are written with forward slashes: a Windows path in a TOML basic string would
118	// otherwise read "C:\Users" as an invalid \U escape, and Go accepts / on every
119	// platform.
120	func renderStarterConfig(l config.Layout) string {
121		roots := make([]string, len(l.ScanRoots))
122		for i, r := range l.ScanRoots {
123			roots[i] = strconv.Quote(filepath.ToSlash(r))
124		}
125		r := strings.NewReplacer(
126			"@@SCAN_ROOTS@@", strings.Join(roots, ", "),
127			"@@REPO_PATHS@@", quotedStrings(l.RepoPaths),
128			"@@TRIES_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.TriesRoot),
129			"@@PROJECT_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.ProjectRoot),
130			"@@WORKTREE_ROOT@@", filepath.ToSlash(l.WorktreeRoot),
131		)
132		return r.Replace(starterConfig)
133	}

135	func quotedStrings(values []string) string {
136		quoted := make([]string, len(values))
137		for index, value := range values {
138			quoted[index] = strconv.Quote(filepath.ToSlash(value))
139		}
140		return strings.Join(quoted, ", ")
141	}

143	const starterConfig = `# dev configuration.
144	#
145	# The paths below were detected on this machine by "dev config init"; everything
146	# else is dev's built-in default. Delete anything you do not want to override.
147
148	[paths]
149	# Where dev looks for repositories. Each root is scanned to a depth of 3, so
150	# both <root>/<Repo> and <root>/<Category>/<Repo> are found.
151	scan_roots = [@@SCAN_ROOTS@@]
152
153	# Exact repositories which do not sit below a useful scan root. Exact paths
154	# are considered first and may point through a symlink navigation alias.
155	repo_paths = [@@REPO_PATHS@@]
156
157	# Where "dev try" creates dated experiment directories.
158	tries_root = "@@TRIES_ROOT@@"
159
160	# Where "dev repo clone|new" and "dev graduate" place real projects.
161	project_root = "@@PROJECT_ROOT@@"
162
163	# Where linked worktrees live. Keep this OUTSIDE any repository: a checkout
164	# nested inside another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and ripgrep
165	# run see a second copy of the tree.
166	#
167	# Put it wherever suits the machine — a faster volume, a larger disk:
168	#   worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
169	worktree_root = "@@WORKTREE_ROOT@@"
170
171	# The full path template. Variables: worktree_root, repo, repo_path, branch,
172	# category, host, date. Filters: |slug (filesystem-safe), |lower, |base.
173	#
174	#   "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}"        ~/Worktrees/api/feat-auth
175	#   "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}" flat, one directory deep
176	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}"
177
178	# Task registry, stats database and caches. Point this at a private git repo to
179	# carry your "what am I working on" state between machines.
180	# state_dir = "~/.local/share/dev"
181
182	[runtime]
183	# auto prefers herdr, then tmux, then zellij, then none. "none" makes dev print a cd
184	# directive for the shell wrapper instead of opening a session.
185	backend = "auto"
186
187	# Namespace for the workspace metadata dev reports (herdr only).
188	metadata_source = "dev"
189
190	[worktree]
191	# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH
192	# matched here AND gitignored are copied: a tracked file is already in the new
193	# checkout on the correct branch, so listing it would overwrite it.
194	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
195
196	# Directories to symlink instead of copying. Opt-in and empty by default:
197	# sharing node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that
198	# it must never happen by accident.
199	link = []
200
201	# "auto" detects from lockfiles (uv.lock -> uv sync, package-lock.json ->
202	# npm ci, go.mod -> go mod download, ...). Or give an explicit list:
203	#   post_create = ["uv sync", "pre-commit install"]
204	post_create = "auto"
205
206	# How a new worktree gets its installed dependencies:
207	#   reinstall  run the install command (always correct, can be slow)
208	#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)
209	#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, and risky)
210	#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies
211	#
212	# dev narrows an unsound choice back to reinstall and says why — copying a
213	# virtualenv cannot work, because it bakes its own absolute path into
214	# pyvenv.cfg and bin/activate.
215	strategy = "reinstall"
216
217	# Per project type. See what applies to a given repo with "dev wt plan".
218	# [worktree.strategies]
219	# node = "copy"       # node_modules copies soundly and reinstalling is slow
220
221	# Cap on a single post-create command.
222	provision_timeout = "10m"
223
224	[forge]
225	# The complete REMOTE inventory is cached privately. Fresh cache is reused;
226	# stale cache is shown immediately while the TUI refreshes in the background.
227	cache_ttl = "15m"
228
229	# Azure DevOps inventory is opt-in because az repos list requires both an
230	# organization and a team project. Repeat this table for every project wanted.
231	# [[forge.azure_devops]]
232	# organization = "https://dev.azure.com/acme"
233	# project = "Platform"
234
235	[bootstrap]
236	# Recursive scan policy. Zero max_depth means unlimited; the default reaches
237	# flat, Category/Repo and ghq host/owner/Repo layouts.
238	max_depth = 8
239	follow_symlinks = true
240
241	# Optional non-destructive symlink catalog. Leave empty until wanted; once set,
242	# a plain "dev bootstrap" includes its plan and "dev bootstrap --apply" syncs it.
243	# Put this path first in paths.scan_roots if the catalog should be the UI.
244	index_root = ""
245	layout = "flat"              # flat | preserve
246	relative_links = false
247
248	[tui]
249
250	[tui.repos]
251	# Exact columns and order for the local repository view:
252	# repo | branch | git | remote | size | live | latest | worktrees | tasks | notes | category | path
253	# "notes" is opt-in to preserve width; selected detail shows it regardless.
254	columns = ["repo", "branch", "git", "size", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"]
255	# activity puts HOT/live/dirty repos first. Other values: latest, name, git, size, tasks.
256	sort = "activity"
257	reverse = false
258
259	# External programs the dashboard hands the terminal to, each on its own key.
260	# They run through your shell in the selected row's checkout, so arguments,
261	# environment variables and your own scripts all behave as typed.
262	#
263	# Listed in full rather than left implicit: what is bound should be something
264	# you can read, not something you discover by pressing keys. Replace freely —
265	# a configured list replaces these entirely. See "dev tui tools".
266	#
267	# Keys are case-sensitive, and cannot take one the dashboard already uses
268	# (j k g G h l tab / enter o p c s d a r q e H O R 0 1 2 3 ?); dev reports a clash on load.
269
270	[[tui.tools]]
271	key  = "L"
272	name = "lazygit"
273	run  = "lazygit"
274
275	[[tui.tools]]
276	key  = "Y"
277	name = "yazi"
278	run  = "yazi"
279
280	[[tui.tools]]
281	key  = "E"
282	name = "editor"
283	run  = "$EDITOR ."
284
285	[[tui.tools]]
286	key  = "S"
287	name = "shell"
288	run  = "$SHELL"
289
290	# Add your own — an editor, a script, an alias you already reach for:
291	#
292	# [[tui.tools]]
293	# key  = "V"
294	# name = "nvim"
295	# run  = "nvim ."
296	#
297	# [[tui.tools]]
298	# key  = "B"
299	# name = "vibe"
300	# run  = "vibe"
301	# interactive = true   # load + evaluate aliases/functions after the rc file
302	#
303	# [[tui.tools]]
304	# key  = "P"
305	# name = "plans here"
306	# run  = "claude-plans-here"
307	# interactive = true
308
309	[stats]
310	# Record activity locally for "dev stats --heatmap".
311	sampler = true
312
313	# Also import durations from WakaTime, which covers editor time dev cannot see.
314	wakatime = false
315	wakatime_config = "~/.wakatime.cfg"
316	`
317
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6
7	import (
8		"crypto/sha256"
9		"encoding/binary"
10		"encoding/hex"
11		"fmt"
12		"strings"
13		"time"
14	)
15
16	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
17	type State string
18
19	const (
20		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
21		Hot State = "hot"
22		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
23		Warm State = "warm"
24		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
25		Cold State = "cold"
26		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
27		Done State = "done"
28	)
29
30	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.

33	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.

84	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.

94		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
95		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
96		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
97		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
98		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
99		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
100		// integrate without re-guessing.
101		Base string `toml:"base"`
102		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
103		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
104		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
105		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
106		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
107		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
108
109		State State `toml:"state"`
110		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
111		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
112		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
113		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
114		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
115		Next string   `toml:"next"`
116		Note string   `toml:"note"`
117		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
118
119		// AgentSession reserves a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"). The
120		// production start/park/resume flow does not yet capture or attach it.
121		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
122		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a Herdr
123		// workspace id). RuntimeName records which backend owns that opaque handle.
124		// Both are advisory and must be revalidated against live checkout coverage.
125		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
126		RuntimeName   string `toml:"runtime_name"`
127
128		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
129		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
130
131		// storedRevision is populated only by Store after a successful read/write.
132		// It never enters TOML or Revision and lets legacy Save callers participate
133		// in compare-and-swap without adding a persisted field older binaries erase.
134		storedRevision string

137	// Revision returns a deterministic fingerprint of the task identity and every
138	// field represented by its TOML record. It is deliberately computed rather
139	// than persisted: older dev binaries can continue to read and rewrite task
140	// files without erasing a revision field they do not know about.
141	func (t Task) Revision() string {
142		hash := sha256.New()
143		writeString := func(value string) {
144			var length [8]byte
145			binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(length[:], uint64(len(value)))
146			_, _ = hash.Write(length[:])
147			_, _ = hash.Write([]byte(value))
148		}
149		writeTime := func(value time.Time) {
150			writeString(value.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))
151		}
152
153		writeString("dev-task-revision-v1")
154		writeString(t.ID)
155		writeString(t.Name)
156		writeString(t.Repo)
157		writeString(t.RepoPath)
158		writeString(t.Branch)
159		writeString(t.Base)
160		writeString(t.WorktreePath)
161		writeString(string(t.Mode))
162		writeString(string(t.State))
163		writeString(t.Owner)
164		writeString(t.Next)
165		writeString(t.Note)
166		writeString(fmt.Sprint(len(t.Tags)))
167		for _, tag := range t.Tags {
168			writeString(tag)
169		}
170		writeString(t.AgentSession)
171		writeString(t.RuntimeHandle)
172		writeString(t.RuntimeName)
173		writeTime(t.Created)
174		writeTime(t.Updated)
175
176		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil))
177	}

179	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
180	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
181	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
182	// semantics and must be explicit.
183	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
184		if t.Mode != "" {

186		}
187		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
188			return ModeWorktree
189		}
190		return ModeBranch
191	}

193	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
194	func (t Task) Title() string {

197		}
198		return t.Branch

203	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }

205	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
206	func (t Task) Validate() error {

209				return fmt.Errorf("task ID: %w", err)

211		}
212		switch {

217		case t.RepoPath == "":

224		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
225		default:
226			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
227		}
228		return nil
229	}
```

```text
76	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
77	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {

80			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
81				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
82			}
83			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
84		}
85		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
86		if r == "" {

88		}
89		if b == "" {
90			b = "branch"
91		}
92		return r + "__" + b
93	}

97	// Save creates a task or updates one read by this Store. Existing-task writes
98	// compare the task's private loaded revision under the cross-process lock, so
99	// legacy callers cannot silently overwrite a newer process's mutation.
100	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
101		candidate, err := prepareCandidate(t, true)
102		if err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		err = s.withMutationLock(func() error {
106			current, currentErr := s.get(candidate.ID)
107			switch {
108			case currentErr == nil:

110					return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
111				}

114				}

116				if candidate.storedRevision != "" {

128		})
129		if err != nil {
130			return err
131		}
132		*t = *candidate
133		return nil
134	}
```

```text
252	func prepareCandidate(t *Task, deriveID bool) (*Task, error) {
253		if t == nil {

258		if candidate.ID == "" && deriveID {

278	func (s *Store) withMutationLock(operation func() error) error {

285	func (s *Store) writeAtomic(t *Task) error {
286		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
287			return fmt.Errorf("create task state directory: %w", err)
288		}
289		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
290		if err != nil {
291			return fmt.Errorf("create task %s temp file: %w", t.ID, err)
292		}
293		name := tmp.Name()
294		defer os.Remove(name)
295		if err := tmp.Chmod(0o644); err != nil {
296			_ = tmp.Close()
297			return fmt.Errorf("set task %s file mode: %w", t.ID, err)
298		}
299		if err := toml.NewEncoder(tmp).Encode(t); err != nil {
300			_ = tmp.Close()
301			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
302		}
303		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
304			_ = tmp.Close()
305			return fmt.Errorf("sync task %s temp file: %w", t.ID, err)
306		}
307		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
308			return fmt.Errorf("close task %s temp file: %w", t.ID, err)
309		}
310		if err := replaceFile(name, s.path(t.ID)); err != nil {
311			return fmt.Errorf("replace task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
312		}
313		if err := errors.Join(syncDirectory(s.Dir), syncDirectory(filepath.Dir(s.Dir))); err != nil {
314			return fmt.Errorf("sync task %s directory: %w", t.ID, err)
315		}
316		return nil
317	}

319	// List loads every valid task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
320	// It retains the historical warning behavior; completeness-sensitive callers
321	// should use ListWithDiagnostics instead of treating a partial list as whole.
322	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
323		tasks, diagnostics, err := s.ListWithDiagnostics()
324		if err != nil {
325			return nil, err
326		}
327		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
328			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: %s\n", diagnostic.Error())
329		}
330		return tasks, nil
331	}

333	// ListWithDiagnostics returns every valid task plus deterministic per-record
334	// errors. A corrupt record never hides valid work and never silently satisfies
335	// an inventory-completeness gate.
336	func (s *Store) ListWithDiagnostics() ([]*Task, []Diagnostic, error) {
337		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
338		if err != nil {
339			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
340				return nil, nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
341			}
342			return nil, nil, err
343		}
344		var tasks []*Task
345		var diagnostics []Diagnostic
346		for _, entry := range entries {
347			name := entry.Name()
348			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
349				continue
350			}
351			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
352			tracked, err := s.Get(id)
353			if err != nil {
354				diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err})
355				continue
356			}
357			tasks = append(tasks, tracked)
358		}
359		Sort(tasks)
360		sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
361		return tasks, diagnostics, nil
362	}

385	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
386	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
387	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
388	// than a silent pick.
389	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
390		if ref == "" {
391			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
392		}
393		all, err := s.List()
394		if err != nil {
395			return nil, err
396		}
397		for _, t := range all {
398			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
399				return t, nil
400			}
401		}
402		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
403		var hits []*Task
404		for _, t := range all {
405			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
406			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
407				hits = append(hits, t)
408			}
409		}
410		switch len(hits) {
411		case 1:
412			return hits[0], nil
413		case 0:
414			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
415		default:
416			names := make([]string, len(hits))
417			for i, t := range hits {
418				names[i] = t.ID
419			}
420			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
421		}
422	}
```

```text
 // Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
 // exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
 // branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
 // than a silent pick.
 func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
    if ref == "" {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
    }
    all, err := s.List()
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    for _, t := range all {
        if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
            return t, nil
        }
    }
    needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
    var hits []*Task
    for _, t := range all {
        hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
        if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
            hits = append(hits, t)
        }
    }
    switch len(hits) {
    case 1:
        return hits[0], nil
    case 0:
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
    default:
        names := make([]string, len(hits))
        for i, t := range hits {
            names[i] = t.ID
        }
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
    }
 }

 // Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
 // change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
 // the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
 // worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
 package task

 import (
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/binary"

 // State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
 type State string

 const (
    // Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
    Hot State = "hot"
    // Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
    Warm State = "warm"
    // Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
    Cold State = "cold"
    // Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
    Done State = "done"
 )

 // States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
 var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}

 // ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
 func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
    got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
    for _, valid := range States {
        if got == valid {
            return got, nil
        }
    }
    return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
 }

 // JoinStates renders the valid state names.
 func JoinStates(sep string) string {
    parts := make([]string, len(States))
    for i, s := range States {
        parts[i] = string(s)
    }
    return strings.Join(parts, sep)

 }

 // EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
 // modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
 // branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
 // semantics and must be explicit.
 func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
    if t.Mode != "" {
        return t.Mode
    }
    if t.WorktreePath != "" {
        return ModeWorktree
    }
    return ModeBranch
 }

 // Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
 func (t Task) Title() string {
    if t.Name != "" {
        return t.Name
    }
    return t.Branch
 }

 // OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
 // unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
 func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }

 // Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
 func (t Task) Validate() error {
+	if t.ID != "" {
+		if err := ValidateID(t.ID); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("task ID: %w", err)
+		}
+	}
    switch {
    case t.Repo == "":
        return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
    case t.Branch == "":
        return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
    case t.RepoPath == "":
        return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
    }
    if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
    }
    switch t.Mode {
    case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
    default:
        return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
    }
    return nil
 }
```

```text
1	package forge

4		"encoding/json"

7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"time"
10	)
11
12	// Cache is the on-disk forge inventory. It exists for UI latency, not as a
13	// source of truth: the REMOTE tab should open instantly, and r refreshes it.
14	type Cache struct {
15		Version   int                     `json:"version,omitempty"`
16		FetchedAt time.Time               `json:"fetched_at"`
17		Complete  bool                    `json:"complete,omitempty"`
18		Providers map[Kind]ProviderStatus `json:"providers,omitempty"`
19		Repos     []RemoteRepo            `json:"repos"`
20	}
21
22	const CacheVersion = 2
23
24	type ProviderStatus struct {
25		FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at,omitempty"`
26		Complete  bool      `json:"complete"`
27		Error     string    `json:"error,omitempty"`
28	}
29
30	// LoadCache returns only a fresh, complete cache. TUI callers that can label
31	// stale rows while refreshing use LoadCacheAny instead.
32	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
33		c, ok := LoadCacheAny(path)
34		if !ok || !c.Fresh(maxAge) {
35			return Cache{}, false
36		}
37		return c, true
38	}
39
40	// LoadCacheAny returns a cache regardless of age or completeness. This powers
41	// stale-while-revalidate UI behavior; callers must inspect Fresh/Complete.
42	func LoadCacheAny(path string) (Cache, bool) {
43		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
44		if err != nil {
45			return Cache{}, false
46		}
47		var c Cache
48		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil || c.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
49			return Cache{}, false
50		}
51		if c.Version == 0 {
52			// Version 1 caches were valid snapshots but capped per provider, so they
53			// are useful for instant display and must immediately be refreshed.
54			c.Complete = false
55		}
56		return c, true
57	}
58
59	func (c Cache) Fresh(maxAge time.Duration) bool {
60		if c.Version != CacheVersion || !c.Complete {
61			return false
62		}
63		if maxAge <= 0 {
64			return true
65		}
66		if len(c.Providers) == 0 {
67			return time.Since(c.FetchedAt) <= maxAge
68		}
69		for _, provider := range c.Providers {
70			if !provider.Complete || provider.Error != "" || provider.FetchedAt.IsZero() || time.Since(provider.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
71				return false
72			}
73		}
74		return true
75	}
76
77	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
78	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
79	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
80		now := time.Now().UTC()
81		providers := map[Kind]ProviderStatus{}
82		for _, repo := range repos {
83			providers[repo.Forge] = ProviderStatus{FetchedAt: now, Complete: true}
84		}
85		return SaveCacheState(path, Cache{Version: CacheVersion, FetchedAt: now, Complete: true, Providers: providers, Repos: repos})
86	}
87
88	// SaveCacheState atomically replaces the versioned inventory cache.
89	func SaveCacheState(path string, cache Cache) error {
90		if path == "" {
91			return errors.New("empty cache path")
92		}
93		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
94			return err
95		}
96		if cache.Version == 0 {
97			cache.Version = CacheVersion
98		}
99		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
100			cache.FetchedAt = time.Now().UTC()
101		}
102		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(cache, "", "  ")
103		if err != nil {
104			return err
105		}
106		b = append(b, '\n')
107		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
108		if err != nil {
109			return err
110		}
111		name := tmp.Name()
112		defer os.Remove(name)
113		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
114			tmp.Close()
115			return err
116		}
117		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
118			return err
119		}
120		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		return os.Rename(name, path)
124	}
125
126	// CacheExists reports whether any cache file exists, even stale. Used only for
127	// diagnostics.
128	func CacheExists(path string) bool {
129		_, err := os.Stat(path)
130		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
131	}
```

```text
108	func TestFleetFilesFakeSSHProcess(t *testing.T) {
109		if os.Getenv("DEV_FAKE_SSH") != "1" {
110			return
111		}
112		remoteCommand := os.Args[len(os.Args)-1]
113		helper := ""
114		for _, candidate := range []string{"_capability", "_files-plan", "_files-apply"} {
115			if strings.Contains(remoteCommand, "'"+candidate+"'") {
116				helper = candidate
117				break
118			}
119		}
120		if helper == "" {
121			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "unsupported fake SSH command")
122			os.Exit(127)
123		}
124		log, err := os.OpenFile(os.Getenv("DEV_FAKE_SSH_LOG"), os.O_CREATE|os.O_APPEND|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
125		if err == nil {
126			fmt.Fprintln(log, helper)
127			_ = log.Close()
128		}
129		remoteHome := os.Getenv("DEV_FAKE_SSH_REMOTE_HOME")
130		_ = os.Setenv("HOME", remoteHome)
131		_ = os.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(remoteHome, ".config"))
132		_ = os.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(remoteHome, ".local", "share"))
133		_ = os.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(remoteHome, ".cache"))
134		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
135		root.SetArgs([]string{"--config", os.Getenv("DEV_FAKE_SSH_TARGET_CONFIG"), "fleet", helper})
136		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
137			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "remote protocol failed")
138			os.Exit(2)
139		}
140		os.Exit(0)
141	}

169			t.Fatalf("configured pin = %v", report.ConfiguredMachineID)

172		writeFleetFilesRemotes(t, h.remotes, fakeWrongMachine)
173		if report := assertState("mismatch"); report.ConfiguredMachineID == nil || *report.ConfiguredMachineID != fakeWrongMachine {
174			t.Fatalf("mismatched configured pin = %v", report.ConfiguredMachineID)
175		}
176
177		writeFleetFilesRemotes(t, h.remotes, "")
178		if report := assertState("unpinned"); report.ConfiguredMachineID != nil {
179			t.Fatalf("unpinned report exposed configured value %v", report.ConfiguredMachineID)
180		}
181		out, errOut, err := h.run("fleet", "machine-id", "target")
182		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(out, fakeTargetMachine) || !strings.Contains(out, "unpinned") || !strings.Contains(out, "machine_id =") {
183			t.Fatalf("human machine-id output = %q, stderr=%q, err=%v", out, errOut, err)

354	func assertNoSecretBelow(t *testing.T, root, secret string) {
```

```text
19	const SchemaVersion = 1
20
21	type document struct {
22		SchemaVersion int    `json:"schema_version"`
23		MachineID     string `json:"machine_id"`
24	}
25
26	type Store struct {
27		Path     string
28		generate func() string
29	}
30
31	func DefaultPath() string {
32		return filepath.Join(devconfig.DataHome(), "dev", "machine", "v1", "identity.json")
33	}
34
35	func NewStore(path string) *Store {
36		if path == "" {
37			path = DefaultPath()
38		}
39		if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path); err == nil {
40			path = absolute
41		}
42		return &Store{Path: filepath.Clean(path), generate: uuid.NewString}
43	}
44
45	// LoadOrCreate returns this machine's stable ID from the default private store.
46	func LoadOrCreate(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
47		return NewStore("").LoadOrCreate(ctx)
48	}
49
50	func Validate(value string) error {
51		parsed, err := uuid.Parse(value)
52		if err != nil || parsed == uuid.Nil || parsed.String() != value {
53			return fmt.Errorf("machine_id %q is not a canonical non-zero UUID", value)
54		}
55		return nil
56	}
57
58	func (s *Store) Load() (string, error) {
59		if s == nil || s.Path == "" {
60			return "", errors.New("load machine identity from nil store")
61		}
62		if err := checkPrivateDir(filepath.Dir(s.Path)); err != nil {
63			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect machine identity directory: %w", err)
64		}
65		info, err := os.Lstat(s.Path)
66		if err != nil {
67			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect machine identity: %w", err)
68		}
69		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
70			return "", fmt.Errorf("machine identity %s is not a regular file", s.Path)
71		}
72		private, err := privateModeMatches(s.Path, info.Mode(), 0o600)
73		if err != nil {
74			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect machine identity permissions: %w", err)
75		}
76		if !private {
77			return "", fmt.Errorf("machine identity %s permissions are not private (want 0600 or a protected owner-only policy)", s.Path)
78		}
79		file, err := os.Open(s.Path)
80		if err != nil {
81			return "", fmt.Errorf("open machine identity: %w", err)
82		}
83		defer file.Close()
84		decoder := json.NewDecoder(file)
85		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
86		var payload document
87		if err := decoder.Decode(&payload); err != nil {
88			return "", fmt.Errorf("decode machine identity: %w", err)
89		}
90		var extra any
91		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
92			if err == nil {
93				return "", errors.New("decode machine identity: multiple JSON values")
94			}
95			return "", fmt.Errorf("decode machine identity trailing data: %w", err)
96		}
97		if payload.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("machine identity schema_version %d: want %d", payload.SchemaVersion, SchemaVersion)
99		}
100		if err := Validate(payload.MachineID); err != nil {
101			return "", err
102		}
103		return payload.MachineID, nil
104	}
105
106	func (s *Store) LoadOrCreate(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
107		if s == nil || s.Path == "" {
108			return "", errors.New("create machine identity with nil store")
109		}
110		if ctx == nil {
111			ctx = context.Background()
112		}
113		directory := filepath.Dir(s.Path)
114		if err := ensurePrivateDir(directory); err != nil {
115			return "", fmt.Errorf("prepare machine identity directory: %w", err)
116		}
117		lockDirectory := filepath.Join(directory, ".lock")
118		if err := ensurePrivateDir(lockDirectory); err != nil {
119			return "", fmt.Errorf("prepare machine identity lock: %w", err)
120		}
121		var result string
122		err := lockx.WithDir(ctx, lockDirectory, "machine identity", func() error {
123			loaded, err := s.Load()
124			if err == nil {
125				result = loaded
126				return nil
127			}
128			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
129				return err
130			}
131			generate := s.generate
132			if generate == nil {
133				generate = uuid.NewString
134			}
135			candidate := generate()
136			if err := Validate(candidate); err != nil {
137				return fmt.Errorf("generate machine identity: %w", err)
138			}
139			if err := s.write(candidate); err != nil {
140				return err
141			}
142			result = candidate
143			return nil
144		})
145		return result, err
146	}
147
148	func (s *Store) write(id string) error {
149		if err := Validate(id); err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		directory := filepath.Dir(s.Path)
153		if err := ensurePrivateDir(directory); err != nil {
154			return err
155		}
156		temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(directory, ".identity-*.tmp")
157		if err != nil {
158			return fmt.Errorf("create machine identity temp file: %w", err)
159		}
160		name := temporary.Name()
161		defer os.Remove(name)
162		if err := setPrivateMode(name, 0o600); err != nil {
163			_ = temporary.Close()
164			return err
165		}
166		encoder := json.NewEncoder(temporary)
167		encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
168		if err := encoder.Encode(document{SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, MachineID: id}); err != nil {
169			_ = temporary.Close()
170			return fmt.Errorf("encode machine identity: %w", err)
171		}
172		if err := temporary.Sync(); err != nil {
173			_ = temporary.Close()
174			return fmt.Errorf("sync machine identity: %w", err)
175		}
176		if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
177			return fmt.Errorf("close machine identity: %w", err)
178		}
179		if err := replaceFile(name, s.Path); err != nil {
180			return fmt.Errorf("publish machine identity: %w", err)
181		}
182		if err := syncDirectory(directory); err != nil {
183			return fmt.Errorf("sync machine identity directory: %w", err)
184		}
185		return nil
186	}
187
188	func ensurePrivateDir(path string) error {
189		created := false
190		if _, err := os.Lstat(path); errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
191			if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o700); err != nil {
192				return err
193			}
194			created = true
195		} else if err != nil {
196			return err
197		}
198		if created {
199			if err := setPrivateMode(path, 0o700); err != nil {
200				return err
201			}
202		}
203		return checkPrivateDir(path)
204	}
205
206	func checkPrivateDir(path string) error {
207		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
208		if err != nil {
209			return err
210		}
211		if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
212			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a private directory", path)
213		}
214		private, err := privateModeMatches(path, info.Mode(), 0o700)
215		if err != nil {
216			return fmt.Errorf("inspect machine identity directory permissions: %w", err)
217		}
218		if !private {
219			return fmt.Errorf("machine identity directory %s permissions are not private (want 0700 or a protected owner-only policy)", path)
220		}
221		return nil
222	}
```

```text
1	package fleet

4		"bytes"

10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/machineid"

13	const (
14		// ProtocolSchemaVersion is the outer schema shared by new bounded fleet
15		// protocols. Feature protocol versions evolve independently inside it.
16		ProtocolSchemaVersion = 1
17		// LocalFilesProtocolVersion is the first portable local-file protocol.
18		LocalFilesProtocolVersion = 1
19		// MaxCapabilityBytes bounds either side of capability negotiation.
20		MaxCapabilityBytes int64 = 16 << 10
21	)
22
23	var ErrProtocolLimit = errors.New("fleet protocol size limit exceeded")
24
25	// FileLimits is the wire representation of a target's downward-clamped
26	// portable-file policy. It deliberately does not carry include patterns.
27	type FileLimits struct {
28		MaxFiles          int   `json:"max_files"`
29		MaxFileBytes      int64 `json:"max_file_bytes"`
30		MaxTotalBytes     int64 `json:"max_total_bytes"`
31		MaxPathBytes      int   `json:"max_path_bytes"`
32		MaxComponentBytes int   `json:"max_component_bytes"`
33		MaxPathDepth      int   `json:"max_path_depth"`
34	}
35
36	func (l FileLimits) Validate() error {
37		switch {
38		case l.MaxFiles <= 0:
39			return errors.New("max_files must be positive")
40		case l.MaxFileBytes <= 0:
41			return errors.New("max_file_bytes must be positive")
42		case l.MaxTotalBytes <= 0:
43			return errors.New("max_total_bytes must be positive")
44		case l.MaxPathBytes <= 0:
45			return errors.New("max_path_bytes must be positive")
46		case l.MaxComponentBytes <= 0:
47			return errors.New("max_component_bytes must be positive")
48		case l.MaxPathDepth <= 0:
49			return errors.New("max_path_depth must be positive")
50		default:
51			return nil
52		}
53	}
54
55	// CapabilityRequest is content-free and is always exchanged before any
56	// feature payload.
57	type CapabilityRequest struct {
58		SchemaVersion   int    `json:"schema_version"`
59		Feature         string `json:"feature"`
60		ProtocolVersion int    `json:"protocol_version"`
61	}
62
63	func LocalFilesCapabilityRequest() CapabilityRequest {
64		return CapabilityRequest{
65			SchemaVersion: ProtocolSchemaVersion, Feature: "local-files",
66			ProtocolVersion: LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
67		}
68	}
69
70	func (r CapabilityRequest) Validate() error {
71		if r.SchemaVersion != ProtocolSchemaVersion {
72			return fmt.Errorf("capability schema_version %d: want %d", r.SchemaVersion, ProtocolSchemaVersion)
73		}
74		if r.Feature != "local-files" {
75			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported capability feature %q", r.Feature)
76		}
77		if r.ProtocolVersion != LocalFilesProtocolVersion {
78			return fmt.Errorf("local-files protocol_version %d: want %d", r.ProtocolVersion, LocalFilesProtocolVersion)
79		}
80		return nil
81	}
82
83	// CapabilityResponse contains only non-secret host facts. Unsupported native
84	// platforms return a stable reason before the caller constructs a payload.
85	type CapabilityResponse struct {
86		SchemaVersion   int        `json:"schema_version"`
87		Feature         string     `json:"feature"`
88		ProtocolVersion int        `json:"protocol_version"`
89		MachineID       string     `json:"machine_id"`
90		Platform        string     `json:"platform"`
91		Supported       bool       `json:"supported"`
92		Reason          string     `json:"reason,omitempty"`
93		Limits          FileLimits `json:"limits"`
94	}
95
96	func (r CapabilityResponse) Validate(request CapabilityRequest) error {
97		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		if r.SchemaVersion != request.SchemaVersion || r.Feature != request.Feature || r.ProtocolVersion != request.ProtocolVersion {
101			return errors.New("capability response does not match the request")
102		}
103		if err := machineid.Validate(r.MachineID); err != nil {
104			return err
105		}
106		if r.Platform == "" {
107			return errors.New("capability response has no platform")
108		}
109		if r.Supported {
110			if r.Reason != "" {
111				return errors.New("supported capability must not include a reason")
112			}
113			if err := r.Limits.Validate(); err != nil {
114				return fmt.Errorf("capability limits: %w", err)
115			}
116		} else if !validCapabilityReason(r.Reason) {
117			return errors.New("unsupported capability has no valid reason code")
118		}
119		return nil
120	}
121
122	func validCapabilityReason(reason string) bool {
123		if reason == "" || len(reason) > 128 {
124			return false
125		}
126		for _, character := range reason {
127			if character >= 'a' && character <= 'z' || character >= '0' && character <= '9' || character == '-' {
128				continue
129			}
130			return false
131		}
132		return true
133	}

135	// DecodeStrict reads exactly one bounded JSON value, rejects unknown fields,
136	// and requires EOF after optional JSON whitespace.
137	func DecodeStrict(reader io.Reader, maxBytes int64, target any) error {
138		if reader == nil || target == nil {
139			return errors.New("fleet protocol decode requires a reader and target")
140		}
141		if maxBytes <= 0 {
142			return errors.New("fleet protocol decode requires a positive limit")
143		}
144		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(reader, maxBytes+1))
145		if err != nil {
146			return fmt.Errorf("read fleet protocol: %w", err)
147		}
148		if int64(len(data)) > maxBytes {
149			return fmt.Errorf("fleet protocol exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrProtocolLimit)
150		}
151		decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
152		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
153		if err := decoder.Decode(target); err != nil {
154			return fmt.Errorf("decode fleet protocol: %w", err)
155		}
156		var extra any
157		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
158			if err == nil {
159				return errors.New("decode fleet protocol: multiple JSON values")
160			}
161			return fmt.Errorf("decode fleet protocol trailing data: %w", err)
162		}
163		return nil
164	}
165
166	// MarshalBounded encodes one protocol value and enforces the matching bound
167	// before it can be handed to Transport.
168	func MarshalBounded(value any, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
169		if maxBytes <= 0 {
170			return nil, errors.New("fleet protocol encode requires a positive limit")
171		}
172		data, err := json.Marshal(value)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, fmt.Errorf("encode fleet protocol: %w", err)
175		}
176		if int64(len(data))+1 > maxBytes {
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fleet protocol exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrProtocolLimit)
178		}
179		return append(data, '\n'), nil
180	}
181
182	// UnmarshalStrict applies DecodeStrict to an in-memory transport response.
183	func UnmarshalStrict(data []byte, maxBytes int64, target any) error {
184		return DecodeStrict(bytes.NewReader(data), maxBytes, target)
185	}
```

```text
115	func resolveFleetOpenRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, request fleet.OpenRequest) (repo.Repo, error) {
116		repositories, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
117		if err != nil {
118			return repo.Repo{}, err
119		}
120		var matches []repo.Repo
121		wantedIdentity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(request.RemoteIdentity)
122		for _, repository := range repositories {
123			if request.Path != "" && (sameCleanPath(request.Path, repository.Path) || sameCleanPath(request.Path, repository.RealPath)) {
124				return repository, nil
125			}
126			if wantedIdentity == "" {
127				continue
128			}
129			topology, topologyErr := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, repository.Path)
130			if topologyErr == nil && matchingSnapshotIdentity(topology, wantedIdentity) {
131				matches = append(matches, repository)
132			}
133		}
134		if len(matches) == 1 {
135			return matches[0], nil
136		}
137		if len(matches) > 1 {
138			return repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("remote identity matches multiple repositories")
139		}
140		return repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("repository %q is no longer discoverable", request.Name)
141	}

143	func matchingSnapshotIdentity(topology gitx.RecoveryTopology, identity string) bool {
144		for _, remote := range topology.Remotes {
145			for _, raw := range append(append([]string{}, remote.FetchURLs...), remote.PushURLs...) {
146				if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw) == identity {
147					return true
148				}
149			}
150		}
151		return false
152	}

192						process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
193						if err := process.Run(); err == nil {

197						}

205	func selectFleetRepository(repositories []fleet.RepoSnapshot, query string) (fleet.RepoSnapshot, error) {
206		for _, repository := range repositories {
207			if query == repository.Name || query == repository.Display || query == repository.Path {
208				return repository, nil
209			}
210			for _, identity := range repository.RemoteIdentities {
211				if query == identity {
212					return repository, nil
213				}
214			}
215		}
216		needle := strings.ToLower(query)
217		var matches []fleet.RepoSnapshot
218		for _, repository := range repositories {
219			haystack := strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{repository.Name, repository.Display, repository.Path, strings.Join(repository.RemoteIdentities, " ")}, " "))
220			if strings.Contains(haystack, needle) {
221				matches = append(matches, repository)
222			}
223		}
224		switch len(matches) {
225		case 1:
226			return matches[0], nil
227		case 0:
228			return fleet.RepoSnapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("remote repository %q not found", query)
229		default:
230			return fleet.RepoSnapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("remote repository %q is ambiguous", query)
```

```text
368		}
```

```text
303	func Build(input BuildInput) (Report, error) {

317				Bare:      input.Context.Repo.Bare, HasGit: input.Context.Repo.HasGit,
318			},

321			Remotes:      []Remote{},
322			Errors:       []CollectionError{},
323		}

326		if input.SelectedCheckout >= 0 && input.SelectedCheckout < len(report.Local.Checkouts) {
327			checkout := report.Local.Checkouts[input.SelectedCheckout]
328			report.SelectedCheckout = &CheckoutSelection{

330				Canonical: checkout.Canonical, Ownership: checkout.Ownership,
331			}
332		} else {
333			message := "selected checkout is not present in the local checkout inventory"
334			if input.SelectionErr != nil {
335				message = cleanError(input.SelectionErr)
336			}
337			report.Errors = append(report.Errors, CollectionError{

344		report.Fleet, report.Errors = buildFleetFacts(now, input.Fleet, localIdentities, report.Errors)
345
346		sources := buildSources(now, input, report)

371		}
372		report.Assessment = assessmentReport
373
374		sort.Slice(report.Errors, func(i, j int) bool {
375			left, right := report.Errors[i], report.Errors[j]
376			return strings.Join([]string{left.Scope, left.Code, left.Subject, left.Message}, "\x00") <
```

```text
321	func prepareFleetSync(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref, requestedRemote string, push bool) (fleet.SyncRequest, fleet.SyncResult, error) {
322		repository, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), ref)
323		if err != nil {
324			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, err
325		}
326		if repository.Bare {
327			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("%s is bare and has no checkout to publish", repository.Display())
328		}
329		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repository.Path)
330		if err != nil {
331			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, err
332		}
333		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
334			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, errors.New("fleet sync requires an attached branch")
335		}
336		if status.Dirty() || status.Conflicted > 0 {
337			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("source checkout must be clean (%s)", status.Summary())
338		}
339		remote := requestedRemote
340		if remote == "" && status.Upstream != "" {
341			remote, _, _ = strings.Cut(status.Upstream, "/")
342		}
343		if remote == "" {
344			remote = "origin"
345		}
346		remoteURL := gitx.Remote(ctx, repository.Path, remote)
347		identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(remoteURL)
348		if identity == "" {
349			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("remote %q has no cross-host identity", remote)
350		}
351		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Path, "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", remote); err != nil {
352			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, err
353		}
354		if push {
355			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Path, "push", "--set-upstream", remote, status.Branch); err != nil {
356				return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", status.Branch, err)
357			}
358		} else {
359			remoteOID, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Path, "rev-parse", "--verify", remote+"/"+status.Branch+"^{commit}")
360			if err != nil {
361				return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("fetched %s/%s is unavailable", remote, status.Branch)
362			}
363			head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
364			if err != nil {
365				return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, err
366			}
367			if head != remoteOID {
368				return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, fmt.Errorf("source HEAD does not equal %s/%s after fetch; push or reconcile it first", remote, status.Branch)
369			}
370		}
371		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
372		if err != nil {
373			return fleet.SyncRequest{}, fleet.SyncResult{}, err
374		}
375		request := fleet.SyncRequest{RemoteIdentity: identity, Branch: status.Branch, ExpectedOID: head}
376		source := fleet.SyncResult{
377			Host: config.Hostname(), State: fleet.SyncCurrent, Repo: repository.Display(), Path: repository.Path,
378			Branch: status.Branch, Remote: remote, BeforeOID: head, AfterOID: head, ExpectedOID: head,
379		}
380		return request, source, nil
```

```text
124	type forgeEndpoint struct {
125		transport string
126		host      string
127		segments  []string
128	}

130	func parseForgeEndpoint(raw string) (forgeEndpoint, bool) {
131		if !safeRawURLText(raw) {
132			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
133		}
134		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
135		if raw == "" {
136			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
137		}
138		if strings.Contains(raw, "://") {
139			u, err := url.Parse(raw)
140			if err != nil || u.Opaque != "" || u.Hostname() == "" || !validWebHost(u.Hostname()) {
141				return forgeEndpoint{}, false
142			}
143			host := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
144			segments, ok := decodeURLPath(u.EscapedPath())
145			if !ok {
146				return forgeEndpoint{}, false
147			}
148			switch strings.ToLower(u.Scheme) {
149			case "https":
150				if u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
151					return forgeEndpoint{}, false
152				}
153				return forgeEndpoint{transport: "https", host: host, segments: segments}, true
154			case "ssh":
155				if u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "22" || u.User == nil || u.User.Username() != "git" {
156					return forgeEndpoint{}, false
157				}
158				if _, hasPassword := u.User.Password(); hasPassword {
159					return forgeEndpoint{}, false
160				}
161				return forgeEndpoint{transport: "ssh", host: host, segments: segments}, true
162			default:
163				return forgeEndpoint{}, false
164			}
165		}
166
167		at := strings.IndexByte(raw, '@')
168		if at <= 0 || raw[:at] != "git" {
169			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
170		}
171		colon := strings.IndexByte(raw[at+1:], ':')
172		if colon < 0 {
173			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
174		}
175		colon += at + 1
176		host := raw[at+1 : colon]
177		if host == "" || strings.ContainsAny(host, `/\\[]:`) || !validWebHost(host) {
178			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
179		}
180		path := stripQueryFragment(raw[colon+1:])
181		segments, ok := decodeURLPath(path)
182		if !ok {
183			return forgeEndpoint{}, false
184		}
185		return forgeEndpoint{transport: "ssh", host: strings.ToLower(host), segments: segments}, true
186	}

188	func parseSafeHTTPS(raw string) (host string, segments []string, safeURL string, ok bool) {
189		if !safeRawURLText(raw) {
190			return "", nil, "", false
191		}
192		u, err := url.Parse(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
193		if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.Opaque != "" || u.Hostname() == "" || !validWebHost(u.Hostname()) {
194			return "", nil, "", false
195		}
196		if u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
197			return "", nil, "", false
198		}
199		segments, ok = decodeURLPath(u.EscapedPath())
200		if !ok {
201			return "", nil, "", false
202		}
203		host = strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
204		return host, segments, buildHTTPSURL(host, segments), true
205	}

207	func decodeURLPath(path string) ([]string, bool) {
208		path = strings.Trim(path, "/")
209		if path == "" {
210			return nil, false
211		}
212		rawSegments := strings.Split(path, "/")
213		segments := make([]string, 0, len(rawSegments))
214		for _, raw := range rawSegments {
215			if raw == "" || hasEncodedSeparator(raw) {
216				return nil, false
217			}
218			decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(raw)
219			if err != nil || decoded == "" || decoded == "." || decoded == ".." || !utf8.ValidString(decoded) ||
220				strings.ContainsAny(decoded, `/\\`) || hasEncodedSeparator(decoded) || containsControl(decoded) {
221				return nil, false
222			}
223			segments = append(segments, decoded)
224		}
225		return segments, true
226	}
227
228	func stripGitSuffix(segments []string) []string {
229		if len(segments) == 0 {
230			return nil
231		}
232		result := append([]string(nil), segments...)
233		result[len(result)-1] = strings.TrimSuffix(result[len(result)-1], ".git")
234		if result[len(result)-1] == "" {
235			return nil
236		}
237		return result
238	}

240	func validRepositorySegments(provider Kind, segments []string) bool {
241		segments = stripGitSuffix(segments)
242		switch provider {
243		case GitHub:
244			return len(segments) == 2
245		case GitLab:
246			return len(segments) >= 2
247		default:
248			return false
249		}
250	}
251
252	func buildHTTPSURL(host string, segments []string) string {
253		return (&url.URL{Scheme: "https", Host: strings.ToLower(host), Path: "/" + strings.Join(segments, "/")}).String()
254	}

256	func safeRawURLText(value string) bool {
257		return utf8.ValidString(value) && !containsControl(value)
258	}
259
260	func containsControl(value string) bool {
261		return strings.IndexFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
262			return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r)
263		}) >= 0
264	}
265
266	func hasEncodedSeparator(value string) bool {
267		current := value
268		for depth := 0; depth < 8; depth++ {
269			lower := strings.ToLower(current)
270			if strings.Contains(lower, "%2f") || strings.Contains(lower, "%5c") {
271				return true
272			}
273			if !strings.ContainsRune(current, '%') {
274				return false
275			}
276			decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(current)
277			if err != nil || decoded == current {
278				return false
279			}
280			current = decoded
281		}
282		// Deeply nested escaping is unnecessary for repository identities and is
283		// ambiguous across clients with different decode counts.
284		return true
285	}
286
287	func stripQueryFragment(value string) string {
288		if index := strings.IndexAny(value, "?#"); index >= 0 {
289			return value[:index]
290		}
291		return value
292	}

299	func webHostPolicy(request WebURLRequest) hostPolicy {
300		policy := hostPolicy{github: map[string]struct{}{}, gitlab: map[string]struct{}{}}
301		for _, host := range append([]string{"github.com", os.Getenv("GH_HOST")}, request.GitHubHosts...) {

306		for _, host := range append([]string{"gitlab.com", os.Getenv("GITLAB_HOST")}, request.GitLabHosts...) {
307			if normalized, ok := normalizeConfiguredHost(host); ok {
308				policy.gitlab[normalized] = struct{}{}
309			}
310		}
311		return policy

314	func (policy hostPolicy) provider(host string, ssh bool) Kind {
315		host = strings.ToLower(host)
316		if configured, decided := policy.configuredProvider(host); decided {
317			return configured
318		}
319		if ssh {
320			// An unconfigured SSH hostname may be an alias whose real web host is
321			// unrelated. Only explicit web-host configuration or public defaults can
322			// authorize an SSH transform.
323			return Unknown
324		}
325		return literalForgeHost(host)
326	}

328	func (policy hostPolicy) identityProvider(host string) Kind {
329		host = strings.ToLower(host)
330		if configured, decided := policy.configuredProvider(host); decided {
331			return configured
332		}
333		// Legacy identity classification may recognize provider-named enterprise
334		// hosts. Unlike DeriveWebURL, this does not manufacture a browser hostname.
335		return literalForgeHost(host)
336	}

338	func (policy hostPolicy) configuredProvider(host string) (Kind, bool) {
339		_, github := policy.github[host]
340		_, gitlab := policy.gitlab[host]
341		switch {
342		case github && gitlab:
343			return Unknown, true
344		case github:
345			return GitHub, true
346		case gitlab:
347			return GitLab, true
348		default:
349			return Unknown, false
350		}
351	}
352
353	func literalForgeHost(host string) Kind {
354		switch {
355		case host == "github.com", strings.HasPrefix(host, "github."):
356			return GitHub
357		case host == "gitlab.com", strings.HasPrefix(host, "gitlab."):
358			return GitLab
359		default:
360			return Unknown
361		}
362	}
363
364	func normalizeConfiguredHost(raw string) (string, bool) {
365		if !safeRawURLText(raw) {
366			return "", false
367		}
368		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
369		if raw == "" {
370			return "", false
371		}
372		if strings.Contains(raw, "://") {
373			u, err := url.Parse(raw)
374			if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil || u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" ||
375				u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/" || u.Hostname() == "" || u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
376				return "", false
377			}
378			raw = u.Hostname()
379		} else if strings.ContainsAny(raw, `/\\@?#`) {
380			return "", false
381		} else {
382			u, err := url.Parse("//" + raw)
383			if err != nil || u.Hostname() == "" || u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
384				return "", false
385			}
386			raw = u.Hostname()
387		}
388		if !validWebHost(raw) || !strings.Contains(raw, ".") {
389			return "", false
390		}
391		return strings.ToLower(raw), true
392	}
393
394	func validWebHost(host string) bool {
395		if host == "" || strings.HasSuffix(host, ".") || !utf8.ValidString(host) {
396			return false
397		}
398		for _, r := range host {
399			if r > unicode.MaxASCII || !(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' || r == '-' || r == '.') {
400				return false
401			}
402		}
403		for _, label := range strings.Split(host, ".") {
404			if label == "" || strings.HasPrefix(label, "-") || strings.HasSuffix(label, "-") {
405				return false
406			}
407		}
408		return true
409	}
```

```text
39		}
40		if strings.ContainsAny(value, "[]{}") {

42		}
43		components := strings.Split(value, "/")
44		if len(components) > safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth {
45			return fmt.Errorf("pattern has %d components; maximum is %d", len(components), safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth)
46		}
47		for _, component := range components {
48			if localFileDependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)] {

50			}
51			if component == "**" {
```
