```text
 func validateRelativePath(value string) error {
    if value == "" {
        return fmt.Errorf("path must not be empty")
    }
    if filepath.IsAbs(value) || filepath.VolumeName(value) != "" {
        return fmt.Errorf("path %q must be repository-relative", value)
    }
    for _, part := range strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool { return r == '/' || r == '\\' }) {
        if part == ".." {
            return fmt.Errorf("path %q contains parent traversal", value)
        }
    }
    if filepath.Clean(value) == "." {
        return fmt.Errorf("path %q names the repository root", value)
    }
```

```text
207	func decodeURLPath(path string) ([]string, bool) {
208		path = strings.Trim(path, "/")
209		if path == "" {
210			return nil, false
211		}
212		rawSegments := strings.Split(path, "/")
213		segments := make([]string, 0, len(rawSegments))
214		for _, raw := range rawSegments {
215			if raw == "" || hasEncodedSeparator(raw) {
216				return nil, false
217			}
218			decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(raw)
219			if err != nil || decoded == "" || decoded == "." || decoded == ".." || !utf8.ValidString(decoded) ||
220				strings.ContainsAny(decoded, `/\\`) || hasEncodedSeparator(decoded) || containsControl(decoded) {
221				return nil, false
222			}
223			segments = append(segments, decoded)
224		}
225		return segments, true
226	}

229		if len(segments) == 0 {

231		}
232		result := append([]string(nil), segments...)
233		result[len(result)-1] = strings.TrimSuffix(result[len(result)-1], ".git")
234		if result[len(result)-1] == "" {

236		}

238	}

245		case GitLab:

266	func hasEncodedSeparator(value string) bool {
267		current := value

269			lower := strings.ToLower(current)
270			if strings.Contains(lower, "%2f") || strings.Contains(lower, "%5c") {
271				return true
272			}
273			if !strings.ContainsRune(current, '%') {
274				return false
275			}
276			decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(current)
277			if err != nil || decoded == current {
278				return false
279			}
280			current = decoded
281		}

283		// ambiguous across clients with different decode counts.
284		return true
285	}

364	func normalizeConfiguredHost(raw string) (string, bool) {
365		if !safeRawURLText(raw) {

367		}
368		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
369		if raw == "" {

371		}
372		if strings.Contains(raw, "://") {
373			u, err := url.Parse(raw)
374			if err != nil || !strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https") || u.User != nil || u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" ||
375				u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/" || u.Hostname() == "" || u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
376				return "", false

379		} else if strings.ContainsAny(raw, `/\\@?#`) {
380			return "", false

383			if err != nil || u.Hostname() == "" || u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {

394	func validWebHost(host string) bool {
395		if host == "" || strings.HasSuffix(host, ".") || !utf8.ValidString(host) {

398		for _, r := range host {
399			if r > unicode.MaxASCII || !(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z' || r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z' || r >= '0' && r <= '9' || r == '-' || r == '.') {
400				return false
401			}
402		}
403		for _, label := range strings.Split(host, ".") {
404			if label == "" || strings.HasPrefix(label, "-") || strings.HasSuffix(label, "-") {
405				return false
406			}
407		}
408		return true
409	}
```

```text
424	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
425	//
426	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
427	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
428	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
429	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
430	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
431	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
432		all, err := s.List()
433		if err != nil {
434			return nil, err
435		}
436		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
437			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
438		}
439		var best *Task
440		var bestLen int
441		for _, t := range all {
442			root := t.WorktreePath
443			if root == "" {
444				root = t.RepoPath
445			}
446			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
447				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
448			}
449		}
450		if best == nil {
451			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
452		}
453		return best, nil
454	}

456	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
457	func stateRank(s State) int {
458		switch s {
459		case Hot:
460			return 0
461		case Warm:
462			return 1
463		case Cold:
464			return 2
465		case Done:
466			return 3
467		}
468		return 4
469	}

471	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
472	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
473		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
474			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
475			if ri != rj {
476				return ri < rj
477			}
478			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
479				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
480			}
481			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
482		})
483	}
```

```text
55	// CapabilityRequest is content-free and is always exchanged before any

58		SchemaVersion   int    `json:"schema_version"`

87		Feature         string     `json:"feature"`

96	func (r CapabilityResponse) Validate(request CapabilityRequest) error {
97		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {

99		}
100		if r.SchemaVersion != request.SchemaVersion || r.Feature != request.Feature || r.ProtocolVersion != request.ProtocolVersion {
101			return errors.New("capability response does not match the request")
102		}
103		if err := machineid.Validate(r.MachineID); err != nil {
104			return err
105		}
106		if r.Platform == "" {

108		}
109		if r.Supported {
110			if r.Reason != "" {
111				return errors.New("supported capability must not include a reason")
112			}
113			if err := r.Limits.Validate(); err != nil {
114				return fmt.Errorf("capability limits: %w", err)
115			}
116		} else if !validCapabilityReason(r.Reason) {

118		}

121
122	func validCapabilityReason(reason string) bool {
123		if reason == "" || len(reason) > 128 {
124			return false
125		}
126		for _, character := range reason {
127			if character >= 'a' && character <= 'z' || character >= '0' && character <= '9' || character == '-' {
128				continue
129			}
130			return false
131		}
132		return true
133	}

135	// DecodeStrict reads exactly one bounded JSON value, rejects unknown fields,
136	// and requires EOF after optional JSON whitespace.
137	func DecodeStrict(reader io.Reader, maxBytes int64, target any) error {
138		if reader == nil || target == nil {
139			return errors.New("fleet protocol decode requires a reader and target")
140		}
141		if maxBytes <= 0 {
142			return errors.New("fleet protocol decode requires a positive limit")
143		}
144		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(reader, maxBytes+1))
145		if err != nil {
146			return fmt.Errorf("read fleet protocol: %w", err)
147		}
148		if int64(len(data)) > maxBytes {
149			return fmt.Errorf("fleet protocol exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrProtocolLimit)
150		}
151		decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
152		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
153		if err := decoder.Decode(target); err != nil {
154			return fmt.Errorf("decode fleet protocol: %w", err)
155		}
156		var extra any
157		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
158			if err == nil {
159				return errors.New("decode fleet protocol: multiple JSON values")
160			}
161			return fmt.Errorf("decode fleet protocol trailing data: %w", err)
162		}
163		return nil
164	}
165
166	// MarshalBounded encodes one protocol value and enforces the matching bound
167	// before it can be handed to Transport.
168	func MarshalBounded(value any, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
169		if maxBytes <= 0 {
170			return nil, errors.New("fleet protocol encode requires a positive limit")
171		}
172		data, err := json.Marshal(value)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, fmt.Errorf("encode fleet protocol: %w", err)
175		}
176		if int64(len(data))+1 > maxBytes {
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fleet protocol exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrProtocolLimit)
178		}
179		return append(data, '\n'), nil
180	}
181
182	// UnmarshalStrict applies DecodeStrict to an in-memory transport response.
183	func UnmarshalStrict(data []byte, maxBytes int64, target any) error {
184		return DecodeStrict(bytes.NewReader(data), maxBytes, target)
185	}
```

```text
16	type cacheFile struct {

23	func CacheRoot() string { return filepath.Join(devconfig.CacheHome(), "dev", "fleet", "v1") }
24
25	func cachePath(host Host) string {
26		name := devconfig.Slug(host.Name)
27		return filepath.Join(CacheRoot(), name+".json")
28	}
29
30	func EndpointID(host Host) string {
31		parts := []string{host.Name, host.MachineID, host.SSHAlias, host.Hostname, host.User, strconv.Itoa(host.Port), host.IdentityFile, host.DevPath}
32		parts = append(parts, time.Duration(host.ConnectTimeout.Duration).String(), time.Duration(host.CommandTimeout.Duration).String())
33		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(strings.Join(parts, "\x00")))
34		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
35	}
36
37	func SaveCache(host Host, snapshot Snapshot) error {
38		path := cachePath(host)
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return err
41		}
42		payload := cacheFile{Version: 1, EndpointID: EndpointID(host), FetchedAt: time.Now().UTC(), Snapshot: snapshot}
43		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(payload, "", "  ")
44		if err != nil {
45			return err
46		}
47		data = append(data, '\n')
48		temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".fleet-*.tmp")
49		if err != nil {
50			return err
51		}
52		name := temporary.Name()
53		defer os.Remove(name)
54		if _, err := temporary.Write(data); err != nil {
55			_ = temporary.Close()
56			return err
57		}
58		if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
59			return err
60		}
61		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
62			return err
63		}
64		return os.Rename(name, path)
65	}
66
67	func LoadCache(host Host) (Snapshot, time.Time, bool) {
68		data, err := os.ReadFile(cachePath(host))
69		if err != nil {
70			return Snapshot{}, time.Time{}, false
71		}
72		var payload cacheFile

74			return Snapshot{}, time.Time{}, false
75		}
76		if payload.Snapshot.SchemaVersion != SnapshotSchemaVersion {
77			return Snapshot{}, time.Time{}, false
78		}
79		return payload.Snapshot, payload.FetchedAt, true
```

```text
31	// MaybeServeAskpass turns the dev executable into a one-shot SSH_ASKPASS

33	func MaybeServeAskpass() (bool, int) {

202	func runSSHCommand(cmd *exec.Cmd, password string) error {
203		if password == "" {
204			return cmd.Run()
205		}
206		executable, err := os.Executable()
207		if err != nil {
208			return err
209		}
210		reader, writer, err := os.Pipe()
211		if err != nil {
212			return err
213		}
214		cmd.ExtraFiles = []*os.File{reader}
215		cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env,
216			askpassMarker+"=1", askpassFD+"=3", "SSH_ASKPASS="+executable,
217			"SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force", "DISPLAY=dev-fleet")
218		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
219			_ = reader.Close()
220			_ = writer.Close()
221			return err
222		}
223		// The child owns its inherited descriptor after Start; closing the parent
224		// copy lets an early SSH exit interrupt a blocked write.
225		readerCloseErr := reader.Close()
226		writeDone := make(chan error, 1)
227		go func() {
228			_, writeErr := io.Copy(writer, strings.NewReader(password+"\n"))
229			writeDone <- errors.Join(writeErr, writer.Close())
230		}()
```

```text
341	type captureBuffer struct {
342		limit    int64
343		buffer   bytes.Buffer
344		exceeded bool

346
347	func newCaptureBuffer(limit int64) *captureBuffer {
348		return &captureBuffer{limit: limit}
349	}
350
351	func (b *captureBuffer) Write(value []byte) (int, error) {
352		remaining := b.limit - int64(b.buffer.Len())
353		if remaining > 0 {
354			keep := int64(len(value))
355			if keep > remaining {
356				keep = remaining
357			}
358			_, _ = b.buffer.Write(value[:int(keep)])
359		}
360		if int64(len(value)) > remaining {
361			b.exceeded = true
362		}
363		// Consume excess output without retaining it. The command timeout still
364		// bounds a peer that writes forever, while the parent process stays bounded.
365		return len(value), nil
366	}
367
368	func (b *captureBuffer) Bytes() []byte {
369		return append([]byte(nil), b.buffer.Bytes()...)
370	}
371
372	func (b *captureBuffer) Exceeded() bool { return b.exceeded }

374	func effectiveLimit(configured, fallback int64) int64 {
375		if configured <= 0 {
376			return fallback
377		}
378		return configured
379	}

385		}

388		}

390	}

392	func boundedBytes(value []byte, limit int64) []byte {
393		if int64(len(value)) > limit {
394			value = value[:int(limit)]
395		}
396		return append([]byte(nil), value...)
397	}

399	func appendBounded(current, suffix []byte, limit int64) []byte {
400		if int64(len(current)) >= limit {
401			return append([]byte(nil), current...)
402		}
403		available := limit - int64(len(current))
404		if int64(len(suffix)) > available {
405			suffix = suffix[:int(available)]
406		}
407		return append(append([]byte(nil), current...), suffix...)
408	}

411		return Result{ExitCode: 125, Stderr: []byte(message), CaptureError: message, TransportError: message}
```

```text
        _ = temporary.Close()
        return err

    if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {

    }

 func MaybeServeAskpass() (bool, int) {
    if os.Getenv(askpassMarker) != "1" {

    }
    fd, err := strconv.Atoi(os.Getenv(askpassFD))
    if err != nil || fd < 3 {

    _, err = os.Stdout.Write(append(password, '\n'))

    }

+// runSSHCommand starts SSH before writing an askpass secret. Starting first is
+// load-bearing: a secret larger than the pipe capacity must remain cancellable
+// through the command context instead of blocking before SSH exists.
+func runSSHCommand(cmd *exec.Cmd, password string) error {
+	if password == "" {
+		return cmd.Run()
+	}
+	executable, err := os.Executable()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	reader, writer, err := os.Pipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	cmd.ExtraFiles = []*os.File{reader}
+	cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env,
+		askpassMarker+"=1", askpassFD+"=3", "SSH_ASKPASS="+executable,
+		"SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force", "DISPLAY=dev-fleet")
+	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+		_ = reader.Close()
+		_ = writer.Close()
+		return err
+	}
+	// The child owns its inherited descriptor after Start; closing the parent
+	// copy lets an early SSH exit interrupt a blocked write.
+	readerCloseErr := reader.Close()
+	writeDone := make(chan error, 1)
+	go func() {
+		_, writeErr := io.Copy(writer, strings.NewReader(password+"\n"))
+		writeDone <- errors.Join(writeErr, writer.Close())
+	}()
+	waitErr := cmd.Wait()
+	// A descendant could retain the inherited read descriptor after SSH exits.
+	// Close our writer so that cannot strand the write goroutine.
+	_ = writer.Close()
+	writeErr := <-writeDone
+	return errors.Join(waitErr, readerCloseErr, writeErr)
+}

 func sshArgs(host Host, pty, password bool) []string {
    connect := host.ConnectTimeout.Duration
    if connect <= 0 {
        connect = 15 * time.Second
    }
    seconds := int(connect.Round(time.Second) / time.Second)
    if seconds < 1 {
        seconds = 1
    }
    args := []string{"-o", "ConnectTimeout=" + strconv.Itoa(seconds), "-o", "ServerAliveInterval=15", "-o", "ServerAliveCountMax=2"}
    if password {
        args = append(args, "-o", "BatchMode=no", "-o", "PubkeyAuthentication=no", "-o", "PreferredAuthentications=keyboard-interactive,password", "-o", "NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1")
    } else {
        args = append(args, "-o", "BatchMode=yes")
    }
    if pty {
        args = append(args, "-t")
+	} else {

+		// Do not add host-key overrides here: OpenSSH's configured strict host-key
+		// verification remains authoritative.

+			"-o", "ForwardAgent=no",
+			"-o", "ForwardX11=no",

    if host.User != "" && host.SSHAlias != "" {
        args = append(args, "-l", host.User)

 }

 func remoteCommand(host Host, args []string) string {
    devPath := host.DevPath
    if devPath == "" {
        devPath = "auto"
    }
    quotedArgs := make([]string, len(args))
    for index, arg := range args {
        quotedArgs[index] = shellQuote(arg)
    }
    joined := strings.Join(quotedArgs, " ")
    if devPath != "auto" {
        return "exec " + shellQuote(devconfig.Expand(devPath)) + " " + joined
    }
    path := `PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:/opt/homebrew/bin:/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/snap/bin:$PATH"`
    return path + "; export PATH; command -v dev >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 127; exec dev " + joined
 }

 func shellQuote(value string) string {
    return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(value, "'", "'\"'\"'") + "'"
 }

 func permissionDenied(stderr []byte) bool {
    return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(string(stderr)), "permission denied")
 }

 func (t Transport) resolvePassword(host Host) (string, error) {
    source := host.SSHLoginPasswordSource
    switch host.PasswordKind() {
    case "plain":
        return source.Value, nil
    case "bitwarden":
        cmd := exec.Command("bw", "get", "password", source.Item)
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve Bitwarden SSH password for %s: %w", host.Name, err)
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), nil
    case "prompt":
        promptPasswordMu.Lock()
        defer promptPasswordMu.Unlock()
        writer := t.Err
        if writer == nil {
            writer = os.Stderr
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(writer, "SSH password for %s: ", host.Name)
        terminal, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
        if err != nil {
            return "", fmt.Errorf("open terminal for SSH password: %w", err)
        }
        defer terminal.Close()
        password, err := term.ReadPassword(terminal.Fd())
        fmt.Fprintln(writer)
        if err != nil {
            return "", err
        }
        return string(password), nil
    default:
        return "", nil
    }
 }

+type captureBuffer struct {
+	limit    int64
+	buffer   bytes.Buffer
+	exceeded bool
+}
+
+func newCaptureBuffer(limit int64) *captureBuffer {
+	return &captureBuffer{limit: limit}
+}
+
+func (b *captureBuffer) Write(value []byte) (int, error) {
+	remaining := b.limit - int64(b.buffer.Len())
+	if remaining > 0 {
+		keep := int64(len(value))
+		if keep > remaining {
+			keep = remaining
+		}
+		_, _ = b.buffer.Write(value[:int(keep)])
+	}
+	if int64(len(value)) > remaining {
+		b.exceeded = true
+	}
+	// Consume excess output without retaining it. The command timeout still
+	// bounds a peer that writes forever, while the parent process stays bounded.
+	return len(value), nil
+}
+
+func (b *captureBuffer) Bytes() []byte {
+	return append([]byte(nil), b.buffer.Bytes()...)
+}
+
+func (b *captureBuffer) Exceeded() bool { return b.exceeded }
+
+func effectiveLimit(configured, fallback int64) int64 {
+	if configured <= 0 {
+		return fallback
+	}
+	return configured
+}
+
+func captureLimitMessage(stdout, stderr *captureBuffer) string {
+	streams := make([]string, 0, 2)
+	if stdout.Exceeded() {
+		streams = append(streams, fmt.Sprintf("stdout exceeded %d-byte capture limit", stdout.limit))
+	}
+	if stderr.Exceeded() {
+		streams = append(streams, fmt.Sprintf("stderr exceeded %d-byte capture limit", stderr.limit))
+	}
+	return "fleet transport: remote " + strings.Join(streams, " and ")
+}
+
+func boundedBytes(value []byte, limit int64) []byte {
+	if int64(len(value)) > limit {
+		value = value[:int(limit)]
+	}
+	return append([]byte(nil), value...)
+}
+
+func appendBounded(current, suffix []byte, limit int64) []byte {
+	if int64(len(current)) >= limit {
+		return append([]byte(nil), current...)
+	}
+	available := limit - int64(len(current))
+	if int64(len(suffix)) > available {
+		suffix = suffix[:int(available)]
+	}
+	return append(append([]byte(nil), current...), suffix...)
+}
+
+func localTransportFailure(message string) Result {
+	return Result{ExitCode: 125, Stderr: []byte(message), CaptureError: message, TransportError: message}
+}
```

```text
105	// WithLock runs operation while holding the catalog's cross-process advisory
106	// lock. It is intended for short read-match-write transactions; expensive
107	// discovery belongs before the lock. The operating system releases the lock if
108	// the process exits unexpectedly.
109	func (s *Store) WithLock(ctx context.Context, operation func() error) error {
110		if s == nil {
111			return errors.New("lock nil catalog store")
112		}
113		if operation == nil {
114			return errors.New("catalog lock requires an operation")
115		}
116		s.mu.Lock()
117		defer s.mu.Unlock()
118		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "catalog", operation)
119	}
120	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }

122	// Create assigns a random stable ID and atomically persists entry. The caller's
123	// value is updated only after the rename succeeds.
124	func (s *Store) Create(entry *Entry) error {
125		if err := s.validateCreateInput(entry); err != nil {
126			return err
127		}
128		return s.WithLock(context.Background(), func() error { return s.CreateUnderLock(entry) })
129	}

131	// CreateUnderLock is the non-reentrant form used only inside Store.WithLock.
132	// Calling it without that transaction guard is a programming error.
133	func (s *Store) CreateUnderLock(entry *Entry) error {
134		if entry == nil {
135			return errors.New("create nil catalog entry")
136		}
137		if entry.ID != "" {
138			return fmt.Errorf("create catalog asset: ID is assigned by the store")
139		}
140		prepare := func() (*Entry, error) {
141			candidate := entry.Clone()
142			candidate.ID = s.nextID()
143			if err := ValidateID(candidate.ID); err != nil {
144				return nil, fmt.Errorf("generated catalog ID: %w", err)
145			}
146			now := s.now()
147			candidate.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
148			if candidate.Created.IsZero() {
149				candidate.Created = now
150			}
151			if candidate.Discovered.IsZero() {
152				candidate.Discovered = now
153			}
154			candidate.Updated = now
155			prepareNewNested(candidate, now)
156			candidate.Normalize()
157			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
158				return nil, err
159			}
160			return candidate, nil
161		}
162		candidate, err := prepare()
163		if err != nil {
164			return err
165		}
166		for range 32 {
167			if _, err := os.Lstat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
168				candidate, err = prepare()
169				if err != nil {
170					return err
171				}
172				continue
173			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
174				return fmt.Errorf("check catalog ID %s: %w", candidate.ID, err)
175			}
176			if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
177				return err
178			}
179			*entry = *candidate
180			return nil
181		}
182		return fmt.Errorf("generate unique catalog ID: %w", ErrAlreadyExists)
183	}

208	// Import merges portable metadata for an exact stable ID and records location as
209	// host's local view. Source locations are deliberately ignored: only the caller-
210	// supplied target location may claim a path on this machine. Move intents and
211	// recovery receipts are host-owned lifecycle authority and cannot be imported.
212	// The complete read-check-write transaction runs under the catalog's advisory
213	// lock so concurrent processes cannot claim the same target path.
214	func (s *Store) Import(ctx context.Context, source *Entry, host string, location Location) (*Entry, error) {
215		if s == nil {
216			return nil, errors.New("import into nil catalog store")
217		}
218		if source == nil {
219			return nil, errors.New("import nil catalog entry")
220		}
221		if source.MoveIntent != nil {
222			return nil, importConflict(source.ID, source.ID, "move_intent", "host-local move authority cannot be imported")
223		}
224		if source.RecoveryReceipt != nil {
225			return nil, importConflict(source.ID, source.ID, "recovery_receipt", "recovery authority cannot be imported before target verification")
226		}
227		if err := validateLocationForSet(host, location); err != nil {
228			return nil, fmt.Errorf("catalog import target location: %w", err)
229		}
230
231		incoming := source.Clone()
232		if incoming.SchemaVersion == 0 {
233			incoming.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
234		}
235		incoming.Locations = nil
236		incoming.RecoveryReceipt = nil
237		incoming.MoveIntent = nil
238		incoming.Normalize()
239
240		// Validate all source-owned fields before locking or creating the store. A
241		// zero location timestamp is allowed at the API boundary and is stamped only
242		// after the lock is held so a replay can retain the first import's timestamp.
243		validationLocation := location
244		if validationLocation.Updated.IsZero() {
245			validationLocation.Updated = incoming.Updated
246		}
247		incoming.Locations = map[string]Location{host: validationLocation}
248		if err := incoming.Validate(); err != nil {
249			return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate imported catalog asset %s: %w", incoming.ID, err)
250		}
251
252		var imported *Entry
253		err := s.WithLock(ctx, func() error {
254			entries, diagnostics, err := s.ListWithDiagnostics()
255			if err != nil {
256				return err
257			}
258			if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
259				return incompleteCatalogError(diagnostics)
260			}
261
262			var current *Entry
263			for _, entry := range entries {
264				if entry.ID == incoming.ID {
265					current = entry
266					break
267				}
268			}
269			if current != nil && current.MoveIntent != nil {
270				return importConflict(current.ID, current.ID, "move_intent",
271					fmt.Sprintf("target has a pending %s move", current.MoveIntent.Operation))
272			}
273
274			targetLocation := location
275			if targetLocation.Updated.IsZero() {
276				if previous, ok := currentLocation(current, host); ok && !locationPayloadChanged(previous, targetLocation) {
277					targetLocation.Updated = previous.Updated
278				} else {
279					targetLocation.Updated = s.now()
280				}
281			} else if previous, ok := currentLocation(current, host); ok &&
282				!locationPayloadChanged(previous, targetLocation) && previous.Updated.After(targetLocation.Updated) {
283				// Replaying an older observation of the same path must not move the
284				// target's location timestamp backwards.
285				targetLocation.Updated = previous.Updated
286			}
287			if err := validateLocation(host, targetLocation); err != nil {
288				return fmt.Errorf("catalog import target location: %w", err)
289			}
290			if err := rejectImportedPathOwner(entries, incoming.ID, host, targetLocation); err != nil {
291				return err
292			}
293
294			if current == nil {
295				created := incoming.Clone()
296				created.Locations = map[string]Location{host: targetLocation}
297				if err := created.Validate(); err != nil {
298					return fmt.Errorf("validate imported catalog asset %s: %w", created.ID, err)
299				}
300				if err := s.writeAtomic(created); err != nil {
301					return err
302				}
303				imported = created.Clone()
304				return nil
305			}
306
307			merged, changed, err := mergeImportedEntry(current, incoming, host, targetLocation)

310			}
311			if !changed {
312				imported = current.Clone()
313				return nil
314			}
315			if err := s.writeAtomic(merged); err != nil {
316				return err
317			}
318			imported = merged.Clone()
319			return nil
320		})
321		return imported, err
322	}

324	func importConflict(id, existingID, field, reason string) error {

328	func currentLocation(entry *Entry, host string) (Location, bool) {

335	func rejectImportedPathOwner(entries []*Entry, importedID, host string, target Location) error {
336		targetPaths, err := canonicalLocationPaths(target)
337		if err != nil {
338			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize imported location on host %s: %w", host, err)
339		}
340		for _, entry := range entries {
341			if entry.ID == importedID {
342				continue
343			}
344			owned, ok := entry.LocationFor(host)
345			if !ok {
346				continue
347			}
348			ownedPaths, err := canonicalLocationPaths(owned)
349			if err != nil {
350				return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize catalog asset %s location on host %s: %w", entry.ID, host, err)
351			}
352			ownedSet := make(map[string]struct{}, len(ownedPaths))
353			for _, path := range ownedPaths {
354				ownedSet[path] = struct{}{}
355			}
356			for _, path := range targetPaths {
357				if _, exists := ownedSet[path]; exists {
358					return importConflict(importedID, entry.ID, "location",
359						fmt.Sprintf("target path %q on host %s is already owned", path, host))
360				}
361			}
362		}
363		return nil
364	}

366	func canonicalLocationPaths(location Location) ([]string, error) {
367		fields := []struct {
368			name  string
369			value string
370		}{
371			{"current_path", location.CurrentPath},
372			{"restore_path", location.RestorePath},
373			{"real_path", location.RealPath},
374			{"git_common_dir", location.GitCommonDir},
375		}
376		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(fields))
377		for _, field := range fields {
378			if field.value == "" {
379				continue
380			}
381			canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(field.value)
382			if err != nil {
383				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s %q: %w", field.name, field.value, err)
384			}
385			seen[canonical] = struct{}{}
386		}
387		paths := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
388		for path := range seen {
389			paths = append(paths, path)
390		}
391		sort.Strings(paths)
392		return paths, nil
393	}

395	func mergeImportedEntry(current, incoming *Entry, host string, location Location) (*Entry, bool, error) {

397			return nil, false, importConflict(incoming.ID, current.ID, "schema_version", "schema versions differ")

402		}

406		}

409		changed := false

414		case currentSummary != "" && incomingSummary != "" && merged.Note != incoming.Note:
415			return nil, false, importConflict(incoming.ID, current.ID, "note", "nonempty summaries differ")

431		case merged.RemoteIdentity == "" && incoming.RemoteIdentity != "":
432			merged.RemoteIdentity = incoming.RemoteIdentity

443		}
444
445		if value := earlierTime(merged.Created, incoming.Created); !value.Equal(merged.Created) {
446			merged.Created = value
447			changed = true
448		}
449		if value := earlierTime(merged.Discovered, incoming.Discovered); !value.Equal(merged.Discovered) {
450			merged.Discovered = value
451			changed = true
452		}
453		if value := laterTime(merged.LastOpened, incoming.LastOpened); !value.Equal(merged.LastOpened) {
454			merged.LastOpened = value
455			changed = true
456		}
457		if value := laterTime(merged.Updated, incoming.Updated); !value.Equal(merged.Updated) {
458			merged.Updated = value
459			changed = true
460		}
461
462		previous, exists := merged.LocationFor(host)
463		if !exists || locationPayloadChanged(previous, location) || !previous.Updated.Equal(location.Updated) {
464			if merged.Locations == nil {
465				merged.Locations = make(map[string]Location)
466			}
467			merged.Locations[host] = location
468			changed = true
469		}
470		merged.Normalize()
471		if err := merged.Validate(); err != nil {
472			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("validate merged catalog asset %s: %w", merged.ID, err)
473		}
474		return merged, changed, nil
475	}

477	func experimentsEqual(left, right Experiment) bool {
478		return left.Phase == right.Phase &&

480			left.OriginURL == right.OriginURL &&
481			left.Started.Equal(right.Started) &&

490		if left.IsZero() || !right.IsZero() && right.Before(left) {

492		}

499		}
```

```text
99	// Import writes a transported note with its exact durable identity and

101	// a source Path is never trusted. An identical revision is an idempotent replay,
102	// while reusing an ID for different content is a conflict. Import changes only
103	// Markdown source data and deliberately does not update or rebuild the FTS cache.
104	func (s *Store) Import(ctx context.Context, source *Note) (*Note, error) {

107		}

110		}
111		if ctx == nil {
112			ctx = context.Background()
113		}
114
115		candidate := clone(source)
116		candidate.Path = ""

118			candidate.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion

120		originalRevision := source.Revision()
121		candidate.Normalize()
122		if candidate.Revision() != originalRevision {
123			return nil, fmt.Errorf("import note %s must already be normalized to preserve its revision: %w",
124				source.ID, ErrInvalid)
125		}
126		if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
127			return nil, err
128		}
129
130		s.mu.Lock()
131		defer s.mu.Unlock()
132		var imported *Note
133		err := s.withFileLock(ctx, func() error {
134			target, err := s.confinedImportPath(candidate.RepositoryID, candidate.ID)
135			if err != nil {
136				return err
137			}
138			current, err := s.importedNoteByID(candidate.ID)

140			case err == nil:

142					return fmt.Errorf("note %s already exists with different content: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
143				}
144				if filepath.Clean(current.Path) != filepath.Clean(target) {
145					return fmt.Errorf("note %s exists outside its imported repository path: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
```

```text
+// Import writes a transported note with its exact durable identity and
+// timestamps. Path is always derived from the validated repository and note IDs;
+// a source Path is never trusted. An identical revision is an idempotent replay,
+// while reusing an ID for different content is a conflict. Import changes only
+// Markdown source data and deliberately does not update or rebuild the FTS cache.
+func (s *Store) Import(ctx context.Context, source *Note) (*Note, error) {
+	if s == nil {
+		return nil, errors.New("import into nil note store")
+	}
+	if source == nil {
+		return nil, errors.New("import nil note")
+	}
+	if ctx == nil {
+		ctx = context.Background()
+	}
+
+	candidate := clone(source)
+	candidate.Path = ""
+	if candidate.SchemaVersion == 0 {
+		candidate.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
+	}
+	originalRevision := source.Revision()
+	candidate.Normalize()
+	if candidate.Revision() != originalRevision {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("import note %s must already be normalized to preserve its revision: %w",
+			source.ID, ErrInvalid)
+	}
+	if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	var imported *Note
+	err := s.withFileLock(ctx, func() error {
+		target, err := s.confinedImportPath(candidate.RepositoryID, candidate.ID)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		current, err := s.importedNoteByID(candidate.ID)
+		switch {
+		case err == nil:
+			if current.Revision() != candidate.Revision() {
+				return fmt.Errorf("note %s already exists with different content: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
+			}
+			if filepath.Clean(current.Path) != filepath.Clean(target) {
+				return fmt.Errorf("note %s exists outside its imported repository path: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
+			}
+			imported = clone(current)
+			return nil
+		case !errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound):
+			return err
+		}
+
+		candidate.Path = target
+		if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		imported = clone(candidate)
+		return nil
+	})
+	return imported, err
+}
+
+func (s *Store) confinedImportPath(repositoryID, id string) (string, error) {
+	root, err := pathx.Canonical(s.Dir)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize note store: %w", err)
+	}
+	repositoryDir := filepath.Join(root, repositoryID)
+	if info, err := os.Lstat(repositoryDir); err == nil {
+		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("note repository directory %s is a symlink: %w", repositoryID, ErrRepository)
+		}
+		if !info.IsDir() {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("note repository path %s is not a directory: %w", repositoryID, ErrRepository)
+		}
+	} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect note repository directory %s: %w", repositoryID, err)
+	}
+
+	path := filepath.Join(repositoryDir, id+".md")
+	if info, err := os.Lstat(path); err == nil {
+		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("note path %s is not a regular file: %w", id, ErrInvalid)
+		}
+	} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect note path %s: %w", id, err)
+	}
+	confined, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("confine imported note path: %w", err)
+	}
+	return confined, nil
+}
```

```text
55	func CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) (string, error) {
```

```text
29	+func TestCreateAndUpdateShareCatalogTransactionLock(t *testing.T) {
30	+	t.Run("create", func(t *testing.T) {
31	+		dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "assets")
32	+		holder := catalog.NewStore(dir)
33	+		writer := catalog.NewStore(dir, catalog.WithIDGenerator(idSequence(firstID)))
34	+		entered := make(chan struct{})
35	+		release := make(chan struct{})
36	+		holderDone := make(chan error, 1)
37	+		go func() {
38	+			holderDone <- holder.WithLock(context.Background(), func() error {
39	+				close(entered)
40	+				<-release
41	+				return nil
42	+			})
43	+		}()
44	+		<-entered
45	+		writeDone := make(chan error, 1)
46	+		go func() { writeDone <- writer.Create(&catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: "created"}) }()
47	+		select {
48	+		case err := <-writeDone:
49	+			t.Fatalf("Create bypassed catalog transaction lock: %v", err)
50	+		case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
51	+		}
52	+		close(release)
53	+		if err := <-holderDone; err != nil {
54	+			t.Fatal(err)
55	+		}
56	+		if err := <-writeDone; err != nil {
57	+			t.Fatal(err)
58	+		}
59	+	})
60	+
61	+	t.Run("update", func(t *testing.T) {
62	+		dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "assets")
63	+		seed := catalog.NewStore(dir, catalog.WithIDGenerator(idSequence(firstID)))
64	+		entry := &catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: "before"}
65	+		if err := seed.Create(entry); err != nil {
66	+			t.Fatal(err)
67	+		}
68	+		holder := catalog.NewStore(dir)
69	+		writer := catalog.NewStore(dir)
70	+		entered := make(chan struct{})
71	+		release := make(chan struct{})
72	+		holderDone := make(chan error, 1)
73	+		go func() {
74	+			holderDone <- holder.WithLock(context.Background(), func() error {
75	+				close(entered)
76	+				<-release
77	+				return nil
78	+			})
79	+		}()
80	+		<-entered
81	+		mutated := make(chan struct{}, 1)
82	+		writeDone := make(chan error, 1)
83	+		go func() {
84	+			_, err := writer.Update(entry.ID, func(candidate *catalog.Entry) error {
85	+				mutated <- struct{}{}
86	+				candidate.Name = "after"
87	+				return nil
88	+			})
89	+			writeDone <- err
90	+		}()
91	+		select {
92	+		case <-mutated:
93	+			t.Fatal("Update read and mutated while catalog transaction lock was held")
94	+		case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
95	+		}
96	+		close(release)
97	+		if err := <-holderDone; err != nil {
98	+			t.Fatal(err)
99	+		}
100	+		if err := <-writeDone; err != nil {
101	+			t.Fatal(err)
102	+		}
103	+	})
104	+}

265	+		{"git@example.test:group/repo.git?token=secret#fragment", "git@example.test:group/repo.git"},
266	+		{"oauth2:password@example.test:group/repo.git?token=secret", "***@example.test:group/repo.git"},
267	+		{"oauth2:password@example.test/group/repo.git?token=secret", "***@example.test/group/repo.git"},
268	+		{"work:group/repo.git?token=secret#fragment", "work:group/repo.git"},
269	+		{"relative/path?literal#name", "relative/path?literal#name"},
270	+		{"https://example.test/group/repo%0a.git", unsafeRemoteLabel},
271	+		{"https://[malformed/secret", unsafeRemoteLabel},
272	+		{"git@example.test:group/repo.git\x1b[31m", unsafeRemoteLabel},
273	+		{"git@example.test:group/" + string(rune(0x202e)) + "repo.git", unsafeRemoteLabel},
274	+		{string([]byte{'b', 'a', 'd', 0xff}), unsafeRemoteLabel},
275	+	} {
276	+		got := RedactRemoteRef(test.input)
277	+		if got != test.want {
278	+			t.Errorf("RedactRemoteRef(%q) = %q, want %q", test.input, got, test.want)
279	+		}
280	+		if strings.IndexFunc(got, func(r rune) bool { return r < ' ' || r == 0x7f }) >= 0 {
281	+			t.Errorf("RedactRemoteRef(%q) retained a control in %q", test.input, got)
282	+		}
283	+	}
284	+}

347	+func TestRevisionCoversPersistedSemanticContent(t *testing.T) {
348	+	base := exactImportTask()
349	+	baseRevision := base.Revision()
350	+	if len(baseRevision) != 64 {
351	+		t.Fatalf("Revision length = %d, want 64 hex characters", len(baseRevision))
352	+	}
353	+
354	+	same := *base
355	+	same.Tags = append([]string(nil), base.Tags...)
356	+	same.Created = base.Created.In(time.FixedZone("created-offset", 9*60*60))
357	+	same.Updated = base.Updated.In(time.FixedZone("updated-offset", -5*60*60))
358	+	if got := same.Revision(); got != baseRevision {
359	+		t.Fatalf("equal instants and semantic content produced %q, want %q", got, baseRevision)
360	+	}
361	+
362	+	mutations := []struct {
363	+		name   string
364	+		mutate func(*task.Task)
365	+	}{
366	+		{"ID", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.ID += "-other" }},
367	+		{"Name", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Name += " other" }},
368	+		{"Repo", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Repo += "-other" }},
369	+		{"RepoPath", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.RepoPath += "-other" }},
370	+		{"Branch", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Branch += "-other" }},
371	+		{"Base", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Base += "-other" }},
372	+		{"WorktreePath", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.WorktreePath += "-other" }},
373	+		{"Mode", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Mode = task.ModeDirect }},
374	+		{"State", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.State = task.Cold }},
375	+		{"Owner", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Owner += "-other" }},
376	+		{"Next", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Next += " other" }},
377	+		{"Note", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Note += " other" }},
378	+		{"Tags", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Tags = []string{"different"} }},
379	+		{"AgentSession", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.AgentSession += "-other" }},
380	+		{"RuntimeHandle", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.RuntimeHandle += "-other" }},
381	+		{"RuntimeName", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.RuntimeName += "-other" }},
382	+		{"Created", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Created = tk.Created.Add(time.Nanosecond) }},
383	+		{"Updated", func(tk *task.Task) { tk.Updated = tk.Updated.Add(time.Nanosecond) }},
384	+	}
385	+	for _, mutation := range mutations {
386	+		t.Run(mutation.name, func(t *testing.T) {
387	+			changed := *base
388	+			changed.Tags = append([]string(nil), base.Tags...)
389	+			mutation.mutate(&changed)
390	+			if got := changed.Revision(); got == baseRevision {
391	+				t.Errorf("Revision did not change after changing %s", mutation.name)
392	+			}
393	+		})
394	+	}
395	+}

397	+func TestLegacyTOMLRemainsReadableWithoutPersistingRevision(t *testing.T) {
398	+	dir := t.TempDir()
399	+	const id = "legacy__feat-old"
400	+	legacy := `name = "legacy"
401	+repo = "legacy"
402	+repo_path = "/src/legacy"
403	+branch = "feat/old"
404	+base = "main"
405	+worktree_path = ""
406	+state = "warm"
407	+owner = "old-host"
408	+next = "continue"
409	+note = ""
410	+tags = ["old"]
411	+agent_session = ""
412	+runtime_handle = ""
413	+runtime_name = ""
414	+created = 2025-01-02T03:04:05Z
415	+updated = 2025-01-03T03:04:05Z
416	+`
417	+	path := filepath.Join(dir, id+".toml")
418	+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(legacy), 0o644); err != nil {
419	+		t.Fatal(err)
420	+	}
421	+
422	+	s := task.NewStore(dir)
423	+	got, err := s.Get(id)
424	+	if err != nil {
425	+		t.Fatalf("Get legacy task: %v", err)
426	+	}
427	+	if got.ID != id || got.Mode != "" || got.EffectiveMode() != task.ModeBranch {
428	+		t.Fatalf("legacy task decoded incorrectly: %+v", got)
429	+	}
430	+	if got.Revision() == "" {
431	+		t.Fatal("legacy task should have a computed revision")
432	+	}
433	+	if err := s.Save(got); err != nil {
434	+		t.Fatalf("Save legacy task: %v", err)
435	+	}
436	+	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
437	+	if err != nil {
438	+		t.Fatal(err)
439	+	}
440	+	if strings.Contains(string(data), "revision") {
441	+		t.Fatalf("computed revision leaked into legacy TOML:\n%s", data)
442	+	}
443	+	if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
444	+		info, err := os.Stat(path)
445	+		if err != nil {
446	+			t.Fatal(err)
447	+		}
448	+		if got := info.Mode().Perm(); got != 0o644 {
449	+			t.Errorf("task mode = %04o, want 0644", got)
450	+		}
451	+	}
452	+}

638	+func TestSaveIfRevisionSerializesConcurrentWriters(t *testing.T) {
639	+	s := task.NewStore(t.TempDir())
640	+	original := newTask("repo", "feat/concurrent", task.Hot)
641	+	if err := s.Save(original); err != nil {
642	+		t.Fatal(err)
643	+	}
644	+	expected := original.Revision()
645	+
646	+	const writers = 12
647	+	type result struct {
648	+		next string
649	+		err  error
650	+	}
651	+	start := make(chan struct{})
652	+	results := make(chan result, writers)
653	+	for i := range writers {
654	+		go func(i int) {
655	+			candidate := *original
656	+			candidate.Next = fmt.Sprintf("writer-%02d", i)
657	+			<-start
658	+			err := s.SaveIfRevision(&candidate, expected)
659	+			results <- result{next: candidate.Next, err: err}
660	+		}(i)
661	+	}
662	+	close(start)
663	+
664	+	successes := 0
665	+	conflicts := 0
666	+	winner := ""
667	+	for range writers {
668	+		result := <-results
669	+		switch {
670	+		case result.err == nil:
671	+			successes++
672	+			winner = result.next
673	+		case errors.Is(result.err, task.ErrConflict):
674	+			conflicts++
675	+		default:
676	+			t.Errorf("concurrent SaveIfRevision returned %v", result.err)
677	+		}
678	+	}
679	+	if successes != 1 || conflicts != writers-1 {
680	+		t.Fatalf("concurrent outcomes: successes=%d conflicts=%d, want 1 and %d", successes, conflicts, writers-1)
681	+	}
682	+	got, err := s.Get(original.ID)
683	+	if err != nil {
684	+		t.Fatal(err)
685	+	}
686	+	if got.Next != winner {
687	+		t.Fatalf("stored writer = %q, successful writer = %q", got.Next, winner)
688	+	}
689	+}
```

Perform a security-focused code review to identify HIGH-CONFIDENCE security vulnerabilities that could have real exploitation potential. This is not a general code review - focus ONLY on security implications newly added by this PR. Do not comment on existing security concerns.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:

3. FOCUS ON IMPACT: Prioritize vulnerabilities that could lead to unauthorized access, data breaches, or system compromise

SECURITY CATEGORIES TO EXAMINE:

**Input Validation Vulnerabilities:**
- SQL injection via unsanitized user input
- Command injection in system calls or subprocesses
- XXE injection in XML parsing
- Template injection in templating engines
- NoSQL injection in database queries
- Path traversal in file operations

**Authentication & Authorization Issues:**
- Authentication bypass logic
- Privilege escalation paths
- Session management flaws
- JWT token vulnerabilities
- Authorization logic bypasses

**Crypto & Secrets Management:**
- Hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens
- Weak cryptographic algorithms or implementations
- Improper key storage or management
- Cryptographic randomness issues
- Certificate validation bypasses

**Injection & Code Execution:**
- Remote code execution via deseralization
- Pickle injection in Python
- YAML deserialization vulnerabilities
- Eval injection in dynamic code execution
- XSS vulnerabilities in web applications (reflected, stored, DOM-based)

**Data Exposure:**
- Sensitive data logging or storage
- PII handling violations
- API endpoint data leakage
- Debug information exposure

Additional notes:
- Even if something is only exploitable from the local network, it can still be a HIGH severity issue

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY:

Phase 1 - Repository Context Research (Use file search tools):
- Identify existing security frameworks and libraries in use
- Look for established secure coding patterns in the codebase
- Examine existing sanitization and validation patterns
- Understand the project's security model and threat model

Phase 2 - Comparative Analysis:
- Compare new code changes against existing security patterns
- Identify deviations from established secure practices
- Look for inconsistent security implementations
- Flag code that introduces new attack surfaces

Phase 3 - Vulnerability Assessment:
- Examine each modified file for security implications
- Trace data flow from user inputs to sensitive operations
- Look for privilege boundaries being crossed unsafely
- Identify injection points and unsafe deserialization

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT:

You MUST output your findings in markdown. The markdown output should contain the file, line number, severity, category (e.g. `sql_injection` or `xss`), description, exploit scenario, and fix recommendation.

For example:

# Vuln 1: XSS: `foo.py:42`

* Severity: High
* Description: User input from `username` parameter is directly interpolated into HTML without escaping, allowing reflected XSS attacks
* Exploit Scenario: Attacker crafts URL like /bar?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute JavaScript in victim's browser, enabling session hijacking or data theft
* Recommendation: Use Flask's escape() function or Jinja2 templates with auto-escaping enabled for all user inputs rendered in HTML

SEVERITY GUIDELINES:
- **HIGH**: Directly exploitable vulnerabilities leading to RCE, data breach, or authentication bypass
- **MEDIUM**: Vulnerabilities requiring specific conditions but with significant impact
- **LOW**: Defense-in-depth issues or lower-impact vulnerabilities

CONFIDENCE SCORING:
- 0.9-1.0: Certain exploit path identified, tested if possible
- 0.8-0.9: Clear vulnerability pattern with known exploitation methods
- 0.7-0.8: Suspicious pattern requiring specific conditions to exploit
- Below 0.7: Don't report (too speculative)

FINAL REMINDER:

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING:

> HARD EXCLUSIONS - Automatically exclude findings matching these patterns:

> 4. Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.

> 12. Log spoofing concerns. Outputting un-sanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability.
> 13. SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF is only a concern if it can control the host or protocol.

> 3. Environment variables and CLI flags are trusted values. Attackers are generally not able to modify them in a secure environment. Any attack that relies on controlling an environment variable is invalid.

> 5. Subtle or low impact web vulnerabilities such as tabnabbing, XS-Leaks, prototype pollution, and open redirects should not be reported unless they are extremely high confidence.
> 6. React and Angular are generally secure against XSS. > 8. A lack of permission checking or authentication in client-side JS/TS code is not a vulnerability. Client-side code is not trusted and does not need to implement these checks, they are handled on the server-side. > 9. Only include MEDIUM findings if they are obvious and concrete issues.

> 12. Command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts are generally not exploitable in practice since shell scripts generally do not run with untrusted user input. 24	// TrustRecord intentionally stores no command, script, config bytes, or
```text
25	// display metadata. Approval is tied only to canonical repository identity
26	// and the exact execution-bearing content digest.
27	type TrustRecord struct {
28		Repository    string    `json:"repository"`
29		ExecutionHash string    `json:"execution_hash"`
30		ApprovedAt    time.Time `json:"approved_at"`
31	}

38	// TrustStore is a private, local JSON trust database. Path should live under
39	// dev's host state directory, never inside the repository.
40	type TrustStore struct {
41		Path  string
42		Clock func() time.Time
43
44		mu sync.Mutex
45	}
46
47	// NewTrustStore returns a store at path.
48	func NewTrustStore(path string) *TrustStore {
49		return &TrustStore{Path: path, Clock: time.Now}
50	}
51
52	// CanonicalRepoIdentity returns Git's canonical common directory when path is
53	// a repository, making every linked worktree share one trust identity. A
54	// not-yet-initialized project falls back to its canonical physical root.
55	func CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) (string, error) {
56		root, err := pathx.Canonical(repoRoot)
57		if err != nil {
58			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize repository: %w", err)
59		}
60		info, err := os.Stat(root)
61		if err != nil {
62			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect repository %s: %w", root, err)
63		}
64		if !info.IsDir() {
65			return "", fmt.Errorf("repository path %s is not a directory", root)
66		}
67		if ctx == nil {
68			ctx = context.Background()
69		}
70		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, root)
71		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
72			return root, nil
73		}
74		if err != nil {
75			return "", fmt.Errorf("discover repository identity: %w", err)
76		}
77		identity, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
78		if err != nil {
79			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git common directory: %w", err)
80		}
81		return identity, nil
82	}
83
84	// Approve trusts hash for repoRoot. A new approval replaces every older hash
85	// for that repository, so changing and later reverting executable config still
86	// requires a fresh explicit approval.
87	func (s *TrustStore) Approve(ctx context.Context, repoRoot, hash string) (TrustRecord, error) {
88		if err := validateExecutionHash(hash); err != nil {
89			return TrustRecord{}, err
90		}
91		identity, err := CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx, repoRoot)
92		if err != nil {
93			return TrustRecord{}, err
94		}
95		record := TrustRecord{Repository: identity, ExecutionHash: hash, ApprovedAt: s.now()}
96
97		s.mu.Lock()
98		defer s.mu.Unlock()
99		records, err := s.loadLocked()
100		if err != nil {
101			return TrustRecord{}, err
102		}
103		kept := records[:0]
104		for _, existing := range records {
105			if existing.Repository != identity {
106				kept = append(kept, existing)
107			}
108		}
109		records = append(kept, record)
110		if err := s.saveLocked(records); err != nil {
111			return TrustRecord{}, err
112		}
113		return record, nil
114	}
115
116	// Check reports whether the exact current repository identity and hash are
117	// approved. Missing stores and missing records are ordinary false results.
118	func (s *TrustStore) Check(ctx context.Context, repoRoot, hash string) (bool, error) {
119		if err := validateExecutionHash(hash); err != nil {
120			return false, err
121		}
122		identity, err := CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx, repoRoot)
123		if err != nil {
124			return false, err
125		}
126		s.mu.Lock()
127		defer s.mu.Unlock()
128		records, err := s.loadLocked()
129		if err != nil {
130			return false, err
131		}
132		for _, record := range records {
133			if record.Repository == identity && record.ExecutionHash == hash {
134				return true, nil
135			}
136		}
137		return false, nil
138	}

140	// Revoke removes all approvals for repoRoot and reports whether anything was

142	func (s *TrustStore) Revoke(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) (bool, error) {
143		identity, err := CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx, repoRoot)
144		if err != nil {
145			return false, err
146		}
147		s.mu.Lock()
148		defer s.mu.Unlock()
149		records, err := s.loadLocked()
150		if err != nil {
151			return false, err
152		}
153		kept := records[:0]
154		removed := false
155		for _, record := range records {
156			if record.Repository == identity {
157				removed = true
158				continue
159			}
160			kept = append(kept, record)
161		}
162		if !removed {
163			return false, nil
164		}
165		return true, s.saveLocked(kept)
166	}

168	// List returns a stable snapshot sorted by canonical repository and hash.

177		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
```

```text
133	func (p *Provisioner) copyFileStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
134		from, to := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)

145		if err := rejectSymlinkParents(dst, filepath.Dir(to)); err != nil {
146			return fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", rel, err)
147		}
148		if _, err := os.Lstat(to); err == nil {
149			return errAlreadyPresent // never clobber what the checkout already has
150		} else if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {

206	func rejectSymlinkParents(root, parent string) error {
207		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, parent)
208		if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
209			return errors.New("destination escapes worktree")
210		}
211		current := filepath.Clean(root)
212		if rel == "." {
213			return nil
214		}
215		for _, part := range strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)) {
216			current = filepath.Join(current, part)
217			info, err := os.Lstat(current)
218			switch {
219			case errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist):
220				continue
221			case err != nil:
222				return err
223			case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
224				return fmt.Errorf("destination parent %s is a symlink", current)
225			case !info.IsDir():
226				return fmt.Errorf("destination parent %s is not a directory", current)
227			}
228		}
229		return nil
```

```text
226	func parseAzureDevOpsRemote(raw string) (identity, webURL string, ok bool) {
227		if !safeRawURLText(raw) {
228			return "", "", false
229		}
230		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
231		if raw == "" {
232			return "", "", false
233		}
234		if strings.Contains(raw, "://") {
235			u, err := url.Parse(raw)
236			if err != nil || u.Fragment != "" || u.RawQuery != "" {
237				return "", "", false
238			}
239			switch strings.ToLower(u.Scheme) {
240			case "https":
241				if u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "443" {
242					return "", "", false
243				}
244				return parseAzureDevOpsHTTPS(u)
245			case "ssh":
246				if u.User == nil || (u.Port() != "" && u.Port() != "22") {
247					return "", "", false
248				}
249				if _, hasPassword := u.User.Password(); hasPassword {
250					return "", "", false
251				}
252				return parseAzureDevOpsSSH(u.User.Username(), strings.ToLower(u.Hostname()), escapedSegments(u.EscapedPath()))
253			default:
254				return "", "", false
255			}
256		}
257		at := strings.IndexByte(raw, '@')
258		if at <= 0 {
259			return "", "", false
260		}
261		colon := strings.IndexByte(raw[at+1:], ':')
262		if colon < 0 {
263			return "", "", false
264		}
265		colon += at + 1
266		path := raw[colon+1:]
267		if strings.ContainsAny(path, "?#") {
268			return "", "", false
269		}
270		return parseAzureDevOpsSSH(raw[:at], strings.ToLower(raw[at+1:colon]), decodeSegments(strings.Split(strings.Trim(path, "/"), "/")))
271	}

351		if len(segments) == 1 && segments[0] == "" {
352			return nil
353		}
354		out := make([]string, 0, len(segments))
355		for _, segment := range segments {
```

```text
209	func forgeCacheStale(cache forge.Cache, ttl time.Duration, now time.Time) bool {
210		if cache.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
211			return true
212		}
213		if ttl <= 0 {
214			return false
215		}
216		return now.Sub(cache.FetchedAt) > ttl
217	}
218
219	func forgeCacheErrors(cache forge.Cache) error {
220		var providerErrors []error
221		kinds := make([]string, 0, len(cache.Providers))
222		byKind := map[string]forge.ProviderStatus{}
223		for kind, status := range cache.Providers {
224			name := string(kind)
225			kinds = append(kinds, name)
226			byKind[name] = status
227		}
228		sort.Strings(kinds)
229		for _, kind := range kinds {
230			status := byKind[kind]
231			if status.Error != "" {
232				providerErrors = append(providerErrors, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", kind, status.Error))
233			} else if !status.Complete {
234				providerErrors = append(providerErrors, fmt.Errorf("%s: provider inventory is incomplete", kind))
235			}
236		}
237		return errors.Join(providerErrors...)
238	}
```

```text
1	// Package lockx provides a cross-platform advisory lock over a directory.
2	//
3	// It is a leaf package on purpose. Both the catalog store and Git transaction
4	// code need to serialize mutations, and neither should have to depend on the
5	// other to get a lock.
6	package lockx
7
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"os"
13		"path/filepath"
14	)
15
16	// WithDir runs operation while holding an exclusive lock for dir. The lock file
17	// lives beside dir rather than inside it, so locking never adds a file to the
18	// directory being protected. label names the caller in wrapped errors.
19	func WithDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string, operation func() error) (err error) {
20		if operation == nil {
21			return fmt.Errorf("%s lock requires an operation", label)
22		}
23		if ctx == nil {
24			ctx = context.Background()
25		}
26		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
27			return fmt.Errorf("create %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
28		}
29		absoluteDir, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
30		if err != nil {
31			return fmt.Errorf("make %s directory absolute for lock: %w", label, err)
32		}
33		canonicalDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absoluteDir)
34		if err != nil {
35			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
36		}
37		lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")
38		lock, err := acquire(ctx, lockPath)
39		if err != nil {
40			return fmt.Errorf("acquire %s lock: %w", label, err)
41		}
42		defer func() {
43			if releaseErr := lock.Close(); releaseErr != nil {
44				err = errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("release %s lock: %w", label, releaseErr))
45			}
46		}()
47		return operation()
48	}
49
```

```text
42	// ResolvePaths canonicalizes repoRoot and proves both fixed files remain below
43	// it. This also rejects a .dev-cli directory or file symlink that escapes the

46		root, err := pathx.Canonical(repoRoot)

55		if err != nil {
56			return FilePaths{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve %s: %w", ScaffoldsRelativePath, err)
57		}
58		return FilePaths{Root: root, Config: configPath, Scaffolds: scaffoldsPath}, nil
59	}
```

```text
100	// checkout merely because that checkout is its lexical parent.
101	func (c RepoContext) CheckoutIndexForPath(path string) (int, bool) {
102		best, bestLen := -1, -1

237				return false, nil
238			}
239			return false, err
240		}

242			return false, fmt.Errorf("checkout path is not a directory")
243		}

247	func checkoutActivity(ctx context.Context, path string, status gitx.Status) (time.Time, time.Time, string) {
248		latest := status.LatestChange
249		var commit time.Time
250		var subject string
251		if unix, lastSubject, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
252			commit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
253			if commit.After(latest) {
254				latest = commit
255			}
256			subject = lastSubject
257		}
258		return latest, commit, subject
259	}
```

```text
291	// assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
292	// checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
293	// x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
294	func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
295		for _, session := range sessions {
296			assigned := map[int]bool{}
297			for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
298				best, bestLen := -1, -1
299				for i := range out.Checkouts {
300					for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Repo, i, out.Checkouts[i]) {
301						if pathContains(root, dir) && len(filepath.Clean(root)) > bestLen {
302							best, bestLen = i, len(filepath.Clean(root))
303						}
304					}
305				}
306				if best >= 0 {
307					assigned[best] = true
308				}
309			}
310			for i := range assigned {
311				out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
312			}
313		}

316	func checkoutRoots(r repo.Repo, index int, checkout RepoCheckout) []string {

324	func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
325		if root == "" || path == "" {
326			return false
327		}
328		rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
329		if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
330			return false
331		}
332		return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
333	}
334
335	func samePath(a, b string) bool {
336		return a != "" && b != "" && normalizePath(a) == normalizePath(b)
337	}
338
339	// normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
340	// paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
341	// also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
342	// is not sufficient.
343	func normalizePath(path string) string {
344		clean := filepath.Clean(path)
345		cur := clean
346		for {
347			if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); err == nil {
348				rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(cur, clean)
349				if relErr == nil && rel != "." {
350					return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(real, rel))
351				}
352				return filepath.Clean(real)
353			}
354			parent := filepath.Dir(cur)
355			if parent == cur {
356				return clean
357			}
358			cur = parent
359		}
360	}

403	func writeCheckoutMarkdown(b *strings.Builder, c RepoContext, checkout RepoCheckout, canonical bool) {
404		label := string(checkout.Ownership)
405		if canonical {
406			label = "canonical"
407		}
408		fmt.Fprintf(b, "### %s — %s\n\n", displayBranch(checkout), label)
409		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Path: `%s`\n", checkout.Worktree.Path)
410		fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Branch: `%s`\n", displayBranch(checkout))
411		if checkout.Worktree.Bare {
412			b.WriteString("- Git: bare repository\n")
413		} else if checkout.PathErr != nil {
414			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: unavailable (%s)\n", checkout.PathErr)
415		} else if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || !checkout.Exists {
416			b.WriteString("- Git: unavailable (checkout path is missing)\n")
417		} else if checkout.StatusErr != nil {
418			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: unavailable (%s)\n", checkout.StatusErr)
419		} else {
420			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Git: %s", checkout.Status.Summary())
421			if checkout.Status.Dirty() {
422				fmt.Fprintf(b, " — %s", checkout.Status.Breakdown())
423			}
424			b.WriteString("\n")
425			if checkout.Status.Upstream != "" {
426				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Upstream: `%s`\n", checkout.Status.Upstream)
427			} else {
428				b.WriteString("- Upstream: not published\n")
429			}
430		}
431		if checkout.Worktree.Locked {
432			reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.LockedReason)
433			if reason == "" {
434				reason = "no reason recorded"
435			}
436			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: locked — %s\n", reason)
437		}
438		if checkout.Worktree.Prunable || checkout.PathErr == nil && !checkout.Exists {
439			reason := strings.TrimSpace(checkout.Worktree.PrunableReason)
440			if reason == "" {
441				reason = "checkout path is missing"
442			}
443			fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Worktree: prunable — %s\n", reason)
444		}
445		if len(checkout.Sessions) == 0 {
446			if c.RuntimeErr != nil {
447				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Runtime: unavailable (%s)\n", c.RuntimeErr)
448			} else {
449				b.WriteString("- Runtime: closed\n")
450			}
451		} else {
452			for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
453				status := session.AgentStatus
454				if status == "" {
455					status = "unknown"
456				}
457				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Runtime: `%s %s` (%s)\n", c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
458				if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
459					fmt.Fprintf(b, "  - Agent sessions: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
460				}
461			}
462		}
463		if len(checkout.Tasks) == 0 {
464			if c.TaskErr != nil {
465				fmt.Fprintf(b, "- Task: unavailable (%s)\n", c.TaskErr)
466			} else {
467				b.WriteString("- Task: untracked\n")
468			}
469		} else {
470			for _, t := range checkout.Tasks {
471				writeTaskMarkdown(b, t)
472			}
473		}
474	}
```

```text
13	// carries no authority to mutate; the full Report binds the same result to

15	type Readiness struct {
16		Outcome assessment.Outcome
17		Reasons []assessment.Reason
18	}

20	// LocalReadiness keeps independently actionable checkout, task, and worktree
21	// scopes separate. There is deliberately no global safe boolean.
22	type LocalReadiness struct {
23		Checkout Readiness
24		Task     Readiness
25		Worktree Readiness

32			"task " + string(r.Task.Outcome),
33			"worktree " + string(r.Worktree.Outcome),

37	// AssessLocal derives readiness from facts already collected by inventory. It
38	// does not run Git, inspect a runtime, or contact a forge/fleet host.
39	func AssessLocal(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int, hostname string) LocalReadiness {
40		return LocalReadiness{
41			Checkout: assessCheckout(context, selectedIndex),
42			Task:     assessTasks(context, selectedIndex, hostname),
43			Worktree: assessWorktrees(context, selectedIndex),
44		}

47	func assessCheckout(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int) Readiness {
48		if selectedIndex < 0 || selectedIndex >= len(context.Checkouts) {
49			return indeterminate("checkout-selection-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "the selected checkout is absent from the local inventory", "rerun context from an existing checkout")
50		}
51		checkout := context.Checkouts[selectedIndex]
52		switch {
53		case checkout.Worktree.Bare || context.Repo.Bare:
54			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeNotApplicable}
55		case checkout.PathErr != nil:
56			return indeterminate("checkout-path-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "the checkout path could not be inspected", "restore path access and rerun context")
57		case !checkout.Exists || checkout.Worktree.Prunable:
58			return blocked("checkout-missing", "selected-checkout", "the checkout path is missing or prunable", "repair or remove the stale worktree registration")
59		case checkout.StatusErr != nil:
60			return indeterminate("checkout-status-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "Git status could not be collected", "repair the checkout and rerun context")
61		case checkout.Worktree.Detached || checkout.Status.Detached || checkout.Branch() == "":
62			return blocked("checkout-detached", "selected-checkout", "the checkout does not have an attached branch", "check out an explicit branch")
63		case checkout.Status.Conflicted > 0:
64			return blocked("checkout-conflicted", "selected-checkout", fmt.Sprintf("the checkout has %d unmerged path(s)", checkout.Status.Conflicted), "resolve the Git operation before transfer or retirement")
65		case checkout.Status.Dirty():
66			return blocked("checkout-dirty", "selected-checkout", fmt.Sprintf("the checkout has %d changed path(s)", checkout.Status.Changed), "commit or deliberately preserve the changes")
67		default:
68			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeEligible}
69		}
70	}
71
72	func assessTasks(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int, hostname string) Readiness {
73		if context.TaskErr != nil {
74			return indeterminate("task-inventory-unavailable", "task-inventory", "task records could not be collected", "repair the task store and rerun context")
75		}
76		if selectedIndex < 0 || selectedIndex >= len(context.Checkouts) {
77			return indeterminate("checkout-selection-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "task scope cannot be selected without a checkout", "rerun context from an existing checkout")
78		}
79		// Transfer/repository readiness covers every non-DONE task attached to the
80		// clone, including cold and branch-only records without a local checkout.
81		// Looking only at the selected checkout can otherwise hide another machine's
82		// ownership claim and incorrectly report not-applicable.
83		active := make([]*task.Task, 0, len(context.OtherTasks)+len(context.Checkouts[selectedIndex].Tasks))
84		sessionCount := map[string]int{}
85		seen := map[string]struct{}{}
86		add := func(candidate *task.Task, sessions int) {
87			if candidate == nil || candidate.State == task.Done {
88				return
89			}
90			if _, exists := seen[candidate.ID]; exists {
91				return
92			}
93			seen[candidate.ID] = struct{}{}
94			active = append(active, candidate)
95			sessionCount[candidate.ID] = sessions
96		}
97		for _, checkout := range context.Checkouts {
98			for _, candidate := range checkout.Tasks {
99				add(candidate, len(checkout.Sessions))
100			}
101		}
102		for _, candidate := range context.OtherTasks {
103			add(candidate, 0)
104		}
105		if len(active) == 0 {
106			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeNotApplicable}
107		}
108		var reasons []assessment.Reason
109		hasIndeterminate := false
110		for _, candidate := range active {
111			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
112				hasIndeterminate = true
113				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
114					Code: "task-record-invalid", Subject: "task", Detail: "a selected task record is invalid",
115					Remediation: "repair or recreate the task record",
116				})
117				continue
118			}
119			if hostname != "" && candidate.Owner != "" && candidate.Owner != hostname {
120				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
121					Code: "task-owned-elsewhere", Subject: "task", Detail: "a selected task is owned by another machine",
122					Remediation: "complete an explicit ownership handoff before writing",
123				})
124			}
125			if candidate.State == task.Hot {
126				if context.RuntimeErr != nil {
127					hasIndeterminate = true
128					reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
129						Code: "runtime-inventory-unavailable", Subject: "task", Detail: "a HOT task cannot be checked against live runtime state",
130						Remediation: "restore runtime inspection and rerun context",
131					})
132				} else if sessionCount[candidate.ID] == 0 {
133					reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
134						Code: "hot-task-runtime-missing", Subject: "task", Detail: "a HOT task has no observed runtime session",
135						Remediation: "resume the task or reconcile its lifecycle state",
136					})
137				}
138			}
139		}
140		if hasReason(reasons, "task-owned-elsewhere") || hasReason(reasons, "hot-task-runtime-missing") {
141			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeBlocked, Reasons: reasons}
142		}
143		if hasIndeterminate {
144			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeIndeterminate, Reasons: reasons}
145		}
146		return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeEligible}
147	}

149	func assessWorktrees(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int) Readiness {
150		if context.WorktreeErr != nil {
151			return indeterminate("worktree-inventory-unavailable", "worktrees", "linked worktrees could not be enumerated", "repair Git worktree metadata and rerun context")
152		}
153		if selectedIndex < 0 || selectedIndex >= len(context.Checkouts) {
154			return indeterminate("checkout-selection-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "worktree scope cannot be selected without a checkout", "rerun context from an existing checkout")
155		}
156		indices := []int{}
157		if selectedIndex > 0 {
158			indices = append(indices, selectedIndex)
159		} else {
160			for index := 1; index < len(context.Checkouts); index++ {
161				indices = append(indices, index)
162			}
163		}
164		if len(indices) == 0 {
165			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeNotApplicable}
166		}
167		var reasons []assessment.Reason
168		hasUnknown := context.RuntimeErr != nil
169		if hasUnknown {
170			reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
171				Code: "runtime-inventory-unavailable", Subject: "worktrees",
172				Detail:      "worktree runtime coverage could not be collected",
173				Remediation: "restore runtime inspection and rerun context",
174			})
175		}
176		for _, index := range indices {
177			checkout := context.Checkouts[index]
178			subject := fmt.Sprintf("worktree:%d", index)
179			switch {
180			case checkout.PathErr != nil:
181				hasUnknown = true
182				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-path-unavailable", Subject: subject, Detail: "the worktree path could not be inspected", Remediation: "restore path access and rerun context"})
183			case !checkout.Exists || checkout.Worktree.Prunable:
184				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-missing", Subject: subject, Detail: "the worktree path is missing or prunable", Remediation: "repair or remove the stale worktree registration"})
185			case checkout.StatusErr != nil:
186				hasUnknown = true
187				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-status-unavailable", Subject: subject, Detail: "Git status could not be collected for the worktree", Remediation: "repair the worktree and rerun context"})
188			case checkout.Worktree.Locked:
189				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-locked", Subject: subject, Detail: "the worktree is locked", Remediation: "verify the lock owner before unlocking it"})
190			case checkout.Status.Conflicted > 0:
191				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-conflicted", Subject: subject, Detail: "the worktree has unmerged paths", Remediation: "resolve the Git operation before transfer or retirement"})
192			case checkout.Status.Dirty():
193				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-dirty", Subject: subject, Detail: "the worktree contains uncommitted changes", Remediation: "commit or deliberately preserve the changes"})
194			case len(checkout.Sessions) > 0:
195				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{Code: "worktree-runtime-live", Subject: subject, Detail: "a runtime session still covers the worktree", Remediation: "quiesce and close the runtime before retirement"})
196			}

198		if len(reasons) == 0 {

200		}
201		if hasKnownBlocker(reasons) {

203		}
204		if hasUnknown {
205			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeIndeterminate, Reasons: reasons}
206		}
207		return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeBlocked, Reasons: reasons}
```

```text
115	func humanAge(seconds int64) string {
116		switch {
117		case seconds < 60:
118			return fmt.Sprintf("%ds", seconds)
119		case seconds < 3600:
120			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", seconds/60)
121		case seconds < 86400:
122			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", seconds/3600)
123		default:
124			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", seconds/86400)
125		}
```

```text
 // Sessions returns the repo's live sessions once each, preserving checkout
 // order so a pasted context reads canonical-first.
 func (c RepoContext) Sessions() []runtime.Session {
    seen := map[string]bool{}
    var out []runtime.Session
    for _, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
        for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
            key := session.Handle
            if key == "" {
                key = session.Label + "\x00" + strings.Join(session.Dirs, "\x00")
            }
            if seen[key] {
                continue
            }
            seen[key] = true
            out = append(out, session)
        }
    }
    return out

 func samePath(a, b string) bool {
    return a != "" && b != "" && normalizePath(a) == normalizePath(b)

 // normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
 // paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
 // also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
 // is not sufficient.
 func normalizePath(path string) string {
    clean := filepath.Clean(path)
    cur := clean
    for {
        if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); err == nil {
            rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(cur, clean)
            if relErr == nil && rel != "." {
                return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(real, rel))
            }
            return filepath.Clean(real)
        }
        parent := filepath.Dir(cur)
        if parent == cur {
            return clean
        }
        cur = parent
    }
 }
```

```text
55	func CanonicalRepoIdentity(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) (string, error) {
56		root, err := pathx.Canonical(repoRoot)
57		if err != nil {
58			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize repository: %w", err)
59		}

63		}
64		if !info.IsDir() {
65			return "", fmt.Errorf("repository path %s is not a directory", root)
66		}
67		if ctx == nil {
68			ctx = context.Background()
69		}
70		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, root)
71		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
72			return root, nil
73		}
74		if err != nil {
75			return "", fmt.Errorf("discover repository identity: %w", err)

77		identity, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
```
