2972	 ## Repository bootstrap
2973
2974	 Repository setup remains separate from acquisition. For acquisition,
2975	 `new`/`create` distinguishes a plain repository name from a clear clone
2976	 reference:
2977
2978	 | Command | Behavior |
2979	 |---|---|
2980	 | `dev repo new` | interactive wizard; its first field accepts either a new name or a clone reference |
2981	 | `dev repo new NAME` / `dev repo create NAME` | create a new local repository; a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name instead routes to clone and preserves history/remote |
2982	 | `dev repo clone [owner/name\|url]` | clone into the configured destination, then optionally apply a preset; setup defaults off |
2983	 | `dev repo setup [repo-or-path]` | repeat-safely merge native initializers and preset files into an existing clean checkout; defaults to the current repository and does not commit unless requested |
2984
2985	 A clone-routed `new` retains the source `origin`; it therefore rejects
2986	 new-upstream creation flags. It also rejects `--template*`, whose explicit
2987	 meaning is “copy content into a fresh history.”

3031

3033	@@ -304,68 +307,74 @@ required = true

3037	 `builtin = "project-knowledge-harness"`; these fixed reviewed initializers do
3038	 not execute downloaded skill code.

3040	 A preset may extend one parent. Scalars override; simple lists replace; files,
3041	 hooks, and skills merge by `id`, and an inherited item can be disabled with
3042	 `enabled = false`. A `[[presets.*.files]]` rendering source must remain in the
3043	 `templates/` tree next to its config source; that file-level mechanism is
3044	 separate from the repository snapshot `template` scalar above. Destinations
3045	 must remain inside the repository, and a skill setup script must remain inside
3046	 the installed skill directory. `initial_check_in` accepts `commit`, `stage`, or
3047	 `none`; the legacy `initial_commit` boolean remains readable, but a preset must
3048	 not set both.

3050	 ### Safe project overlays
3051
3052	 A repository may commit these fixed files:
3053
3054	-- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning and repository
3055	-  setup wizard defaults.
3056	+- `.dev-cli/config.toml`: allowlisted worktree provisioning, separately
3057	+  proposed portable local-file patterns, and repository setup wizard defaults.
3058	 - `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`: project presets, templates, hooks, and skill
3059	   setup using the same versioned schema.
3060
3061	 ```toml
3062	 # .dev-cli/config.toml
3063	 version = 1
3064
3065	 [worktree]
3066	 include = [".env.example"]
3067	 strategy = "reinstall"
3068
3069	+# Proposed candidates only; export still requires explicit fleet files --to.
3070	+[local_files]
3071	+include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
3072	+
3073	 [repo.setup]
3074	 preset = "team"
3075	 handoff = "cd"
3076	 check_in = "stage"
3077	 ```
3078
3079	 Effective precedence, lowest to highest, is built-ins, global config/scaffolds,
3080	 legacy `.dev.toml`, the target repository's `.dev-cli/*`, then explicit CLI or
3081	 wizard choices. `.dev.toml` remains readable for compatibility; new project
3082	 configuration should use `.dev-cli/config.toml`. Global `default_preset` and the
3083	 project `[repo.setup]` preset, handoff, and check-in fields seed interactive
3084	 wizard choices; they do not change scripted defaults, which are controlled by
3085	 the corresponding flags. The legacy `commit` boolean remains readable, but may
3086	 not be combined with `check_in` in the same layer.
3087
3088	+`[local_files].include` never inherits `[worktree].include`: provisioning a local checkout is not authorization to export a secret. Project overlays may propose only the portable include list; host-owned count/size/path ceilings come from global config and cannot be raised by a repository. The command remains report-only until an explicit `--apply`, target pin, and confirmation.
3089	+
3090	 Project files cannot override host paths, state location, runtime backend,
3091	 forge inventory or credentials, stats, update, bootstrap, or TUI policy. They
3092	 also cannot silently publish a repository. Before a post-create command from
3093	 `.dev-cli/config.toml`, or a hook or skill setup from project
3094	 `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml`, executes, dev asks to trust the canonical repository
3095	 plus an execution-content hash. Changed executable content requires new
3096	 consent; non-interactive use without a matching trust record fails closed.
3097	 Legacy `.dev.toml` retains its compatibility behavior. Keep credentials and
3098	 host-specific paths in user config or ignored environment files, never in a
3099	 committed project overlay.
3100
3101	 Project-authored skill setup must use a local source so its bytes can be bound
3102	 to the trust hash. Remote project skills may still be installed, but cannot
3103	 declare executable setup; global presets remain host-owned policy.

3105	 ## Colored output
3106
3107	 Every human-readable surface applies semantic ANSI color through a small set of roles: `title`/`header`/`prompt` (bold cyan), `label`/`dim` (dim), `success` (green), `warning` (yellow), `danger` (bold red), `review` (magenta, for a PR/review handoff), and `strong`/`code` for Markdown. Values that carry their own meaning are colored by that meaning rather than by a fixed role:
3108
3109	 | Value | Green | Yellow | Red |

3329	 # Compatibility and known limitations
3330
3331	 This page separates graceful degradation from real limitations. Reverify it whenever command/runtime code or version-sensitive Claude Code documentation changes.
3332
3333	 ## dev-cli capability matrix
3334
3335	 | Capability | Dependency | Without it |
3336	 |---|---|---|
3337	 | core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
3338	 | rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |
3339	 | named terminal session | tmux or compatible Zellij | `none` preserves core behavior and shell navigation |
3340	 | GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
3341	 | GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |
3342	 | repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` or `glab` | local repository/scaffold still works; the wizard explains how to log in |
3343	 | remote repository snapshot template | Git plus network/authentication for the source | validation fails before the destination is created and rendered URL userinfo is redacted; local templates still work |
3344	 | setup-capable project skills | skills provider plus the entrypoint interpreter | unselected skills are skipped; selected required setup fails before scaffold mutation when its interpreter is unavailable; a clone acquired first is retained |
3345	 | staged lazygit message prefill | a lazygit version that reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT` | files remain staged and dev prints the suggested message; normal Git commit remains available |
3346	 | worktree dependency setup | ecosystem manager (`uv`, npm, Cargo, etc.) | plan reports the missing tool and keeps the checkout |
3347	+| remote portable-file plan/apply | Git, SSH target running a compatible `dev`, matching existing clone/branch/commit; apply also needs a verified machine UUID pin | fails before content is sent or leaves the target unchanged; no clone/task fallback is inferred |
3348	 | interactive dashboard | terminal input/output | bare `dev` prints the plain task list when piped |
3349	 | repository-note search | linked `modernc.org/sqlite` with FTS5 | no external `sqlite3` executable is required |
3350	 | terminal multiplexing on Windows | tmux/Zellij/Herdr (POSIX only) | Windows always uses the `none` backend; `dev shell-init powershell` still moves the shell |
3351	 | in-place self-update | standalone install (not Homebrew/Scoop/`go install`) | `dev upgrade` prints the package manager's upgrade command instead |
3352
3353	 ## Confirmed project limitations
3354
3355	 ### Note search and filesystem durability vary by text and platform
3356
3357	 Latin note queries use term-wise prefix FTS and SQLite ranking. Non-ASCII queries use literal term-wise substring matching because SQLite's `unicode61` tokenizer does not segment arbitrary CJK substrings; those results do not use the same FTS ranking.
3358
3359	 Note writes sync the file and atomically rename it on every supported platform. Unix also syncs the containing directory after rename/delete. The Windows implementation cannot provide that directory-fsync step, so a sudden power loss has a narrower durability guarantee there. Concurrent mutations by cooperating `dev` processes are serialized and each Markdown replacement is atomic; arbitrary external writers do not participate in that lock.
3360
3361	 ### Pull-request completion is not tracked automatically
3362
3363	 `dev done --pr` pushes and opens a pull/merge request, then leaves the task, runtime, and worktree unchanged because review owns integration. Current `dev sweep` does not query the forge to infer that a request later merged. Verify integration and finish/reconcile deliberately; do not assume remote merge implies local DONE.
3364
3365	 ### Agent session capture is reserved, not wired
3366
3367	 The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live agent session IDs. The production start/park/resume path does not yet capture or attach that ID. Treat the field and live inventory as observability/future integration, not a promise that `dev resume` restores the coding-agent conversation.
3368	@@ -49,62 +50,71 @@ The task schema has an `AgentSession` field and Herdr inventory can expose live
3369
3370	 `dev config init` writes `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`. With no config file, the current built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` zero value means an existing valid cache is not rejected by age; explicit `r` refresh still replaces it. Run `config init` or set the TTL when freshness matters.
3371
3372	 Older generated configs may contain `forge.remote_limit = 100`. The field is
3373	 still accepted, but complete forge inventories are now paginated and it no
3374	 longer caps synchronization. `dev config init` no longer writes it. The
3375	 `--limit` flag on `dev repo remote` limits rendered matches after the complete
3376	 inventory has been searched.
3377
3378	 ### Lazygit staged-message prefill is best effort
3379
3380	 `repo --check-in=stage` writes a pending message in the exact worktree Git
3381	 directory. [Lazygit v0.59.0 uses that file for lowercase
3382	 `c`](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216), but it is a
3383	 lazygit implementation detail rather than a Git interface; uppercase `C` and
3384	 plain `git commit` do not consume it. Dev never overwrites a different existing
3385	 draft. A draft-write failure is warning-only: staging remains successful and
3386	 is never rolled back. If the integration changes upstream, the staged index
3387	 and printed message remain the recovery path.
3388
3389	+### Portable files are not project transfer or backup
3390	+
3391	+`dev fleet files` moves only explicitly selected, bounded files that both hosts prove are untracked and ignored. It does not acquire a missing clone, transfer task ownership/catalog/notes, run worktree provisioning, watch for later changes, propagate deletion, remove source bytes, produce a remote-backup receipt, verify restore, or authorize eviction. Private transaction staging is not a user-facing backup/restore promise.
3392	+
3393	+The source and target must already match by fetch identity, attached branch, and exact commit. An apply additionally needs a verified `machine_id` pin. Native Windows payloads remain disabled until ACL, reparse-point, held-root, and atomic replacement guarantees are implemented and tested there; machine identity diagnostics remain content-free.
3394	+
3395	 ### Windows is a build target, not a full-feature platform
3396
3397	 `dev` compiles and runs on `windows/amd64` and `windows/arm64`, and every release ships a `.zip` for each. Core repository, task and worktree operations work. What differs:
3398
3399	 - There is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the runtime backend is always `none`. Grouped runtime/agent activity and named sessions are unavailable; the `cd` directive and PowerShell wrapper still work.
3400	 - Shell integration is `dev shell-init powershell`. POSIX shells hand the directory back on file descriptor 3; PowerShell cannot inherit it, so the wrapper passes a temp-file path in `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` instead.
3401	 - `dev fleet open` starts a child shell (`%COMSPEC%`) rather than replacing the process, because Windows has no `exec(2)`.
3402	+- `dev fleet machine-id` can perform its content-free probe, but native `fleet files` payload apply is capability-blocked before content is sent.
3403	 - The domain test suites still assume a POSIX filesystem in places, so Windows CI runs the tests advisory-only while compilation, `go vet` and the build are enforced.
3404
3405	 ### Direct mode has a smaller lifecycle
3406
3407	 A direct task uses the canonical checkout and cannot go COLD, because cold cleanup would remove a directory the repository needs. Use branch-only or worktree mode for cross-machine reconstruction.
3408
3409	 ## Current behaviors that are implemented
3410
3411	 These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
3412
3413	 - `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
3414	 - `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
3415	 - Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
3416	 - Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The `agent-history-hygiene` initializer writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
3417	 - Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
3418	+- `dev repo context --json` exposes additive schema-v1 local/remote evidence with source, age, freshness, completeness, null/error preservation, and scoped readiness; external probes happen only with `--refresh`.
3419	+- `dev fleet machine-id` reports an observed UUID without changing configuration. `dev fleet files` is report-only by default, uses a separate `[local_files]` allowlist, negotiates downward-only limits before content, and requires explicit apply/replacement controls plus a matching target pin.
3420
3421	 - `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
3422	 - TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
3423	 - Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
3424	 - `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
3425
3426	 - `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
3427	 - Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
3428	 - `dev done` records MERGED only: it never closes the invoking runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. Cleanup moved to `dev retire`, which runs from outside the target workspace, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, and revalidates Git state after every runtime closure. `dev done --delete-branch` is now an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
3429	 - `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
3430	 - `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
3431	 - An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
3432	 - A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
3433	 - Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
3434	 - Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
3435	 - Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
3436	 - `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
3437	 - `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
3438	 - `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
3439	 - `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
3440	@@ -137,22 +147,25 @@ These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
3441

3488	 ## dev-cli capability matrix
3489
3490	 | Capability | Dependency | 缺少時 |
3491	 |---|---|---|
3492	 | 核心 repository/task/worktree 操作 | Git | 無法使用；Git 是唯一 hard runtime dependency |
3493	 | grouped runtime 與 agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` 改試 tmux、Zellij，最後 none |
3494	 | named terminal session | tmux 或相容 Zellij | `none` 保留核心 behavior 與 shell navigation |
3495	 | GitHub pull requests/remotes | authenticated `gh` | Git 可用時 branch 仍能 push，可能需 browser/manual flow |
3496	 | GitLab merge requests/remotes | authenticated `glab` | 同樣 graceful fallback |
3497	 | repository bootstrap publishing | authenticated `gh` 或 `glab` | local repository/scaffold 仍可使用；wizard 會說明如何 login |

3508	 ## 已確認的專案限制
3509
3510	 ### Note search 與 filesystem durability 依文字及平台而異
3511
3512	 Latin note query 使用 term-wise prefix FTS 與 SQLite ranking。Non-ASCII query 改用 literal term-wise substring matching，因為 SQLite 的 `unicode61` tokenizer 不會切分任意 CJK substrings；這些結果不使用相同的 FTS ranking。
3513
3514	 所有支援平台的 note write 都會 sync file 並 atomic rename。Unix 也會在 rename/delete 後 sync containing directory。Windows implementation 無法提供 directory-fsync 步驟，因此 sudden power loss 時的 durability guarantee 較窄。Cooperating `dev` processes 的 concurrent mutations 會被 serialized，且每次 Markdown replacement 都是 atomic；任意 external writer 不會參與這個 lock。
3515
3516	 ### Pull request completion 不會自動追蹤
3517
3518	 `dev done --pr` push 並建立 pull/merge request，之後保留 task、runtime 與 worktree，因為 integration 由 review 負責。目前 `dev sweep` 不會 query forge 推斷 request 後來已 merge。請驗證 integration 後再刻意 finish/reconcile；不能假設 remote merge 代表 local DONE。
3519
3520	 ### Agent session capture 只有保留欄位，尚未接線
3521
3522	 Task schema 有 `AgentSession`，Herdr inventory 也能顯示 live agent session ID；production start/park/resume path 尚未 capture 或 attach 該 ID。這個欄位與 live inventory 只能視為 observability/future integration，不能承諾 `dev resume` 會恢復 coding-agent conversation。
3523
3524	 ### Built-in forge cache TTL 與 generated config 不同
3525
3526	 `dev config init` 會寫 `forge.cache_ttl = "15m"`。沒有 config file 時，目前 built-in `Forge.CacheTTL` 的 zero value 代表既有 valid cache 不會因 age 被拒絕；explicit `r` 仍會 refresh。Freshness 重要時請執行 `config init` 或設定 TTL。
3527
3528	 較舊的 generated config 可能包含 `forge.remote_limit = 100`。此欄位仍可解析，
3529	 但 forge inventory 現在會完整 pagination，因此不再限制 synchronization。
3530	 `dev config init` 不再寫入它；`dev repo remote --limit` 只在完整 inventory 搜尋
3531	 完成後限制 rendered matches。
3532
3533	 ### Lazygit staged-message prefill 是 best effort
3534
3535	 `repo --check-in=stage` 會在正確的 worktree Git directory 寫入 pending message。
3536	 [Lazygit v0.59.0 的小寫 `c` 會使用該
3537	 檔案](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/blob/v0.59.0/pkg/gui/controllers/helpers/working_tree_helper.go#L191-L216)，但這是 lazygit implementation detail，不是 Git
3538	 interface；大寫 `C` 與一般 `git commit` 不會讀取它。Dev 不會覆寫內容不同的既有
3539	 draft。Draft write failure 只會產生 warning；staging 仍視為成功且不會 rollback。若
3540	 upstream integration 日後改變，staged index 與已印出的 message 仍是 recovery path。
3541
3542	+### Portable files 不是 project transfer 或 backup
3543	+
3544	+`dev fleet files` 只會傳送 explicit selected、bounded，且兩端都證明為 untracked 與 ignored 的 files。它不會取得 missing clone、轉移 task ownership/catalog/notes、執行 worktree provisioning、監看後續變更、傳播 deletion、移除 source bytes、建立 remote-backup receipt、驗證 restore，或授權 eviction。Private transaction staging 不是 user-facing backup/restore promise。
3545	+
3546	+Source 與 target 必須已依 fetch identity、attached branch 與 exact commit 相符；apply 另外需要 verified `machine_id` pin。Native Windows payload 在 ACL、reparse-point、held-root 與 atomic replacement guarantees 完成並測試前保持 disabled；machine identity diagnostics 仍是 content-free。
3547	+
3548	 ### Windows 是 build target，不是 full-feature 平台
3549
3550	 `dev` 可在 `windows/amd64` 與 `windows/arm64` 編譯並執行，每個 release 都會附各自的 `.zip`。核心的 repository、task 與 worktree 操作可用。差異：
3551
3552	 - 沒有 tmux、Zellij 或 Herdr，因此 runtime backend 一律是 `none`。Grouped runtime/agent activity 與 named session 無法使用；`cd` 指令與 PowerShell wrapper 仍可運作。
3553	 - Shell integration 是 `dev shell-init powershell`。POSIX shell 透過 file descriptor 3 回傳目錄；PowerShell 無法繼承它，wrapper 改用 `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` 傳入 temp-file path。
3554	 - `dev fleet open` 會啟動子 shell（`%COMSPEC%`），而非取代 process，因為 Windows 沒有 `exec(2)`。
3555	+- `dev fleet machine-id` 可執行 content-free probe，但 native `fleet files` payload apply 會在 content 傳送前被 capability-block。
3556	 - Domain test suites 仍有部分假設 POSIX filesystem，因此 Windows CI 的 test 僅供參考，compilation、`go vet` 與 build 則為強制項。
3557
3558	 ### Direct mode 的 lifecycle 較小
3559
3560	 Direct task 使用 canonical checkout，不能進入 COLD，因為 cold cleanup 會移除 repository 必需的 directory。需要跨機器 reconstruction 時使用 branch-only 或 worktree mode。
3561
3562	 ## 已實作、不能再列為 limitation 的 behavior
3563
3564	 以下是歷史缺口，現行版本已實作：
3565
3566	 - `dev repo new|create`、`repo clone` 與 `repo setup` 共用 preset-driven bootstrap pipeline。Plain explicit `repo new NAME` 仍維持 minimal；清楚的 Git URL、local Git path 或 owner/name 會改走 clone acquisition，保留 source history/remote。無參數 wizard 的第一個欄位也會偵測同樣 reference；建立新 repository 時，預設為 no 的 customization gate 讓正常 `agent-ready` flow 保持精簡。Text fields 使用 TTY inline editor，因此 cursor keys 會編輯內容，不會插入 raw escape bytes；non-TTY reader 維持 line-oriented behavior。
3567	 - `repo new` 可從 local directory/repository 或 Git source 的 optional branch、tag、commit 與 confined subdirectory 建立 fresh-history snapshot。未 pin 的 local Git tree 包含 tracked 加 untracked non-ignored files；non-Git directory 包含完整 current tree。Source `.git` metadata 會排除、URL userinfo 會 redact，不安全的 file types/paths 會在 destination 建立前失敗，held root/file handles 會限制 mutable-path races。Human plan 會預覽 paths 並警告 live snapshot，preset 也可選擇 catalog-repository subfolder。
3568	 - Repository setup 支援 `--check-in=commit|stage|none`（`auto` 用於 preset compatibility）。Staged setup 會執行 before-commit setup 與 `git add -A`，但不執行 `after_commit` phase；它不能 publish 或 handoff 到 `start`，並可依前述方式預填 lazygit 小寫 `c`。
3569	 - Source 與 agent targets 相同的 selected skills 會共用一次 installer invocation。`agent-history-hygiene` initializer 會寫入 pre-commit/gitleaks policy，並將缺少的 machine-local `.project.json`／`statistics.json` 規則 merge 進 `.specstory/.gitignore`；custom content 與 transcript history 都保持可追蹤。
3570	 - Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` 與 `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` 僅能保存 portable setup policy。Executable project configuration 會綁定 canonical Git common directory 與 exact content hash；hash 改變後必須重新信任。
3571	+- `dev repo context --json` 提供 additive schema-v1 local/remote evidence，包含 source、age、freshness、completeness、null/error preservation 與 scoped readiness；只有 `--refresh` 執行 external probes。
3572	+- `dev fleet machine-id` 回報 observed UUID，不修改設定。`dev fleet files` 預設 report-only，使用獨立 `[local_files]` allowlist，在 content 前協商只能調低的 limits，並要求 explicit apply/replacement controls 與 matching target pin。
3573
3574	 - `dev start --focus` 會在 non-JSON creation 後 activate runtime。
3575	 - TUI navigation 會拒絕開啟 checkout 不存在的 COLD task，並要求使用 `dev resume`。
3576	 - Runtime handle 現在保存 backend provenance，cleanup 前會重新驗證。
3577	 - `auto` runtime selection 已在 tmux 與 none 之間加入 Zellij。
3578
3579	 - `dev done` 在省略 `--ff`/`--pr` 且為 TTY 時會開啟 interactive finish wizard，把 dirty checkout 拿去跟 base 比較（commit、discard 或 cancel），不再直接拒絕任何 uncommitted change；non-interactive caller 仍須明確傳入 `--dirty` policy，且 destructive discard 需要 `--yes`。
3580	 - Human-readable output 現在具備 semantic color（`--color auto|always|never`），在 `NO_COLOR` 已設定、`TERM=dumb`，或 stdout/stderr 不是 terminal 時會自動停用。
3581	 - `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED：它不會關閉呼叫端 runtime、移除 worktree 或刪除 branch。Cleanup 已移交 `dev retire`，後者必須從目標 workspace 之外執行，會拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，並在每次關閉 runtime 之後重新驗證 Git state。`dev done --delete-branch` 現在會直接報錯並指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`，`--keep-worktree` 則以 no-op 警告。
3582	 - `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` 直接從 Git 列舉 linked worktrees，而非從 task registry，因此 branch 已被 base 包含的 unmanaged worktree 也能被 retire。Containment 本身絕不等於許可；dirty state、未 finalize 的 artifact、進行中的 Git operation 與 runtime 拒絕條件都仍會阻擋，且未加 `--delete-branches` 時 branch 一律保留。
3583	 - `dev sweep` 會把 branch 已不存在於 Git 的 branch-backed task 視為 dead，並提供 reap 該 record 的建議。這種 task 無法 finish、resume 或 retire，因為這些路徑都必須先解析 branch；在 `--apply` 之前該建議仍只是報告。
3584	 - 未知 command 會被回報，而不是被丟棄。`dev` 關閉了 cobra 自己的 error 輸出，先前又額外略過所有訊息開頭為 `unknown command` 的 error，因此打錯 command 時兩個 stream 都沒有任何輸出。現在會把訊息、cobra 的「Did you mean this?」建議，以及指向 `--help` 的提示寫到 stderr，exit status 為 1。
3585	 - 對 command family 傳入多餘的 argument 現在是 error，而不是安靜地印出 help。`dev wt bogus` 過去會印出 `dev wt` help 並 exit 0，因為 family 本身沒有 `Run`；現在每個 family node 都會回報未知 subcommand 並 exit 1，而單獨執行 family 仍會印出 help 並 exit 0。
3586	 - Argument 數量與 flag 錯誤會印出該 command 的 usage block。該 block 是否上色仍由 `--color` 決定。
3587	 - 每個 command family 的 help 都附上 ASCII orientation diagram 與 `See also: dev help <topic>` 指引，且 `dev help <command>` 會把 command 名稱或 alias 解析成對應 topic，因此 `dev help wt` 會連到 worktrees 頁面。
3588	 - Semantic color 已覆蓋所有 human-readable 介面，包含 interactive dashboard：`dev --color never`、`NO_COLOR` 與 `TERM=dumb` 現在也會關閉 dashboard 的顏色，先前並不會。
3589	 - `dev sweep` 會 reap repository 目錄已不存在的 task。這種 record 先前無法被 binary 中任何 command 觸及：`done`、`resume`、`park` 與 `retire` 都會先解析 repository，dead-branch 規則排除 direct mode，stale-worktree 規則又需要有記錄的 worktree path。若有 live runtime session 則不會提出此建議，且 reap 只移除 dev 的 intent record。
3590	 - `dev sweep` 會回報 task 記錄中存在、但 Git 未註冊，且只包含 agent artifact 目錄的 checkout。只有在其中每個檔案都與 repository 既有檔案 byte-identical 時才提議移除；其餘一律回報為 salvage 工作，即使加上 `--apply` 也絕不移除。
3591	 - `dev sweep` 會處理 worktree 仍在磁碟上的 cold task。Inventory 一直有為 `dev ls` 與 dashboard 計算這項 drift，但 sweep 從未讀取它，因此只能顯示、無法處理。
3592	 - `dev retire <path>` 會 reap 對應的 task record。先前只有 by-task 形式會設定 task identity，因此以 path 退休同一個 checkout 會留下 record；DONE 狀態與 identity 檢查維持不變。

3632	 # Sources and freshness
3633
3634	 This site mixes product documentation, external specifications, fast-moving harness behavior, project policy, and history. Every page identifies which kind of statement it contains and when it was checked.
3635
3636	 ## Authority order
3637
3638	 1. **dev-cli behavior:** repository code, tests, E2E, and generated command reference.
3639	 2. **Git semantics:** current `git-scm.com` manuals for the relevant installed Git version.
3640	 3. **GitHub collaboration:** current GitHub Docs.
3641	 4. **Claude Code behavior:** current Anthropic documentation, with preview/experimental/version labels.
3642	 5. **Standards:** named versioned specifications such as Conventional Commits 1.0.0 and SemVer 2.0.0.
3643	 6. **Historical context:** dated archives and older project essays, never a current operating rule.
3644	 7. **Project policy:** explicitly labeled recommendations; not presented as an upstream guarantee.
3645
3646	 A lower item may explain motivation but cannot override a higher authority's implementation claim.

3779	 ## Configure hosts
3780
3781	 ```bash
3782	 dev fleet config init
3783	 dev fleet config edit
3784	 dev fleet status
3785	+dev fleet machine-id lab
3786	 ```
3787
3788	 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` follows the same connection model as an
3789	 ordinary OpenSSH invocation. Prefer `ssh_alias`; explicit
3790	 `hostname`/`user`/`port`/`identity_file` fields are available when needed.
3791	 Password fallback supports `prompt`, `plain` and `bitwarden`, but key or agent
3792	-authentication is always attempted first.
3793	+authentication is always attempted first. Read-only commands tolerate an
3794	+unpinned host. Before a mutating file transfer, run `dev fleet machine-id
3795	+<host>`, verify the UUID independently, and add it as that host's `machine_id`;
3796	+the command reports but never writes the pin.

3798	 ## Inspect and open
3799
3800	 ```bash
3801	 dev fleet list
3802	 dev fleet list --host lab --repo api
3803	 dev fleet list --cached
3804	 dev fleet list --json
3805	 dev fleet open lab api
3806	 ```
3807
3808	 Every host runs its own `dev`, so its `config.toml`, scan roots, exact repo
3809	 paths, task registry and runtime remain authoritative. A missing remote `dev`
3810	 is `no-dev`, not a fleet-wide failure. Unreachable hosts reuse the last
3811	 successful private XDG snapshot when available.
3812
3813	 Opening a remote repo prefers native Herdr remoting when an active remote Herdr
3814	 server is visible. It otherwise opens `ssh -t`, validates the repository path
3815	 through remote dev, changes directory and starts a login shell.
3816
3817	 ## Safely propagate a branch
3818
3819	 ```bash
3820	 dev fleet sync api --push
3821	 dev fleet sync api                 # HEAD must already equal fetched upstream
3822	 dev fleet sync api --host lab
3823	 ```
3824
3825	 The source must be clean and attached. Targets are matched by normalized Git
3826	 remote identity, not directory name. Each target fetches first; only a clean
3827	 checkout of the same branch that is strictly behind is advanced with
3828	 `merge --ff-only`. Different branches are not switched. Dirty, ahead,
3829	 divergent, ambiguous and unreachable targets remain untouched and make sync
3830	 return non-zero. Hosts without dev or without that repository are ignored and
3831	 reported explicitly.
3832
3833	 There is no automatic rebase, force push, background hook or all-repository
3834	 pull. Resolve divergent work interactively on the machine that owns it.
3835	+
3836	+## Transfer explicit ignored files
3837	+
3838	+```bash
3839	+dev fleet files api --to lab
3840	+dev fleet files api --to lab --apply --yes
3841	+dev fleet files api --to lab --replace --apply
3842	+```
3843	+
3844	+The report-only default expands `[local_files].include` plus repeatable `--file`
3845	+patterns into exact source paths. Source and target must already match by fetch
3846	+identity, attached branch and commit. Both sides must prove each path untracked
3847	+and ignored; only bounded regular files pass. `--replace` separately authorizes
3848	+a target whose bytes differ, and `--yes` never implies replacement.
3849	+
3850	+Apply requires a matching `machine_id` pin, uses a bounded non-PTY protocol,
3851	+keeps file content and hashes out of public output/cache, writes owner-only
3852	+files through held roots, and journals rollback before publication. It does not
3853	+clone, switch branches, transfer tasks/catalog/notes, provision dependencies,
3854	+delete source files, or evict a repository. Native Windows payloads are blocked.

4005	 ## When to use this skill
4006
4007	 - "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
4008	 - Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
4009	 - Spawning independent background agents without disturbing a live checkout.
4010	 - "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
4011	 - A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
4012	 - Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
4013	 - Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
4014	 - Promoting an experiment into a real project.
4015	 - "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
4016	 - Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
4017	 - Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
4018	 - Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.

4021	 - **`dev` may be a shell wrapper around the binary.** The trusted `shell-init`
4022	   output defines a wrapper that gives navigation commands a private side channel
4023	   (a child-only file descriptor for POSIX shells, a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp
4024	   file for `shell-init powershell`), reads one NUL-terminated path and calls
4025	   `builtin cd` / `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. Without the
4026	   wrapper, the binary's printable legacy directive cannot change the parent
4027	   shell — that is not a bug.

524	 func canonicalValues(values ...string) map[string]struct{} {
525	 	out := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
526	 	for _, value := range values {
527	 		if canonical := canonicalValue(value); canonical != "" {
528	 			out[canonical] = struct{}{}
529	 		}
530	 	}
531	 	return out
532	 }

554	 // NormalizeRemoteIdentity converts common HTTPS and SCP-style Git URLs into a
555	 // stable host/path key. Hosts are case-insensitive, but paths are preserved
556	 // because arbitrary Git servers may use a case-sensitive repository namespace.
557	 // The result remains only a hint for matching.
558	 func NormalizeRemoteIdentity(identity string) string {
559	 	identity = strings.TrimSpace(identity)
560	 	if identity == "" {
561	 		return ""
562	 	}
563	 	if azure := normalizeAzureDevOpsRemoteIdentity(identity); azure != "" {
564	 		return azure
565	 	}
566	 	if parsed, err := url.Parse(identity); err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" {
567	 		if strings.EqualFold(parsed.Scheme, "file") {
568	 			return ""
569	 		}
570	 		if parsed.Host != "" {
571	 			return remoteIdentityKey(parsed.Host, parsed.EscapedPath())
572	 		}
573	 	}
574	 	if looksLikeLocalRemote(identity) {
575	 		return ""
576	 	}
577
578	 	afterUser := identity
579	 	user := ""
580	 	if at := strings.LastIndexByte(afterUser, '@'); at >= 0 {
581	 		user, afterUser = afterUser[:at], afterUser[at+1:]
582	+		// A colon in an scp-like user prefix is a password/token separator,
583	+		// not a stable SSH username. Reject the identity rather than persisting
584	+		// credential material in catalog keys, reports, or protocol journals.
585	+		if strings.Contains(user, ":") {
586	+			return ""
587	+		}
588	 	}
589	 	if host, remotePath, ok := splitSCPLike(afterUser); ok {
590	 		if user != "" && !strings.EqualFold(user, "git") && !strings.HasPrefix(remotePath, "/") {
591	 			remotePath = "~" + user + "/" + remotePath
592	 		}
593	 		return remoteIdentityKey(host, remotePath)
594	 	}
595
596	 	identity = strings.Trim(identity, "/")
597	 	if host, remotePath, ok := strings.Cut(identity, "/"); ok {
598	 		return remoteIdentityKey(host, remotePath)
599	 	}
600	 	return ""
601	 }
602
603	 func normalizeAzureDevOpsRemoteIdentity(identity string) string {
604	 	if kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(identity); kind == forge.AzureDevOps && name != "" {
605	 		return string(forge.AzureDevOps) + "/" + name
606	 	}
607
608	 	// Records written before Azure support already contain the generic
609	 	// host/path form. Recognize it so existing catalog entries migrate on read.
610	 	trimmed := strings.Trim(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(identity), ".git"), "/")
611	 	parts := strings.Split(trimmed, "/")
612	 	decode := func(values []string) ([]string, bool) {
613	 		out := make([]string, len(values))
614	 		for i, value := range values {
615	 			decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(value)
616	 			if err != nil || decoded == "" || strings.Contains(decoded, "/") {
617	 				return nil, false
618	 			}
619	 			out[i] = decoded
620	 		}
621	 		return out, true
622	 	}
623	 	if len(parts) == 5 && strings.EqualFold(parts[0], "dev.azure.com") && strings.EqualFold(parts[3], "_git") {
624	 		if decoded, ok := decode([]string{parts[1], parts[2], parts[4]}); ok {
625	 			return string(forge.AzureDevOps) + "/" + strings.Join(decoded, "/")
626	 		}
627	 	}
628	 	if len(parts) == 5 && strings.EqualFold(parts[0], "ssh.dev.azure.com") && strings.EqualFold(parts[1], "v3") {
629	 		if decoded, ok := decode(parts[2:]); ok {
630	 			return string(forge.AzureDevOps) + "/" + strings.Join(decoded, "/")
631	 		}
632	 	}
633	 	if len(parts) >= 4 && strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(parts[0]), ".visualstudio.com") &&
634	 		!strings.EqualFold(parts[0], "vs-ssh.visualstudio.com") && strings.EqualFold(parts[len(parts)-2], "_git") {
635	 		organization := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.ToLower(parts[0]), ".visualstudio.com")
636	 		if decoded, ok := decode([]string{organization, parts[len(parts)-3], parts[len(parts)-1]}); ok {
637	 			return string(forge.AzureDevOps) + "/" + strings.Join(decoded, "/")
638	 		}
639	 	}
640	 	if len(parts) == 5 && strings.EqualFold(parts[0], "vs-ssh.visualstudio.com") &&
641	 		strings.HasPrefix(parts[1], "~") && strings.EqualFold(parts[3], "_ssh") {
642	 		if decoded, ok := decode([]string{strings.TrimPrefix(parts[1], "~"), parts[2], parts[4]}); ok {
643	 			return string(forge.AzureDevOps) + "/" + strings.Join(decoded, "/")
644	 		}
645	 	}
646	 	return ""
647	 }
648
649	 func looksLikeLocalRemote(identity string) bool {
650	 	if filepath.IsAbs(identity) || strings.HasPrefix(identity, `\\`) {
651	 		return true
652	 	}
653	 	for _, prefix := range []string{"./", "../", "~/", `.\`, `..\`, `~\`} {
654	 		if strings.HasPrefix(identity, prefix) {
655	 			return true
656	 		}
657	 	}
658	 	if len(identity) >= 2 && identity[1] == ':' {
659	 		letter := identity[0]
660	 		if letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z' {
661	 			return true
662	 		}
663	 	}
664	 	return !strings.ContainsAny(identity, `/\:@`)
665	 }

1349	 func (s *Store) get(id string) (*Entry, error) {
1350	 	data, err := os.ReadFile(s.path(id))
1351	 	if err != nil {
1352	 		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1353	 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
1354	 		}
1355	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
1356	 	}
1357	 	var header struct {
1358	 		SchemaVersion int `toml:"schema_version"`
1359	 	}
1360	 	if _, err := toml.Decode(string(data), &header); err != nil {
1361	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode catalog asset %s schema: %w", id, err)
1362	 	}
1363	 	if header.SchemaVersion != 0 && header.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
1364	 		return nil, &UnsupportedSchemaError{ID: id, Version: header.SchemaVersion}
1365	 	}
1366
1367	 	var entry Entry
1368	 	metadata, err := toml.Decode(string(data), &entry)
1369	 	if err != nil {
1370	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
1371	 	}
1372	 	if undecoded := metadata.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
1373	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode catalog asset %s: unknown field(s): %v", id, undecoded)
1374	 	}
1375	 	entry.ID = id
1376	 	// Version zero is the only implicit form: it means the schema marker was
1377	 	// absent, not that an unknown future layout should be guessed.
1378	 	if entry.SchemaVersion == 0 {
1379	 		entry.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
1380	 	}
1381	 	entry.Normalize()
1382	 	if err := entry.Validate(); err != nil {
1383	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
1384	 	}
1385	 	return &entry, nil
1386	 }

1388	 // List loads every valid record in deterministic ID order. Per-record failures

1391	 func (s *Store) List() ([]*Entry, error) {
1392	 	entries, diagnostics, err := s.ListWithDiagnostics()

1400	 func (s *Store) reportDiagnostics(diagnostics []Diagnostic) {
1401	 	if s.diagnostics == nil {
1402	 		return
1403	 	}
1404	 	for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
1405	 		s.diagnostics(diagnostic)
1406	 	}
1407	 }
1408
1409	 // ListWithDiagnostics is List's explicit diagnostic form. It is useful to
1410	 // services that want to aggregate notices rather than render them immediately.
1411	 func (s *Store) ListWithDiagnostics() ([]*Entry, []Diagnostic, error) {
1412	 	directoryEntries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
1413	 	if err != nil {
1414	 		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
1415	 			return nil, nil, nil
1416	 		}
1417	 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog directory: %w", err)
1418	 	}
1419
1420	 	var entries []*Entry
1421	 	var diagnostics []Diagnostic
1422	 	for _, directoryEntry := range directoryEntries {
1423	 		name := directoryEntry.Name()
1424	 		if directoryEntry.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") {
1425	 			continue
1426	 		}
1427	 		id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
1428	 		entry, err := s.Get(id)
1429	 		if err != nil {
1430	 			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err})
1431	 			continue
1432	 		}
1433	 		entries = append(entries, entry)
1434	 	}
1435	 	Sort(entries)
1436	 	sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
1437	 	return entries, diagnostics, nil
1438	 }

1501	 // Sort orders entries by stable ID.
1502	 func Sort(entries []*Entry) {
1503	 	sort.SliceStable(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
1504	 		return entries[i].ID < entries[j].ID
1505	 	})

1508	 func (s *Store) writeAtomic(entry *Entry) error {
1509	 	temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+entry.ID+".*.tmp")
1510	 	if err != nil {
1511	 		return fmt.Errorf("create catalog temp file: %w", err)
1512	 	}
1513	 	name := temporary.Name()
1514	 	defer os.Remove(name)
1515
1516	 	if err := toml.NewEncoder(temporary).Encode(entry); err != nil {
1517	 		_ = temporary.Close()
1518	 		return fmt.Errorf("encode catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
1519	 	}
1520	 	if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
1521	 		return fmt.Errorf("close catalog temp file: %w", err)
1522	 	}
1523	 	if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o644); err != nil {
1524	 		return fmt.Errorf("set catalog file mode: %w", err)
1525	 	}
1526	 	if err := os.Rename(name, s.path(entry.ID)); err != nil {
1527	 		return fmt.Errorf("replace catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
1528	 	}
1529	 	return nil
1530	 }

1855	 func decodeOpenRequest(value string) (fleet.OpenRequest, error) {
1856	 	data, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(value)
1857	 	if err != nil {
1858	 		return fleet.OpenRequest{}, err
1859	 	}
1860	 	var request fleet.OpenRequest
1861	 	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &request); err != nil {
1862	 		return fleet.OpenRequest{}, err
1863	 	}
1864	 	return request, nil
1865	 }

1990	 const fleetStarterConfig = `# dev remote fleet configuration.
1991	 schema_version = 1
1992
1993	 [defaults]
1994	 connect_timeout = "15s"
1995	 command_timeout = "5m"
1996	 cache_ttl = "15m"
1997	 max_parallel = 4
1998	 dev_path = "auto"
1999
2000	 # Prefer an alias from ~/.ssh/config so ProxyJump, IdentityAgent and host-key
2001	 # policy behave exactly like an ordinary ssh invocation.
2002	 # [[hosts]]
2003	 # name = "lab"
2004	 # ssh_alias = "lab"
2005	+# Run dev fleet machine-id lab, verify the UUID independently, then pin it
2006	+# before any mutating fleet operation:
2007	+# machine_id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
2008
2009	 # Explicit connection fields are also supported. Password login is retried only
2010	 # after key/agent authentication is rejected.
2011	 # [[hosts]]
2012	 # name = "vps"
2013	 # hostname = "203.0.113.10"
2014	 # user = "dev"
2015	 # port = 22
2016	 # identity_file = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
2017	 # ssh_login_password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-vps-login" }
2018	 `
2019

2027	 func newFleetConfigInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

2036	 			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists (use --force to overwrite)", config.Contract(path))
2037	 		}
2038	 		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
2039	 			return err
2040	 		}
2041	 		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(fleetStarterConfig), 0o600); err != nil {
2042	 			return err
2043	 		}
2044	 		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
2045	 		return nil
2046	 	}}

2048	 	cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&stdout, "stdout", false, "print without writing")
2049	 	return cmd

2052	 // fleetConfigEditorProcess builds the editor invocation for remotes.toml,
2053	 // seeding the starter file when there is none. The TUI runs the same command
2054	 // under tea.ExecProcess, so the two entry points cannot drift.
2055	 func fleetConfigEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
2056	 	path := fleetConfigPath(app)
2057	 	if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
2058	 		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
2059	 			return nil, err
2060	 		}
2061	 		// 0600: remotes.toml may carry a plaintext SSH password.
2062	 		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(fleetStarterConfig), 0o600); err != nil {
2063	 			return nil, err
2064	 		}
2065	 	}
2066	 	chosen, err := resolveEditor(editor)
2067	 	if err != nil {
2068	 		return nil, err
2069	 	}
2070	 	process := exec.Command(shellPath(), "-c", chosen+" "+shellQuote(path))
2071	 	process.Stdin, process.Stdout, process.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
2072	 	return process, nil
2073	 }

2112	 func noteRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string) (*catalog.Entry, repo.Repo, error) {
2113	 	if ref != "" {
2114	 		// A stable catalog ID is accepted anywhere a repo name is.
2115	 		if entry, err := app.Registry.Get(ref); err == nil {
2116	 			if entry.Kind != catalog.KindRepository {
2117	 				return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s is %s, not a repository", ref, entry.Kind)
2118	 			}
2119	 			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname())
2120	 			if !ok || location.CurrentPath == "" {
2121	 				return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("catalog repository %s has no path on this host", ref)
2122	 			}
2123	 			r := repo.Repo{Name: entry.Name, Path: location.CurrentPath,
2124	 				RealPath: location.RealPath, CommonDir: location.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true}
2125	 			return entry, r, nil
2126	 		}
2127	 		resolved, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, ref)
2128	 		if err != nil {
2129	 			return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
2130	 		}
2131	 		return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: resolved})
2132	 	}
2133	 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
2134	 	if err != nil {
2135	 		return nil, repo.Repo{}, err
2136	 	}
2137	 	g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
2138	 	if err != nil {
2139	 		return nil, repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("%s is not in a repository; pass --repo", config.Contract(cwd))
2140	 	}
2141	 	r := repo.Repo{Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
2142	 		CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, MainRoot: g.MainRoot, HasGit: true}
2143	 	return ensureNoteRepository(ctx, app, tui.NoteTarget{Repo: r})
2144	 }

2188	 func resolveNote(app *App, ref string) (*note.Note, error) {
2189	 	ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
2190	 	if len(ref) < 8 {
2191	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("note ID/prefix must be at least 8 characters")
2192	 	}
2193	 	if n, err := app.Notes.Get(ref); err == nil {
2194	 		return n, nil
2195	 	}
2196	 	notes, err := app.Notes.List("")
2197	 	if err != nil {
2198	 		return nil, err
2199	 	}
2200	 	var hits []*note.Note
2201	 	for _, n := range notes {
2202	 		if strings.HasPrefix(n.ID, ref) {
2203	 			hits = append(hits, n)
2204	 		}
2205	 	}
2206	 	switch len(hits) {
2207	 	case 1:
2208	 		return hits[0], nil
2209	 	case 0:
2210	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", ref, note.ErrNotFound)
2211	 	default:
2212	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("note prefix %q is ambiguous (%d matches)", ref, len(hits))
2213	 	}
2214	 }

2216	 func renderNotes(app *App, notes []*note.Note, jsonOut bool) error {

2227	 	for _, n := range notes {
2228	 		t.Add(n.ID[:8], humanAge(time.Since(n.Created)), n.Repository,
2229	 			dash(strings.Join(n.Tags, ",")), truncate(n.Preview(80), 80))
2230	 	}
2231	 	t.Render(app.Out)
2232	 	return nil
2233	 }

3310	 // Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
3311	 // dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
3312	 // falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
3313	 func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
3314	 	cfg := Default()
3315	 	if path == "" {
3316	 		path = ConfigFile()
3317	 	}
3318	 	md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
3319	 	switch {
3320	 	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
3321	 		return cfg, nil
3322	 	case err != nil:
3323	 		return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
3324	 	}
3325	 	if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
3326	 		// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
3327	 		// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
3328	 		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
3329	 	}
3330	 	cfg.Source = path
3331	 	return cfg, cfg.Validate()
3332	 }

3334	 // Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
3335	 // worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
3336	 func (c Config) Validate() error {
3337	 	switch c.Runtime.Backend {
3338	 	case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "zellij", "none":
3339	 	default:
3340	 		return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux, zellij or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
3341	 	}
3342	 	if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
3343	 		return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
3344	 	}
3345	 	if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
3346	 		return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
3347	 	}
3348	+	if err := c.LocalFiles.Limits().Validate(); err != nil {
3349	+		return fmt.Errorf("local_files: %w", err)
3350	+	}
3351	 	switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
3352	 	case "", "flat", "preserve":
3353	 	default:
3354	 		return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
3355	 	}
3356	 	if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
3357	 		return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
3358	 	}
3359	 	if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
3360	 		return fmt.Errorf("deprecated forge.remote_limit must be zero or positive")
3361	 	}
3362	 	seenAzureTargets := map[string]bool{}
3363	 	for i, target := range c.Forge.AzureDevOps {
3364	 		organization := strings.TrimSpace(target.Organization)
3365	 		project := strings.TrimSpace(target.Project)
3366	 		if !validAzureDevOpsOrganization(organization) {
3367	 			return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].organization %q: want an Azure DevOps Services URL like https://dev.azure.com/acme", i, target.Organization)
3368	 		}
3369	 		if project == "" {
3370	 			return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d].project must not be empty", i)
3371	 		}
3372	 		key := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimRight(organization, "/") + "/" + project)
3373	 		if seenAzureTargets[key] {
3374	 			return fmt.Errorf("forge.azure_devops[%d] duplicates organization/project %s / %s", i, organization, project)
3375	 		}
3376	 		seenAzureTargets[key] = true
3377	 	}
3378	 	validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
3379	 		switch v {
3380	 		case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
3381	 			return true
3382	 		}
3383	 		return false
3384	 	}
3385	 	if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
3386	 		return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
3387	 	}
3388	 	for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
3389	 		if !validStrategy(strategy) {
3390	 			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
3391	 				ecosystem, strategy)
3392	 		}
3393	 	}
3394	 	validColumns := map[string]bool{
3395	 		"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "remote": true, "size": true, "live": true,
3396	 		"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true, "notes": true,
3397	 		"category": true, "path": true,
3398	 	}
3399	 	for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
3400	 		if !validColumns[column] {
3401	 			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
3402	 		}
3403	 	}
3404	 	switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
3405	 	case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "size", "tasks":
3406	 	default:
3407	 		return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git, size or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
3408	 	}
3409	 	seen := map[string]string{}
3410	 	for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
3411	 		switch {
3412	 		case t.Key == "":
3413	 			return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
3414	 		case t.Run == "":
3415	 			return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
3416	 		}
3417	 		if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
3418	 			return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
3419	 				i, t.Key, binding)
3420	 		}
3421	 		if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
3422	 			return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
3423	 		}
3424	 		seen[t.Key] = t.Name
3425	 	}
3426	 	return nil
3427	 }

4095	 	})
4096	 	return candidates

4924	+func (b *captureBuffer) Write(value []byte) (int, error) {
4925	+	remaining := b.limit - int64(b.buffer.Len())
4926	+	if remaining > 0 {
4927	+		keep := int64(len(value))
4928	+		if keep > remaining {
4929	+			keep = remaining
4930	+		}
4931	+		_, _ = b.buffer.Write(value[:int(keep)])
4932	+	}
4933	+	if int64(len(value)) > remaining {
4934	+		b.exceeded = true
4935	+	}
4936	+	// Consume excess output without retaining it. The command timeout still
4937	+	// bounds a peer that writes forever, while the parent process stays bounded.
4938	+	return len(value), nil
4939	+}

5870	 // IsEphemeralWorktree recognises turn-scoped checkouts owned by an agent
5871	 // harness. They stay visible, but the label prevents an agent from treating

5873	 func IsEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {

5876	 		strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")

5919	 func checkoutActivity(ctx context.Context, path string, status gitx.Status) (time.Time, time.Time, string) {
5920	 	latest := status.LatestChange
5921	 	var commit time.Time
5922	 	var subject string
5923	 	if unix, lastSubject, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
5924	 		commit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
5925	 		if commit.After(latest) {
5926	 			latest = commit
5927	 		}
5928	 		subject = lastSubject
5929	 	}
5930	 	return latest, commit, subject
5931	 }

5933	 func assignTasks(out *RepoContext, tasks []*task.Task) {
5934	 	for _, t := range tasks {
5935	 		assigned := false
5936	 		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
5937	 			for i := 1; i < len(out.Checkouts); i++ {
5938	 				if samePath(t.WorktreePath, out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Path) {
5939	 					out.Checkouts[i].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, t)
5940	 					out.Checkouts[i].Ownership = CheckoutDev
5941	 					assigned = true
5942	 					break
5943	 				}
5944	 			}
5945	 		} else if len(out.Checkouts) > 0 && t.Branch == out.Checkouts[0].Branch() {
5946	 			out.Checkouts[0].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[0].Tasks, t)
5947	 			assigned = true
5948	 		}
5949	 		if !assigned {
5950	 			out.OtherTasks = append(out.OtherTasks, t)
5951	 		}
5952	 	}
5953	 	for i := range out.Checkouts {
5954	 		sort.SliceStable(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, func(a, b int) bool {
5955	 			return out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[a].ID < out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[b].ID
5956	 		})
5957	 	}
5958	 	sort.SliceStable(out.OtherTasks, func(i, j int) bool {
5959	 		return out.OtherTasks[i].ID < out.OtherTasks[j].ID
5960	 	})
5961	 }

5963	 // assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
5964	 // checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
5965	 // x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
5966	 func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
5967	 	for _, session := range sessions {
5968	 		assigned := map[int]bool{}
5969	 		for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
5970	 			best, bestLen := -1, -1
5971	 			for i := range out.Checkouts {
5972	 				for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Repo, i, out.Checkouts[i]) {
5973	 					if pathContains(root, dir) && len(filepath.Clean(root)) > bestLen {
5974	 						best, bestLen = i, len(filepath.Clean(root))
5975	 					}
5976	 				}
5977	 			}
5978	 			if best >= 0 {
5979	 				assigned[best] = true
5980	 			}
5981	 		}
5982	 		for i := range assigned {
5983	 			out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
5984	 		}
5985	 	}
5986	 }

5988	 func checkoutRoots(r repo.Repo, index int, checkout RepoCheckout) []string {
5989	 	roots := []string{checkout.Worktree.Path}
5990	 	if index == 0 && r.RealPath != "" && !samePath(r.RealPath, r.Path) {
5991	 		roots = append(roots, r.RealPath)
5992	 	}
5993	 	return roots
5994	 }

5996	 func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
5997	 	if root == "" || path == "" {
5998	 		return false
5999	 	}
6000	 	rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
6001	 	if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
6002	 		return false
6003	 	}
6004	 	return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
6005	 }
6006
6007	 func samePath(a, b string) bool {
6008	 	return a != "" && b != "" && normalizePath(a) == normalizePath(b)
6009	 }
6010
6011	 // normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
6012	 // paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
6013	 // also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
6014	 // is not sufficient.
6015	 func normalizePath(path string) string {
6016	 	clean := filepath.Clean(path)
6017	 	cur := clean
6018	 	for {
6019	 		if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); err == nil {
6020	 			rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(cur, clean)
6021	 			if relErr == nil && rel != "." {
6022	 				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(real, rel))
6023	 			}
6024	 			return filepath.Clean(real)
6025	 		}
6026	 		parent := filepath.Dir(cur)
6027	 		if parent == cur {
6028	 			return clean
6029	 		}
6030	 		cur = parent
6031	 	}
6032	 }

6172	 func markdownCodes(values []string) string {

6180	 // FormatSessions renders the ys payload. checkoutIndex < 0 selects the whole
6181	 // repository; otherwise it selects one checkout.
6182	 func FormatSessions(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
6183	 	indices := make([]int, 0, len(c.Checkouts))
6184	 	if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
6185	 		indices = append(indices, checkoutIndex)
6186	 	} else {
6187	 		for i := range c.Checkouts {
6188	 			indices = append(indices, i)
6189	 		}
6190	 	}
6191	 	var b strings.Builder
6192	 	for _, i := range indices {
6193	 		checkout := c.Checkouts[i]
6194	 		for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
6195	 			status := session.AgentStatus
6196	 			if status == "" {
6197	 				status = "unknown"
6198	 			}
6199	 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s`: `%s %s` (%s)\n",
6200	 				checkout.Worktree.Path, c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
6201	 			if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
6202	 				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - agents: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))
6203	 			}
6204	 		}
6205	 	}
6206	 	return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
6207	 }

6209	 // LinkedWorktreePaths returns the yw payload: absolute linked-worktree paths,
6210	 // one per line. The canonical checkout is intentionally excluded because WT
6211	 // counts linked worktrees only.
6212	 func LinkedWorktreePaths(c RepoContext) string {
6213	 	paths := make([]string, 0, len(c.Linked()))
6214	 	for _, checkout := range c.Linked() {
6215	 		paths = append(paths, checkout.Worktree.Path)
6216	 	}
6217	 	return strings.Join(paths, "\n")
6218	 }

6481	 // Revision fingerprints every field an editor is allowed to preserve or
6482	 // replace. Update compares it while holding the mutation lock, preventing a
6483	 // stale editor session from silently overwriting another process's changes.
6484	 func (n Note) Revision() string {
6485	 	payload := strings.Join([]string{
6486	 		n.ID, n.RepositoryID, n.Repository,
6487	 		n.Created.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
6488	 		n.Updated.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
6489	 		strings.Join(n.Tags, "\x00"), n.Body,
6490	 	}, "\x00")
6491	 	return fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256([]byte(payload)))
6492	 }

6804	 func (s *Store) Update(ctx context.Context, id, expectedRevision, body string, tags []string) (*Note, error) {
6805	 	if ctx == nil {
6806	 		ctx = context.Background()
6807	 	}

6809	 	defer s.mu.Unlock()
6810	 	var updated *Note
6811	 	err := s.withFileLock(ctx, func() error {
6812	 		current, err := s.Get(id)
6813	 		if err != nil {
6814	 			return err
6815	 		}
6816	 		if expectedRevision == "" || current.Revision() != expectedRevision {
6817	 			return fmt.Errorf("note %s: %w", id, ErrConflict)
6818	 		}
6819	 		candidate := *current
6820	 		candidate.Body, candidate.Tags, candidate.Updated = body, tags, s.now()
6821	 		candidate.Normalize()
6822	 		if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
6823	 			return err
6824	 		}
6825	 		if err := s.writeAtomic(&candidate); err != nil {
6826	 			return err
6827	 		}
6828	 		updated = clone(&candidate)
6829	 		return nil
6830	 	})

6954	 func split(data []byte) ([]byte, []byte, error) {
6955	 	if !bytes.HasPrefix(data, []byte(delimiter+"\n")) {
6956	 		return nil, nil, errors.New("missing opening +++ frontmatter delimiter")
6957	 	}
6958	 	rest := data[len(delimiter)+1:]
6959	 	marker := []byte("\n" + delimiter + "\n")
6960	 	i := bytes.Index(rest, marker)
6961	 	if i < 0 {
6962	 		return nil, nil, errors.New("missing closing +++ frontmatter delimiter")
6963	 	}
6964	 	meta := rest[:i]
6965	 	body := rest[i+len(marker):]
6966	 	body = bytes.TrimPrefix(body, []byte("\n"))
6967	 	return meta, body, nil
6968	 }

7071	 // Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
7072	 // path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
7073	 // appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
7074	 // before creating or moving anything into it.
7075	 func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
7076	 	if path == "" {
7077	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
7078	 	}
7079	 	absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
7080	 	if err != nil {
7081	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
7082	 	}
7083	 	absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
7084
7085	 	probe := absolute
7086	 	var missing []string
7087	 	for {
7088	 		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
7089	 		if err == nil {
7090	 			slices.Reverse(missing)
7091	 			parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
7092	 			return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
7093	 		}
7094	 		if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
7095	 			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
7096	 		}
7097	 		// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
7098	 		// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
7099	 		// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
7100	 		// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
7101	 		// still-missing suffix.
7102	 		if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
7103	 			target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
7104	 			if readErr != nil {
7105	 				return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
7106	 			}
7107	 			if hasParentTraversal(target) {
7108	 				return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
7109	 			}
7110	 			if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
7111	 				target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
7112	 			}
7113	 			resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
7114	 			if resolveErr != nil {
7115	 				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
7116	 			}
7117	 			slices.Reverse(missing)
7118	 			parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
7119	 			return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
7120	 		} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
7121	 			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
7122	 		}
7123	 		parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
7124	 		if parent == probe {
7125	 			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
7126	 		}
7127	 		missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
7128	 		probe = parent
7129	 	}

7132	 // CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
7133	 // below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
7134	 // confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
7135	 func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
7136	 	if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
7137	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
7138	 	}
7139	 	canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
7140	 	if err != nil {
7141	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
7142	 	}
7143	 	canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
7144	 	if err != nil {
7145	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
7146	 	}
7147
7148	 	rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
7149	 	if err != nil {
7150	 		// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
7151	 		// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
7152	 		// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
7153	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
7154	 	}
7155	 	switch {
7156	 	case rel == ".":
7157	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
7158	 	case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
7159	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
7160	 	default:
7161	 		return canonicalCandidate, nil
7162	 	}
7163	 }

7167	 func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {

7306	+		children map[string]*collisionNode
7307	+	}
7308	+	root := &collisionNode{children: map[string]*collisionNode{}}
7309	+	for _, value := range paths {
7310	+		if err := ValidatePortableSlashPath(value, limits); err != nil {
7311	+			return fmt.Errorf("portable path %q: %w", value, err)
7312	+		}
7313	+		current := root
7314	+		for _, component := range strings.Split(value, "/") {
7315	+			key := portableCollisionKey(component)
7316	+			next, exists := current.children[key]
7317	+			if exists && next.spelling != component {
7318	+				return fmt.Errorf("paths %q and %q collide on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems at %q and %q: %w",
7319	+					next.first, value, next.spelling, component, ErrPathCollision)
7320	+			}
7321	+			if !exists {
7322	+				next = &collisionNode{spelling: component, first: value, children: map[string]*collisionNode{}}
7323	+				current.children[key] = next
7324	+			}
7325	+			current = next
7326	+		}
7327	+	}
7328	+	return nil
7329	+}
7330	+
7331	+func portableCollisionKey(component string) string {
7332	+	return norm.NFC.String(cases.Fold().String(norm.NFC.String(component)))
7333	+}
7334	+
7335	+func isPortableControl(r rune) bool {
7336	+	return unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r)
7337	+}
7338	+
7339	+func windowsReservedName(component string) bool {
7340	+	base := component
7341	+	if dot := strings.IndexByte(base, '.'); dot >= 0 {
7342	+		base = base[:dot]
7343	+	}
7344	+	base = strings.TrimRight(base, " ")
7345	+	upper := strings.ToUpper(base)
7346	+	switch upper {
7347	+	case "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", "CONIN$", "CONOUT$", "CLOCK$":
7348	+		return true
7349	+	}
7350	+	if len([]rune(upper)) != 4 {
7351	+		return false
7352	+	}
7353	+	runes := []rune(upper)
7354	+	prefix := string(runes[:3])
7355	+	if prefix != "COM" && prefix != "LPT" {
7356	+		return false
7357	+	}
7358	+	last := runes[3]
7359	+	return last >= '1' && last <= '9' || last == '¹' || last == '²' || last == '³'
7360	+}

7362	 // JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
7363	 // canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
7364	 // <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
7365	 // single component.
7366	 func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
7367	 	if len(components) == 0 {
7368	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
7369	 	}
7370	 	for i, component := range components {
7371	 		if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
7372	 			return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
7373	 		}
7374	 	}
7375	 	canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
7376	 	if err != nil {
7377	 		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
7378	 	}
7379	 	return CanonicalChild(canonicalRoot, filepath.Join(append([]string{canonicalRoot}, components...)...))
7380	 }

7383	 	if len(component) < 2 || component[1] != ':' {
7384	 		return false
7385	 	}
7386	 	letter := component[0]
7387	 	return letter >= 'a' && letter <= 'z' || letter >= 'A' && letter <= 'Z'

7393	 	}) {
7394	 		if component == ".." {
7395	 			return true
7396	 		}
7397	 	}
7398	 	return false
7399	 }

7531	 func diagnosticsForUndecoded(source string, keys []toml.Key) []Diagnostic {
7532	 	diagnostics := make([]Diagnostic, 0, len(keys))
7533	 	seenDenied := map[string]bool{}
7534	 	seenUnknown := map[string]bool{}
7535	 	for _, undecoded := range keys {
7536	 		key := undecoded.String()
7537	 		top, _, _ := strings.Cut(key, ".")
7538	 		if deniedTopLevelSections[top] {
7539	 			if seenDenied[top] {
7540	 				continue
7541	 			}
7542	 			seenDenied[top] = true
7543	 			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{
7544	 				Kind: DiagnosticDenied, Source: source, Key: top,
7545	 				Message: fmt.Sprintf("project config cannot override host section %s", top),
7546	 			})
7547	 			continue
7548	 		}
7549	 		if seenUnknown[key] {
7550	 			continue
7551	 		}
7552	 		seenUnknown[key] = true
7553	 		diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{
7554	 			Kind: DiagnosticUnknown, Source: source, Key: key,
7555	 			Message: fmt.Sprintf("unknown project config key %s was ignored", key),
7556	 		})
7557	 	}
7558	 	return diagnostics
7559	 }

7561	 func scaffoldDiagnostics(source string, document map[string]any) []Diagnostic {
7562	 	var diagnostics []Diagnostic
7563	 	for key := range document {
7564	 		if allowedScaffoldTopLevel[key] {
7565	 			continue
7566	 		}
7567	 		kind := DiagnosticUnknown
7568	 		message := fmt.Sprintf("unknown scaffold config section %s was ignored", key)
7569	 		if deniedTopLevelSections[key] {
7570	 			kind = DiagnosticDenied
7571	 			message = fmt.Sprintf("scaffold config cannot override host section %s", key)
7572	 		}
7573	 		diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{Kind: kind, Source: source, Key: key, Message: message})
7574	 	}
7575	 	return diagnostics
7576	 }

7756	 // FilePaths are the fixed project configuration paths below one canonical

7764	 // ResolvePaths canonicalizes repoRoot and proves both fixed files remain below
7765	 // it. This also rejects a .dev-cli directory or file symlink that escapes the
7766	 // repository.
7767	 func ResolvePaths(repoRoot string) (FilePaths, error) {
7768	 	root, err := pathx.Canonical(repoRoot)
7769	 	if err != nil {
7770	 		return FilePaths{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize repository root: %w", err)
7771	 	}
7772	 	configPath, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, filepath.Join(root, DirectoryName, ConfigFilename))
7773	 	if err != nil {
7774	 		return FilePaths{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve %s: %w", ConfigRelativePath, err)
7775	 	}
7776	 	scaffoldsPath, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, filepath.Join(root, DirectoryName, ScaffoldsFilename))
7777	 	if err != nil {
7778	 		return FilePaths{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve %s: %w", ScaffoldsRelativePath, err)
7779	 	}
7780	 	return FilePaths{Root: root, Config: configPath, Scaffolds: scaffoldsPath}, nil
7781	 }

8753	 // Apply writes a prepared snapshot into a newly initialized, otherwise empty
8754	 // repository. All traversal and creation stays relative to a held os.Root, and
8755	 // file permissions are applied through the opened file descriptor.
8756	 func (snapshot Snapshot) Apply(destination string) (ApplyResult, error) {
8757	 	result := ApplyResult{Summary: snapshot.Summary()}
8758	 	if err := validateSnapshot(snapshot); err != nil {
8759	 		return result, err

8764	 	}
8765	 	defer root.Close()
8766	 	entries, err := readRootEntries(root)
8767	 	if err != nil {
8768	 		return result, fmt.Errorf("inspect template destination: %w", err)
8769	 	}
8770	 	gitMetadata := false
8771	 	for _, entry := range entries {
8772	 		if entry.Name() == ".git" {
8773	 			info, err := root.Lstat(entry.Name())
8774	 			if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
8775	 				return result, errors.New("template destination has unsafe Git metadata")
8776	 			}

8778	 			continue
8779	 		}

8794	 		return result, fmt.Errorf("template destination changed during apply: %w", err)

8796	 	return result, nil

9148	 // MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.

9162	 		b = "branch"
9163	 	}
9164	 	return r + "__" + b

9498	 // Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
9499	 // exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
9500	 // branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
9501	 // than a silent pick.
9502	 func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
9503	 	if ref == "" {
9504	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
9505	 	}
9506	 	all, err := s.List()
9507	 	if err != nil {
9508	 		return nil, err
9509	 	}
9510	 	for _, t := range all {
9511	 		if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
9512	 			return t, nil
9513	 		}
9514	 	}
9515	 	needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
9516	 	var hits []*Task
9517	 	for _, t := range all {
9518	 		hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
9519	 		if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
9520	 			hits = append(hits, t)
9521	 		}
9522	 	}
9523	 	switch len(hits) {
9524	 	case 1:
9525	 		return hits[0], nil
9526	 	case 0:
9527	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
9528	 	default:
9529	 		names := make([]string, len(hits))
9530	 		for i, t := range hits {
9531	 			names[i] = t.ID
9532	 		}
9533	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
9534	 	}
9535	 }

9537	 // FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
9538	 //
9539	 // A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
9540	 // the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
9541	 // claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
9542	 // every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
9543	 // match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
9544	 func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
9545	 	all, err := s.List()
9546	 	if err != nil {
9547	 		return nil, err
9548	 	}
9549	 	under := func(dir, root string) bool {
9550	 		return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
9551	 	}
9552	 	var best *Task
9553	 	var bestLen int
9554	 	for _, t := range all {
9555	 		root := t.WorktreePath
9556	 		if root == "" {
9557	 			root = t.RepoPath
9558	 		}
9559	 		if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
9560	 			best, bestLen = t, len(root)
9561	 		}
9562	 	}
9563	 	if best == nil {
9564	 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
9565	 	}
9566	 	return best, nil
9567	 }
