20	// grammar accepted by [local_files]. Literal path components use portable slash
21	// paths; '*' and '?' match within one component and a component equal to '**'
22	// matches zero or more components. Character classes, escaping, volumes, and
23	// platform-specific separators are intentionally unsupported.
24	func ValidateLocalFilePattern(value string) error {
25		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) {
26			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is required and must be trimmed")
27		}
28		if !utf8.ValidString(value) {
29			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is not valid UTF-8")
30		}
31		if len(value) > safefile.CompiledMaxPathBytes {
32			return fmt.Errorf("pattern is %d bytes; maximum is %d", len(value), safefile.CompiledMaxPathBytes)
33		}
34		if strings.ContainsRune(value, '\\') {
35			return fmt.Errorf("pattern must use '/' separators")
36		}
37		if strings.HasPrefix(value, "/") || strings.HasSuffix(value, "/") || strings.Contains(value, "//") {
38			return fmt.Errorf("pattern must be a clean repository-relative slash path")
39		}
40		if strings.ContainsAny(value, "[]{}") {
41			return fmt.Errorf("pattern supports only '*', '?' and whole-component '**' wildcards")
42		}
43		components := strings.Split(value, "/")
44		if len(components) > safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth {
45			return fmt.Errorf("pattern has %d components; maximum is %d", len(components), safefile.CompiledMaxPathDepth)
46		}
47		for _, component := range components {
48			if localFileDependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)] {
49				return fmt.Errorf("pattern enters dependency directory %q", component)
50			}
51			if component == "**" {
52				continue
53			}
54			if strings.Contains(component, "**") {
55				return fmt.Errorf("'**' must occupy a complete path component")
56			}
57			placeholder := strings.NewReplacer("*", "x", "?", "x").Replace(component)
58			if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(placeholder, safefile.CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
59				return fmt.Errorf("component %q: %w", component, err)
60			}

64				}
65			}
66		}
67		return nil
68	}

86	// AtomicReplace stages and syncs data in the target directory, revalidates the
87	// existing regular file against observed, and atomically renames the staged file
88	// over it. Atomic describes publication, not a filesystem compare-and-swap: the
89	// metadata check and rename are separate syscalls. Callers performing digest-CAS
90	// must hold an exclusive cooperative operation lease, obtain observed from a
91	// fresh stable read/hash, and retain any rollback copy before invoking this
92	// primitive. It never follows a symlink or reparse point.
93	func AtomicReplace(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, observed fs.FileInfo, data []byte, finalMode fs.FileMode) (fs.FileInfo, error) {
94		if root == nil {
95			return nil, errors.New("atomic replace: nil root")
96		}
97		if observed == nil {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("replace %q without observed state: %w", name, ErrReplaceTarget)
99		}
100		if err := validateTargetName(name); err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		if err := verifyReplaceTarget(root, name, observed); err != nil {
104			return nil, err
105		}
106		stagedName, staged, err := stageRegular(ctx, root, data, finalMode)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		defer func() {
111			if stagedName != "" {
112				_ = root.Remove(stagedName)
113			}
114		}()
115		if err := verifyReplaceTarget(root, name, observed); err != nil {
116			return nil, err
117		}
118		if err := root.Rename(stagedName, name); err != nil {
119			return nil, fmt.Errorf("atomically replace %q: %w", name, err)
120		}
121		stagedName = ""
122		published, err := root.Lstat(name)
123		if err != nil {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("verify replacement %q: %w", name, err)
125		}
126		if unsafeLink(published) || !published.Mode().IsRegular() || !SameFileState(staged, published) {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("replacement %q does not match staging file: %w", name, ErrChanged)
128		}
129		if err := syncRoot(root); err != nil {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sync destination directory after replacing %q: %w", name, err)
131		}
132		return published, nil
133	}

47	func assessCheckout(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int) Readiness {
48		if selectedIndex < 0 || selectedIndex >= len(context.Checkouts) {
49			return indeterminate("checkout-selection-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "the selected checkout is absent from the local inventory", "rerun context from an existing checkout")
50		}
51		checkout := context.Checkouts[selectedIndex]
52		switch {
53		case checkout.Worktree.Bare || context.Repo.Bare:
54			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeNotApplicable}
55		case checkout.PathErr != nil:
56			return indeterminate("checkout-path-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "the checkout path could not be inspected", "restore path access and rerun context")
57		case !checkout.Exists || checkout.Worktree.Prunable:
58			return blocked("checkout-missing", "selected-checkout", "the checkout path is missing or prunable", "repair or remove the stale worktree registration")
59		case checkout.StatusErr != nil:
60			return indeterminate("checkout-status-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "Git status could not be collected", "repair the checkout and rerun context")
61		case checkout.Worktree.Detached || checkout.Status.Detached || checkout.Branch() == "":
62			return blocked("checkout-detached", "selected-checkout", "the checkout does not have an attached branch", "check out an explicit branch")
63		case checkout.Status.Conflicted > 0:
64			return blocked("checkout-conflicted", "selected-checkout", fmt.Sprintf("the checkout has %d unmerged path(s)", checkout.Status.Conflicted), "resolve the Git operation before transfer or retirement")
65		case checkout.Status.Dirty():
66			return blocked("checkout-dirty", "selected-checkout", fmt.Sprintf("the checkout has %d changed path(s)", checkout.Status.Changed), "commit or deliberately preserve the changes")
67		default:
68			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeEligible}
69		}
70	}

72	func assessTasks(context inventory.RepoContext, selectedIndex int, hostname string) Readiness {
73		if context.TaskErr != nil {
74			return indeterminate("task-inventory-unavailable", "task-inventory", "task records could not be collected", "repair the task store and rerun context")
75		}
76		if selectedIndex < 0 || selectedIndex >= len(context.Checkouts) {
77			return indeterminate("checkout-selection-unavailable", "selected-checkout", "task scope cannot be selected without a checkout", "rerun context from an existing checkout")
78		}
79		// Transfer/repository readiness covers every non-DONE task attached to the
80		// clone, including cold and branch-only records without a local checkout.
81		// Looking only at the selected checkout can otherwise hide another machine's
82		// ownership claim and incorrectly report not-applicable.
83		active := make([]*task.Task, 0, len(context.OtherTasks)+len(context.Checkouts[selectedIndex].Tasks))
84		sessionCount := map[string]int{}
85		seen := map[string]struct{}{}
86		add := func(candidate *task.Task, sessions int) {
87			if candidate == nil || candidate.State == task.Done {
88				return
89			}
90			if _, exists := seen[candidate.ID]; exists {
91				return
92			}
93			seen[candidate.ID] = struct{}{}
94			active = append(active, candidate)
95			sessionCount[candidate.ID] = sessions
96		}
97		for _, checkout := range context.Checkouts {
98			for _, candidate := range checkout.Tasks {
99				add(candidate, len(checkout.Sessions))
100			}
101		}
102		for _, candidate := range context.OtherTasks {
103			add(candidate, 0)
104		}
105		if len(active) == 0 {
106			return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeNotApplicable}
107		}
108		var reasons []assessment.Reason
109		hasIndeterminate := false
110		for _, candidate := range active {
111			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
112				hasIndeterminate = true
113				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
114					Code: "task-record-invalid", Subject: "task", Detail: "a selected task record is invalid",
115					Remediation: "repair or recreate the task record",
116				})
117				continue
118			}
119			if hostname != "" && candidate.Owner != "" && candidate.Owner != hostname {
120				reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
121					Code: "task-owned-elsewhere", Subject: "task", Detail: "a selected task is owned by another machine",
122					Remediation: "complete an explicit ownership handoff before writing",
123				})
124			}
125			if candidate.State == task.Hot {
126				if context.RuntimeErr != nil {
127					hasIndeterminate = true
128					reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
129						Code: "runtime-inventory-unavailable", Subject: "task", Detail: "a HOT task cannot be checked against live runtime state",
130						Remediation: "restore runtime inspection and rerun context",
131					})
132				} else if sessionCount[candidate.ID] == 0 {
133					reasons = append(reasons, assessment.Reason{
134						Code: "hot-task-runtime-missing", Subject: "task", Detail: "a HOT task has no observed runtime session",

142		}
143		if hasIndeterminate {

145		}
146		return Readiness{Outcome: assessment.OutcomeEligible}
147	}

139	func checkoutGitSource(ctx context.Context, source, ref string) (string, string, func(), error) {

1	// Package lockx provides a cross-platform advisory lock over a directory.
2	//
3	// It is a leaf package on purpose. Both the catalog store and Git transaction
4	// code need to serialize mutations, and neither should have to depend on the
5	// other to get a lock.
6	package lockx
7
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"os"
13		"path/filepath"
14	)
15
16	// WithDir runs operation while holding an exclusive lock for dir. The lock file
17	// lives beside dir rather than inside it, so locking never adds a file to the
18	// directory being protected. label names the caller in wrapped errors.
19	func WithDir(ctx context.Context, dir, label string, operation func() error) (err error) {
20		if operation == nil {
21			return fmt.Errorf("%s lock requires an operation", label)
22		}
23		if ctx == nil {
24			ctx = context.Background()
25		}
26		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
27			return fmt.Errorf("create %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
28		}
29		absoluteDir, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
30		if err != nil {
31			return fmt.Errorf("make %s directory absolute for lock: %w", label, err)
32		}
33		canonicalDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(absoluteDir)
34		if err != nil {
35			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize %s directory for lock: %w", label, err)
36		}
37		lockPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(canonicalDir), "."+filepath.Base(canonicalDir)+".lock")
38		lock, err := acquire(ctx, lockPath)
39		if err != nil {
40			return fmt.Errorf("acquire %s lock: %w", label, err)
41		}
42		defer func() {
43			if releaseErr := lock.Close(); releaseErr != nil {
44				err = errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("release %s lock: %w", label, releaseErr))
45			}
46		}()
47		return operation()
48	}
49

561	// Apply writes a prepared snapshot into a newly initialized, otherwise empty

564	func (snapshot Snapshot) Apply(destination string) (ApplyResult, error) {
565		result := ApplyResult{Summary: snapshot.Summary()}
566		if err := validateSnapshot(snapshot); err != nil {
567			return result, err
568		}
569		root, rootInfo, err := openNamedRoot(destination)
570		if err != nil {
571			return result, fmt.Errorf("resolve template destination: %w", err)
572		}
573		defer root.Close()
574		entries, err := readRootEntries(root)
575		if err != nil {
576			return result, fmt.Errorf("inspect template destination: %w", err)
577		}
578		gitMetadata := false
579		for _, entry := range entries {
580			if entry.Name() == ".git" {
581				info, err := root.Lstat(entry.Name())
582				if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || !info.IsDir() {
583					return result, errors.New("template destination has unsafe Git metadata")
584				}
585				gitMetadata = true
586				continue
587			}
588			return result, fmt.Errorf("template destination is not a new repository: %q already exists", entry.Name())
589		}
590		if !gitMetadata {
591			return result, errors.New("template destination is not an initialized Git repository")
592		}
593

597		}
598		if err := applyTree(root, tree, &result); err != nil {
599			return result, err

601		if err := verifyNamedRoot(destination, rootInfo); err != nil {
602			return result, fmt.Errorf("template destination changed during apply: %w", err)
603		}

150	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
151	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
152	// integrations.
153	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
154		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
155		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
156		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
157		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
158			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
159		}
160		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
161			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
162			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
163				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
164			}
165			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
166			if file == nil {
167				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
168			}
169			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
170				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
171			}
172			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
173				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
174			}
175			return nil
176		}
177		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
178		return err
179	}

599	func collectTriesWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options experiment.ListOptions,

603			return nil, err
604		}

606		warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)

608			sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)

612			row := tui.TryRow{Item: item}

614				if location, ok := item.Entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname()); ok {
615					copy := location
616					row.Location = &copy
617				}
618			}
619			sizeRepo := item.Live.Repo
620			if sizeRepo == nil && item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
621				if discovered, discoverErr := gitx.Discover(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath); discoverErr == nil {
622					sizeRepo = &discovered
623				}
624			}
625			if sizeRepo != nil {
626				worktreeCount := 0

628					worktreeCount = len(worktrees) - 1
629				}
630				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.FromGit(*sizeRepo, worktreeCount)
631			} else if item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
632				row.SizeTarget = diskusage.Plain(item.Live.CurrentPath)
633			}
634			if item.Live.Present && item.Live.Repo != nil {
635				row.Topology, row.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, item.Live.CurrentPath)
636			}
637			if item.Live.Present {
638				for _, session := range sessions {
639					if session.Covers(item.Live.CurrentPath) ||
640						(item.Live.RealPath != "" && session.Covers(item.Live.RealPath)) {
641						row.Live = true
642						row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = rt.Name(), session.Handle, session.AgentStatus
643						break
644					}
645				}
646			}
647			rows = append(rows, row)

652	func applyTryAction(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, request tui.TryRequest) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {

655			return tui.TryActionResult{}, err

659				IncludeDeprecated: true, IncludeArchived: true,
660				IncludeEvicted: true, IncludeGraduated: true,

670			if openErr != nil {
671				return tui.TryActionResult{}, openErr
672			}
673			result := tui.TryActionResult{Status: status, RefreshRepos: true}
674			if rt.Name() == "none" {
675				result.CD = item.Live.CurrentPath
676			} else {
677				result.Status += fmt.Sprintf(" in %s (%s)", rt.Name(), handle.Handle)
678				result.RuntimeHandle = handle.Handle
679			}
680			if _, touchErr := service.Touch(ctx, item.ID); touchErr != nil {
681				return result, fmt.Errorf("%s, but could not record activity: %w", status, touchErr)
682			}
683			return result, nil

694		case tui.TryCreate:
695			created, createErr := service.ResolveOrCreate(ctx, experiment.CreateRequest{

698			warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, created.Diagnostics)

47			}

197	func (s *operationStore) loadJournal() (journal, error) {
198		data, err := readPrivateFile(s.journalPath(), 2<<20)
199		if err != nil {
200			return journal{}, err
201		}
202		var value journal
203		if err := fleet.UnmarshalStrict(data, 2<<20, &value); err != nil {
204			return journal{}, fmt.Errorf("decode local-files journal: %w", err)
205		}
206		if err := validateJournal(value); err != nil {
207			return journal{}, err
208		}
209		return value, nil
210	}
211
212	func validateJournal(value journal) error {
213		if value.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || value.RequestID == "" || !validDigest(value.PlanDigest) || !validDigest(value.ManifestDigest) {
214			return errors.New("invalid local-files journal binding")
215		}
216		switch value.Phase {
217		case phaseStaged, phaseApplying, phaseCompleted, phaseRolledBack, phaseReconcile:
218		default:
219			return errors.New("invalid local-files journal phase")
220		}
221		for index, file := range value.Files {
222			if index > 0 && value.Files[index-1].Path >= file.Path {
223				return errors.New("local-files journal paths are not sorted")
224			}
225			switch file.Action {
226			case actionCurrent, actionCreate, actionReplace:
227			default:
228				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid action")
229			}
230			if !file.State.validResult() {
231				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid result state")
232			}
233			if file.Size < 0 || file.Mode != "0600" && file.Mode != "0700" {
234				return errors.New("local-files journal has invalid public metadata")
235			}
236			if file.Action == actionReplace && (!validDigest(file.OldSHA256) || !validFileMode(file.OldMode)) {
237				return errors.New("local-files replacement journal lacks rollback binding")
238			}
239		}
240		return nil
241	}
242

245			return err
246		}

248	}

258		}{SchemaVersion, envelope.Request.RequestID, envelope.Request.Binding,

263	func (s *operationStore) writeBlob(filename string, content []byte, executable bool) error {
264		if existing, err := readPrivateFile(filename, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes); err == nil {
265			if digestBytes(existing) != digestBytes(content) {
266				return errors.New("existing local-files blob does not match operation")
267			}
268			return nil
269		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
270			return err
271		}
272		parentPath := filepath.Dir(filename)
273		root, rootInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
274		if err != nil {
275			return err
276		}
277		defer root.Close()
278		name := filepath.Base(filename)
279		if _, err := safefile.CreatePrivateNoClobber(context.Background(), root, name, content, executable); err != nil {
280			return err
281		}
282		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, rootInfo); err != nil {
283			return err
284		}
285		readback, err := readPrivateFile(filename, safefile.CompiledMaxFileBytes)
286		if err != nil || digestBytes(readback) != digestBytes(content) {
287			return errors.New("local-files blob failed post-write verification")
288		}
289		return nil

28	// Diagnostic describes one task record omitted from a partial listing.

34	func (d Diagnostic) Error() string {

38	func (d Diagnostic) Unwrap() error { return d.Err }

40	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
41	//
42	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
43	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
44	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
45	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
46	type Store struct{ Dir string }
47
48	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
49	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
50
51	// ImportOutcome reports what ImportExact observed or changed.
52	type ImportOutcome string
53
54	const (
55		// ImportCreated means no task used the imported ID and a file was created.
56		ImportCreated ImportOutcome = "created"
57		// ImportIdentical means the same ID and semantic content were already stored.
58		ImportIdentical ImportOutcome = "identical"
59		// ImportConflict means the ID already held different semantic content.
60		ImportConflict ImportOutcome = "conflict"
61	)

64		idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
65		validID  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`)
66	)
67
68	// ValidateID checks that id can be used as exactly one visible filename stem.
69	func ValidateID(id string) error {
70		if !validID.MatchString(id) || filepath.Base(id) != id || id == "." || id == ".." {
71			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrInvalidID)
72		}
73		return nil
74	}
75
76	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
77	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
78		clean := func(s string) string {
79			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
80			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
81				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
82			}
83			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
84		}
85		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
86		if r == "" {
87			r = "repo"
88		}
89		if b == "" {
90			b = "branch"
91		}
92		return r + "__" + b
93	}

95	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }

97	// Save creates a task or updates one read by this Store. Existing-task writes
98	// compare the task's private loaded revision under the cross-process lock, so
99	// legacy callers cannot silently overwrite a newer process's mutation.
100	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
101		candidate, err := prepareCandidate(t, true)
102		if err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		err = s.withMutationLock(func() error {
106			current, currentErr := s.get(candidate.ID)
107			switch {
108			case currentErr == nil:
109				if candidate.storedRevision == "" || candidate.storedRevision != current.Revision() {
110					return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
111				}
112				if !candidate.Created.Equal(current.Created) {
113					return fmt.Errorf("task %s changed its creation time: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
114				}
115			case errors.Is(currentErr, ErrNotFound):
116				if candidate.storedRevision != "" {
117					return fmt.Errorf("task %s was removed after it was read: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
118				}
119			default:
120				return currentErr
121			}
122			stampForSave(candidate)
123			if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
124				return err
125			}
126			candidate.storedRevision = candidate.Revision()
127			return nil
128		})
129		if err != nil {
130			return err
131		}
132		*t = *candidate
133		return nil
134	}

97	// CheckoutIndexForPath returns the most-specific checkout containing path. It
98	// uses the same symlink-aware matching as runtime assignment, so a current
99	// directory under a nested linked worktree never resolves to the canonical
100	// checkout merely because that checkout is its lexical parent.
101	func (c RepoContext) CheckoutIndexForPath(path string) (int, bool) {
102		best, bestLen := -1, -1
103		for index := range c.Checkouts {
104			for _, root := range checkoutRoots(c.Repo, index, c.Checkouts[index]) {
105				if pathContains(root, path) && len(filepath.Clean(root)) > bestLen {
106					best, bestLen = index, len(filepath.Clean(root))
107				}
108			}
109		}
110		return best, best >= 0
111	}

113	// Sessions returns the repo's live sessions once each, preserving checkout
114	// order so a pasted context reads canonical-first.
115	func (c RepoContext) Sessions() []runtime.Session {
116		seen := map[string]bool{}
117		var out []runtime.Session
118		for _, checkout := range c.Checkouts {
119			for _, session := range checkout.Sessions {
120				key := session.Handle
121				if key == "" {
122					key = session.Label + "\x00" + strings.Join(session.Dirs, "\x00")
123				}
124				if seen[key] {
125					continue
126				}
127				seen[key] = true
128				out = append(out, session)
129			}
130		}
131		return out
132	}

134	// CollectRepoContext joins Git, task and runtime state for one repository.
135	// Repositories with no linked-worktree admin entries deliberately skip

137	func CollectRepoContext(ctx context.Context, r repo.Repo, tasks []*task.Task,
138		sessions []runtime.Session, runtimeName string) RepoContext {
139
140		out := RepoContext{Repo: r, Runtime: runtimeName}

146		if r.Bare {

151			main.Worktree.Detached = main.Status.Detached
152			main.LastActivity, main.LastCommit, main.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(ctx, r.Path, main.Status)
153		}
154		out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, main)
155
156		out.WorktreeCount, out.WorktreeErr = linkedAdminCount(r.CommonDir)
157		if out.WorktreeErr == nil && out.WorktreeCount > 0 {
158			worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
159			if err != nil {
160				out.WorktreeErr = err
161			} else {
162				out.WorktreeCount = 0
163				for _, w := range worktrees {
164					if w.Main {
165						continue
166					}
167					exists, pathErr := pathIsDir(w.Path)
168					checkout := RepoCheckout{
169						Worktree: w, Exists: exists, PathErr: pathErr, Ownership: CheckoutExternal,
170					}
171					if checkout.Exists && checkout.PathErr == nil && !w.Prunable {
172						checkout.Status, checkout.StatusErr = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, w.Path)
173						checkout.LastActivity, checkout.LastCommit, checkout.LastSubject = checkoutActivity(ctx, w.Path, checkout.Status)
174					}
175					if IsEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
176						checkout.Ownership = CheckoutEphemeral
177					}
178					out.Checkouts = append(out.Checkouts, checkout)
179					out.WorktreeCount++
180				}
181			}
182		}
183
184		assignTasks(&out, tasks)
185		assignSessions(&out, sessions)
186		for _, checkout := range out.Checkouts {
187			if checkout.LastActivity.After(out.LastActivity) {
188				out.LastActivity = checkout.LastActivity
189			}
190			for _, t := range checkout.Tasks {
191				if t.Updated.After(out.LastActivity) {
192					out.LastActivity = t.Updated
193				}
194			}
195		}
196		for _, t := range out.OtherTasks {
197			if t.Updated.After(out.LastActivity) {
198				out.LastActivity = t.Updated
199			}
200		}
201		return out
202	}

204	// IsEphemeralWorktree recognises turn-scoped checkouts owned by an agent
205	// harness. They stay visible, but the label prevents an agent from treating

207	func IsEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
208		slashPath := filepath.ToSlash(path)
209		return strings.Contains(slashPath, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
210			strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
211	}

213	func linkedAdminCount(commonDir string) (int, error) {
214		if commonDir == "" {
215			return 0, nil
216		}
217		entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(commonDir, "worktrees"))
218		if err != nil {
219			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
220				return 0, nil
221			}
222			return 0, err
223		}
224		n := 0
225		for _, entry := range entries {
226			if entry.IsDir() {
227				n++
228			}
229		}
230		return n, nil
231	}

233	func pathIsDir(path string) (bool, error) {
234		info, err := os.Stat(path)

236			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
237				return false, nil
238			}
239			return false, err
240		}
241		if !info.IsDir() {
242			return false, fmt.Errorf("checkout path is not a directory")
243		}
244		return true, nil

 func checkoutActivity(ctx context.Context, path string, status gitx.Status) (time.Time, time.Time, string) {
    latest := status.LatestChange
    var commit time.Time
    var subject string
    if unix, lastSubject, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, path); err == nil && unix > 0 {
        commit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
        if commit.After(latest) {
            latest = commit
        }
        subject = lastSubject
    }
    return latest, commit, subject
 }

 func assignTasks(out *RepoContext, tasks []*task.Task) {
    for _, t := range tasks {
        assigned := false
        if t.WorktreePath != "" {
            for i := 1; i < len(out.Checkouts); i++ {
                if samePath(t.WorktreePath, out.Checkouts[i].Worktree.Path) {
                    out.Checkouts[i].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, t)
                    out.Checkouts[i].Ownership = CheckoutDev
                    assigned = true
                    break
                }
            }
        } else if len(out.Checkouts) > 0 && t.Branch == out.Checkouts[0].Branch() {
            out.Checkouts[0].Tasks = append(out.Checkouts[0].Tasks, t)
            assigned = true
        }
        if !assigned {
            out.OtherTasks = append(out.OtherTasks, t)
        }
    }
    for i := range out.Checkouts {
        sort.SliceStable(out.Checkouts[i].Tasks, func(a, b int) bool {
            return out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[a].ID < out.Checkouts[i].Tasks[b].ID
        })
    }
    sort.SliceStable(out.OtherTasks, func(i, j int) bool {
        return out.OtherTasks[i].ID < out.OtherTasks[j].ID
    })
 }

 // assignSessions assigns each observed directory to the most-specific
 // checkout. A session rooted in repo/.claude/worktrees/x therefore belongs to
 // x, not to the canonical checkout which also happens to contain that path.
 func assignSessions(out *RepoContext, sessions []runtime.Session) {
    for _, session := range sessions {
        assigned := map[int]bool{}
        for _, dir := range session.Dirs {
            best, bestLen := -1, -1
            for i := range out.Checkouts {
                for _, root := range checkoutRoots(out.Repo, i, out.Checkouts[i]) {
                    if pathContains(root, dir) && len(filepath.Clean(root)) > bestLen {
                        best, bestLen = i, len(filepath.Clean(root))
                    }
                }
            }
            if best >= 0 {
                assigned[best] = true
            }
        }
        for i := range assigned {
            out.Checkouts[i].Sessions = append(out.Checkouts[i].Sessions, session)
        }
    }
 }

 func checkoutRoots(r repo.Repo, index int, checkout RepoCheckout) []string {
    roots := []string{checkout.Worktree.Path}
    if index == 0 && r.RealPath != "" && !samePath(r.RealPath, r.Path) {
        roots = append(roots, r.RealPath)
    }
    return roots
 }

 func pathContains(root, path string) bool {
    if root == "" || path == "" {
        return false
    }
    rel, err := filepath.Rel(normalizePath(root), normalizePath(path))
    if err != nil || rel == ".." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
        return false
    }
    return rel == "." || !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
 }

 func samePath(a, b string) bool {
    return a != "" && b != "" && normalizePath(a) == normalizePath(b)
 }

 // normalizePath resolves symlinks in the longest existing prefix. macOS temp
 // paths commonly arrive as both /var/... and /private/var/...; runtime CWDs may
 // also name a not-yet-created descendant, so EvalSymlinks on the whole string
 // is not sufficient.
 func normalizePath(path string) string {
    clean := filepath.Clean(path)
    cur := clean
    for {
        if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(cur); err == nil {
            rel, relErr := filepath.Rel(cur, clean)
            if relErr == nil && rel != "." {
                return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(real, rel))
            }
            return filepath.Clean(real)
        }
        parent := filepath.Dir(cur)
        if parent == cur {
            return clean
        }
        cur = parent
    }
 }

 // FormatSessions renders the ys payload. checkoutIndex < 0 selects the whole
 // repository; otherwise it selects one checkout.
 func FormatSessions(c RepoContext, checkoutIndex int) string {
    indices := make([]int, 0, len(c.Checkouts))
    if checkoutIndex >= 0 && checkoutIndex < len(c.Checkouts) {
        indices = append(indices, checkoutIndex)
    } else {
        for i := range c.Checkouts {
            indices = append(indices, i)
        }

    var b strings.Builder
    for _, i := range indices {
        checkout := c.Checkouts[i]

            status := session.AgentStatus
            if status == "" {
                status = "unknown"
            }
            fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s`: `%s %s` (%s)\n",
                checkout.Worktree.Path, c.Runtime, session.Handle, status)
            if len(session.AgentSessions) > 0 {
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  - agents: %s\n", markdownCodes(session.AgentSessions))

    paths := make([]string, 0, len(c.Linked()))
    for _, checkout := range c.Linked() {
        paths = append(paths, checkout.Worktree.Path)
    }
    return strings.Join(paths, "\n")
 }

 package tui

 import (

 )

 // listHeight budgets rows from what the current detail and footer actually
 // render. REPOS has more detail and more key hints than TASKS; the old fixed
 // chrome allowance let the complete view exceed terminal height, so Bubble
 // Tea scrolled the first lines and the top tab bar appeared to disappear.
 func (m Model) listHeight() int {
    // Header + its blank line, table header, blank before detail, blank before
    // footer. Detail and footer can each wrap/change by view and terminal width.
    fixed := 2 + 1 + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
    h := m.height - fixed
    if h < 3 {
        return 3
    }
    // A long list adds the "… x–y of n" scroll note.
    if m.count() > h && h > 3 {
        h--
    }
    return h
 }

 func lineCount(s string) int {
    s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\n")
    if s == "" {
        return 0
    }
    return strings.Count(s, "\n") + 1
 }

 // View implements tea.Model.
 func (m Model) View() string {
    if m.quitting {
        return ""
    }
    if m.noteMode() {
        return m.renderNotes()
    }
    if m.overlay.kind != overlayNone {
        return m.renderOverlay()
    }
    if m.mode == modeStats {
        return m.renderStats()
    }
    var b strings.Builder
    b.WriteString(m.renderHeader())
    b.WriteString("\n")

    switch m.view {
    case ViewRepos:
        b.WriteString(m.renderRepos())
    case ViewFleet:
        b.WriteString(m.renderFleet())
    case ViewTries:
        b.WriteString(m.renderTries())
    case ViewRemote:
        b.WriteString(m.renderRemotes())
    case ViewSkills:
        b.WriteString(m.renderSkills())
    default:
        b.WriteString(m.renderTasks())
    }

    b.WriteString("\n")
    b.WriteString(m.renderDetail())
    b.WriteString("\n")
    b.WriteString(m.renderFooter())
    return b.String()
 }

 func (m Model) renderStats() string {
    var b strings.Builder
    title := "repo activity"

83	// collectLocalRepoContext is the single CLI collector used by repo context and
84	// status. It executes only local Git/task/runtime probes; includeTopology adds
85	// repository-wide remote/ref facts but never performs fetch or other network I/O.
86	func collectLocalRepoContext(ctx context.Context, app *App, repository repo.Repo, selectedPath string, includeTopology bool) localRepoContext {
87		var (
88			tasks    = []*task.Task{}
89			tasksErr error
90		)
91		if app.Tasks == nil {
92			tasksErr = errors.New("task store is unavailable")
93		} else {
94			listed, diagnostics, err := app.Tasks.ListWithDiagnostics()
95			if err != nil {
96				tasksErr = err
97			} else {
98				tasks = tasksForRepo(listed, repository)
99				for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
100					tasksErr = errors.Join(tasksErr, diagnostic)
101				}
102			}
103		}
104
105		rt := app.Runtime()
106		sessions, runtimeErr := rt.List(ctx)
107		local := localRepoContext{
108			Context: inventory.CollectRepoContext(ctx, repository, tasks, sessions, rt.Name()),
109			Runtimes: []repocontext.RuntimeInput{{
110				Backend: rt.Name(), Available: rt.Available(), Sessions: sessions, Err: runtimeErr,
111			}},
112			SelectedCheckout: -1,
113		}
114		local.Context.TaskErr = tasksErr
115		local.Context.RuntimeErr = runtimeErr
116		if selected, ok := local.Context.CheckoutIndexForPath(selectedPath); ok {
117			local.SelectedCheckout = selected
118		} else {
119			local.SelectionErr = fmt.Errorf("selected path %s is not represented by the repository worktree inventory", config.Contract(selectedPath))
120		}
121		if includeTopology && repository.HasGit {
122			local.Topology, local.TopologyErr = gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, repository.Path)
123		}
124		return local
125	}

127	func resolveRepoContextTarget(ctx context.Context, app *App, args []string) (repo.Repo, string, error) {
128		if len(args) == 1 {
129			resolved, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, args[0])
130			if err != nil {
131				return repo.Repo{}, "", err
132			}
133			return resolved, resolved.Path, nil
134		}
135		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
136		if err != nil {
137			return repo.Repo{}, "", err
138		}
139		discovered, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
140		if err != nil {
141			return repo.Repo{}, "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository — pass a repo", config.Contract(cwd))
142		}
143		selectedPath := discovered.Root
144		if selectedPath == "" {
145			selectedPath = discovered.MainRoot
146		}
147		return repo.Repo{
148			Name: discovered.Name, Path: discovered.MainRoot, RealPath: discovered.MainRoot,
149			GitDir: discovered.GitCommonDir, CommonDir: discovered.GitCommonDir,
150			MainRoot: discovered.MainRoot, HasGit: true, Bare: discovered.Bare,
151		}, selectedPath, nil
152	}

154	func collectRepoContextForge(ctx context.Context, app *App, refresh bool, now time.Time) repocontext.ForgeInput {
155		cacheInput := func(cache forge.Cache, collectionErr error) repocontext.ForgeInput {
156			freshness := assessment.FreshnessFresh

1	// Package lease provides cooperative, durable repository operation fencing.
2	// Its default authority lives in private XDG state, outside repository roots.
3	package lease

20

22

24		ScopeRepository Scope = "repository"
25		ScopeBranch     Scope = "branch"
26	)
27

31		Branch     string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
32	}

36		Digest      string `json:"digest"`
37		MachineID   string `json:"machine_id,omitempty"`
38	}
39
40	// Binding permanently associates an idempotency ID with one manifest digest.
41	type Binding struct {
42		OperationID string `json:"operation_id"`
43		Digest      string `json:"digest"`
44	}
45
46	type Token struct {
47		OperationID string `json:"operation_id"`
48		Digest      string `json:"digest"`
49		Epoch       uint64 `json:"epoch"`
50	}
51
52	type Claim struct {

57

60	const (
61		TombstoneAborted  TombstoneKind = "aborted"
62		TombstoneReturned TombstoneKind = "returned"
63	)
64
65	type Tombstone struct {
66		Kind          TombstoneKind `json:"kind"`
67		Token         Token         `json:"token"`
68		AdvancedEpoch uint64        `json:"advanced_epoch"`
69		CreatedAt     time.Time     `json:"created_at"`
70	}
71
72	// Record is the durable state for one canonical operation key. At most one of
73	// Reservation and Fence can be active.
74	type Record struct {
75		Key         Key         `json:"key"`
76		Epoch       uint64      `json:"epoch"`
77		Reservation *Claim      `json:"reservation,omitempty"`
78		Fence       *Claim      `json:"fence,omitempty"`

80	}
81
82	type Snapshot struct {
83		SchemaVersion int       `json:"schema_version"`
84		LastEpoch     uint64    `json:"last_epoch"`
85		Bindings      []Binding `json:"bindings"`
86		Records       []Record  `json:"records"`
87	}
88
89	var (
90		ErrBlocked       = errors.New("operation lease blocked")
91		ErrConflict      = errors.New("operation lease conflict")
92		ErrEpochMismatch = errors.New("operation lease epoch mismatch")
93		ErrReturned      = errors.New("operation lease token is terminal")
94
95		operationIDPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`)
96	)
97
98	type BlockedError struct {
99		Key         Key
100		Kind        string
101		OperationID string
102	}
103
104	func (e *BlockedError) Error() string {
105		return fmt.Sprintf("%s lease for %s is blocked by %s operation %s", e.Key.Scope, e.Key.subject(), e.Kind, e.OperationID)
106	}
107
108	func (e *BlockedError) Unwrap() error { return ErrBlocked }
109
110	func RepositoryKey(repository string) Key {
111		return Key{Repository: repository, Scope: ScopeRepository}
112	}
113
114	func BranchKey(repository, branch string) Key {
115		return Key{Repository: repository, Scope: ScopeBranch, Branch: branch}
116	}
117
118	func (k Key) Validate() error {
119		if err := validateIdentity("repository identity", k.Repository); err != nil {
120			return err
121		}
122		switch k.Scope {
123		case ScopeRepository:
124			if k.Branch != "" {
125				return errors.New("repository lease key must not name a branch")
126			}
127		case ScopeBranch:
128			if err := validateIdentity("branch", k.Branch); err != nil {
129				return err
130			}
131		default:
132			return fmt.Errorf("unknown lease scope %q", k.Scope)
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136
137	func (k Key) canonical() string {
138		// Length prefixes keep arbitrary valid identities unambiguous.
139		return fmt.Sprintf("%08x:%s:%s:%08x:%s", len(k.Repository), k.Repository, k.Scope, len(k.Branch), k.Branch)
140	}
141
142	func (k Key) subject() string {
143		if k.Scope == ScopeBranch {
144			return k.Repository + " branch " + k.Branch
145		}
146		return k.Repository
147	}
148
149	func (r Request) Validate() error {
150		if !operationIDPattern.MatchString(r.OperationID) {
151			return fmt.Errorf("invalid operation id %q", r.OperationID)
152		}
153		if !assessment.ValidFingerprint(r.Digest) {
154			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s has invalid digest %q", r.OperationID, r.Digest)
155		}
156		if r.MachineID != "" {
157			if err := machineid.Validate(r.MachineID); err != nil {
158				return err
159			}
160		}
161		return nil
162	}
163
164	func (b Binding) Validate() error {
165		return (Request{OperationID: b.OperationID, Digest: b.Digest}).Validate()
166	}
167
168	func (t Token) Validate() error {
169		if err := (Request{OperationID: t.OperationID, Digest: t.Digest}).Validate(); err != nil {
170			return err
171		}
172		if t.Epoch == 0 {
173			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s has zero lease epoch", t.OperationID)
174		}
175		return nil
176	}
177
178	func (t Token) matches(other Token) bool {
179		return t.OperationID == other.OperationID && t.Digest == other.Digest && t.Epoch == other.Epoch
180	}
181
182	func (t Token) sameOperation(request Request) bool {
183		return t.OperationID == request.OperationID && t.Digest == request.Digest
184	}
185
186	// CanonicalKeys validates, deduplicates, and sorts keys in the one order used
187	// by every multi-key acquisition.
188	func CanonicalKeys(keys []Key) ([]Key, error) {
189		if len(keys) == 0 {
190			return nil, errors.New("operation lease requires at least one key")
191		}
192		unique := make(map[string]Key, len(keys))
193		for _, key := range keys {
194			if err := key.Validate(); err != nil {
195				return nil, err
196			}
197			unique[key.canonical()] = key
198		}
199		canonical := make([]Key, 0, len(unique))
200		for _, key := range unique {
201			canonical = append(canonical, key)
202		}
203		sort.Slice(canonical, func(i, j int) bool { return canonical[i].canonical() < canonical[j].canonical() })
204		return canonical, nil
205	}
206
207	func validateIdentity(name, value string) error {
208		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) {
209			return fmt.Errorf("%s is required and must be trimmed", name)
210		}
211		if !utf8.ValidString(value) {
212			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not valid UTF-8", name)
213		}
214		for _, char := range value {
215			if unicode.IsControl(char) {
216				return fmt.Errorf("%s contains a control character", name)
217			}
218		}
219		return nil
220	}
221

51	// Reserve creates a blocking pre-publication claim. Repeating the exact
52	// operation and key set is idempotent; reusing an operation ID with a different

58	// Fence drains existing cooperative guards and durably prevents new ordinary
59	// mutations. It can promote an exact reservation or create a direct fence.

64	func (a *Authority) activate(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, request Request, fence bool) (Token, error) {
65		if a == nil {

67		}

77			return a.updateState(ctx, func(state *Snapshot) (bool, error) {
78				if err := checkOperationReuse(*state, claimed, request); err != nil {

80				}

88				claimKinds := make([]string, len(canonical))

90					record := findRecord(state.Records, key)
91					if record == nil {
92						continue
93					}
94					switch {
95					case record.Reservation != nil:
96						claims[index], claimKinds[index] = record.Reservation, "reservation"
97					case record.Fence != nil:
98						claims[index], claimKinds[index] = record.Fence, "fence"
99					}
100				}
101
102				allSameKind := true

106					if fence {
107						wantedKind = "fence"
108					}

153					} else {

155						record.Fence = nil

164	// ReleaseReservation clears an exact reservation and advances the authority
165	// epoch. It is non-terminal; AbortReservation should be used for a terminal
166	// pre-fence cancellation.
167	func (a *Authority) ReleaseReservation(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, token Token) (uint64, error) {
168		return a.finishClaim(ctx, keys, token, "reservation", "")
169	}
170
171	// AbortReservation clears an exact reservation and retains a permanent
172	// terminal tombstone so delayed prepare replays cannot recreate it.
173	func (a *Authority) AbortReservation(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, token Token) (uint64, error) {
174		return a.finishClaim(ctx, keys, token, "reservation", TombstoneAborted)
175	}

177	// Return clears an exact fence and retains a permanent terminal tombstone so
178	// delayed accepts carrying the old epoch fail closed.

183	func (a *Authority) finishClaim(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, token Token, claimKind string, terminal TombstoneKind) (uint64, error) {
184		if a == nil {
185			return 0, errors.New("use nil operation lease authority")
186		}
187		if err := token.Validate(); err != nil {
188			return 0, err
189		}
190		claimed, err := CanonicalKeys(keys)
191		if err != nil {

193		}

196			return a.updateState(ctx, func(state *Snapshot) (bool, error) {
197				canonical := claimed
198				if terminal != "" {
199					if epoch, found, err := matchingTerminal(*state, canonical, token, terminal); err != nil {

204					}

206				if err := validateClaimKeySet(*state, canonical, token, claimKind); err != nil {
207					return false, err

209				for _, key := range canonical {

211					if record == nil {
212						return false, fmt.Errorf("%s has no active %s: %w", key.subject(), claimKind, ErrEpochMismatch)
213					}
214					var claim *Claim
215					if claimKind == "reservation" {
216						claim = record.Reservation
217					} else {
218						claim = record.Fence
219					}
220					if claim == nil || !claim.Token.matches(token) {

222					}

224				epoch, err := allocateEpoch(state)

227				}
228				advanced = epoch
229				now := canonicalTime(a.clock())
230				for _, key := range canonical {
231					record := findRecord(state.Records, key)
232					record.Epoch = epoch
233					if claimKind == "reservation" {
234						record.Reservation = nil
235					} else {
236						record.Fence = nil
237					}
238					if terminal != "" {

248	// WithMutation runs an ordinary mutator only when no requested key is reserved
249	// or fenced. A branch key automatically includes its repository ancestor so a
250	// repository fence covers every branch. The locks remain held until operation
251	// returns.
252	func (a *Authority) WithMutation(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, operation func() error) error {
253		return a.WithGuard(ctx, keys, nil, operation)
254	}

256	// WithGuard permits the exact owner of an active reservation or fence to work
257	// while rejecting stale, returned, and mismatched tokens. A nil token is an
258	// ordinary mutation guard and includes repository ancestors. It is
259	// non-reentrant: operation must not reacquire an overlapping key.
260	func (a *Authority) WithGuard(ctx context.Context, keys []Key, token *Token, operation func() error) error {
261		if a == nil {
262			return errors.New("use nil operation lease authority")
263		}
264		if operation == nil {
265			return errors.New("operation lease guard requires an operation")
266		}
267		claimed, err := CanonicalKeys(keys)
268		if err != nil {
269			return err
270		}

272		if token != nil {

275			}
276		} else {

281			}

283		return a.withKeyLocks(ctx, mutationKeys(claimed), func(locked []Key) error {
284			checked := locked
285			if token != nil {

287				// branch-scoped token's ownership claim.
288				checked = claimed
289			}
290			if err := a.readState(ctx, func(state Snapshot) error {
291				matched := 0
292				for _, key := range checked {

346			}

348			case actionCreate:
349				if !observed.exists {
350					continue
351				}
352				if observed.digest != spec.SHA256 {
353					return errors.New("created target changed before rollback")
354				}

356				if err != nil {
357					return err
358				}
359				err = parent.parent.Remove(pathBase(spec.Path))

16	const maxWalkEntries = 200_000

18	var dependencyComponents = map[string]struct{}{
19		"node_modules": {}, ".venv": {}, "venv": {}, "vendor": {},
20		"__pycache__": {}, ".tox": {}, "target": {}, ".terraform": {},

24	// Expand resolves validated project and --file patterns locally into a sorted,
25	// duplicate-free list of exact slash paths. It never follows links or descends
26	// into Git metadata, nested repositories, submodules, or dependency trees.
27	func Expand(root string, patterns []Pattern, limits safefile.Limits) ([]string, error) {
28		if err := limits.Validate(); err != nil {
29			return nil, err
30		}
31		if len(patterns) == 0 {
32			return nil, errors.New("no local-file patterns were configured or passed with --file")
33		}
34		for _, pattern := range patterns {
35			if err := projectconfig.ValidateLocalFilePattern(pattern.Value); err != nil {
36				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s: %w", patternSource(pattern), err)
37			}
38			for _, component := range strings.Split(pattern.Value, "/") {
39				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
40					return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s enters dependency directory %q", patternSource(pattern), component)
41				}
42			}
43		}
44		rootInfo, err := os.Lstat(root)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, fmt.Errorf("inspect source checkout: %w", err)
47		}
48		if !rootInfo.IsDir() || rootInfo.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
49			return nil, errors.New("source checkout is not a held regular directory")
50		}
51
52		matches := map[string]struct{}{}
53		matchedPatterns := make([]bool, len(patterns))
54		visited := 0
55		err = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(filename string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
56			if walkErr != nil {
57				return walkErr
58			}
59			if filename == root {
60				return nil
61			}
62			visited++
63			if visited > maxWalkEntries {
64				return fmt.Errorf("source checkout exceeds %d entries while expanding local-file patterns", maxWalkEntries)
65			}
66			relative, err := filepath.Rel(root, filename)
67			if err != nil {
68				return err
69			}
70			slash := filepath.ToSlash(relative)
71			components := strings.Split(slash, "/")
72			base := strings.ToLower(components[len(components)-1])
73			if entry.IsDir() {
74				if base == ".git" {
75					return filepath.SkipDir
76				}
77				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[base]; blocked {
78					for _, pattern := range patterns {
79						if matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
80							return fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern enters dependency directory %q", slash)
81						}
82					}
83					return filepath.SkipDir
84				}
85				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(filename, ".git")); err == nil {
86					return filepath.SkipDir
87				} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
88					return fmt.Errorf("inspect nested repository boundary %s: %w", slash, err)
89				}
90			}
91			matched := false
92			for index, pattern := range patterns {
93				if !entry.IsDir() && matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
94					matchedPatterns[index] = true
95					matched = true
96				}
97			}
98			if matched {
99				matches[slash] = struct{}{}
100			}
101			if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 && entry.IsDir() {
102				return filepath.SkipDir
103			}
104			return nil
105		})
106		if err != nil {
107			return nil, err
108		}
109		for index, matched := range matchedPatterns {
110			if !matched {
111				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s matched no source path", patternSource(patterns[index]))
112			}
113		}
114		paths := make([]string, 0, len(matches))
115		for path := range matches {
116			paths = append(paths, path)
117		}
118		sort.Strings(paths)
119		if len(paths) > limits.MaxFiles {
120			return nil, fmt.Errorf("patterns expanded to %d paths; maximum is %d", len(paths), limits.MaxFiles)
121		}
122		return paths, nil
123	}
124
125	func patternSource(pattern Pattern) string {
126		if strings.TrimSpace(pattern.Source) == "" {
127			return "explicit input"
128		}
129		return pattern.Source
130	}
131
132	func matchPattern(pattern, candidate string) bool {
133		patternParts := strings.Split(pattern, "/")
134		candidateParts := strings.Split(candidate, "/")
135		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
136		memo := map[key]bool{}
137		seen := map[key]bool{}
138		var match func(int, int) bool
139		match = func(patternIndex, candidateIndex int) bool {
140			state := key{patternIndex, candidateIndex}
141			if seen[state] {
142				return memo[state]
143			}
144			seen[state] = true
145			var result bool
146			switch {
147			case patternIndex == len(patternParts):
148				result = candidateIndex == len(candidateParts)
149			case patternParts[patternIndex] == "**":
150				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex) ||
151					candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && match(patternIndex, candidateIndex+1)
152			case candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && matchComponent(patternParts[patternIndex], candidateParts[candidateIndex]):
153				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex+1)
154			}
155			memo[state] = result
156			return result
157		}
158		return match(0, 0)
159	}
160
161	func matchComponent(pattern, candidate string) bool {
162		p, c := []rune(pattern), []rune(candidate)
163		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
164		memo := map[key]bool{}
165		seen := map[key]bool{}
166		var match func(int, int) bool
167		match = func(pi, ci int) bool {
168			state := key{pi, ci}
169			if seen[state] {
170				return memo[state]
171			}
172			seen[state] = true
173			var result bool
174			switch {
175			case pi == len(p):
176				result = ci == len(c)
177			case p[pi] == '*':
178				result = match(pi+1, ci) || ci < len(c) && match(pi, ci+1)
179			case ci < len(c) && (p[pi] == '?' || p[pi] == c[ci]):
180				result = match(pi+1, ci+1)
181			}
182			memo[state] = result
183			return result
184		}
185		return match(0, 0)
186	}
187
188	func hasDependencyComponent(path string) bool {
189		for _, component := range strings.Split(path, "/") {
190			if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
191				return true
192			}
193		}
194		return false
195	}

56		case SyncUpdated, SyncCurrent, SyncFetched, SyncAbsent, SyncNoDev:
57			return true

68	func ApplySync(ctx context.Context, cfg devconfig.Config, request SyncRequest) SyncResult {
69		result := SyncResult{Host: devconfig.Hostname(), Branch: request.Branch, ExpectedOID: request.ExpectedOID}
70		request.RemoteIdentity = catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(request.RemoteIdentity)
71		if request.RemoteIdentity == "" || request.Branch == "" || request.ExpectedOID == "" {
72			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, "sync request requires remote identity, branch and expected OID"
73			return result
74		}
75		repositories, err := repo.Discover(ctx, cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
76		if err != nil {
77			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
78			return result
79		}
80		var candidates []syncCandidate
81		for _, repository := range repositories {
82			if repository.Bare || !repository.HasGit {
83				continue
84			}
85			topology, topologyErr := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, repository.Path)
86			if topologyErr != nil {
87				continue
88			}
89			if remote := matchingRemoteAt(ctx, repository.Path, topology, request.RemoteIdentity); remote != "" {
90				candidates = append(candidates, syncCandidate{repository: repository, remote: remote})
91			}
92		}
93		sort.Slice(candidates, func(i, j int) bool { return candidates[i].repository.Path < candidates[j].repository.Path })
94		switch len(candidates) {
95		case 0:
96			result.State = SyncAbsent
97			return result
98		case 1:
99		default:
100			result.State = SyncAmbiguous
101			paths := make([]string, len(candidates))
102			for index, candidate := range candidates {
103				paths[index] = candidate.repository.Path
104			}
105			result.Error = "remote identity matches multiple clones: " + strings.Join(paths, ", ")
106			return result
107		}
108		candidate := candidates[0]
109		result.Repo, result.Path, result.Remote = candidate.repository.Display(), candidate.repository.Path, candidate.remote
110		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.repository.Path, "fetch", "--prune", "--quiet", candidate.remote); err != nil {
111			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
112			return result
113		}
114		remoteRef := candidate.remote + "/" + request.Branch
115		remoteOID, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.repository.Path, "rev-parse", "--verify", remoteRef+"^{commit}")
116		if err != nil {
117			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, fmt.Sprintf("remote branch %s is unavailable after fetch: %v", remoteRef, err)
118			return result
119		}
120		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.repository.Path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", request.ExpectedOID, remoteOID); err != nil {
121			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, "fetched remote branch does not contain the source commit"
122			return result
123		}
124		worktree, checkedOut, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, candidate.repository.Path, request.Branch)
125		if err != nil {
126			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
127			return result
128		}
129		if !checkedOut {
130			result.State, result.AfterOID = SyncFetched, remoteOID
131			return result
132		}
133		result.Path = worktree.Path
134		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, worktree.Path)
135		if err != nil {
136			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
137			return result
138		}
139		if status.Dirty() || status.Conflicted > 0 {
140			result.State, result.Error = SyncDirty, status.Summary()
141			return result
142		}
143		localOID, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
144		if err != nil {
145			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
146			return result
147		}
148		result.BeforeOID = localOID
149		if localOID == remoteOID {
150			result.State, result.AfterOID = SyncCurrent, localOID
151			return result
152		}
153		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", localOID, remoteOID); err != nil {
154			if _, aheadErr := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", remoteOID, localOID); aheadErr == nil {
155				result.State, result.Error = SyncAhead, "checked-out branch contains commits not on the fetched remote"
156			} else {
157				result.State, result.Error = SyncDiverged, "checked-out branch diverged; rebase or merge manually"
158			}
159			return result
160		}
161		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "merge", "--ff-only", remoteRef); err != nil {
162			result.State, result.Error = SyncFailed, err.Error()
163			return result
164		}
165		after, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
166		if err != nil || after != remoteOID {
167			result.State = SyncFailed
168			result.Error = "fast-forward completed without reaching the fetched remote revision"
169			return result
170		}
171		result.State, result.AfterOID = SyncUpdated, after
172		return result
173	}

175	func matchingRemote(topology gitx.RecoveryTopology, identity string) string {
176		var names []string
177		for _, remote := range topology.Remotes {
178			matched := false
179			for _, raw := range append(append([]string{}, remote.FetchURLs...), remote.PushURLs...) {
180				if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw) == identity {
181					matched = true
182					break
183				}
184			}
185			if matched {
186				names = append(names, remote.Name)
187			}
188		}
189		sort.Strings(names)
190		if len(names) == 0 {
191			return ""
192		}
193		return names[0]
194	}
195
196	func matchingRemoteAt(ctx context.Context, path string, topology gitx.RecoveryTopology, identity string) string {
197		var names []string
198		for _, remote := range topology.Remotes {
199			matched := false
200			for _, key := range []string{"remote." + remote.Name + ".url", "remote." + remote.Name + ".pushurl"} {
201				raw, err := gitx.Run(ctx, path, "config", "--get-all", key)
202				if err != nil {
203					continue
204				}
205				for _, value := range strings.Split(raw, "\n") {
206					if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(value) == identity {
207						matched = true
208						break
209					}
210				}
211				if matched {
212					break
213				}
214			}
215			if matched {
216				names = append(names, remote.Name)
217			}
218		}
219		if len(names) == 0 {
220			return matchingRemote(topology, identity)
221		}
222		sort.Strings(names)
223		return names[0]
224	}

package localfiles

import (
    "context"
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "strings"

    "github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
    "github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
)

// FetchRemoteIdentity resolves the one normalized fetch identity used to bind a
// portable-file operation. Push URLs are intentionally excluded because they
// may name a publication mirror unrelated to the fetched repository.
func FetchRemoteIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout, branch string) (string, error) {
    var preferred []string
    if remote, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "config", "--get", "branch."+branch+".remote"); err == nil && remote != "" && remote != "." {
        preferred = append(preferred, remote)
    }
    preferred = append(preferred, "origin")
    remotes, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote")
    if err != nil {
        return "", err
    }
    preferred = append(preferred, strings.Fields(remotes)...)
    seenRemote := map[string]bool{}
    for _, remote := range preferred {
        if remote == "" || seenRemote[remote] {
            continue
        }
        seenRemote[remote] = true
        urls, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote", "get-url", "--all", remote)
        if err != nil {
            continue
        }
        identities := map[string]struct{}{}
        for _, raw := range strings.Split(urls, "\n") {
            if identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw); identity != "" {
                identities[identity] = struct{}{}
            }
        }
        if len(identities) == 1 {
            for identity := range identities {
                return identity, nil
            }
        }
    }
    return "", errors.New("checkout has no unambiguous normalized fetch remote identity")
}

func verifySourceBinding(ctx context.Context, checkout string, binding Binding) error {
    status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if status.Detached || status.Branch != binding.Branch {
        return fmt.Errorf("source branch changed from %s: %w", binding.Branch, ErrDrift)
    }
    head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}")
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if head != binding.HeadOID {
        return fmt.Errorf("source HEAD changed from %s: %w", binding.HeadOID, ErrDrift)
    }
    identity, err := FetchRemoteIdentity(ctx, checkout, binding.Branch)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if identity != binding.RemoteIdentity {
        return fmt.Errorf("source fetch identity changed: %w", ErrDrift)
    }
    return nil
}

14	func gitRun(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) string {

17		cmd.Dir = dir
18		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null", "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null")
19		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
20		if err != nil {
21			t.Fatalf("git %v in %s: %v\n%s", args, dir, err, out)
22		}
23		return string(out)
24	}

32
33	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
34	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
35	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
36	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
37
38	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
39	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, session closed, worktree
40	                  removed. Reconstruct it anywhere later with dev resume.
41
42	--cold and --keep-session are incompatible: a runtime cannot stay pointed at a
43	checkout that cold parking removes.
44
45	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
46	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
47	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
48			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),

51				if cold && keepRT {

53				}
54				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}
58
59				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
60				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
61					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
62						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
63				}
64				target := task.Warm
65				if cold {
66					target = task.Cold
67				}
68				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
69
70				if next != "" {
71					t.Next = next
72				}
73				if note != "" {
74					t.Note = note
75				}
76				if t.Next == "" {
77					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
78				}
79
80				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
81				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
82					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
83					if err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					switch {
87					case wip && st.Dirty():
88						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
89						if t.Next != "" {
90							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
91						}
92						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
93						if err != nil {
94							return err
95						}
96						if made {
97							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s  %s\n", app.outStyle().label("committed"), msg)
98						}
99					case st.Dirty() && cold:
100						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
101							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
102							config.Contract(checkout))
103					case st.Dirty():
104						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
105							config.Contract(checkout))
106					}
107
108					if push {

110							return err
111						}
112					}
113					if cold {
114						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
115						if err != nil {
116							return err
117						}
118						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
119							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
120								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
121						}

202	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
203	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
204		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
205			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
206		}
207		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s     origin/%s\n", app.outStyle().label("pushed"), branch)
208		return nil
209	}
210
211	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
212	// directory when no argument is given.
213	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
214		if len(args) == 1 {
215			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
216		}
217		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
218		if err != nil {
219			return nil, err
220		}
221		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
222		if err != nil {
223			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
224				config.Contract(cwd))
225		}
226		return t, nil
227	}

782	func collectReposWithOptions(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, options repoCollectOptions) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
783		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
784		if err != nil {
785			return nil, err
786		}
787		assets, catalogComplete, err := joinRepoAssets(app, repos)
788		if err != nil {
789			return nil, err
790		}
791		if !options.IncludeTries {
792			visibleRepos := make([]repo.Repo, 0, len(repos))
793			visibleAssets := make([]*catalog.Entry, 0, len(repos))
794			for index, repository := range repos {
795				if suppressTryRepo(assets[index], catalogComplete) {
796					continue
797				}
798				visibleRepos = append(visibleRepos, repository)
799				visibleAssets = append(visibleAssets, assets[index])
800			}
801			repos, assets = visibleRepos, visibleAssets
802		}
803		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
804		if err != nil {
805			return nil, err
806		}
807		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
808		for _, t := range tasks {
809			byRepo[t.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[t.RepoPath], t)
810		}
811		sessions := options.Sessions
812		if !options.SessionsSet {
813			sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
814		}
815		notesByRepo := map[string][]*note.Note{}
816		if app.Notes != nil {
817			allNotes, noteErr := app.Notes.List("")
818			if noteErr != nil {
819				return nil, noteErr
820			}
821			for _, n := range allNotes {
822				notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID] = append(notesByRepo[n.RepositoryID], n)
823			}
824		}
825
826		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, len(repos))
827		// Each repo needs status, worktree and remote subprocesses. Serialising
828		// ~3*56 git processes was the measured 4.2s startup bottleneck; eight
829		// workers brings that down without forking hundreds at once.

832		for i, r := range repos {

834			go func(i int, r repo.Repo) {

838

97	// Save creates a task or updates one read by this Store. Existing-task writes
98	// compare the task's private loaded revision under the cross-process lock, so
99	// legacy callers cannot silently overwrite a newer process's mutation.
100	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
101		candidate, err := prepareCandidate(t, true)
102		if err != nil {
103			return err
104		}
105		err = s.withMutationLock(func() error {
106			current, currentErr := s.get(candidate.ID)
107			switch {
108			case currentErr == nil:
109				if candidate.storedRevision == "" || candidate.storedRevision != current.Revision() {
110					return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
111				}
112				if !candidate.Created.Equal(current.Created) {
113					return fmt.Errorf("task %s changed its creation time: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
114				}
115			case errors.Is(currentErr, ErrNotFound):
116				if candidate.storedRevision != "" {
117					return fmt.Errorf("task %s was removed after it was read: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
118				}
119			default:
120				return currentErr
121			}
122			stampForSave(candidate)
123			if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
124				return err
125			}
126			candidate.storedRevision = candidate.Revision()
127			return nil
128		})
129		if err != nil {
130			return err
131		}
132		*t = *candidate
133		return nil
134	}

139	func (s *Store) ReplaceDone(t *Task, expectedRevision string) error {

198	// ImportExact creates t under its supplied ID without changing any semantic
199	// field or timestamp. Replaying identical content is a no-op; reusing an ID
200	// for different content reports ImportConflict and ErrConflict.
201	func (s *Store) ImportExact(t *Task) (ImportOutcome, error) {
202		candidate, err := prepareCandidate(t, false)
203		if err != nil {
204			return "", err
205		}
206		var outcome ImportOutcome
207		err = s.withMutationLock(func() error {
208			current, err := s.get(candidate.ID)
209			switch {
210			case err == nil && current.Revision() == candidate.Revision():
211				outcome = ImportIdentical
212				return nil
213			case err == nil:
214				outcome = ImportConflict
215				return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", candidate.ID, ErrConflict)
216			case !errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound):
217				return err
218			}
219			if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
220				return err
221			}
222			outcome = ImportCreated
223			return nil
224		})
225		return outcome, err
226	}

1134	func redactTextToken(token string) string {
1135		prefix := strings.TrimLeft(token, "([{<\"'")
1136		leading := token[:len(token)-len(prefix)]
1137		core := strings.TrimRight(prefix, ")]}>\"',;.")
1138		trailing := prefix[len(core):]
1139		if parsed, err := url.Parse(core); err == nil && parsed.Scheme != "" && parsed.Host != "" {
1140			parsed.User = nil
1141			parsed.RawQuery = ""
1142			parsed.ForceQuery = false
1143			parsed.Fragment = ""
1144			return leading + parsed.String() + trailing
1145		}
1146		colon := strings.IndexByte(core, ':')
1147		at := strings.LastIndexByte(core, '@')
1148		if at > 0 && colon > at {
1149			core = "[redacted]@" + core[at+1:]
1150			if query := strings.IndexAny(core, "?#"); query >= 0 {
1151				core = core[:query]
1152			}
1153		}
1154		return leading + core + trailing
1155	}

570	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
571	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
572	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
573	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
574
575	## Rich Git state
576
577	Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:
578
579	```text
580	⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
581	```
582
583	- `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
584	- `=` — conflicted paths
585	- `+` — staged paths
586	- `!` — unstaged paths
587	- `?` — untracked paths
588
589	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
590	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
591	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
592	staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
593
594	## Worktree ownership
595
596	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
597	to improvise:
598
599	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
600	|---|---|---|---|
601	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
```

43

45

func TestCreateNoClobberRollsBackPostPublicationFailures(t *testing.T) {

        name  string
        hooks func() createNoClobberHooks
    }{
        {
            name: "staging link cleanup",
            hooks: func() createNoClobberHooks {

                    return errors.New("injected staging cleanup failure")
                }}

        },
        {
            name: "directory sync",
            hooks: func() createNoClobberHooks {
                calls := 0
                return createNoClobberHooks{syncRoot: func(*os.Root) error {
                    calls++
                    if calls == 1 {
                        return errors.New("injected directory sync failure")
                    }
                    return nil
                }}
            },
        },

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.
## Phase 1 — Find candidates (10 angles, single pass)

Work through **10 angles** yourself, in sequence, in this same
context — do not spawn subagents. Each surfaces candidate findings with
`file`, `line`, a one-line `summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level

26	- `indeterminate`: probe 失敗、stale、unsupported 或 coverage 不完整；

32
