77	# Architecture
78
79	## Shared domains
80
81	- 新增 `internal/assessment`: schema/version、evidence provenance/freshness/completeness、gate/outcome/reason code、canonical fingerprint 與 outcome reduction；保持 presentation-neutral，讓 inventory/transfer/recovery/local-files 各自產生 evidence。
82	- 擴充 `internal/inventory/repo_context.go`: 保留每個 checkout 的 status error、runtime enumeration error、Git topology、catalog/note/artifact摘要、safe remotes、fleet observations 與 scoped gates；CLI/TUI 消費同一 aggregate，不能再以 `tui.RepoRow` 當 domain contract。
83	- 新增 `internal/lease`: 獨立於 task/transfer 的 cooperative operation authority；以 canonical Git identity + branch/repository scope 鎖定，保存 reservation/fence epoch，讓所有目前版本的 Git/worktree/artifact/local-file/task mutator 在任何 side effect 前共用同一 lock/guard。
84	- 新增 `internal/transfer`: portable task DTO、source/target plan、strict wire protocol、private object/sidecar staging、journal/store、phase transition、sidecar import、fencing/abort/return/reconciliation。
85	- 新增 `internal/localfiles`: project manifest resolution、ignored-file expansion、held-root snapshot、plan/conflict policy、bounded wire payload、target apply/rollback/immutable recovery copy/receipt；供 `fleet files` 與 `fleet transfer --with-local-files` 共用。
86	- 新增 `internal/recovery`: all-ref 與 Git-administrative manifest/artifact/receipt、reclaim assessment、restore drill/apply、eviction intent/reconciliation。
87	- 擴充 `internal/wt` provisioning service：以 checkout/OID + plan hash 為 key 的 private setup journal；content-addressed/idempotent steps 可重播，任意 command 逐步記錄 `pending/running/completed/indeterminate`。
88	- 新增 `internal/forge/weburl.go`: 從 live Git endpoint 或 exact forge match 保守產生 display-safe HTTPS URL；raw Git URL 與 public DTO 分離。

90
91	Reuse rather than duplicate:
92
93	- repository/checkout identity: `gitx.Discover`, `repo.Resolve/Discover`, `pathx.Canonical/Contains`;
94	- local Git: `gitx.StatusOf`, `Worktrees`, `WorktreeFor`, `RecoveryTopologyOf`, `InProgress`, `AnalyzeFinish`, `Run`;

101
102	## Stable machine and protocol identity
103
104	Create a private, durable machine UUID (independent state stores make this host-local) and expose it through a non-secret capability command. Add an optional expected machine ID to each `remotes.toml` host; any mutating transfer/files/restore operation requires it to be pinned and match, while list/status may merely warn. SSH host-key validation remains mandatory.
105
106	All new hidden commands use separate strict v1 envelopes, bounded stdin/stdout/stderr, `DisallowUnknownFields`, EOF checks, schema/capability negotiation, exact machine/repo/branch/OID binding and idempotency IDs. Add non-PTY `ssh -T` protocol mode and disable agent/X11/port forwarding; probe compatibility before sending note bodies or file content. Old/no-dev/incompatible targets fail before payload transmission.
107
108	# Repository context and safe remote links
109
110	Extend `dev repo context` rather than adding another status synonym. Human/JSON sections:
111
112	1. identity, selected checkout, generated time and source provenance;
113	2. canonical + linked worktrees, per-checkout Git/error/activity;
114	3. tasks, owner/fence, artifacts and every observed runtime backend;
115	4. every Git remote with role (current upstream/origin/upstream), sanitized endpoint identity, provider and safe plain HTTPS web URL when confidently derivable;
116	5. matching configured fleet hosts, path/branch/task/runtime summaries, live/stale/unreachable/incompatible state and snapshot age;
117	6. scoped readiness and stable blocker/remediation codes;
118	7. coverage/errors, including the explicit statement that fleet means configured hosts only.
119
120	`--json` is a new additive schema-v1 report; unknown/error values remain null/status entries, never zeroed or silently omitted. Raw credential-bearing Git URLs, note bodies, local-file hashes/content and secret query/fragment/userinfo never enter public output. `--refresh` may update caches, but cached forge/fleet facts are display-only and can never satisfy a mutating gate. TUI gets only the cheap local readiness summary and shared renderer; ordinary row rendering must not trigger SSH, forge refresh or all-object scans.
121
122	Web URL order: exact live forge record URL, strict Azure transform, literal recognized/configured GitHub/GitLab host transform, otherwise unavailable. Strip/reject userinfo, query, fragment, controls, ambiguous escaping and unsupported ports; SSH aliases do not become browser hosts. Render a plain URL (terminal may linkify it) rather than introducing OSC-8 width/security complexity.
123
124	# Portable local files
125
126	Add a new project-owned `[local_files]` section in `.dev-cli/config.toml` with explicit portable relative patterns, plus repeatable ad-hoc `--file`. Do not inherit existing `worktree.include` defaults: a repository may propose candidates, but only the explicit `fleet files` invocation or `transfer --with-local-files` authorizes off-machine export. Define a small portable glob grammar, expand it locally to sorted exact paths, and send no glob over the wire.
127
128	For every file, both hosts must prove it is untracked and ignored under their own Git configuration; tracked files travel through Git. Only bounded regular files are accepted—no directories, symlinks/reparse points, sockets, devices, FIFOs, `.git`, nested repositories or submodule boundaries. Initial hard ceilings: 128 files, 8 MiB/file, 32 MiB total, bounded path/component depth; host settings may lower but not raise compiled limits.
129
130	Plan states are `ready`, `current`, `blocked-conflict`, `blocked-ineligible`, `blocked-unsafe`, `missing`, `failed`. Source and target must be the same normalized repo identity, branch and exact OID. Apply preflights the complete set, reopens both roots through held handles, and journals the transfer:
131
132	- missing target: stage private temp (`0600`), stream/hash exact length, sync, then publish atomically without replacement;
133	- identical target: no-op/current;
134	- differing target: block unless `--replace`; replace requires the target digest observed in the displayed plan, private rollback copy, atomic swap, post-write rehash and rollback/reconciliation on failure;
135	- `--yes` never implies `--replace`; no deletion or last-writer-wins mode.
136
137	Target acceptance additionally retains each transferred file as an immutable, manifest-bound private recovery blob under the target transfer store; it materializes and rehashes that blob in staging. A source-deletion acknowledgement releases only ownership coordination: the blob, manifest and receipt reference remain immutable for the full recovery-receipt lifetime, including after A is gone and B’s working checkout is modified or evicted. They may be released only by a separately confirmed durable-receipt purge or after an independently restore-verified immutable backup supersedes them. B’s current-version replace/files/evict flows must honor this retention record. A must not treat a mutable working copy as deletion proof and must preserve its staged source if the target blob cannot be revalidated. Standalone `fleet files` may release the blob when source is retained, or use explicit `--retain-for-evict` to create recovery evidence.
138
139	Clamp final privacy to owner-only (`0600`, or `0700` only for explicitly executable source); do not copy ACL/xattr/owner/timestamps. Public human/JSON results contain path/size/state only—no content or hash. Native Windows targets remain capability-blocked before content is sent until the transport, ACL, reparse-point and atomicity contract is fully implemented and tested.
140
141	# Transfer protocol
142
143	## Target preparation
144
145	Separate branch/ref evidence from checkout evidence. For every selected task/current branch, A resolves `refs/heads/<branch>` directly through the shared Git common directory and captures exact OID/object format without requiring it to be checked out. Only branches with an existing checkout require conflict-free, operation-free, fully clean checkout evidence. COLD/unattached task refs must equal the freshly fetched/advertised remote tip before transfer and remain COLD on B with no checkout; this lets one repository transfer several serial branch-mode tasks without pretending they are all attached. Every published ref uses an explicit `<oid>:refs/heads/<branch>` ordinary push and the live remote tip must equal exactly that OID (not merely contain it).
146
147	Before A is fenced, B may only create a durable reservation, validate conflicts, and fetch expected objects into a private, non-discoverable transfer staging repository. Existing clones are reserved through the shared lease authority but no branch/worktree is moved; absent clones are staged under the private transfer directory rather than passed directly to `repo.Acquire`. Operation-owned incomplete staging can be verified and safely recreated/reused on retry, while any pre-existing or user-modified destination remains untouched.
148
149	After A’s fence is durable, B holds its repository/branch leases while publishing the target state. It matches all configured fetch/push identities and reuses exactly one clone; ambiguity blocks. If absent, it computes the final destination from B’s own path policy and materializes the verified staging clone without exposing a partial canonical checkout. It then creates/fast-forwards only the checkouts required by task state/mode. Ahead/diverged/dirty/live-agent targets block. Worktree tasks use B’s configured path and explicit expected ref; WARM worktree tasks get a checkout, COLD tasks do not. Branch/direct tasks may use canonical checkout only when unique and safe—never silently change mode. Acceptance may apply only deterministic, journaled portable files; it never runs `post_create`, dependency installers/copies, or other arbitrary provisioning inside the replayable distributed transaction. Transfer does not copy trust/credentials or open a runtime. Accepted HOT tasks become WARM; WARM/COLD stay as-is. After acceptance, B runs provisioning as a separate B-owned setup transaction through `dev resume` or `dev wt provision`; accepted existing WARM checkouts must enter this flow just like newly recreated worktrees. A private journal is bound to checkout identity/OID and provisioning-plan hash. Before each arbitrary command, fsync `running`; after success, fsync `completed`. A crash in `running` becomes `indeterminate` and is never auto-replayed—only explicit `--retry-indeterminate` or operator-attested `--mark-complete` can advance it. A journal cannot promise exactly-once for an external side effect, so automatic resume is limited to content-addressed/proven-idempotent steps. Context separately reports `transfer-complete` and `setup-pending/indeterminate/ready` so acceptance is never misrepresented as a fully provisioned environment.
150
151	## Sidecar rehydration
152
153	Portable task DTO contains stable ID, name/repo display, branch/base/mode/state/next/note/tags/timestamps and source provenance, but never A paths or runtime handles. On B, bind `RepoPath`/`WorktreePath` from B, clear runtime/agent hints, and import with exact-ID + revision conflict detection. Add task-store cross-process locking/CAS, but make the operation lease—not the task file—the authoritative fence so a selected branch with no task is still protected. Retrofit every current `dev` path that can mutate or expose a certified repository/branch/checkout/sidecar (`dev git`, lifecycle/TUI, adopt, worktree/repo/bootstrap/fleet setup, artifact finalization, local-file apply) to acquire/check the same lease before its first effect and hold it through Git/filesystem changes plus final CAS.
154
155	Catalog import preserves stable ID, metadata/tags/remote identity, adds B’s machine-specific location, and blocks pending move or conflicting ID/path/non-empty summaries. Note import preserves ID/repository ID/timestamps/tags/body; exact revision is idempotent, differing same-ID content blocks. Durable Markdown is written before disposable FTS rebuild; FTS failure is reported without rolling back durable notes. Note/file content travels only via bounded SSH stdin and is never echoed or cached.
156
157	## Idempotent no-two-writer handoff
158
159	Persist strict private source and target journals keyed by random transfer ID + manifest digest. Sequence:
160
161	1. **Plan**: live source/target assessment, no mutation.
162	2. **Publish**: create source intent; revalidate fingerprint; push/verify exact branch OIDs.
163	3. **Reserve/stage B**: durably reserve the target identities, validate sidecar/path conflicts and fetch objects into private staging only. Do not publish a working checkout, provision, write portable files, or expose target tasks.
164	4. **Fence A**: from an external coordinator, require caller/runtime outside all selected checkouts. Acquire all selected branch/repository operation leases in deterministic order, thereby drain already-started current-version mutators; while still holding them, revalidate Git/sidecar revisions, record B machine ID + fencing epoch durably, normalize HOT→WARM and then release the locks. Every later current-version source mutation sees the fence and fails. Keep every A byte.
165	5. **Accept/publish B**: under the same target reservations/leases, require the exact epoch/digest, revalidate staging and target state, publish/create the required checkouts, apply optional deterministic portable files, and import catalog/notes/tasks idempotently. Do not run arbitrary provisioning. Set B owner and write the acceptance receipt last; only then release the target reservation so ordinary B commands can see a writable accepted state and later run local `dev resume` provisioning.
166	6. **Complete/reconcile**: lost response is resolved through `fleet transfer status`; no distributed rollback. A remains present but fenced until explicit eviction or ownership return.
167
168	Same ID+digest resumes; same ID+different digest rejects. `abort` is terminal only before source fence and cleans solely journal-owned staging. After fence, `return` first acquires B’s leases, quiesces the exact manifest, writes a durable `returned` tombstone keyed by ID/digest/epoch that permanently rejects delayed prepare/accept replays, then lets A verify it and CAS-unfence the unchanged source while advancing the epoch. If B is unreachable or indeterminate, A remains safely fenced; generic `resume --force` cannot override a transfer fence. This permits a zero-writer window but never intentionally two cooperative writers. Document that raw Git and old binaries can bypass dev’s lease.
169
170	# Backup, reclaim, restore, and eviction
171
172	## Backup receipt
173
174	Add a fresh `gitx` recovery snapshot that inventories all local `refs/heads/*`, tags, notes, stash and other refs/OIDs; dirty/untracked/ignored/unreadable paths; Git operations/worktrees; LFS; submodules/nested repositories; shallow/partial clone, alternates and external/shared Git storage. Do not derive eviction cleanliness solely from `StatusOf`/`AnalyzeFinish`: enumerate index flags (`assume-unchanged`, `skip-worktree`, sparse-index state) without mutating the real index, then read/hash every materialized tracked path through held roots into a raw-byte manifest. The restore drill must independently materialize the receipt and compare exact working-tree bytes; hidden edits, unsafe sparse entries, clean/smudge-filter differences or missing external filter behavior must either enter an immutable recovery artifact or block/require a named discard. Repeat the flag/raw-byte proof during final eviction under the operation leases. Separately enumerate every private GitDir/common-dir administrative entry (config, hooks, info/exclude/attributes, rr-cache, reflogs and unknown files) through held roots. Classify only proven Git-managed/regenerable entries as reconstructible; preserve each remaining regular file in a private recovery artifact outside the eviction roots or require an item-scoped discard. Credential-bearing config is never uploaded to a Git remote. `RecoveryTopology` remains descriptive and is never promoted to proof.
175
176	`backup --push` authorizes one resolved effective push endpoint, not merely a remote name. Resolve Git rewrites plus every `pushurl`; if more than one effective destination exists, fail closed and require a dedicated single-endpoint recovery remote. Show the sanitized endpoint and exact ref mappings, bind both to the plan fingerprint, re-resolve immediately before push, refuse non-fast-forward/conflicting writes, and verify mappings at that same endpoint. Stash/custom refs require explicit receipt-scoped recovery mappings; unresolved reflog-only/unreachable objects remain blockers unless separately acknowledged for discard. Write an append-only private schema-v1 receipt only after verification; it records endpoint-set digest, exact ref/OID mappings, object/admin-artifact manifest digests, exclusions, source fingerprint and protocol versions—not credentials/raw URLs.
177
178	## Reclaim and restore proof
179
180	`reclaim` joins fresh evidence for every checkout/root, ref/object, Git-administrative entry, ignored file, immutable portable-file recovery blob, task/fence, catalog/note revision, artifact, all available runtime backends, caller containment, owned/shared bytes and configured fleet state. Each potentially unique item must map to an immutable recovery artifact/receipt, retained XDG state outside every deletion root, or a separately named item/category discard acknowledgement; a mutable live B working copy alone never qualifies. Stale/no-dev/unreachable evidence is indeterminate, never pass.
181
182	`restore --verify` restores into an isolated new staging directory, fetches every receipt mapping, verifies exact refs/OIDs and reachable object closure, restores and byte-verifies the classified Git-administrative artifact at the correct post-clone phase, and checks LFS/submodule proof where supported. It also materializes every portable-file recovery blob used by the eviction gate without exposing contents in output. Unsupported LFS/submodule/nested/external-object layouts block eviction rather than weakening the claim. Regular `restore --apply` uses the same plan/revalidation to reconstruct a real destination. A backup receipt without a successful matching restore drill cannot authorize eviction.
183
184	## Journaled actual eviction
185
186	`evict` never runs inside transfer. It defaults to the same report as reclaim and requires explicit `--apply`, exact target, matching receipt, current verified restore, and exact confirmation (`YES`; noninteractive `--yes` only with explicit target). Named acknowledgements such as `--discard-ignored`, `--discard-dirty`, `--discard-unreachable`, `--override-keep` are independent; `--yes` does not imply data loss and there is no generic `--force`.
187
188	Under recovery/task/catalog/Git operation leases, evict re-runs every check, closes only eligible runtime surfaces from outside them, waits and re-enumerates all backends, and freezes every reviewed checkout/Git root. Apply filesystem custody to **each** owned linked worktree before removal: write a per-root intent, use a Git-aware move into an unguessable same-parent private staging path so registration/common-dir remain valid, revoke traversal/new opens, completely enumerate file and directory descriptors into that staged inode tree, wait for existing handles to close, rerun that worktree’s index-flag/raw-byte proof, then remove the staged registration while preserving its branch/common-dir. A linked root that cannot be moved/probed/reproved blocks instead of falling back to ordinary `git worktree remove`.
189
190	After all linked roots are safely retired, apply the same sequence to the ordinary canonical clone: write/finalize its intent, atomically rename it into same-parent private staging, revoke new opens, drain all handles, and rerun the full raw-byte/Git-administrative manifest proof under custody before physical removal. If handle enumeration is unavailable/incomplete, any writer remains, or evidence changes at any root, preserve every affected staged root/intent and return indeterminate for later reconcile—never continue on an acknowledgement disguised as proof. External git dirs, alternates, cross-filesystem/shared-common-dir ambiguity, and platforms without the custody/open-handle contract block actual eviction.
191
192	Only after target bytes are absent: durably record source deletion completion on A, have B acknowledge it to release the transfer ownership hold (not the recovery blobs), remove A task records whose exact portable revisions were accepted by B (transfer receipt retains audit data), mark A catalog location `evicted` with recovery/restore reference, and clear the intent. Retain catalog metadata, quick-note copies, Git-administrative recovery artifacts, portable-file blobs, stats and transfer/recovery receipts outside clone roots for their receipt lifetimes; deleting those durable recovery assets is a future separately scoped, confirmed purge. Other ignored data blocks or needs its named discard acknowledgement.

 ## Rich Git state

 Every inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:

 ```text
 ⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
 ```

 - `⇡` / `⇣` / `⇕` — ahead, behind, diverged
 - `=` — conflicted paths
 - `+` — staged paths
 - `!` — unstaged paths
 - `?` — untracked paths

 `dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
 and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
 then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the
 staged and unstaged categories. JSON output exposes all counts separately.
+`dev status` also renders independent local `checkout`, `task`, and `worktree`
+readiness outcomes. It never contacts a forge/fleet host, and unavailable task,
+runtime, or worktree evidence remains indeterminate instead of looking clean.

 ## Worktree ownership

 Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
 to improvise:

 | Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
 | Harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | owned by that harness; no history-relocation guarantee |
 | `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |

 **If code, history, or plans must remain reviewable—or you may return tomorrow—
 use `dev`.**

 `dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
 on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
 herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
 its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.

 `dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
 another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
 copy of the tree.

 ### Provisioning

 A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
 Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
 files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
 command detected from the lockfiles. Included files must remain the same
 regular file through open; source swaps and symlinked destination parents are
 refused, existing destinations are reported as skipped, and contents are never
 logged:

 ```toml
 [worktree]
 include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
 link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
 post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
+
+# Separate opt-in export policy for dev fleet files; worktree.include is never
+# inherited for off-machine transfer.
+[local_files]
+include = [".env", ".mcp/**"]
 ```

+`[local_files]` may be committed in `.dev-cli/config.toml`, but it only proposes
+portable patterns. Nothing leaves the host until an explicit `dev fleet files`
+invocation selects one target; every pattern expands locally to sorted exact
+paths before the protocol begins.
+
 `.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal include. Add that exact path
 only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude launcher and verify it
 arrives. `claude-copilot-once` preserves an existing Copilot pin and creates/
 removes only one it added when absent; its proxy must already run.
 `codex-copilot-once` injects backend via CLI and may auto-start its proxy path,
 so neither wrapper needs the copied file.

 **Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
 copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
 That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:

 ```toml
 [worktree]
 strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip

 [worktree.strategies]
 node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
 ```

 Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
 absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
 reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.

 `dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
 which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
 command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds
 `<repo>/.dev-cli/config.toml` from it, so
 a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.

 ```
 $ dev wt plan
 PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
 node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
 python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed

    ACTION    WHAT          WHY
 ✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
 ✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
 ✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
 ```

 ## Other things it does

 ```bash
 dev repo list --sizes          # repos, remote topology and owned logical size
 dev repo list --no-remote      # find local Git with no configured backup remote
 dev repo context api           # agent-ready paths, Git, WT, runtime and tasks
 dev repo new                   # interactive local/published repository bootstrap
 dev repo setup . --preset agent-ready   # safely initialize an existing repo
 dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # expand forge shorthand, then clone with Git
 dev repo clone https://dev.azure.com/acme/Platform/_git/api -c Work
 dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
 dev fleet list                 # Git/task/runtime state from every configured machine
+dev fleet machine-id lab       # inspect/compare the target's stable machine pin
 dev fleet sync api --push      # push, then safely fast-forward clean remote checkouts
+dev fleet files api --to lab   # report-only plan for explicit ignored local files

 dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
 dev tries archive redis-streams    # reversible local archive; does not delete
 dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project

 dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
 dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks

 dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
 dev summary                    # current machine-wide project snapshot
 dev journal                    # today's commits plus current task/WIP context
 dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
 dev help wt                    # same page, reached by command name
 ```

 ### Repository quick notes

 Quick thoughts live beside repos in dev state, not inside each checkout:

 ```bash
 dev note add "try event subscription" --repo api --tag idea
 dev note list api
 dev note search "event subscription"
 dev note edit <id-or-prefix>
 dev note delete <id-or-prefix>
 ```

 An ID prefix must be unique and at least eight characters.

 In TASKS/REPOS, `n` quick-adds and `N` opens a browse/search/edit/delete overlay.
@@ -949,74 +972,105 @@ user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
 ## Multiple machines

 Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
 the handoff boundary:

 ```bash
 dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
 dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
 ```

 `dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
 without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
 to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.

 Configure SSH machines separately from host-local paths:

 ```toml
 # $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml
 schema_version = 1

 [defaults]
 connect_timeout = "15s"
 command_timeout = "5m"
 cache_ttl = "15m"
 max_parallel = 4
 dev_path = "auto"

 [[hosts]]
 name = "jingle"
 ssh_alias = "jingle-235"
+# After `dev fleet machine-id jingle` and independent verification:
+machine_id = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
 ```

+The UUID pin is optional for read-only inventory and diagnostics, but mandatory
+for `fleet files --apply`. `dev fleet machine-id <host>` is itself read-only: it
+shows the observed UUID, the configured value, and `unpinned`, `match`, or
+`mismatch`; it never edits `remotes.toml`.
+
 `dev fleet list` runs each machine's own `dev`, so its XDG config and paths stay
 host-local. Missing `dev` installations are reported as `no-dev`; unreachable
 hosts can fall back to the last private XDG snapshot. The FLEET TUI view exposes
 the same inventory and Enter opens a selected path through remote Herdr when its
 server is active, otherwise through `ssh -t` and a login shell.

 `dev fleet sync <repo> --push` publishes the clean source branch, then fetches
 matching clones by normalized Git remote identity. Only a clean checkout of the
 same branch that is strictly behind is fast-forwarded. Dirty, ahead, divergent,
 ambiguous and unreachable targets remain untouched and make the command fail;
 hosts without `dev` or without that repository are explicitly ignored.

+`dev fleet files [repo-or-path] --to <host>` is a separate, one-shot channel for
+explicit ignored local files:
+
+```bash
+dev fleet files api --to jingle                    # plan only
+dev fleet files api --to jingle --apply --yes      # create absent files
+dev fleet files api --to jingle --replace --apply  # separately authorize conflicts
+```
+
+The source and target must already be the same fetch identity, attached branch,
+and exact commit. Both Git configurations must classify every selected path as
+untracked and ignored. Only bounded regular files are accepted (128 files,
+8 MiB each, 32 MiB total at most); directories, links, special files, nested
+repositories, `.git`, and submodule boundaries fail closed. The target reopens
+held roots, journals before staging payloads, publishes owner-only files
+atomically, and rolls back changed files on failure. It deliberately leaves
+unprovably-owned empty parent directories rather than risk deleting another
+process's replacement. Native Windows payload apply remains disabled.
+
+This is **not** repository/task ownership transfer, backup, restore, or clone
+eviction. It does not clone a missing target, switch branches, run provisioning,
+synchronize catalog/notes, delete source files, watch for changes, or merge in
+both directions.
+
 ## The agent skill

 `dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
 same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
 tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
 reading none.

 ```bash
 dev skill list       # merged project + global inventory
 dev skill list --check --json
 dev skill add        # interactive wizard for daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
 dev skill update project-knowledge-harness --global --yes
 dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
 dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
 dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
 dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
 ```

 `dev skill add [package]` is only a shortcut into the upstream interactive
 wizard. It never selects all skills or agents. Listing uses an already
 available/cached `skills` CLI and never downloads it; add/update are explicit
 actions and may access the network. Project scope resolves to the current Git
 checkout root, so invoking the command from a nested directory gives the same
 inventory.

 The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
 SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
 worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
 responsibility.

 # Remote fleet

 See repository, task and runtime state from several machines without sharing
 their filesystem paths or copying their dev configuration.

 ## Configure hosts

 ```bash
 dev fleet config init
 dev fleet config edit
 dev fleet status
+dev fleet machine-id lab
 ```

 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml` follows the same connection model as an
 ordinary OpenSSH invocation. Prefer `ssh_alias`; explicit
 `hostname`/`user`/`port`/`identity_file` fields are available when needed.
 Password fallback supports `prompt`, `plain` and `bitwarden`, but key or agent
-authentication is always attempted first.
+authentication is always attempted first. Read-only commands tolerate an
+unpinned host. Before a mutating file transfer, run `dev fleet machine-id
+<host>`, verify the UUID independently, and add it as that host's `machine_id`;
+the command reports but never writes the pin.

 ## Inspect and open

 ```bash
 dev fleet list
 dev fleet list --host lab --repo api
 dev fleet list --cached
 dev fleet list --json
 dev fleet open lab api
 ```

 Every host runs its own `dev`, so its `config.toml`, scan roots, exact repo
 paths, task registry and runtime remain authoritative. A missing remote `dev`
 is `no-dev`, not a fleet-wide failure. Unreachable hosts reuse the last
 successful private XDG snapshot when available.

 Opening a remote repo prefers native Herdr remoting when an active remote Herdr
 server is visible. It otherwise opens `ssh -t`, validates the repository path
 through remote dev, changes directory and starts a login shell.

 ## Safely propagate a branch

 ```bash
 dev fleet sync api --push
 dev fleet sync api                 # HEAD must already equal fetched upstream
 dev fleet sync api --host lab
 ```

 The source must be clean and attached. Targets are matched by normalized Git
 remote identity, not directory name. Each target fetches first; only a clean
 checkout of the same branch that is strictly behind is advanced with
 `merge --ff-only`. Different branches are not switched. Dirty, ahead,
 divergent, ambiguous and unreachable targets remain untouched and make sync
 return non-zero. Hosts without dev or without that repository are ignored and
 reported explicitly.

 There is no automatic rebase, force push, background hook or all-repository
 pull. Resolve divergent work interactively on the machine that owns it.
+
+## Transfer explicit ignored files
+
+```bash
+dev fleet files api --to lab
+dev fleet files api --to lab --apply --yes
+dev fleet files api --to lab --replace --apply
+```
+
+The report-only default expands `[local_files].include` plus repeatable `--file`
+patterns into exact source paths. Source and target must already match by fetch
+identity, attached branch and commit. Both sides must prove each path untracked
+and ignored; only bounded regular files pass. `--replace` separately authorizes
+a target whose bytes differ, and `--yes` never implies replacement.
+
+Apply requires a matching `machine_id` pin, uses a bounded non-PTY protocol,
+keeps file content and hashes out of public output/cache, writes owner-only
+files through held roots, and journals rollback before publication. It does not
+clone, switch branches, transfer tasks/catalog/notes, provision dependencies,
+delete source files, or evict a repository. Native Windows payloads are blocked.

 Every dev inventory surface uses the same compact, starship-like status:

 ```text
 ⇕⇡3⇣2 =1 +4 !2 ?3
 ```

 | Symbol | Meaning |
 |---|---|
 | `⇡N` | N commits ahead of upstream |
 | `⇣N` | N commits behind upstream |
 | `⇕⇡A⇣B` | diverged: A ahead and B behind |
 | `=N` | conflicted paths |
 | `+N` | staged paths |
 | `!N` | unstaged paths |
 | `?N` | untracked paths |
 | `clean` | published, no divergence or file changes |
 | `local` | clean, but no upstream configured |

 `dev status` and the TUI detail pane add two lines:

 ```text
 changes    4 changed paths (+1 staged, !2 unstaged, ?1 untracked)
 types      1 modified, 1 deleted, 1 renamed/copied
 ```

 `changed paths` is a unique-path total. A path staged and then modified again
 is one changed path, but correctly appears in both staged and unstaged
 categories — those category counts are not intended to be added together.

+`dev status` also adds one local-only readiness line with independent checkout,
+task, and worktree outcomes. It reuses the same collected facts as repository
+context, performs no forge/fleet network probe, and reports unavailable evidence
+as `indeterminate` rather than clean.
+
 Machine-readable output keeps every count separate:

 ```bash
 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | {
   repo, branch, changed, staged, unstaged, untracked, conflicted,
   added, modified, deleted, renamed, ahead, behind
 }'
 ```


 ## Latest repository activity

 The REPOS `LATEST` column is the maximum of:

 1. newest mtime among dirty tracked/untracked files that still exist;
 2. latest commit time;
 3. latest update to a task in that repo.

 This prevents a long uncommitted debugging session from looking like a repo
 that has not been touched in weeks. Deleted-file mtimes no longer exist, so
 those fall back to commit/task time.

291				}
292				file.content = payloads[spec.Path]
293			default:
294				return nil, errors.New("invalid local-files target action")
295			}
296			if int64(len(file.content)) != spec.Size || digestBytes(file.content) != spec.SHA256 {
297				return nil, fmt.Errorf("content for %q no longer matches the plan", spec.Path)
298			}
299			files[index] = file
300		}
301		return files, nil
302	}
303
304	func (s *Service) failAndRollback(ctx context.Context, checkout targetCheckout, envelope ApplyEnvelope, store *operationStore, value *journal, cause error) error {
305		value.Phase = phaseReconcile
306		_ = store.writeJournal(*value)
307		if err := s.rollback(ctx, checkout, envelope, store, value); err != nil {
308			value.Phase = phaseReconcile
309			_ = store.writeJournal(*value)
310			return errors.New("local-files apply failed and requires reconciliation")
311		}
312		value.Phase = phaseRolledBack
313		for index := range value.Files {
314			if value.Files[index].Action != actionCurrent {
315				value.Files[index].State = StateRolledBack
316				value.Files[index].Published = false
317			}
318		}
319		if err := store.writeJournal(*value); err != nil {
320			return errors.New("local-files apply rolled back but journal finalization failed")
321		}
322		if err := store.cleanupPayloads(false); err != nil {
323			return errors.New("local-files apply rolled back but private staging cleanup is incomplete")
324		}
325		return fmt.Errorf("local-files apply failed and was rolled back: %w", cause)
326	}
327
328	func (s *Service) rollback(ctx context.Context, checkout targetCheckout, envelope ApplyEnvelope, store *operationStore, value *journal) error {
329		for index := len(value.Files) - 1; index >= 0; index-- {
330			entry := &value.Files[index]
331			if entry.Action == actionCurrent {
332				continue
333			}
334			spec := envelope.Request.Files[index]
335			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path); err != nil {
336				return err
337			}
338			observed, err := observePath(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path, envelope.Request.SafeLimits(), true)
339			if err != nil {
340				return err
341			}
342			switch entry.Action {
343			case actionCreate:
344				if !entry.Published {
345					if observed.exists {
346						return errors.New("unproven target appeared before create rollback")
347					}
348					continue
349				}
350				if !observed.exists {
351					continue
352				}
353				if observed.digest != spec.SHA256 || observedFileMode(observed) != spec.Mode {
354					return errors.New("created target changed before rollback")
355				}
356				parent, err := openHeldParent(checkout.root, spec.Path, false)
357				if err != nil {
358					return err
359				}
360				err = parent.parent.Remove(pathBase(spec.Path))
361				err = errors.Join(err, syncHeldRoot(parent.parent), parent.close())
362				if err != nil {
363					return err
364				}
365			case actionReplace:
366				oldState := observed.exists && observed.digest == entry.OldSHA256 && observedFileMode(observed) == entry.OldMode
367				if !entry.Published {
368					if oldState {
369						continue
370					}
371					return errors.New("replacement publication cannot be proven during rollback")
372				}
373				if oldState {
374					continue
375				}
376				if !observed.exists || observed.digest != spec.SHA256 || observedFileMode(observed) != spec.Mode {
377					return errors.New("replacement target changed before rollback")
378				}
379				oldContent, err := store.readBlob(index, true, envelope.Request.SafeLimits().MaxFileBytes)
380				if err != nil || digestBytes(oldContent) != entry.OldSHA256 {
381					return errors.New("replacement rollback blob is unavailable")
382				}
383				parent, err := openHeldParent(checkout.root, spec.Path, false)
384				if err != nil {
385					return err
386				}
387				current, err := parent.parent.Lstat(pathBase(spec.Path))
388				oldMode, modeErr := strconv.ParseUint(entry.OldMode, 8, 12)
389				err = errors.Join(err, modeErr)
390				if err == nil {
391					_, err = safefile.AtomicReplace(ctx, parent.parent, pathBase(spec.Path), current, oldContent, fs.FileMode(oldMode))
392				}
393				err = errors.Join(err, parent.close())
394				if err != nil {
395					return err
396				}
397			}
398		}
399		// Empty parent directories are intentionally retained. A path alone cannot
400		// prove that a directory still has the identity created by this operation;
401		// deleting it after a crash could remove another process's replacement.
402		return verifyRollback(ctx, checkout.root, envelope, *value)
403	}
404
405	func verifyRollback(ctx context.Context, checkout string, envelope ApplyEnvelope, value journal) error {
406		for index, entry := range value.Files {
407			spec := envelope.Request.Files[index]
408			observed, err := observePath(ctx, checkout, spec.Path, envelope.Request.SafeLimits(), true)
409			if err != nil {
410				return err
411			}
412			switch entry.Action {
413			case actionCurrent:
414				if !observed.exists || observed.digest != spec.SHA256 || fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm()) != envelope.Plan.Files[index].TargetMode {
415					return errors.New("current target changed during rollback")
416				}
417			case actionCreate:
418				if observed.exists {
419					return errors.New("created target remains after rollback")
420				}
421			case actionReplace:
422				if !observed.exists || observed.digest != entry.OldSHA256 || fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm()) != entry.OldMode {
423					return errors.New("replacement target was not restored")
424				}
425			}
426		}
427		return nil
428	}
429
430	func (s *Service) verifyCompleted(ctx context.Context, checkout targetCheckout, envelope ApplyEnvelope, store *operationStore, value journal) (ApplyResponse, error) {
431		if err := verifyAllCurrent(ctx, checkout.root, envelope.Request.Files, envelope.Request.SafeLimits()); err != nil {
432			return ApplyResponse{}, errors.New("completed local-files journal no longer matches the checkout")
433		}
434		if value.RetainForEvict {
435			for index, spec := range envelope.Request.Files {
436				content, err := store.readBlob(index, false, envelope.Request.SafeLimits().MaxFileBytes)
437				if err != nil || int64(len(content)) != spec.Size || digestBytes(content) != spec.SHA256 {
438					return ApplyResponse{}, errors.New("retained local-files recovery blob is unavailable")
439				}
440			}
441		} else if err := store.cleanupPayloads(false); err != nil {
442			return ApplyResponse{}, errors.New("completed local-files staging cleanup is incomplete")
443		}
444		return responseFromJournal(value), nil
445	}
446
447	func observedFileMode(observed observation) string {
448		if !observed.exists || observed.info == nil {
449			return ""
450		}
451		return fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm())
452	}
453
454	func verifyAllCurrent(ctx context.Context, checkout string, specs []FileSpec, limits safefile.Limits) error {
455		for _, spec := range specs {
456			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, checkout, spec.Path); err != nil {
457				return err
458			}
459			observed, err := observePath(ctx, checkout, spec.Path, limits, true)
460			if err != nil || !observed.exists || observed.digest != spec.SHA256 || observed.info.Size() != spec.Size {
461				return fmt.Errorf("target path %q failed post-write verification", spec.Path)
462			}
463			if fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm()) != spec.Mode {
464				return fmt.Errorf("target path %q permissions do not match the manifest", spec.Path)
465			}
466		}
467		return nil
468	}
469
470	func responseFromJournal(value journal) ApplyResponse {
471		files := make([]PublicFile, len(value.Files))
472		for index, entry := range value.Files {
473			files[index] = PublicFile{Path: entry.Path, Size: entry.Size, Mode: entry.Mode, State: entry.State}
474		}
475		return ApplyResponse{
476			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
477			RequestID: value.RequestID, PlanDigest: value.PlanDigest, Files: files,
478		}
479	}
480
481	func (s *Service) fault(point, path string) error {
482		if s.Fault == nil {
483			return nil
484		}
485		return s.Fault(point, path)
486	}
487
488	type heldParent struct {
489		checkout string
490		rootInfo fs.FileInfo
491		root     *os.Root
492		parent   *os.Root
493		roots    []*os.Root
494		edges    []heldEdge
495	}
496
497	type heldEdge struct {
498		parent *os.Root
499		name   string
500		info   fs.FileInfo
501	}
502
503	func openHeldParent(checkout, slashPath string, create bool) (*heldParent, error) {
504		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableSlashPath(slashPath, safefile.DefaultLimits().PathLimits()); err != nil {
505			return nil, err
506		}
507		root, rootInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(checkout)
508		if err != nil {
509			return nil, err
510		}
511		held := &heldParent{checkout: checkout, rootInfo: rootInfo, root: root, parent: root, roots: []*os.Root{root}}
512		components := strings.Split(slashPath, "/")
513		prefix := make([]string, 0, len(components)-1)
514		for _, component := range components[:len(components)-1] {
515			prefix = append(prefix, component)
516			child, info, err := safefile.OpenChildRoot(held.parent, component)
517			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) && create {
518				if err := held.parent.Mkdir(component, 0o700); err != nil {
519					_ = held.close()
520					return nil, err
521				}
522				child, info, err = safefile.OpenChildRoot(held.parent, component)
523			}
524			if err != nil {
525				_ = held.close()
526				return nil, err
527			}
528			if _, err := child.Lstat(".git"); err == nil {
529				_ = child.Close()
530				_ = held.close()
531				return nil, ErrUnsafe
532			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
533				_ = child.Close()
534				_ = held.close()
535				return nil, err
536			}
537			held.edges = append(held.edges, heldEdge{parent: held.parent, name: component, info: info})
538			held.roots = append(held.roots, child)
539			held.parent = child
540		}
541		return held, nil
542	}
543
544	func (h *heldParent) close() error {
545		if h == nil {
546			return nil
547		}
548		var result error
549		for index := len(h.edges) - 1; index >= 0; index-- {
550			result = errors.Join(result, safefile.VerifyChildRoot(h.edges[index].parent, h.edges[index].name, h.edges[index].info))
551		}
552		result = errors.Join(result, safefile.VerifyRoot(h.checkout, h.rootInfo))
553		for index := len(h.roots) - 1; index >= 0; index-- {
554			result = errors.Join(result, h.roots[index].Close())
555		}
556		h.roots = nil
557		return result
558	}
559
560	func syncHeldRoot(root *os.Root) error {
561		file, err := root.Open(".")
562		if err != nil {
563			return err
564		}
565		defer file.Close()
566		return file.Sync()
567	}
568
569	func pathBase(slashPath string) string {
570		parts := strings.Split(slashPath, "/")
571		return parts[len(parts)-1]
572	}

38	func PrepareSource(ctx context.Context, options SourceOptions) (*Source, Report, error) {

59		request := PlanRequest{
60			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
61			RequestID: requestID, Binding: options.Binding, Limits: limitsToWire(options.Limits),
62			Replace: options.Replace,
63		}
64		report := Report{SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion}
65		blocked := false
66		for _, path := range paths {
67			public := PublicFile{Path: path, Mode: "0600", State: StateFailed}
68			observed, observeErr := observePath(ctx, options.Checkout, path, options.Limits, true)
69			if observeErr != nil {
70				public.State = stateForError(observeErr)
71				report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
72				blocked = true
73				continue
74			}
75			if !observed.exists {
76				public.State = StateMissing
77				report.Files = append(report.Files, public)
78				blocked = true
79				continue
80			}
81			public.Size = observed.info.Size()
82			if observed.info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 != 0 {
83				public.Mode = "0700"
84			}
85			if eligibilityErr := proveGitEligibility(ctx, options.Checkout, path); eligibilityErr != nil {
86				public.State = stateForError(eligibilityErr)

109	// BuildEnvelope performs the source-side apply revalidation and includes bytes
110	// only for target actions that create or explicitly replace a file.
111	func (s *Source) BuildEnvelope(ctx context.Context, plan PlanResponse, retainForEvict bool) (ApplyEnvelope, error) {
112		if s == nil {
113			return ApplyEnvelope{}, errors.New("build local-files envelope from nil source")
114		}
115		if err := verifySourceBinding(ctx, s.checkout, s.request.Binding); err != nil {
116			return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source checkout changed after planning: %w", err)
117		}
118		if err := plan.Validate(s.request); err != nil {
119			return ApplyEnvelope{}, err
120		}
121		envelope := ApplyEnvelope{
122			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
123			Request: s.request, Plan: plan, RetainForEvict: retainForEvict,
124		}
125		for index, planned := range plan.Files {
126			if planned.Action == actionCurrent {
127				continue
128			}
129			if planned.Action != actionCreate && planned.Action != actionReplace {
130				return ApplyEnvelope{}, ErrPlanBlocked
131			}
132			spec := s.request.Files[index]
133			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, s.checkout, spec.Path); err != nil {
134				return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source path %q changed eligibility: %w", spec.Path, ErrDrift)
135			}
136			observed, err := observePath(ctx, s.checkout, spec.Path, s.request.SafeLimits(), true)
137			if err != nil || !observed.exists || observed.info.Size() != spec.Size || observed.digest != spec.SHA256 ||
138				(observed.info.Mode().Perm()&0o111 != 0) != spec.executable() {
139				return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source path %q changed after planning: %w", spec.Path, ErrDrift)
140			}
141			envelope.Payloads = append(envelope.Payloads, Payload{
142				Path: spec.Path, Content: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(observed.data),
143			})
144		}
145		if err := verifySourceBinding(ctx, s.checkout, s.request.Binding); err != nil {
146			return ApplyEnvelope{}, fmt.Errorf("source checkout changed while building payload: %w", err)
147		}
148		if err := envelope.Validate(); err != nil {
149			return ApplyEnvelope{}, err
150		}
151		return envelope, nil
152	}

154	func (e ApplyEnvelope) Validate() error {
155		if e.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion || e.ProtocolVersion != fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion {
156			return errors.New("unsupported local-files apply protocol")
157		}
158		if err := e.Request.Validate(); err != nil {
159			return err
160		}
161		if err := e.Plan.Validate(e.Request); err != nil {
162			return err
163		}
164		expected := map[string]FileSpec{}
165		for index, planned := range e.Plan.Files {
166			if planned.Action == actionCreate || planned.Action == actionReplace {
167				expected[e.Request.Files[index].Path] = e.Request.Files[index]
168			}
169		}
170		if len(e.Payloads) != len(expected) {
171			return errors.New("apply payload count does not match target actions")
172		}
173		seen := map[string]bool{}
174		var total int64
175		for index, payload := range e.Payloads {
176			if index > 0 && e.Payloads[index-1].Path >= payload.Path {
177				return errors.New("apply payload paths must be unique and sorted")
178			}
179			spec, ok := expected[payload.Path]
180			if !ok || seen[payload.Path] {
181				return fmt.Errorf("unexpected apply payload for %q", payload.Path)
182			}
183			seen[payload.Path] = true
184			decoded, err := base64.StdEncoding.Strict().DecodeString(payload.Content)
185			if err != nil || base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(decoded) != payload.Content {
186				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q is not canonical base64", payload.Path)
187			}
188			if int64(len(decoded)) != spec.Size || digestBytes(decoded) != spec.SHA256 {
189				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q does not match its manifest", payload.Path)
190			}
191			if int64(len(decoded)) > e.Request.SafeLimits().MaxFileBytes || int64(len(decoded)) > e.Request.SafeLimits().MaxTotalBytes-total {
192				return fmt.Errorf("payload for %q exceeds negotiated limits", payload.Path)
193			}
194			total += int64(len(decoded))
195		}
196		return nil
197	}

199	func stateForError(err error) State {
200		switch {
201		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnsafe), errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrUnsafeType), errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrNotPortable), errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrPathCollision):
202			return StateBlockedUnsafe
203		case errors.Is(err, ErrIneligible):
204			return StateBlockedIneligible
205		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
206			return StateMissing
207		default:
208			return StateFailed
209		}
210	}

212	func limitsToWire(limits safefile.Limits) fleet.FileLimits {
213		return fleet.FileLimits{
214			MaxFiles: limits.MaxFiles, MaxFileBytes: limits.MaxFileBytes,
215			MaxTotalBytes: limits.MaxTotalBytes, MaxPathBytes: limits.MaxPathBytes,
216			MaxComponentBytes: limits.MaxComponentBytes, MaxPathDepth: limits.MaxPathDepth,
217		}
218	}

220	// NegotiateLimits takes the lower value for every policy field and validates
221	// both sides against this binary's compiled ceilings.
222	func NegotiateLimits(local safefile.Limits, remote fleet.FileLimits) (safefile.Limits, error) {
223		if err := local.Validate(); err != nil {
224			return safefile.Limits{}, err
225		}
226		remoteLimits := safefile.Limits{
227			MaxFiles: remote.MaxFiles, MaxFileBytes: remote.MaxFileBytes,
228			MaxTotalBytes: remote.MaxTotalBytes, MaxPathBytes: remote.MaxPathBytes,
229			MaxComponentBytes: remote.MaxComponentBytes, MaxPathDepth: remote.MaxPathDepth,
230		}
231		if err := remoteLimits.Validate(); err != nil {
232			return safefile.Limits{}, err
233		}
234		result := safefile.Limits{
235			MaxFiles:          min(local.MaxFiles, remoteLimits.MaxFiles),
236			MaxFileBytes:      min(local.MaxFileBytes, remoteLimits.MaxFileBytes),
237			MaxTotalBytes:     min(local.MaxTotalBytes, remoteLimits.MaxTotalBytes),
238			MaxPathBytes:      min(local.MaxPathBytes, remoteLimits.MaxPathBytes),
239			MaxComponentBytes: min(local.MaxComponentBytes, remoteLimits.MaxComponentBytes),
240			MaxPathDepth:      min(local.MaxPathDepth, remoteLimits.MaxPathDepth),
241		}
242		return result, result.Validate()
243	}

13	// FetchRemoteIdentity resolves the one normalized fetch identity used to bind a
14	// portable-file operation. Push URLs are intentionally excluded because they
15	// may name a publication mirror unrelated to the fetched repository.
16	func FetchRemoteIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout, branch string) (string, error) {
17		var preferred []string
18		if remote, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "config", "--get", "branch."+branch+".remote"); err == nil && remote != "" && remote != "." {
19			preferred = append(preferred, remote)
20		}
21		preferred = append(preferred, "origin")
22		remotes, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote")
23		if err != nil {
24			return "", err
25		}
26		preferred = append(preferred, strings.Fields(remotes)...)
27		seenRemote := map[string]bool{}
28		for _, remote := range preferred {
29			if remote == "" || seenRemote[remote] {
30				continue
31			}
32			seenRemote[remote] = true
33			urls, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote", "get-url", "--all", remote)
34			if err != nil {
35				continue
36			}
37			identities := map[string]struct{}{}
38			for _, raw := range strings.Split(urls, "\n") {
39				if identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw); identity != "" {
40					identities[identity] = struct{}{}
41				}
42			}
43			if len(identities) == 1 {
44				for identity := range identities {
45					return identity, nil
46				}
47			}
48		}
49		return "", errors.New("checkout has no unambiguous normalized fetch remote identity")
50	}
51
52	func verifySourceBinding(ctx context.Context, checkout string, binding Binding) error {
53		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
54		if err != nil {
55			return err
56		}
57		if status.Detached || status.Branch != binding.Branch {
58			return fmt.Errorf("source branch changed from %s: %w", binding.Branch, ErrDrift)
59		}
60		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}")
61		if err != nil {
62			return err
63		}
64		if head != binding.HeadOID {
65			return fmt.Errorf("source HEAD changed from %s: %w", binding.HeadOID, ErrDrift)
66		}
67		identity, err := FetchRemoteIdentity(ctx, checkout, binding.Branch)
68		if err != nil {
69			return err
70		}
71		if identity != binding.RemoteIdentity {
72			return fmt.Errorf("source fetch identity changed: %w", ErrDrift)
73		}
74		return nil
75	}

14	)
15
16	const maxWalkEntries = 200_000
17
18	var dependencyComponents = map[string]struct{}{
19		"node_modules": {}, ".venv": {}, "venv": {}, "vendor": {},
20		"__pycache__": {}, ".tox": {}, "target": {}, ".terraform": {},
21		"dist": {}, "build": {}, ".next": {},

24	// Expand resolves validated project and --file patterns locally into a sorted,
25	// duplicate-free list of exact slash paths. It never follows links or descends
26	// into Git metadata, nested repositories, submodules, or dependency trees.
27	func Expand(root string, patterns []Pattern, limits safefile.Limits) ([]string, error) {
28		if err := limits.Validate(); err != nil {
29			return nil, err
30		}
31		if len(patterns) == 0 {
32			return nil, errors.New("no local-file patterns were configured or passed with --file")
33		}
34		for _, pattern := range patterns {
35			if err := projectconfig.ValidateLocalFilePattern(pattern.Value); err != nil {
36				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s: %w", patternSource(pattern), err)
37			}
38			for _, component := range strings.Split(pattern.Value, "/") {
39				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
40					return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s enters dependency directory %q", patternSource(pattern), component)
41				}
42			}
43		}
44		rootInfo, err := os.Lstat(root)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, fmt.Errorf("inspect source checkout: %w", err)
47		}
48		if !rootInfo.IsDir() || rootInfo.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
49			return nil, errors.New("source checkout is not a held regular directory")
50		}
51
52		matches := map[string]struct{}{}
53		matchedPatterns := make([]bool, len(patterns))
54		visited := 0
55		err = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(filename string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
56			if walkErr != nil {
57				return walkErr
58			}
59			if filename == root {
60				return nil
61			}
62			visited++
63			if visited > maxWalkEntries {
64				return fmt.Errorf("source checkout exceeds %d entries while expanding local-file patterns", maxWalkEntries)
65			}
66			relative, err := filepath.Rel(root, filename)
67			if err != nil {
68				return err
69			}
70			slash := filepath.ToSlash(relative)
71			components := strings.Split(slash, "/")
72			base := strings.ToLower(components[len(components)-1])
73			if entry.IsDir() {
74				if base == ".git" {
75					return filepath.SkipDir
76				}
77				if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[base]; blocked {
78					for _, pattern := range patterns {
79						if matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
80							return fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern enters dependency directory %q", slash)
81						}
82					}
83					return filepath.SkipDir
84				}
85				nested, err := nestedRepositoryBoundary(filename)
86				if err != nil {
87					return fmt.Errorf("inspect nested repository boundary %s: %w", slash, err)
88				}
89				if nested {
90					return filepath.SkipDir
91				}
92			}
93			matched := false
94			for index, pattern := range patterns {
95				if !entry.IsDir() && matchPattern(pattern.Value, slash) {
96					matchedPatterns[index] = true
97					matched = true
98				}
99			}
100			if matched {
101				matches[slash] = struct{}{}
102			}
103			if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 && entry.IsDir() {
104				return filepath.SkipDir
105			}
106			return nil
107		})
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, err
110		}
111		for index, matched := range matchedPatterns {
112			if !matched {
113				return nil, fmt.Errorf("local-file pattern from %s matched no source path", patternSource(patterns[index]))
114			}
115		}
116		paths := make([]string, 0, len(matches))
117		for path := range matches {
118			paths = append(paths, path)
119		}
120		sort.Strings(paths)
121		if len(paths) > limits.MaxFiles {
122			return nil, fmt.Errorf("patterns expanded to %d paths; maximum is %d", len(paths), limits.MaxFiles)
123		}
124		return paths, nil
125	}
126
127	func nestedRepositoryBoundary(path string) (bool, error) {
128		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
129			return true, nil
130		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
131			return false, err
132		}
133		// Bare repositories have no .git entry. Their required top-level skeleton
134		// is still a repository boundary and may contain credentials, hooks, refs,
135		// or private objects that must never match a portable-file glob.
136		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
137			if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
138				return false, nil
139			} else if err != nil {
140				return false, err
141			}
142		}
143		return true, nil
144	}
145
146	func patternSource(pattern Pattern) string {
147		if strings.TrimSpace(pattern.Source) == "" {
148			return "explicit input"
149		}
150		return pattern.Source
151	}
152
153	func matchPattern(pattern, candidate string) bool {
154		patternParts := strings.Split(pattern, "/")
155		candidateParts := strings.Split(candidate, "/")
156		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
157		memo := map[key]bool{}
158		seen := map[key]bool{}
159		var match func(int, int) bool
160		match = func(patternIndex, candidateIndex int) bool {
161			state := key{patternIndex, candidateIndex}
162			if seen[state] {
163				return memo[state]
164			}
165			seen[state] = true
166			var result bool
167			switch {
168			case patternIndex == len(patternParts):
169				result = candidateIndex == len(candidateParts)
170			case patternParts[patternIndex] == "**":
171				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex) ||
172					candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && match(patternIndex, candidateIndex+1)
173			case candidateIndex < len(candidateParts) && matchComponent(patternParts[patternIndex], candidateParts[candidateIndex]):
174				result = match(patternIndex+1, candidateIndex+1)
175			}
176			memo[state] = result
177			return result
178		}
179		return match(0, 0)
180	}
181
182	func matchComponent(pattern, candidate string) bool {
183		p, c := []rune(pattern), []rune(candidate)
184		type key struct{ pattern, candidate int }
185		memo := map[key]bool{}
186		seen := map[key]bool{}
187		var match func(int, int) bool
188		match = func(pi, ci int) bool {
189			state := key{pi, ci}
190			if seen[state] {
191				return memo[state]
192			}
193			seen[state] = true
194			var result bool
195			switch {
196			case pi == len(p):
197				result = ci == len(c)
198			case p[pi] == '*':
199				result = match(pi+1, ci) || ci < len(c) && match(pi, ci+1)
200			case ci < len(c) && (p[pi] == '?' || p[pi] == c[ci]):
201				result = match(pi+1, ci+1)
202			}
203			memo[state] = result
204			return result
205		}
206		return match(0, 0)
207	}
208
209	func hasDependencyComponent(path string) bool {
210		for _, component := range strings.Split(path, "/") {
211			if _, blocked := dependencyComponents[strings.ToLower(component)]; blocked {
212				return true
213			}
214		}
215		return false
216	}

150			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetAmbiguous}
151		}
152		worktree, checkedOut, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, candidates[0].path, binding.Branch)
153		if err != nil {
154			return targetCheckout{}, err
155		}
156		if !checkedOut || worktree.Bare || worktree.Prunable {
157			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetFetchedOnly}
158		}
159		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, worktree.Path, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}")
160		if err != nil {
161			return targetCheckout{}, err
162		}
163		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, worktree.Path)
164		if err != nil {
165			return targetCheckout{}, err
166		}
167		if status.Detached || status.Branch != binding.Branch || head != binding.HeadOID || worktree.Head != binding.HeadOID {
168			return targetCheckout{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetStale}
169		}
170		checkout := targetCheckout{
171			root: worktree.Path, commonDir: candidates[0].commonDir,
172			identity: binding.RemoteIdentity, branch: binding.Branch, head: head,
173		}
174		checkout.id = digestJSON(struct {
175			Domain    string `json:"domain"`
176			CommonDir string `json:"common_dir"`
177			Root      string `json:"root"`
178			Branch    string `json:"branch"`
179			Head      string `json:"head"`
180		}{"dev-local-files-checkout-v1", checkout.commonDir, checkout.root, checkout.branch, checkout.head})
181		return checkout, nil
182	}
183
184	func checkoutHasIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout, wanted string) (bool, error) {
185		names, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote")
186		if err != nil {
187			return false, err
188		}
189		for _, name := range strings.Fields(names) {
190			// Repository identity is established from fetch URLs. A push-only match
191			// can name a different mirror or publication target and must not authorize
192			// writing local files into an otherwise unrelated clone.
193			urls, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "remote", "get-url", "--all", name)
194			if err != nil {
195				continue
196			}
197			for _, raw := range strings.Split(urls, "\n") {
198				if catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(raw) == wanted {
199					return true, nil
200				}
201			}
202		}
203		return false, nil
204	}
205
206	func (s *Service) Plan(ctx context.Context, request PlanRequest) (PlanResponse, error) {
207		if s == nil {
208			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("nil local-files service")
209		}
210		if s.platform() == "windows" {
211			return PlanResponse{}, &TargetError{Code: TargetIncompatible}
212		}
213		if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
214			return PlanResponse{}, err
215		}
216		id, err := s.machineID(ctx)
217		if err != nil {
218			return PlanResponse{}, err
219		}
220		if id != request.Binding.TargetMachine {
221			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("target machine identity changed after capability probe")
222		}
223		hostLimits := s.Config.LocalFiles.Limits()
224		if err := hostLimits.Validate(); err != nil {
225			return PlanResponse{}, err
226		}
227		negotiated, err := NegotiateLimits(hostLimits, request.Limits)
228		if err != nil || negotiated != request.SafeLimits() {
229			return PlanResponse{}, errors.New("plan limits do not match target policy")
230		}
231		checkout, err := s.resolveTarget(ctx, request.Binding)
232		if err != nil {
233			return PlanResponse{}, err
234		}
235		response := PlanResponse{
236			SchemaVersion: SchemaVersion, ProtocolVersion: fleet.LocalFilesProtocolVersion,
237			RequestID: request.RequestID, ManifestDigest: request.ManifestDigest,
238			TargetMachine: id, TargetCheckout: checkout.id,
239		}
240		for _, spec := range request.Files {
241			planned := PlanFile{PublicFile: spec.public(StateFailed)}
242			if err := proveGitEligibility(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path); err != nil {
243				planned.State = stateForError(err)
244				response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
245				continue
246			}
247			observed, err := observePath(ctx, checkout.root, spec.Path, request.SafeLimits(), true)
248			if err != nil {
249				planned.State = stateForError(err)
250				response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
251				continue
252			}
253			targetMode := ""
254			if observed.exists {
255				targetMode = fmt.Sprintf("%04o", observed.info.Mode().Perm())
256			}
257			switch {
258			case !observed.exists:
259				planned.State, planned.Action = StateReady, actionCreate
260			case observed.digest == spec.SHA256 && targetMode == spec.Mode:
261				planned.State, planned.Action, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateCurrent, actionCurrent, observed.digest, targetMode
262			case request.Replace:
263				planned.State, planned.Action, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateReady, actionReplace, observed.digest, targetMode
264			default:
265				planned.State, planned.TargetSHA256, planned.TargetMode = StateBlockedConflict, observed.digest, targetMode
266			}
267			response.Files = append(response.Files, planned)
268		}
269		response.PlanDigest = planDigest(request, response)
270		if err := response.Validate(request); err != nil {
271			return PlanResponse{}, err
272		}
273		return response, nil
274	}

72
73	// Record is the durable state for one canonical operation key. At most one of
74	// Reservation and Fence can be active.

77		Epoch       uint64      `json:"epoch"`

92		ErrConflict      = errors.New("operation lease conflict")
93		ErrEpochMismatch = errors.New("operation lease epoch mismatch")
94		ErrReturned      = errors.New("operation lease token is terminal")

105	func (e *BlockedError) Error() string {
106		return fmt.Sprintf("%s lease for %s is blocked by %s operation %s", e.Key.Scope, e.Key.subject(), e.Kind, e.OperationID)
107	}
108
109	func (e *BlockedError) Unwrap() error { return ErrBlocked }

111	func RepositoryKey(repository string) Key {

113	}

119	// GitCommonDirIdentity is the host-local canonical lease identity shared by
120	// every remote alias and linked worktree of one clone.
121	func GitCommonDirIdentity(commonDir string) string {
122		if strings.TrimSpace(commonDir) == "" {
123			return ""
124		}
125		return "git-common-dir:" + filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(commonDir))

127
128	func (k Key) Validate() error {
129		if err := validateIdentity("repository identity", k.Repository); err != nil {
130			return err
131		}
132		switch k.Scope {
133		case ScopeRepository:
134			if k.Branch != "" {
135				return errors.New("repository lease key must not name a branch")
136			}
137		case ScopeBranch:
138			if err := validateIdentity("branch", k.Branch); err != nil {
139				return err
140			}
141		default:
142			return fmt.Errorf("unknown lease scope %q", k.Scope)
143		}
144		return nil
145	}
146
147	func (k Key) canonical() string {
148		// Length prefixes keep arbitrary valid identities unambiguous.
149		return fmt.Sprintf("%08x:%s:%s:%08x:%s", len(k.Repository), k.Repository, k.Scope, len(k.Branch), k.Branch)
150	}
151
152	func (k Key) subject() string {
153		if k.Scope == ScopeBranch {
154			return k.Repository + " branch " + k.Branch
155		}
156		return k.Repository
157	}
158
159	func (r Request) Validate() error {
160		if !operationIDPattern.MatchString(r.OperationID) {
161			return fmt.Errorf("invalid operation id %q", r.OperationID)
162		}
163		if !assessment.ValidFingerprint(r.Digest) {
164			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s has invalid digest %q", r.OperationID, r.Digest)
165		}
166		if r.MachineID != "" {
167			if err := machineid.Validate(r.MachineID); err != nil {
168				return err
169			}
170		}
171		return nil
172	}
173
174	func (b Binding) Validate() error {
175		return (Request{OperationID: b.OperationID, Digest: b.Digest}).Validate()
176	}
177
178	func (t Token) Validate() error {
179		if err := (Request{OperationID: t.OperationID, Digest: t.Digest}).Validate(); err != nil {
180			return err
181		}
182		if t.Epoch == 0 {
183			return fmt.Errorf("operation %s has zero lease epoch", t.OperationID)
184		}
185		return nil
186	}
187
188	func (t Token) matches(other Token) bool {
189		return t.OperationID == other.OperationID && t.Digest == other.Digest && t.Epoch == other.Epoch
190	}
191
192	func (t Token) sameOperation(request Request) bool {
193		return t.OperationID == request.OperationID && t.Digest == request.Digest
194	}
195
196	// CanonicalKeys validates, deduplicates, and sorts keys in the one order used
197	// by every multi-key acquisition.
198	func CanonicalKeys(keys []Key) ([]Key, error) {
199		if len(keys) == 0 {
200			return nil, errors.New("operation lease requires at least one key")
201		}
202		unique := make(map[string]Key, len(keys))
203		for _, key := range keys {
204			if err := key.Validate(); err != nil {
205				return nil, err
206			}
207			unique[key.canonical()] = key
208		}
209		canonical := make([]Key, 0, len(unique))
210		for _, key := range unique {
211			canonical = append(canonical, key)
212		}
213		sort.Slice(canonical, func(i, j int) bool { return canonical[i].canonical() < canonical[j].canonical() })
214		return canonical, nil
215	}
216
217	func validateIdentity(name, value string) error {
218		if value == "" || value != strings.TrimSpace(value) {
219			return fmt.Errorf("%s is required and must be trimmed", name)
220		}
221		if !utf8.ValidString(value) {
222			return fmt.Errorf("%s is not valid UTF-8", name)
223		}
224		for _, char := range value {
225			if unicode.IsControl(char) {
226				return fmt.Errorf("%s contains a control character", name)
227			}
228		}
229		return nil
230	}

30	func DefaultRoot() string {

33
34	func New(root string) *Authority {
35		if root == "" {
36			root = DefaultRoot()
37		}
38		if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(root); err == nil {
39			root = absolute
40		}
